In this paper, we propose a novel approach to medical image segmentation that combines semi-supervised learning and graph cuts to achieve robust and accurate segmentation results. Our method leverages the strengths of both approaches to overcome their individual limitations and provide improved performance in comparison to traditional supervised learning methods.

Semi-supervised learning allows us to utilize large amounts of unlabeled data to train our model, which can be particularly useful in medical imaging where labeled data is scarce and expensive to obtain. However, semi-supervised learning alone may not produce accurate enough results since the model is not fully guided by labeled data. This is where graph cuts come into play. By incorporating graph cuts into our framework, we introduce an additional level of consistency and smoothness constraints that help improve the accuracy of the segmentation results.

Our proposed method consists of two stages: (1) pre-processing, where we use semi-supervised learning to initialize the segmentation labels, and (2) refinement, where we apply graph cuts to further refine the labels based on the spatial relationships between neighboring pixels. We evaluate our method using several publicly available datasets and compare it against state-of-the-art segmentation techniques. The experimental results demonstrate that our consensus-based approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

The main contributions of this work are:

* A novel approach to medical image segmentation that combines semi-supervised learning and graph cuts
* An effective way to leverage large amounts of unlabeled data to improve segmentation accuracy
* A robust and efficient algorithm that produces high-quality segmentation masks even when dealing with noisy or low-contrast images

This paper has important implications for medical image analysis tasks, as it provides a reliable and scalable solution for segmenting complex medical structures from images. The proposed method has the potential to significantly reduce the amount of manual effort required for annotating medical images, making it easier for researchers and clinicians to analyze and understand medical data.

This paper discusses the design of oversampled complex filter banks suitable for synthesis applications, with a focus on integer-valued design parameters. The filter banks are realized as direct forms II or III, with modulated complex filters. Design criteria are discussed, and an optimization strategy is proposed. The strategy includes the optimization of the individual filter envelopes, and of the synthesis window. Both objective and subjective criteria are considered. The optimization strategy is based on a genetic algorithm, and a comprehensive set of evaluations is reported. The sets of filter parameters found are evaluated in terms of perceptual quality, using both objective and subjective procedures. The filter banks generated by the proposed design strategy are shown to provide, in several cases, a significant improvement compared to a set of widely used filters.

David John Mays (born November 22, 1896 – died February 17, 1971) was an American lawyer and author. During the Massive Resistance era, Mays represented the Byrd Organization in efforts to hinder racial desegregation. He acted as legal advisor to the Gray Commission, aiming to devise segregationists' countermeasures in reaction to the 1954 and 1955 US Supreme Court decisions in Brown v. Board of Education. Later, Mays unsuccessfully safeguarded actions targeted at NAACP lawyers (having previously opposed such legislation and foreseen its annulment) and substantial legislative redistricting. In 2008, the University of Georgia Press released an annotated edition of excerpts from his diaries detailing the early stages of Massive Resistance (1954-1959).<ref>Reference: Race Reason and Massive Resistance: The Diary of David J. Mays, 1954-1959. Edited by James R. Sweeney (University of Georgia Press 2008)</ref> In 1953, Mays garnered the Pulitzer Prize in Biography or Autobiography for "Edmund Pendleton 1721-1803" (Harvard University Press, 1952), a biography of the late 18th-century Virginia political figure and judge, Edmund Pendleton. Born in Richmond, Mays came from a family that included his father, Harvey James Mays, a chemical company supervisor, and mother, Helga Nelsen, a former Danish immigrant. Rasmus Nelsen, Mays' Danish grandfather, established the Nelsen funeral home in Richmond. With ten siblings, Mays attended schools close to his father's workplaces in Alabama and a Memphis suburb. During a trip to visit Vanderbilt University with his father, they stopped in Ashland, Virginia, where Mays decided to attend Randolph-Macon Academy. Despite not earning a degree from this institution (attending from 1914-1916 and 1919-1920), Mays excelled academically.

Numerous prolonged summers marked by intense heat have passed, obliterating aspirations - no rain, only despair. Fine, powdery, and smooth, reddish soils shift in the scorching winds, relocating from their origins to new destinations, such as garbage cans. Fragile, delicate, and silken sand drifts, inflicting distress and agony, as the offspring of winter's plantings fail to thrive. Sun-scorched and aged faces reflect a distinct type of suffering, one characterized by hunger, thirst, and anxious minds. Vultures patrol above, poised to prey upon weakened beings, as the battle for survival persists in the quest for another day of existence. Previously towering, robust trees, along with native bushes, vegetation, and blossoms, now desperately hold on to life in their final moments. Time stretches out interminably as some clouds accumulate, only to dissipate just as swiftly, leaving beings in a state of frenzy. Eventually, a miraculous event unfolds as one of God's clouds unexpectedly ruptures, releasing a few drops that gradually emerge, perhaps during the most dire of circumstances. In a stunning and disbelieving moment, sparkling, liquid diamonds cascade from the heavens, rushing towards the earth as if escaping, while the gentle rains resume, bringing tranquility once more.

Falconetti's Chicken Thai Sausage Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 2 tablespoons fish sauce
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes
- 1/4 cup chopped cilantro
- 1/4 cup chopped scallions
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh basil leaves
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint leaves
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley leaves
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the chicken thighs with the fish sauce, soy sauce, honey, lime juice, garlic, ginger, red pepper flakes, cilantro, scallions, basil, mint, parsley, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to coat all of the chicken pieces evenly. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight to allow the flavors to marinate into the meat.
2. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3. Remove the chicken from the marinade and pat it dry with paper towels. Heat the vegetable oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken thighs to the skillet and cook until browned on both sides, about 6-8 minutes per side.
4. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for an additional 15-20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and no longer pink.
5. Allow the chicken to cool slightly before slicing into thin strips. Serve hot and enjoy!

Still I can hear your deep sob
Echoing in my heart
Pricking my conscience
I don't know what to say
We all grieve on your fate
But never raised a finger
I can see you stretched on a dingy cot
Your house dilapidated
Your hair undone spreading
Your tears dry
I see your bare neck
Still bearing red with finger prints
Your lips dry with fear
Oh mother your eye lashes wide with fear
Your deep blue eyes move round and round
The nightmare you had had multiple
The pain of life written all over your face
I can imagine all what you have gone through
Your children weep pulling yr skirt
Your torn skirt
Your body smelling sweat and saliva
Of those soldiers
Your breasts bear the stench of their beret
Your veil was hung on the wall stained in blood
Shaming the humanity
I see your children sucking from your dried breasts
Crying for little milk
Poor things they never had a decent meal for a long long time
Oh poor babies
We hear they cry waking you up
But you are tired
In fatigue
Oh my mother now they are bargaining your flesh
The shopkeepers and the Yankees
They want to trade your flesh
Your pride
Your chastity Your righteousness
Your dignity
Oh mother I weep for you
Let my tears mingle with blood flowing
_ in Euphretis and Tigris
I cry louder and louder

The narrative follows the course of a man's life from his schoolboy days to his adulthood. The son of a north German merchant and an Italian artist, Tonio inherited qualities from both sides of his family. As a child, he experiences conflicting feelings for the bourgeois people around him. He feels both superior to them in his insights and envious of their innocent vitality. This conflict continues into Tonio's adulthood, when he becomes a famous writer living in southern Germany. "To be an artist," he comes to believe, "one has to die to everyday life." These issues are only partially resolved when Tonio travels north to visit his hometown. While there, Tonio is mistaken for an escaped criminal, thereby reinforcing his inner suspicion that the artist must be an outsider relative to "respectable" society. As Erich Heller –who knew Thomas Mann personally– observed, Tonio Kröger’s theme is that of the "artist as an exile from reality" (with Goethe’s Torquato Tasso (1790) and Grillparzer’s Sappho (1818) for company). Yet it was also Erich Heller who, earlier, in his own youth, had diagnosed the main theme of Tonio Kröger to be the infatuation and entanglements of a passionate heart, destined to give shape to, intellectualize, its feelings in artistic terms.

The Dynamic Control of Local Field Emission Current from Carbon Nanowalls is a study that investigates the control of local field emission current from carbon nanowalls. The experimental results demonstrate that the emission current can be dynamically controlled by adjusting the voltage applied to the carbon nanowalls. This study has significant implications for the development of advanced nanoscale electronic devices and systems.

Infant health checks, known as newborn screening (NBS), involve identifying hidden conditions in newly born babies through testing. This process aims to diagnose infants at risk for such disorders early enough to administer treatment, modifying the disease's progression and preventing or reducing its symptoms. NBS emerged when it was discovered that phenylketonuria (PKU), an amino acid disorder, could be managed through dietary modifications, necessitating prompt intervention for optimal outcomes. Babies born with PKU exhibit no signs but cannot metabolize the vital amino acid phenylalanine, leading to severe intellectual disabilities.

In the late 1950s and '60s, Robert Guthrie introduced a straightforward technique using a bacterial inhibition assay to detect excessive phenylalanine levels in newborns' blood. He also championed the use of filter paper for collecting and transporting blood samples, understanding the importance of a streamlined system for widespread implementation. Today, most NBS procedures worldwide continue to employ filter paper technology. Initiated in the US during the early 1960s, NBS has since spread globally. National or state entities typically oversee these programs, targeting the screening of all infants within their jurisdiction for a specified range of treatable disorders. Jurisdictions decide the number of diseases to test for, which varies significantly. Majority of NBS assessments involve analyzing metabolites or enzyme activities from whole blood specimens obtained on filter paper. Some advanced programs incorporate bedside examinations for hearing impairments via automated auditory brainstem responses and congenital heart defects using pulse oximetry. Infants displaying positive test results undergo follow-up evaluations to ascertain if they indeed have a disease.

The story follows a young man named Amory Blaine who graduates from an elite Eastern college and begins his search for meaning in life, love, and friendship. He falls in love with a woman named Rosalind Constable but is ultimately rejected by her due to his lack of experience and maturity. Disillusioned, he embarks on a journey to find himself and discovers that true happiness lies within one's own self-discovery rather than external factors such as wealth or social status. Along the way, he encounters various characters each representing different aspects of society including intellectuals, bohemians, and wealthy elites all struggling with their own personal demons. In the end, Amory finds solace in his own understanding of what truly matters most: inner peace and genuine connections with others.

TO Jenny came a gentle youth
From inland leazes lone;
His love was fresh as apple-blooth
By Parrett, Yeo, or Tone.
And duly he entreated her
To be his tender minister,
And call him aye her own.
Fair Jenny's life had hardly been
A life of modesty;
At Casterbridge experience keen
Of many loves had she
From scarcely sixteen years above:
Among them sundry troopers of
The King's-Own Cavalry.
But each with charger, sword, and gun,
Had bluffed the Biscay wave;
And Jenny prized her gentle one
For all the love he gave.
She vowed to be, if they were wed,
His honest wife in heart and head
From bride-ale hour to grave.
Wedded they were. Her husband's trust
In Jenny knew no bound,
And Jenny kept her pure and just,
Till even malice found
No sin or sign of ill to be
In one who walked so decently
The duteous helpmate's round.
Two sons were born, and bloomed to men,
And roamed, and were as not:
Alone was Jenny left again
As ere her mind had sought
A solace in domestic joys,
And ere the vanished pair of boys
Were sent to sun her cot.
She numbered near on sixty years,
And passed as elderly,
When, in the street, with flush of fears,
On day discovered she,
From shine of swords and thump of drum,
Her early loves from war had come,
The King's Own Cavalry.
She turned aside, and bowed her head
Anigh Saint Peter's door;
"Alas for chastened thoughts!" she said;
"I'm faded now, and hoar,
And yet those notes--they thrill me through,
And those gay forms move me anew
As in the years of yore!"...
--'Twas Christmas, and the Phoenix Inn
Was lit with tapers tall,
For thirty of the trooper men
Had vowed to give a ball
As "Theirs" had done (fame handed down)
When lying in the self-same town
Ere Buonaparté's fall.
That night the throbbing "Soldier's Joy,"
The measured tread and sway
Of "Fancy-Lad" and "Maiden Coy,"
Reached Jenny as she lay
Beside her spouse; till springtide blood
Seemed scouring through her like a flood
That whisked the years away.
She rose, and rayed, and decked her head
To hide her ringlets thin;
Upon her cap two bows of red
She fixed with hasty pin;
Unheard descending to the street,
She trod the flags with tune-led feet,
And stood before the Inn.
Save for the dancers', not a sound
Disturbed the icy air;
No watchman on his midnight round
Or traveller was there;
But over All-Saints', high and bright,
Pulsed to the music Sirius white,
The Wain by Bullstake Square.
She knocked, but found her further stride
Checked by a sergeant tall:
"Gay Granny, whence come you?" he cried;
"This is a private ball."
--"No one has more right here than me!
Ere you were born, man," answered she,
"I knew the regiment all!"
"Take not the lady's visit ill!"
Upspoke the steward free;
"We lack sufficient partners still,
So, prithee let her be!"
They seized and whirled her 'mid the maze,
And Jenny felt as in the days
Of her immodesty.
Hour chased each hour, and night advanced;
She sped as shod with wings;
Each time and every time she danced--
Reels, jigs, poussettes, and flings:
They cheered her as she soared and swooped
(She'd learnt ere art in dancing drooped
From hops to slothful swings).
The favorite Quick-step "Speed the Plough"--
(Cross hands, cast off, and wheel)--
"The Triumph," "Sylph," "The Row-dow dow,"
Famed "Major Malley's Reel,"
"The Duke of York's," "The Fairy Dance,"
"The Bridge of Lodi" (brought from France),
She beat out, toe and heel.
The "Fall of Paris" clanged its close,
And Peter's chime told four,
When Jenny, bosom-beating, rose
To seek her silent door.
They tiptoed in escorting her,
Lest stroke of heel or chink of spur
Should break her goodman's snore.
The fire that late had burnt fell slack
When lone at last stood she;
Her nine-and-fifty years came back;
She sank upon her knee
Beside the durn, and like a dart
A something arrowed through her heart
In shoots of agony.
Their footsteps died as she leant there,
Lit by the morning star
Hanging above the moorland, where
The aged elm-rows are;
And, as o'ernight, from Pummery Ridge
To Maembury Ring and Standfast Bridge
No life stirred, near or far.
Though inner mischief worked amain,
She reached her husband's side;
Where, toil-weary, as he had lain
Beneath the patchwork pied
When yestereve she'd forthward crept,
And as unwitting, still he slept
Who did in her confide.
A tear sprang as she turned and viewed
His features free from guile;
She kissed him long, as when, just wooed.
She chose his domicile.
Death menaced now; yet less for life
She wished than that she were the wife
That she had been erstwhile.
Time wore to six. Her husband rose
And struck the steel and stone;
He glanced at Jenny, whose repose
Seemed deeper than his own.
With dumb dismay, on closer sight,
He gathered sense that in the night,
Or morn, her soul had flown.
When told that some too mighty strain
For one so many-yeared
Had burst her bosom's master-vein,
His doubts remained unstirred.
His Jenny had not left his side
Betwixt the eve and morning-tide:
--The King's said not a word.
Well! times are not as times were then,
Nor fair ones half so free;
And truly they were martial men,
The King's-Own Cavalry.
And when they went from Casterbridge
And vanished over Mellstock Ridge,
'Twas saddest morn to see.

Ingredients:

3 pounds bone-in chicken pieces (breasts, thighs, drumsticks, or a mix)
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
Salt and pepper
6 tablespoons olive oil
12 garlic cloves, peeled and smashed
1/2 cup dry white wine
2 cups chicken broth
2 tablespoons unsalted butter
1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:

1. Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then dust with the flour (shaking off the excess). In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the chicken pieces in 2 batches in the olive oil until golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes per batch; transfer to a plate.

2. Reduce the heat to medium, add the garlic to the skillet, and cook until golden, about 1 minute per side. Return all the chicken to the skillet, add the wine, and cook, scraping up any browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan, for about 1 minute. Add the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.

3. Remove the lid and simmer until the sauce is thickened, about 10 minutes. Stir in the butter and parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve.

Beyond the curtain of clouds, relentless sun beats down,
Despite my hopeful whispers, nature wears a frown.
Where are the drizzles I have longed, for idle solitude?
How stubbornly the azure sky doth my prayers elude.

I woke to whispers of leaves, rustling in quiet plea,
Begging the heavens to shower its liquid decree,
The birds too sung, a syncopated refrain,
Hinting at the promise, of a soothing rain.

From the parched flower buds, strained petals held high,
To the arid earth, mirroring the dry sky.
Look at them, longing for the melancholy song,
Yet, the rain remains silent, withholding its throng.

Right there, the riverbed lamenting dried tears,
Yearnings etched into its silty years.
I can almost hear the thirsty ground’s roar,
Why then, does the sky not pour?

I had forgotten the heat of the sun’s glare,
The burnished ground beneath, wearing a bare stare.
Yearned for the rhythm of rain on my window pane,
A lullaby soothe the day's unspoken pain.

Look at the pines, standing tall against the heat,
Mocking clouds offer no solace, no retreat.
I thought it would be a day to watch and muse,
Not to be scorched, by the sun's blatant abuse.

Even the breeze holds its breath, in anticipation,
Greys dance above, a tease of precipitation.
Still, the promise of droplets never falls,
The sun-bleached day merely sprawls.

So here I sit, beneath the shade's rare grace,
Waiting for rain, longing for its embrace.
Unfulfilled promises, hopes intertwined,
In the throbbing silence, only thirst we find. 

I thought it would rain today, alas it drags on,
The once hopeful morning now a weary yawn.
Yet in my heart, I can hear the rain's distant rhyme,
For in the realm of dreams, it is always raining time.

Eric Joseph  Wright (11 December 1912 – 21 December 1979) was an Australian general practitioner, medical administrator and public servant. Wright was born in St Leonards, Sydney, New South Wales and died in Lewisham, Sydney, New South Wales. After obtaining his education at Lewisham Public School he joined the department of public health as a medical assistant in 1930. Eric later established a school for medical assistants in Divinukoiari. Due to medical issues, Eric was unable to join the armed forces and instead studied medicine at the University of Sydney. Once Eric had furthered his education he returned to Papua and New Guinea where he then established a private practice. He would eventually marry his receptionist named Shirley May Chan Wong, née Hee. After accomplishing many other things in Papua and New Guinea Eric's health began to deteriorate so he returned to Sydney to be with his family. He was diagnosed with acute myocardial ischaemia and the disease later took his life on 21 December 1979 at Lewisham Hospital. See also

Mary Jane Blige (born January 11, 1971), an American singer-songwriter and actress, holds the title "Queen of Hip-Hop Soul." With nine Grammy Awards, four American Music Awards, and ten Billboard Music Awards under her belt, she's also earned three Golden Globe nominations and two Academy Award nods - for acting in "Mudbound" (2017) and its original song "Mighty River," marking her as the first person to be nominated for both acting and songwriting in a single year. Her music journey started in 1991 when she signed with Uptown Records. Her debut album, What's the 411? (1992), is known for blending R&B and hip hop into mainstream pop culture. The remixed version was the first album to feature a rapper on each track, thereby making rap a popular choice for collaborations. Two of her early works, What's the 411? and My Life (1994), made it to Rolling Stones 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list, and the latter to Time magazine's All-Time 100 Albums. Over her career, she released 14 studio albums, all reaching the Billboard 200 top ten, including four number-one records. Her notable singles include "Real Love," "Not Gon' Cry," "Be Without You," and the Billboard Hot 100 number-one hit "Family Affair."

Each summer, Celaya and her family return to her grandmother's home in Mexico City. At the house, Celaya meets Candelaria, the maid's daughter, who she secretly admires for her beauty. Here we also meet other members of her family, including the Awful Grandmother, Aunty Light-Skin, and the Little Grandfather. We learn about their stories. For example, the Little Grandfather lived in Chicago for a time and was injured during the Mexican Civil War. Aunty Light-Skin had an affair with an unnamed movie star. Through it all, the ties between families are bound together by the silken rebozo that stays in the family. The narrative turns to a story of Celaya's adolescence. Her family lives in Chicago but decides to move to San Antonio. Unfortunately for the father, his new job as an upholsterer is not well-paid, nor is he respected at work. Celaya learns to deal with a new home and classmates who pick on her. She meets Ernesto, who romances her and eventually brings her to Mexico City, ostensibly to marry. Instead, he runs away and Celaya must be rescued by her father. The Little Grandfather dies. Celaya's father grows old and infirm.

Taxi Driver is certainly not a film for the faint of heart. From the moment it opens with the haunting, atmospheric score, it grabs you by the throat and doesn't let go until the very end. Martin Scorsese's direction is masterful, effortlessly immersing the audience into the gritty underbelly of New York City in the 1970s.

Robert De Niro gives a tour-de-force performance as Travis Bickle, a mentally unstable Vietnam War veteran turned taxi driver. He perfectly captures the character's deep-rooted loneliness and alienation from society. De Niro's physical transformation for the role is also remarkable, further adding to his unsettling portrayal.

The film tackles intense themes such as vigilantism, urban decay, and the dark side of humanity. It forces viewers to confront their own moral compass as they navigate Bickle's descent into madness. The screenplay, written by Paul Schrader, is filled with thought-provoking dialogue and memorable quotes that have become iconic in cinema history.

The supporting cast is equally impressive, with Jodie Foster delivering a stunning performance as the troubled underage prostitute, Iris. Harvey Keitel, as the pimp Sport, is terrifying and manages to elicit a strange mix of fear and empathy from the audience.

The film's cinematography, courtesy of Michael Chapman, is truly outstanding. The use of color and lighting adds a palpable tension to every scene, perfectly complementing the dark and brooding atmosphere of the film. Scorsese's expertise in visual storytelling is on full display, making Taxi Driver a visual feast for cinephiles.

Taxi Driver is a deeply disturbing and thought-provoking masterpiece that continues to hold a significant place in cinematic history. Its exploration of the human psyche and social issues remains relevant today, making it a timeless classic. If you have a strong stomach and an appreciation for gritty, character-driven cinema, this film is an absolute must-watch.

The story starts with the murder of a New York state legislator named Joseph Cianci. The killer has never been identified and no suspect has been picked up as of yet. Cianci was killed at his Albany, New York home because his wife found a note that said in part;

I'm a hit man for the Mob,

I know where to find you,

I am the one that killed you.

The note also left a note warning that the hit man would come for two other Albany legislators that had been killed. And then he would come for the wife of one of the dead legislators.

Cianci's wife, Claudia, quickly takes matters into her own hands and travels to Albany, the capital city of New York and also the home of the politician who had been murdered. When she reaches the mob boss who was behind the murder of her husband, all is not what it seems. For one, the politician was one of Cianci's good friends and had been part of his political team when Cianci was the state's Assemblyman.

The hit man was actually a man named Vito Spatafore who came to Albany from New York City. While working as an agent for the F.B.I., Vito spied on Cianci, his wife, and others he thought was related to Cianci (this is an excerpt from the movie). While Claudia is getting ready to go to Albany to identify and capture the hit man, a second letter arrives in the mail. This letter states, "Your husband and he are about to go to court, where our friend Vito will be forced to testify against them." This "friend" was none other than Tony Soprano.

The movie will end with the testimony of Cianci's good friend. Soprano was hired by Vito to eliminate Cianci, his wife, and the politicians who were murdered. Claudia arrives in Albany and sees that Vito is already there and she has no choice but to turn around and run. Claudia gets her two young daughters to safety as she rushes to the Capitol's entrance and runs through the city to find her husband.

Troy Wayne Grant (born 11 February 1970) is an Australian former politician and former police officer. Grant was the Minister for Police and the Minister for Emergency Services from January 2017 until March 2019 in the Berejiklian government. He was a member of the New South Wales Legislative Assembly representing Dubbo for the Nationals from 2011 to 2019. He is a former Deputy Premier of New South Wales and New South Wales Leader of The Nationals from October 2014 to November 2016. Grant was the Minister for Justice and Police, the Minister for Racing and the Minister for the Arts in the second Baird government, between April 2015 and January 2017. In April 2014, Grant was appointed as the Minister for Hospitality, Gaming and Racing and the Minister for the Arts in the first Baird government. Grant gained additional portfolio responsibilities in October 2014 and in addition to the above responsibilities in the two Baird ministries, he also served as the Minister for Trade and Investment, Minister for Regional Infrastructure and Services, and the Minister for Tourism and Major Events until 2 April 2015. Grant stood down as Nationals leader and Deputy Premier on 15 November 2016. He was Minister for Police until being replaced in that position by David Elliott on 2 April 2019.

Komchén is a community in the Mérida Municipality in the state of Yucatán, located in southeastern Mexico. Komchén is located 15 kilometers north of the city of Mérida, in the northwestern portion of the Yucatán Peninsula and is approximately 20 km from the northern peninsular coast. Its name comes from the Yucatec Mayan and means: In the well of the hollow. Its infrastructure includes, educational services (a kindergarten, a primary school, a high school and a Bachelors School and a municipal library), a clinic of the Mexican Social Security Institute as well as recreational parks and marinas. 90% of Its streets are paved. Pre-Columbian History
Komchén is also the location of a pre-Columbian Maya archaeological site of the same name and is situated close to the site of Dzibilchaltun.  Pre-Columbian Komchén was initially settled during the Mesoamerican Middle Preclassic.  Its earliest settlement consisted of a small residential community with perishable structure.  The site transitioned into a larger community during the Late Preclassic, reaching its peak in construction between the years 350-150 BC and employing permanent stone masonry in architectural construction.  It appears that the site was entirely abandoned by the end of the Late Preclassic (ca. A.D. 250).  Later, however, the site was partially reoccupied by residents of the expanding center of Dzibilchaltun.

Tenedos (Ancient Greek: Τένεδος) was a small island in the Hellespont, located near the city of Troy in ancient Phrygia (modern-day Turkey). The island played a significant role in Greek mythology and history, particularly during the Trojan War.

In Greek mythology, Tenedos was said to be the home of the hero Achilles' son, Neoptolemus, who was born on the island after Achilles' death. According to some sources, Achilles himself was also buried on Tenedos, and his tomb was a place of pilgrimage for heroes and warriors. The island was also associated with the god Apollo, who was worshipped there as Apollo Tenedios.

During the Trojan War, Tenedos served as a base for the Greeks, who used it as a strategic location to launch attacks against Troy. In Book 12 of Homer's Iliad, the island is described as being under the control of the Greek hero Diomedes, who had captured it from the Trojans. The island's fortifications were said to be impregnable, and it was used as a safe haven for ships and soldiers.

The historical accuracy of Tenedos' role in the Trojan War has been debated by scholars, with some arguing that it may have been exaggerated or invented for dramatic effect in the Iliad. However, archaeological evidence suggests that the island was indeed inhabited during the late Bronze Age, around the time period in which the Trojan War is believed to have taken place.

Today, the exact location of Tenedos is unknown, although it is thought to have existed somewhere in the Dardanelles strait, possibly near the modern town of Gökçeada (formerly known as Imbros) in Turkey. Despite its significance in ancient times, little remains of the island today, and it is largely forgotten except in literary and historical circles. Nevertheless, the legend of Tenedos lives on through its mention in works such as the Iliad and other classical texts, serving as a reminder of the rich cultural heritage of ancient Greece.

Season with salt and pepper. Ladle into warmed bowls and serve hot.

For an hour's space--

Us for special grace.

Damned us ere our birth)

Looking for the Earth.
Hand in pulling hand amid

Hunted us along,

Steven Spielberg inquired of a friend, "Why wasn't this film favored by audiences?" In my opinion, I can clarify - "1941" caters primarily to an exclusive demographic. This select group consists of individuals possessing an extensive appreciation and familiarity with Los Angeles and its history. Approximating around 1% of the global cinema audience, this segment finds immense nostalgic worth in the film. Moreover, those among them harboring a peculiar sense of humor, who take delight in observing nostalgic L.A. in destruction, are particularly catered to by this movie. It is essential to note that this subset of the 1% likely constitutes approximately 1% of the initial 1%.

Growing up in L.A. and holding a deep fascination for its history, I personally find humor in visual representations of aircraft clashing above Hollywood Boulevard, the Ferris wheel detaching from the Santa Monica Pier, and aviation craft plummeting into the La Brea Tar Pits. However, for outsiders and individuals unacquainted with the pervasive anxiety that ensued throughout Southern California following Pearl Harbor, this film may appear baffling and absurd. To the historian bearing a warped sense of humor (such as myself, a devoted member of the 1% of the 1%), the movie offers more than just amusement; it often presents surprising historical accuracy. Robert Stack portrays General Joseph Stillwell - a genuine historical figure in L.A.'s past. Remarkably, Stack closely resembles the actual General Stillwell. The entire production is inspired by several authentic occurrences of hysterical anti-aircraft firing over L.A. during 1941-1942, along with a Japanese submarine that bombarded an oil refinery nearby Santa Barbara. Similar to "Chinatown," which is commonly misconstrued as an accurate representation of L.A.'s water politics in the 1930s, "1941" derives inspiration from historical facts and transforms them into wholly fictional narratives. Unlike "Chinatown," however, "1941" transpires as an exaggerated comedy rather than a noir drama. Both productions captivate historians, albeit in distinct manners.

We propose a method to classify cardiac pathology based on a novel approach
to extract image derived features to characterize the shape and motion of the
heart. An original semi-supervised learning procedure, which makes efficient
use of a large amount of non-segmented images and a small amount of images
segmented manually by experts, is developed to generate pixel-wise apparent
flow between two time points of a 2D+t cine MRI image sequence. Combining the
apparent flow maps and cardiac segmentation masks, we obtain a local apparent
flow corresponding to the 2D motion of myocardium and ventricular cavities.
This leads to the generation of time series of the radius and thickness of
myocardial segments to represent cardiac motion. These time series of motion
features are reliable and explainable characteristics of pathological cardiac
motion. Furthermore, they are combined with shape-related features to classify
cardiac pathologies. Using only nine feature values as input, we propose an
explainable, simple and flexible model for pathology classification. On ACDC
training set and testing set, the model achieves 95% and 94% respectively as
classification accuracy. Its performance is hence comparable to that of the
state-of-the-art. Comparison with various other models is performed to outline
some advantages of our model.

The Remains of the Day tells, in first person, the story of Stevens, an English butler who has dedicated his life to the loyal service of Lord Darlington (mentioned in increasing detail in flashbacks). The novel begins with Stevens receiving a letter from a former colleague, Miss Kenton, describing her married life, which he believes hints at an unhappy marriage. The receipt of the letter coincides with Stevens having the opportunity to revisit this once-cherished relationship, if only under the guise of investigating the possibility of re-employment. Stevens's new employer, a wealthy American named Mr Farraday, encourages Stevens to borrow his car to take a well-earned break, a "motoring trip". As he sets out, Stevens has the opportunity to reflect on his immutable loyalty to Lord Darlington, on the meaning of the term "dignity", and even on his relationship with his own late father. Ultimately Stevens is forced to ponder the true nature of his relationship with Miss Kenton. As the book progresses, increasing evidence of Miss Kenton's one-time love for Stevens, and of his for her, is revealed. Working together during the years leading up to the Second World War, Stevens and Miss Kenton fail to admit their true feelings towards each other. All of their recollected conversations show a professional friendship which at times came close to crossing the line into romance, but never dared to do so. Miss Kenton, it later emerges, has been married for over 20 years and therefore is no longer Miss Kenton but has become Mrs Benn. She admits to wondering occasionally what a life with Stevens might have been like, but she has come to love her husband and is looking forward to the birth of their first grandchild. Stevens muses over lost opportunities, both with Miss Kenton and with his long-time employer, Lord Darlington. At the end of the novel, Stevens instead focuses on the "remains of [his] day", referring to his future service with Mr Farraday.

"The Owl and the Pussycat" features four anthropomorphic animals – an owl, a cat, a pig, and a turkey – and tells the story of the love between the title characters who marry in the land "where the Bong-tree grows". The Owl and the Pussycat set out to sea in a pea green boat with honey and "plenty of money" wrapped in a five pound note. The Owl serenades the Pussycat while gazing at the stars and strumming on a small guitar. He describes her as beautiful. The Pussycat responds by describing the Owl as an "elegant fowl" and compliments him on his singing. She urges they marry but they don't have a ring. They sail away for a year and a day to a land where Bong-trees grow and discover a pig with a ring in his nose in a wood. They buy the ring for a shilling and are married the next day by a turkey. They dine on mince and quince using a runcible spoon, then dance hand-in-hand on the sand in the moonlight. Portions of an unfinished sequel, "The Children of the Owl and the Pussycat", were first published posthumously in 1938.

Ingredients:
- 8 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 head of garlic, cloves separated and peeled
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh thyme leaves
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 4 slices of French bread
- 1 cup Gruyere cheese, grated

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Add the garlic cloves to the pot and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3. Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let simmer for 20 minutes.
4. Add the parsley, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and black pepper to the pot. Stir well and continue to simmer for another 10 minutes.
5. While the soup is simmering, preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Place the slices of French bread on a baking sheet and toast in the oven until crispy, about 10 minutes.
6. Remove the bay leaf from the soup and discard. Use an immersion blender or a regular blender to puree the soup until smooth.
7. Ladle the soup into individual oven-safe bowls. Place a slice of toasted French bread on top of each bowl and sprinkle with grated Gruyere cheese.
8. Place the bowls on a baking sheet and broil in the oven until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 3-5 minutes.
9. Carefully remove the bowls from the oven and let cool for a few minutes before serving. Enjoy the L'Aido Boulido hot.

Ralph has befriended a young boy named Ryan, the son of the inn's new maid. Ryan has given Ralph the full name of "Ralph S. Mouse," the middle initial standing for "Smart." (The name is not seen in the previous two books.) Meanwhile, Ralph becomes agitated at his family. Forced by his parents to let numerous younger siblings and cousins ride his motorcycle, which is beginning to wear out due to their careless treatment and also worried that their droppings on the floor will result in anti-mouse retaliation by the hotel staff, he asks Ryan to take him to school, where he plans to hide and live out the rest of his life. Ralph is discovered by Ryan's classmates, who adopt him as a class pet and decide to see how smart he is by building a maze for him to run through. All this time Ryan is having difficulties with an aggressive boy named Brad from his class. Brad accidentally breaks Ralph's motorcycle, and Ralph blames Ryan and runs away to hide in the school. However, Ralph also confronts Brad for breaking his motorcycle, and Brad, realizing that Ralph can talk, offers to set things right for him and Ryan. Ryan and Brad discover that they have much in common and become friends. Ryan reclaims Ralph and brings him home on the school bus on the day that his new friend comes with him to visit at the inn. Brad also atones for his destruction of Ralph's treasured motorcycle by giving him his toy car. Ralph discovers that like the motorcycle, he can move the car by making car engine noises as a boy would do while playing with it. Ralph further discovers that he can safely give his younger relatives rides in the car without worrying that they will be irresponsible with it (but only Ralph can drive the car). Brad's father meets Ryan's mother and they marry six months later, thus Ryan and Brad are now brothers.

Did you hear that piercing scream? it echoed so savagely,
As if a heart heavily laden
Was shattering under the weight of deep sorrow.
Did you observe those hands, so weakly intertwined -
The quivering frame, so frail and thin -
The pained expression etched upon the face?
Did you notice the pleading, tear-filled gaze?
Each glance held anguish, as if a tempest
Of suffering raged within her mind.
She is a mother, deathly pale with fear,
Her child clinging tightly to her side,
Desperately concealing his trembling body
In the folds of her once vibrant skirt.
Yet he is not hers, though she endured
The trials of pregnancy and birth,
Though her essence flowed within his veins.
He is not hers, for harsh hands may violently
Tear asunder the fragile bond
That holds her heart together, shattered.
His presence had been a beacon of delight,
Illuminating her existence with warmth,
A ceaseless wellspring of affection,
Fueling her being amidst life's desolation.
Even his gentlest words had formed melodies
That resonated within her soul,
Their lives, a single river, flowing harmoniously -
Oh, God! Must they be separated?
They wrench him from her loving embrace,
Her final touch, her lasting kiss.
Oh! Never again shall her sad eyes
Rest upon his sorrowful countenance.
No wonder then, these gut-wrenching screams
Pierce the tranquility of the silence;
She is a mother, and her heart lies broken
Beneath the crushing weight of despair.

We introduce Gen-LaneNet, a novel and extensible approach for extracting 3D lanes from individual images. Modeled after the most recent state-of-the-art 3D-LaneNet, Gen-LaneNet is a unified system addressing image encoding, spatial transformation of features, and 3D lane estimation within a single network. Our innovation lies in two key aspects. Initially, we propose a novel geometry-directed lane anchor representation in a fresh coordinate system and employ a distinct geometric conversion to directly compute genuine 3D lane points from network results. Aligning lane points with top-level feature correspondences in the new coordinate system proves essential for a versatile technique when dealing with new environments. Additionally, we put forth a two-tier architecture that separates the acquisition of image segmentation subnetwork and geometry encoding subnetwork learning processes. Unlike 3D-LaneNet, Gen-LaneNet significantly diminishes the quantity of 3D lane labels necessary to generate a reliable resolution in practical applications. Furthermore, we publish a new artificial dataset along with its creation process to stimulate the exploration and assessment of 3D lane detection techniques. In trials, we carry out comprehensive analysis to verify that Gen-LaneNet surpasses 3D-LaneNet in terms of average precision (AP) and F-score.

The US trade gap ballooned to $73.3 billion in October, the largest deficit since 2008, as exports declined faster than imports.

The trade deficit rose 18.2% to $73.3 billion in October, up from a revised deficit of $61.2 billion in September, the Commerce Department said on Thursday.

 exports declined by 3.0% to $140.3 billion, the lowest level since April 2021, while imports rose 0.6% to $213.6 billion, a record high.

The strong dollar, which appreciated by about 7% against the currencies of major US trading partners over the past year, has made American exports more expensive and imports cheaper, contributing to the widening trade deficit.

The White House has been pressing domestic companies to focus on increasing exports and has been pushing for legislative action to lower taxes on foreign profits of US multinational companies in an effort to encourage them to bring home dollars they say are parked overseas.

But the legislation, which is being considered by the Senate, has been stalled by disagreements over the tax treatment of intellectual property.

The story is set in Corrientes, a city in northern Argentina, near the border with Paraguay which can be assumed from the police cars that reads ¨Policía de Corrientes¨. Eduardo Plarr is a young doctor of English descent. As a boy, he left Paraguay with his mother, escaping to Buenos Aires while his English father remained in Paraguay as a political rebel. Aside from a single hand-delivered letter, they never hear from the father again. When Plarr moves to the quiet, subtropical backwater town, he strikes up acquaintance with the only two English inhabitants, a bitter old English teacher, Humphries, and the Honorary Consul of the title, Charles Fortnum, a divorced, self-pitying alcoholic who misuses his position. Plarr's other main acquaintance is Julio Saavedra, a forgotten but self-important Argentine writer of novels full of silent machismo. Visiting the local brothel with Saavedra, Plarr is attracted to a girl, but she is taken by another man. A couple of years later, he is called to treat Fortnum's new wife. Plarr sees that she's the same girl from the brothel, Clara. Plarr regards himself as a cool, self-controlled Englishman (although he has never been to England), he finds himself becoming obsessed by Clara. He later seduces her by buying her some sunglasses and they begin an affair, although he tries to remain emotionally distant from her. "Caring is the only dangerous thing," Plarr says in the novel. "`Love' was a claim which he wouldn't meet, a responsibility he would refuse to accept, a demand. So many times his mother had used the word when he was a child; it was like the threat of an armed robber. `Put up your hands or else ...' Something was always asked in return: obedience, an apology, a kiss which one had no desire to give." Clara becomes pregnant, and Fortnum believes the child is his and starts drinking less. Then some of Plarr's friends from school turn up at his surgery, one of them is a failed priest named Rivas. They have news of Plarr's father; he is alive in a jail in Paraguay. They have a plot, for which they need a doctor's assistance, to kidnap the US ambassador on his trip to Corrientes. They will demand the release of political prisoners in Paraguay, including Plarr's father, in return for the ambassador. But the band kidnaps the wrong man; Charley Fortnum, the Honorary Consul, whom they take to a squalid hut in a shanty town. The rest of the novel charts Plarr's efforts to get Fortnum released, either as a result of diplomatic action from the UK, whose ambassador in BA is a comedy figure, or as a result of his schoolfriends giving up. But no-one listens to him. Saavedra and Humphries fail to help Plarr in his efforts. The police suspect that Plarr is involved in the kidnapping, as they know about his affair with Clara, and his behaviour has been suspicious. And they tell him his father was shot dead in Paraguay while attempting escape. Plarr goes to the hut, where Fortnum has been shot in the leg while attempting escape. Fortnum spends much of his time as he faces up to his death in sentimentalizing about Clara and in remembering the fearsome figure of his father. Then he discovers that Plarr is having an affair with Clara, and that the child is Plarr's. Meanwhile, members of the motley band drift away, and the police close in and surround the hut, while the failed priest, Father Rivas, conducts a makeshift mass inside with the rain coming down and police waiting. The police deadline is about to expire. Plarr goes out to talk to the police, but he is killed by the paratroopers, along with the other kidnappers. The authorities blame Plarr's death on the kidnappers. Plarr's mother, once a beauty and now bloated, and some of his previous older mistresses attend his funeral. Saavedra reads a homily. The UK embassy then relieves Fortnum of his consulship. In the last scene, Fortnum and Clara attempt a reconciliation. Fortnum will name the child Eduardo.

David Prutton of Southampton may face a potential seven-game suspension at the Football Association hearing due to two counts of misconduct. His offenses stem from his ejection against Arsenal, where he failed to depart swiftly, confronted referee Alan Wiley and assistant Paul Norman. A further infraction involves threatening language or behavior towards a match official during the 1-1 encounter. In 1998, Paolo di Canio received a similar seven-game penalty for pushing referee Paul Alcock in a Premiership game between Sheffield Wednesday and Arsenal. At the hearing, Harry Redknapp, Saints manager, will be present, expecting a harsh judgment for Prutton. Redknapp previously intervened on the touchline, helping to remove an agitated Prutton from referee's assistant Norman's presence. Redknapp stated, "Prutton has erred significantly and recognizes it. I cannot endorse his actions. He lost self-control for unknown reasons – he's normally a lovely guy off the pitch." Prutton publicly apologized for his transgressions and expressed regret towards Arsenal's Robert Pires, who sustained injury from a rough challenge by Prutton. He stated, "This is a regrettable circumstance. I extend my apologies to the ref and linesman, carrying out their duties. I've viewed Pires' injury and feel remorseful for that as well. I apologize to those who witnessed it. Sometimes, reactions occur beyond our command."

I've seen this movie three times by now and still think it's brilliant, yet it's not a movie for everybody. It's surely no coincidence that even Martin Scorsese had to struggle for 25 years to scrape together the funds to make it.

I can also understand why so many folks feel the movie is boring and too long even if to me it was neither boring nor too long. In fact, it feels just perfect. The reason I suppose many people don't truly 'feel' this movie -an exception in Mr Scorsese's rich filmography- is because of its theme. For surely, in times of abundant secularism and reductionist materialism, a movie such as this one cannot be other than a dinosaur.

Richard Haynes (27 January 1926 – 6 November 2015) was a Jamaican lawyer, judge and cricket administrator.

Haynes was born in Kingston, Jamaica. He was educated at St. Peter's School, and then at Selwyn College in Toronto, Canada. He graduated from the University of Toronto in 1948 with a BA in physics and chemistry, and then attended Oxford University, where he obtained a degree in jurisprudence in 1950. He was called to the bar by the Middle Temple in 1951.

Haynes returned to Jamaica later that year and practised law in Kingston. He joined the law firm of Lee & Pusey (now fused with others to form Norton Rose Fulbright) in 1953, and from 1966 to 1996 he was a partner in the firm. He became a Queen's Counsel in 1963. From 1993 to 1996 he was the senior partner of the firm.

On 1 August 1996, Haynes was appointed a judge of the Supreme Court of Jamaica. He served until his retirement on 27 January 2001, becoming chief justice of Jamaica on the same day. As chief justice, he was the chairman of the Judicial Service Commission and a member of the Defence Council of Jamaica.

Haynes was involved in cricket administration in Jamaica for many years, serving as a board member of the Jamaica Cricket Association and, for 34 years, as the association's legal adviser. He was also the legal adviser to the West Indies Cricket Board from 1997 to 2006. In 2008 he was made an honorary life member of the Jamaican association.

Haynes died on 6 November 2015 at the age of 89.

In medicine, the mean systemic pressure (mean systemic filling pressure (MSFP)) is defined as the mean pressure that exists in the circulatory system when there is no blood motion. A similar term, mean circulatory filling pressure, (MCFP) is defined as the mean pressure that exists in the combined circulatory system & pulmonary system when there is no blood motion. The value of MSP in animal experimental models is approximately 7 mm Hg. It is an indicator of how full the circulatory system is (i.e. the volume of blood in the system compared to the capacity of the system), and is influenced by the volume of circulating blood and the smooth muscle tone in the walls of the venous system (which determines the capacity of the system). MSP is measured in two ways experimentally, and as a result has two alternative naming conventions. MSFP is measured after clamping the aortic root and the great veins at point of entry to right atrium. On the other hand, MCFP is measured experimentally by briefly inducing cardiac arrest or naturally during cardiac arrest once the blood redistributes.  It may also be estimated in vivo using a series of inspiratory holds when a patient is on a mechanical ventilator. It can be used to demonstrate effects of drugs on the venous tone while the circulating blood volume remains constant, or to measure haemodynamic changes during haemorrhage.

The late John Peel's BBC Radio 1 show is to be succeeded in February by three shows hosted by three DJs focusing on diverse, non-commercial music.

Radio 1 said the show would not try to replace Peel, but would rise to the "challenge" of "keeping his legacy alive" with unpredictable music. Peel died after suffering a heart attack in Peru in October. Radio 1 said the three DJs had been chosen for their "in-depth musical knowledge across a variety of musical genres". Rob Da Bank has been hosting The John Peel Show since the DJ's death. He is also one of the hosts of The Blue Room, an early morning weekend show that plays a mix of old and new electronic and dance music. Huw Stephens is currently one half of the Radio 1 Thursday night show Bethan and Huw in Wales, which explores new music, especially up and coming acts breaking through in Wales. And Ras Kwame is the host of 100% Homegrown on Radio 1's digital station 1Xtra. His show is dedicated to showcasing the best of UK black music and broadcasts live sessions, often giving new artists their first chance to perform on live national radio.
All of the three DJs will continue to host their current shows on Radio 1. "It is widely accepted that John Peel can never be replaced," said the radio station. It added that One Music would support both signed and unsigned talent, and said: "It will seek out those making music for music's sake rather than for commercial success. "Above all it will provide support to emerging genres of music and styles that have not yet and may never reach the mainstream."
One Music is not new to Radio 1 as it already exists as a website, offering advice on aspects of the music industry, such as recording a demo and signing a record contract. Radio 1's controller, Andy Parfitt, said: "We believe that by having a series of DJs hosting a selection of shows under the One Music title, we will ensure that his legacy lives on." Stephens said he grew up "listening to John" and that it was a "massive honour" to continue Peel's work championing new music. The show will be broadcast from 1 February on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays from 2300 GMT - 0100 GMT.

1 1/2 tablespoons unsalted butter
1 large green apple, such as Granny Smith, peeled and diced
1/4 cup raisins
1 1/2 tablespoons sugar
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
Juice of 1 lemon
1 1/2 cups masa harina
1 1/2 tablespoons melted butter
3/4 tablespoon salt
1 1/2 teaspoons light agave nectar
12 tamale husks
1 quart vanilla ice cream, for serving
1/2 cup goats milk caramel, or regular caramel, for serving
For the apple compote: Set a medium saute pan over medium-high heat. Add the butter and green apples. Saute until the apples soften, 1 to 2 minutes, and then add the raisins, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and lemon juice. Add 1/4 cup of water and simmer until the apples are cooked through and the raisins are plumped, about 5 minutes. Set the compote aside to cool on a plate. For the tamales: Mix the masa harina, 1 1/4 cups water, butter, salt and agave into a thick paste. Fold the apple compote into the masa mixture. Set a corn husk out on a flat surface (double up or shingle 2 husks if they are small or have tears). Add 5 tablespoons of the masa mix into the center of the corn husk. Push the mixture to 1 inch from the side of the husk. Fold one edge of the husk to the center and then fold the other side to cover the entire tamale. Fold the ends over by 2 inches and tuck under to hold in place. Place a colander in large pot of boiling water, but do not let the colander touch the water. Place the tamales in the colander, cover and steam the tamales for 30 to 40 minutes. Serve the tamales topped with vanilla ice cream and a drizzle of caramel.

Medical image segmentation through deep neural networks has shown remarkable success in recent years via supervised learning using extensively labeled data. However, obtaining such expert annotations on vast medical datasets can be time-consuming, costly, or even absent. Weakly supervised learning offers a solution with reduced need for expertise, yet it still necessitates some level of involvement. Recent advancements in deep learning suggest that these models may generate more precise predictions than incorrect initial labels. Motivated by this observation, we present a method for detecting and segmenting cystic lesions in lung CT scans using extremely weak supervision, devoid of any manual annotations. This approach operates in a self-learning fashion, utilizing segmentations produced in earlier stages (initially from unsupervised segmentation and subsequently refined by neural networks) as ground truth for subsequent network training. Results on a cystic lung lesion dataset demonstrate that deep learning outperforms the initial unsupervised labeling and continuously enhances its performance post self-learning.

Quantum information based on continuous variables is a domain within quantum information science that employs physical properties, such as the intensity of an electromagnetic field, which have values lying within unbounded ranges. A major application lies in quantum computing; in essence, this form of computation is "analog," whereas computations using qubits are "digital." More technically, infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces characterize continuous-variable quantum computation, whereas finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces apply to collections of qubit systems. Continuous-variable quantum computation research aims to explore the required resources to surpass the capabilities of classical computers with quantum computers.

Implementation in laboratories can be achieved via quantum optics techniques. Each mode of the electromagnetic field is treated as a quantum harmonic oscillator, complete with corresponding creation and annihilation operators. Consequently, a conjugate pair of variables – referred to as "quadratures" – emerges for every mode, serving as position and momentum analogues. The phase space for these observables is established, enabling the definition of Wigner quasiprobability distributions. Measurements on such a system can be carried out using homodyne and heterodyne detectors.

Instead of directly utilizing an observed image including some outliers,
noise or intensity inhomogeneity, the use of its ideal value (e.g. noise-free
image) has a favorable impact on clustering. Hence, the accurate estimation of
the residual (e.g. unknown noise) between the observed image and its ideal
value is an important task. To do so, we propose an $\ell_0$
regularization-based Fuzzy $C$-Means (FCM) algorithm incorporating a
morphological reconstruction operation and a tight wavelet frame transform. To
achieve a sound trade-off between detail preservation and noise suppression,
morphological reconstruction is used to filter an observed image. By combining
the observed and filtered images, a weighted sum image is generated. Since a
tight wavelet frame system has sparse representations of an image, it is
employed to decompose the weighted sum image, thus forming its corresponding
feature set. Taking it as data for clustering, we present an improved FCM
algorithm by imposing an $\ell_0$ regularization term on the residual between
the feature set and its ideal value, which implies that the favorable
estimation of the residual is obtained and the ideal value participates in
clustering. Spatial information is also introduced into clustering since it is
naturally encountered in image segmentation. Furthermore, it makes the
estimation of the residual more reliable. To further enhance the segmentation
effects of the improved FCM algorithm, we also employ the morphological
reconstruction to smoothen the labels generated by clustering. Finally, based
on the prototypes and smoothed labels, the segmented image is reconstructed by
using a tight wavelet frame reconstruction operation. Experimental results
reported for synthetic, medical, and color images show that the proposed
algorithm is effective and efficient, and outperforms other algorithms.

Copula correlation is a novel metric designed to capture dependences between variables, which expands upon the traditional Pearson's correlation coefficient. Unlike Pearson's correlation coefficient that measures linear relationship based on conditional variance, copula correlation incorporates general dependence structures and can be used with continuous or discrete data sets. Furthermore, the copula correlation has two variants - Spearman copula correlation and Kendall copula correlation - each having different interpretations based on their construction. This paper provides an overview of these correlations, including mathematical expressions and derivations of respective results. We also introduce some applications in statistics and finance by illustrating examples of when this correlation measure may provide advantageous information over traditional correlation metrics. Overall, we argue that copula correlation offers a valuable tool for researchers seeking equitable dependence measuring methods, applicable in various fields such as economics, engineering, biology, psychology and more.

A rise has been recorded in the number of students from south of the border applying to universities in Scotland.
However, Lifelong Learning Minister Jim Wallace said that this would not result in Scottish students missing out. Applications from England and Wales rose by 17% between January 2005 and the previous year, up 23,600 to 27,700. Fears had been expressed that a flood of "fee refugees" would try to avoid top-up fees of up to £3,000 a year being introduced in England. In June last year, Mr Wallace announced proposals to increase tuition fees for English students studying in Scotland by £2,000 in an attempt to prevent a cross-border flood, although no figure has yet been agreed. Legislation to introduce the top-up fees in England is not due to take effect until autumn 2006 and students who start before then will not have to pay additional fees at all.
The figures were made public on Thursday by admissions service Ucas. Universities Scotland, which represents university principals, claimed that an increase in applications did not amount to Scottish students being squeezed out. Director, David Caldwell, said some students could be applying in an attempt to avoid the possible increase in annual fees at English universities, but this was not a major factor. He told BBC Radio Scotland's Good Morning Scotland programme: "The reason people are opting for Scottish universities is that they are perceived as being of very high quality, they offer very attractive courses and Scotland is seen as a very attractive place to study.
"They know that when they take up their studies in 2006 they will be hit by top-up fees if they are going to a university in England and that may be part of the reason why the numbers coming to Scotland are so inflated. "However, it does not mean that we will see thousands of additional students from England studying here." Mr Wallace agreed and said the figures had to be looked at in context. He explained that when applications were translated into acceptances, the number was not huge - an additional figure of about 200.
Also, the picture was further blurred by the fact that applications from Wales, where there are no plans for top-up fees, have also risen, by 19%. Mr Wallace said: "Accepting students from all parts of the world does show the high regard in which Scottish higher education is held, not just in Britain. "We want to make sure that when students are making their choice, they do so on the nature of the course and not because they are under some sort of financial pressure to go to Scotland. "We do not want to have a situation where it becomes impossible for Scottish students to get places at Scottish universities because we are seen as the cheap option. "Very often the quality of the university experience is enhanced by the fact there are students coming from a wide range of backgrounds so it would be wrong to go the other way and start excluding students."

Many natural decision problems can be formulated as constraint satisfaction
problems for reducts $\mathbb{A}$ of finitely bounded homogeneous structures.
This class of problems is a large generalisation of the class of CSPs over
finite domains. Our first result is a general polynomial-time reduction from
such infinite-domain CSPs to finite-domain CSPs. We use this reduction to
obtain new powerful polynomial-time tractability conditions that can be
expressed in terms of the topological polymorphism clone of $\mathbb{A}$.
Moreover, we study the subclass $\mathcal{C}$ of CSPs for structures
$\mathbb{A}$ that are reducts of a structure with a unary language. Also this
class $\mathcal{C}$ properly extends the class of all finite-domain CSPs. We
apply our new tractability conditions to prove the general tractability
conjecture of Bodirsky and Pinsker for reducts of finitely bounded homogeneous
structures for the class $\mathcal{C}$.

In the northwest part of the Yucatán Peninsula, within the Mérida Municipality of the state of Yucatán in southeastern Mexico, lies the community of Komchén. This locale is positioned 15 km north of Mérida city and roughly 20 km from the northern coastline of the peninsula. The name "Komchén," which translates from Yucatec Mayan to "In the well of the hollow," reflects its origins. The town boasts an array of amenities, including educational facilities such as a kindergarten, primary school, high school, Bachelors School, and a municipal library, a clinic operated by the Mexican Social Security Institute, recreational parks, and marinas. Approximately 90% of its roads are paved.

Historically, Komchén is renowned for its ancient Mayan archaeological site of the same name, which lies near Dzibilchaltun. The earliest evidence of human presence at this site dates back to the Middle Preclassic period. Initially, it housed a small, ephemeral settlement composed of perishable structures. By the Late Preclassic era, however, the community grew substantially and peaked in construction between 350-150 BC, with the use of permanent stone masonry in architectural projects. The site seems to have been deserted entirely by the termination of the Late Preclassic period around A.D. 250. Nevertheless, the site was later repopulated by inhabitants from the burgeoning center of Dzibilchaltun.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) are used extensively in medical
image segmentation and hence 3D navigation for robot-assisted Minimally
Invasive Surgeries (MISs). However, current DCNNs usually use down sampling
layers for increasing the receptive field and gaining abstract semantic
information. These down sampling layers decrease the spatial dimension of
feature maps, which can be detrimental to image segmentation. Atrous
convolution is an alternative for the down sampling layer. It increases the
receptive field whilst maintains the spatial dimension of feature maps. In this
paper, a method for effective atrous rate setting is proposed to achieve the
largest and fully-covered receptive field with a minimum number of atrous
convolutional layers. Furthermore, a new and full resolution DCNN - Atrous
Convolutional Neural Network (ACNN), which incorporates cascaded atrous
II-blocks, residual learning and Instance Normalization (IN) is proposed.
Application results of the proposed ACNN to Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
and Computed Tomography (CT) image segmentation demonstrate that the proposed
ACNN can achieve higher segmentation Intersection over Unions (IoUs) than U-Net
and Deeplabv3+, but with reduced trainable parameters.

Citrus segregation is an essential aspect of automated citrus harvesting. Although current image segmentation techniques produce satisfactory outcomes via pixel-wise classification, they are reliant on vast quantities of labeled data for training and neglect the dynamic shifts in citrus position over time in practical settings. In this study, we initiate by teaching a basic CNN utilizing a minimal set of tagged citrus images in a supervised environment, enabling it to approximately identify citrus locations within each frame. Subsequently, we adapt a cutting-edge unsupervised learning technique to extract the possible citrus movements between frames from unmarked citrus videos. Leveraging both networks, we implement a multimodal transformer to merge the static data knowledge obtained through supervised learning and the movement data acquired through unsupervised learning. According to the findings, integrating both networks leads to a prediction precision of 88.3% IOU and 93.6% accuracy, surpassing the initial supervised benchmark by 1.2% in intersection over union and 2.4% in precision. Compared to the majority of existing citrus segmentation strategies, our method utilizes limited supervised data and extensive unlabeled data, while simultaneously acquiring pixel-level location details and temporal data about citrus modifications to amplify the segmentation impact.

In computer vision, many problems such as image segmentation, pixel
labelling, and scene parsing can be formulated as binary quadratic programs
(BQPs). For submodular problems, cuts based methods can be employed to
efficiently solve large-scale problems. However, general nonsubmodular problems
are significantly more challenging to solve. Finding a solution when the
problem is of large size to be of practical interest, however, typically
requires relaxation. Two standard relaxation methods are widely used for
solving general BQPs--spectral methods and semidefinite programming (SDP), each
with their own advantages and disadvantages. Spectral relaxation is simple and
easy to implement, but its bound is loose. Semidefinite relaxation has a
tighter bound, but its computational complexity is high, especially for large
scale problems. In this work, we present a new SDP formulation for BQPs, with
two desirable properties. First, it has a similar relaxation bound to
conventional SDP formulations. Second, compared with conventional SDP methods,
the new SDP formulation leads to a significantly more efficient and scalable
dual optimization approach, which has the same degree of complexity as spectral
methods. We then propose two solvers, namely, quasi-Newton and smoothing Newton
methods, for the dual problem. Both of them are significantly more efficiently
than standard interior-point methods. In practice, the smoothing Newton solver
is faster than the quasi-Newton solver for dense or medium-sized problems,
while the quasi-Newton solver is preferable for large sparse/structured
problems. Our experiments on a few computer vision applications including
clustering, image segmentation, co-segmentation and registration show the
potential of our SDP formulation for solving large-scale BQPs.

The Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry anticipates a deceleration in the nation's economic expansion to 1.6% during the upcoming fiscal year commencing in April 2005. Despite this projected decline from the present 2.1% rate, Minister of Economics, Heizo Takenaka, reported optimistic signs towards eliminating deflation. According to his projections, the economy is expected to expand by 2% in the subsequent fiscal year, 2006/07. Furthermore, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) is predicted to exhibit a marginal increase of 0.1% in the forthcoming fiscal year, marking the initial price rise since 2000/01. Mr. Takenaka expressed confidence in these improvements, stating, "We are striving to enhance genuine economic circumstances and eradicate deflation. I believe we are making headway." Japan has grappled with deflation – a persistent decrease in consumer prices – for over five consecutive years. In response, the Bank of Japan has persistently injected surplus funds into the monetary market to maintain short-term interest rates at 0%, stimulating economic activity.

Suddenly, Jacob's world is turned upside down as he is thrust into a realm of colors, shapes, and sights he never knew existed. He is both fascinated and terrified by his newfound ability. Jacob struggles to keep his sight a secret, fearing ostracization from his community. He grapples with the ethical dilemma of whether to embrace his sight or to reject it in favor of the only life he has ever known.

As Jacob navigates his new reality, he discovers the dark secrets hidden beneath the surface of his seemingly utopian society. He learns that the Harmonious have been suppressing their people's ability to see to maintain control and uniformity. Jacob also uncovers a plot to eradicate anyone who regains their sight, making him a target.

With the help of a group of sighted rebels, Jacob embarks on a dangerous journey to expose the truth and free his people from the oppressive regime. Along the way, he learns about courage, friendship, and the power of truth. "Truesight" is a thrilling exploration of perception, identity, and the lengths one will go to for freedom.

Seodaemun Prison History Hall is a museum and former prison in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, South Korea.  It was constructed beginning in 1907. The prison was opened on October 21, 1908, under the name Gyeongseong Gamok. During the early part of the Japanese colonial period it was known as Keijo Prison (, the Japanese pronunciation of Gyeongseong Gamok). Its name was changed to Seodaemun Prison in 1923, and it later had several other names. History
The prison was used during the Japanese colonial period to imprison Korean liberation activists, and could originally hold around 500 inmates. It had a separate facility for women and young girls. In 1911, Kim Koo was imprisoned. He was one of the more important figures in the Korean liberation movement. In 1919, shortly after the March 1st Movement, the number of imprisoned increased drastically. About three thousand liberation activists were imprisoned, and shortly before the colonization ended in 1945, the number of prisoners was at 2980. Among imprisoned after the March 1st Movement was Ryu Gwansun, who died from the torture inflicted on her.

Former All Black star Jonah Lomu says he cannot wait to run out on the pitch for former England rugby union captain Martin Johnson's testimonial on 4 June.
The 29-year-old had a kidney transplant in July 2004 but will play his first full match for three years, leading a southern hemisphere side at Twickenham. "I actually started training three weeks after my operation but I was very limited until a few months ago. "Now it's basically bring it on!" said the giant winger. "The match on 4 June will be my first 15-man game but I have a training schedule which is quite testing and combines with sevens and a whole lot of things," said Lomu. "I have got so much energy since my operation that I train three times a day, six days a week.
"Mohammed Ali has always been my ideal. Coming back to rugby, people said 'you are dreaming' but it always starts off with a dream. "It's up to you whether you want to make it a reality." Opinion has been divided on whether Lomu should attempt to return to the game after such a major operation. But when Lomu was asked whether he was taking a risk he replied: "As much as someone going down the road being hit by a bus. "There are a lot of people in the world with one kidney who just don't know it. "I have talked this over, had a chat with the donor and this is to set my soul at peace and finish something I started in 1994 [when he made his All Blacks debut]." At his lowest ebb Lomu was so ill he could barely walk, but he says he is now getting stronger every day and his long-term target is to play for New Zealand again. "The only person who saw me at my worst was my wife," he added. "I used to take two steps and fall over but now I can run and it is all coming back, and a lot more quickly than I ever thought it would.
