Visual domain adaptation is an important problem in computer vision, and has been studied extensively by researchers at Google, Microsoft Research, and elsewhere. However, there are many challenges to overcome before we can achieve visual domain adaptation that are not well understood. We present VisDA (Visual Domain Adaptation), a novel approach to solving these problems. Our goal is to develop a general framework for visual domain adaptation that allows us to address all of the known issues with existing approaches. In particular, we aim to provide a unified model for visual domain adaptation that can be used to solve any problem involving visual domain adaptation. This includes both simple and complex cases. We also propose a new algorithm for visual domain adaptation that is based on a combination of two previously proposed algorithms. These algorithms have proven successful in other domains such as object recognition and speech recognition, but they do not yet fully capture the complexity of visual domain adaptation. We demonstrate how our new algorithm can be applied to several real-world applications, including image classification, face detection, and object localization.

Addams Family Reunion is a 1998 American direct-to-video comedy horror children's film based on the characters from the cartoon created by cartoonist Charles Addams. This fourth and final installment in the Shrek series has many things going for it, but it never quite comes together as a whole. While the previous installments managed to find a perfect balance between hilarious slapstick humor, witty references, and an actual story, this one seems to have forgotten the latter, favoring instead cheap laughs and spectacle over genuine wit and emotion. As a result, the movie feels long and drawn out, even at a relatively short 84 minutes. 

The story picks up shortly after the events of the third film, with Shrek (Mike Myers) and Fiona (Cameron Diaz) married and dealing with the responsibilities of being parents to their young son Arthur (Diablo Cody). However, Shrek starts to become overwhelmed by the monotony of his daily life and loses his edge. His friends Donkey (Eddie Murphy) and Puss In Boots (Antonio Banderas) try to help Shrek find his former self by transporting him back in time to when he was a scared and nervous teenager who had yet to find his confidence. The majority of the film is then spent with Shrek interacting with his younger self ( Milo Murphy) as he tries to teach him the importance of being true to oneself and not backing down from what you want.

The concept of Shrek losing his edge and needing to be reminded of the importance of being true to oneself is a compelling one, and it could have made for a really powerful and emotional story. However, the movie opts for a much more lighthearted and simplistic approach, with little focus on genuine character development or exploration of the theme. Instead, it relies on cheap gags and slapstick humor, much of which feels forced and unnecessary. 

The animation is as impressive as ever, with the movie's universe expanding to include new locations and characters. However, the characters themselves feel somewhat flat this time around, with little growth or development over the course of the film. The voice acting is also lack-ranging from Myers and Murphy's lackluster performances to Cody's grating teenaged vocal affectations. 

In the end, Shrek Forever After is a disappointing end to an otherwise fantastic series. While it has some memorable moments and laughs, it fails to live up to the standards set by the previous films and feels like a missed opportunity to go out with a bang.

Dictogloss is an open-source software tool used by speech and language therapists, educators, and linguists to transcribe audio recordings into text in real time. It was developed as part of the Open Source Speech Recognition Project (OSSR) with funding from the European Commission's Human Languages Technologies Consortium program.

The software uses state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms to recognize spoken words and convert them into written text. The user simply records a conversation or podcast using their computer microphone, and Dictogloss will automatically generate captions that are displayed on the screen word for word. As the audio plays back, users can also edit and correct any misrecognized words directly within the application.

One advantage of Dictogloss is its ability to transcribe different accents and languages accurately. This makes it a useful tool for anyone who wants to improve their writing skills in another language or needs assistance reading complex material in their native tongue. Additionally, its modular design allows users to customize the experience to meet their specific needs, such as adjusting the speed at which the captions are generated.

Dictogloss has gained popularity due to its accessibility and affordability compared to other commercial transcription services. With its simple interface and rich features, it provides researchers and instructors with a powerful tool to analyze audio content or provide feedback to their students in a more efficient way than ever before.

Bring the butter and egg to room temperature. Toast the walnuts for 7 minutes in a 180C oven (no need to pre-heat). When the walnuts have cooled slightly, crush with your hands into fairly small bits. Strain the egg through a sieve. You will need 20 g for the bread dough, and the rest can be set aside for later. If you have a bread machine, put all of the ingredients into the bread pan and turn it on! (If kneading by hand, see.) In the meantime, make the filling. Work quickly. For this recipe, I would recommend cutting the apples into 5 mm-1 cm slices, as opposed to wedges. When the apples have cooled a bit, drain them well in a colander. When the bread maker finishes, do a "finger check" (coat your finger with flour and poke a hole in the dough. If it doesn't spring back, you know that the first rising is complete). If the dough springs back, it hasn't finished rising. Let it sit for about another 5 minutes. If the dough has shrunk, it means you have let it rise too much. There's nothing you can do about this, so it's best just to proceed to the next step, bearing in mind that your rolls might not turn out the greatest! Carefully take the dough out of the bread machine with a bench scraper. Punch down the dough. Shape the dough into a ball. Make it nice and smooth. Close the seam tightly on the bottom. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 15 minutes. Place the dough seam-side up and, using a rolling pin, lightly mark the dough with a cross. Roll out the dough, but leave approx. 1 cm on either end un-rolled (this helps achieve an even thickness). Roll out the dough into a 25 cm square. (This is easiest if you work from the centre, leaving the top, bottom, and sides until the very end). Thoroughly drain the apple filling and spread it out on the dough, leaving 2 cm at the end furthest from you empty. Roll it up from the end nearest you. Close the seam tightly, as you did when making the dough. Cut the dough into 6 pieces with a bench scraper (start by cutting it in half, then cut each half into 3 pieces.) Spread out the aluminum foil baking cups and place a roll in each cup. Let rise once more, this time at 40C on your oven's 'bread rising' setting. This is what they look like after the second rising. Pre-heat the oven to 190C. While waiting for it to heat, brush the rolls with the leftover egg and top with sliced almonds and walnuts. When heated, pop them into the oven for 12 minutes. Adjust the baking time according to your oven. Take the rolls out of the oven and cool on a wire rack... Mix together the icing ingredients until thick (make sure not to over-mix or it'll be hard). Drizzle the icing on the rolls! Even if you just drizzle it on at random, these will look surprisingly professional when finished, so don't worry too much. And with that, you're done!

Natalie Bookchin (born October 26, 1962) is an American artist and writer who works with sound, video, and other media. She is best known for her experimental and often abstract work, which explores the relationship between humans and technology.

Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Bookchin studied at the University of Pennsylvania and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She began her career as a composer and performer, creating works that combined music with spoken word and video. In the early 1990s, she began to focus more on video and installation art, often using found footage and other materials to create works that explored the impact of technology on society and the environment.

Bookchin's work has been exhibited and screened internationally, and she has received numerous awards and fellowships, including a Guggenheim Fellowship and a Rockefeller Fellowship. She is currently a professor of media studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and is a member of the board of directors of the Electronic Frontier Foundation.

In this text, let "D" denote a confined region in the n-dimensional Euclidean space, whose boundary is continuously differentiable. This study focuses on the non-homogeneous Cauchy issue of a first-order elliptic differential complex {A\_i}, consisting of elliptic operators. We analyze the boundary behavior of the vector-function u belonging to the related Sobolev spaces, specifically discussing the tangential component t\_i (u) and normal component n\_i (u) on the boundary. Under the uniqueness condition of the Laplacians within the complex, we derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for solving the problem and provide formulations for its precise and approximated solutions. For problems in the Lebesgue spaces L²(D), we construct both the precise and approximated solutions to the Cauchy problem with optimal regularity. Furthermore, employing Hilbert space techniques, we establish Carleman's formulas for the vector-function u from the Sobolev space H¹(D) using its Cauchy data t\_i (u) on a subregion "S" of the boundary and the values of A\_i u within D, adjusted for the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Several instructive instances of elliptic complexes with constant coefficients are discussed.

Barbara Harris (December 14, 1935 – August 11, 2020) was an American bishop in the Episcopal Church and the first woman to become a bishop in the Anglican Communion. She was also the first woman to be ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church, and the first woman to serve as a diocesan bishop in the Anglican Communion.

Harris was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Temple University with a degree in education in 1957. She worked as a teacher and counselor in the Philadelphia public school system before attending the Episcopal Divinity School in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where she earned her master of divinity degree in 1966. She was ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church in 1967, and served as curate at All Saints' Church in Worcester, Massachusetts. She became the first woman to serve as a priest in the Episcopal Church. In 1974, she became the chaplain at MIT and minister at Saint Paul's Church in Cambridge, Massachusetts. She was named the eleventh bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts in 1989 and was consecrated on March 16, 1990, by Edmond L. Browning, the presiding bishop of the Episcopal Church. She served as bishop until her retirement in 2003.

Harris was a strong advocate for the full participation of women in the church, and worked to improve the status of women and girls worldwide. She served on the board of the Center for Women in Church and Society, and was a founding member of the National Organization for the Promotion of Episcopal Schools. She also served as a member of the President's Council on Bioethics. In retirement, Harris continued to serve as an assistant bishop in the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts and as a visiting lecturer at Episcopal Divinity School. She died on August 11, 2020, at the age of 84.

Over 5.2 million Germans were jobless in February, according to recent data. This represents 12.6% of the labor force, marking the highest unemployment rate in Germany since the 1930s. The prediction of growth stagnation was made by the head of Germany's economic advisory panel, Bert Ruerup, during a television interview. He revised the earlier estimate of 1.4% growth down to 1% for 2005.

Germany's government has been implementing various labor market reforms to address persistently high unemployment. One such program is the "Hartz-IV" initiative, launched in January, which aims to reform welfare benefits and encourage employment, even if some positions are heavily subsidized. The newly released unemployment figures may intensify criticism towards the Schroeder administration, which initially pledged to reduce unemployment by half.

Despite the alarming statistics, there are indications that the situation might not be as dire. The rise in unemployment numbers can be attributed to a change in calculation methods, causing an additional 500,000 jobless individuals in January. Seasonally adjusted, the overall unemployment rate stood at 4.875 million people, equivalent to 11.7%. Based on the International Labour Organization (ILO) methodology, Germany reported 3.97 million unemployed individuals and 14,000 new net jobs created in January, totaling 38.9 million employed persons. According to the ILO definition, an unemployed individual is someone who searched for work in the preceding four weeks and was available to start working immediately.

Despite the dense fog that enshrouded the forest,
It yielded to Him: grey clouds receded,
submissively parting as He advanced –
approaching me – as if traversing through hazy columns
Of an ancient, powerful temple.
The enigmatic expression hid behind a veil, His thoughts
Centered on mine: thus, I perceived the faint, primal hum
Echoing within the depths of my skull.
On these soundwaves rode His communication.
A glimmer of eyeless gaze fell upon my trembling flesh,
Signaling Him of my reaction as I detected more signals –
For fresh, unfamiliar shivers emerged.
Was I not to hear them as well?
He yearned for verbal affirmation from me:
I had to be torn apart by His authoritative voice –
Bear witness to His overture!
May His intent to reassert such detested goal displease me – I recognized myself as his prey!
His behavior exuded deceit, yet I already knew his wish!
And still I allowed Him near – what other choice was there?
Surrendering to His relentless approach – along a flawless trajectory –
I allowed Him to enforce His toll.
Soon I would be consumed; ingested; transformed

1 whole 12" Round Pre-Cooked Pizza Crust (like Boboli)
1 Tablespoon Olive Oil
9 ounces, weight Frisch's Tartar Sauce
1 pound Cooked Ground Beef, Drained
Dill Pickle Chips/ Slices (to Taste)
1 cup Shredded Mild Cheddar Cheese
Shredded Iceberg Lettuce (pre-packaged Bag), Washed & Dried
Preheat oven (with pizza stone, if you have one) to 450 F. Place pre-cooked pizza crust onto a pizza pan (or a pizza peel if you are using a stone). Using a pastry brush, coat the crust evenly with olive oil from edge to edge. Next, coat the crust evenly with tartar sauce using the back of a large spoon or rubber spatula, leaving about a 3/4 border. Add the drained and cooked ground beef and then place dill pickles evenly across the pizza (as you would pepperoni). Next sprinkle the cheese evenly over the pickles and meat. Put pizza into oven (in the pan or slide it onto the stone). Bake pizza for about 6-8 minutes, then remove it from the oven, add the lettuce, and bake for another 2 minutes or so. (You can add lettuce anytime during cooking, or wait until it is completely done cooking, depending on your preference). Bake pizza for a total of 8-10 minutes, or until cheese is completely melted & edge turn golden brown. Remove pizza from oven and cut into 6-8 wedge pieces. Notes: If you have a pizza stone, I highly recommend using it. This pizza reheats really well, so keep any leftovers in an airtight container, stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. 1/3 cup ranch dressing
1 teaspoon hot chile paste (such as sambal oelek)
4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1 inch pieces
24 (1-inch) pieces red onion
12 slices thick cut bacon
salt and black pepper to taste
12 (6 inch) bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 2 hours
Whisk together ranch dressing and hot chile paste in a large bowl. Mix in chicken pieces and toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 hours. Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove chicken from the bag and transfer to a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Pat chicken pieces dry with more paper towels. Thread a piece of onion about 1 1/2 inches down the skewer. Thread the end portion of one strip of bacon onto skewer so the rest of the strip is hanging down. Skewer on a piece of chicken; thread on the next portion of the bacon. Turn the skewer so that the long end of the bacon is again hanging down. Repeat this process of skewering and turning until the entire strip of bacon is threaded, using 4 to 5 chicken pieces. Thread a second piece of onion onto the end of the skewer. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for all twelve skewers. Season chicken skewers with salt and pepper as desired. Cook the skewers on the preheated grill, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until nicely browned on all sides and the meat is no longer pink in the center, 12 to 16 minutes total per skewer. Serve with ranch dressing as a dipping sauce.

Frederick Peterson (March 1, 1859 – July 9, 1938) was an American neurologist and poet. Peterson was at the forefront of psychoanalysis in the United States, publishing one of the first articles of Freud and Jung's theories of Free Association in 1909. Upon his return to the United States, he became a professor at the University at Buffalo in 1882. For the following decade he practiced as a neurologist in New York City. He was involved in Harold P. Brown's 1888 anti-alternating current dog electrocution demonstrations at Columbia University during the war of the currents and later that year was appointed by the New York Medico-Legal Society to lead up a committee finalizing the method of electrical execution via the electric chair in that state. He spent 1893–1894 as a professor at the University of Vermont.  In 1900 he was appointed president of the New York State Commission on Lunacy. From 1903 until his retirement, he served as a professor of psychiatry at Columbia University. He was also a well known connoisseur and collector of Chinese paintings.

A slimming aid made from a southern African cactus is set to be developed by UK firm Phytopharm and Unilever.
Anglo-Dutch food giant Unilever will help the pharmaceutical firm develop the snacks containing Hoodia extract. Phytopharm shares jumped 10.7% on the news, with analysts saying sales of $600m (£309m) a year were possible. The plant, licensed to Phytopharm in 1997, has been used for thousands of years by the Sans bushmen of the Kalahari desert to stave off hunger. Studies have reportedly shown the plant curbs appetite instead of reducing calorific intake like many existing products.
Phytopharm will receive an initial fee of £6.5m from Unilever - out of a potential total of £21m - as well as future royalties on product sales. Under the deal, production of the Hoodia cactus at Phytopharm's nursery in South Africa will also rise from eight million plants to potentially hundreds of millions, said Phytopharm chief executive Richard Dixey. The firm had initially hoped to market a slimming drug from Hoodia with Pfizer. But the research collaboration came to an end in 2003. Analysts said Unilever could launch the new products in 2007. "This deal goes a long way to restoring the market faith in Phytopharm's pipeline after the Pfizer exit," said analyst Erling Refsum at Nomura.

Deep learning methods have significantly advanced semantic segmentation in biomedical image processing. Yet, their use remains limited in practical applications due to the need for extensive data for model training. This issue is more pronounced in biomedical imaging as data and annotations are hard to acquire. Manual labeling of biomedical images involves experts spending significant time and resources marking pixels on images, often containing numerous instances of the target anatomy (such as neurons, astrocytes, mitochondria). In this study, we propose a Deep Active Learning framework for a real-world scenario. Utilizing the U-Net architecture and overall uncertainty measure, it suggests which sample requires annotation. By employing Monte Carlo sampling and Dropout regularization, it extracts uncertainty measures. Results from experiments on spinal cord and brain microscopic histology samples conducting myelin segmentation tasks demonstrated a peak Dice value following the addition of three uncertainty-designated samples to the original training set, compared to 15 randomly-chosen samples. This reduction in annotation requirements was shown to be statistically significant. We focused on a feasible scenario and provided evidence that our approach delivers superior segmentation results utilizing minimal labeled samples. Researchers in the biomedical field seeking quick and precise image segmentation for their dataset may find our framework beneficial. The associated code can be accessed at https://github.com/neuropoly/deep-active-learning.

These signatures fell into three main categories: signatures of individual women, written endorsements from men, and affirmations from group leaders. Waterford city is situated in south eastern Ireland, on the river Suir [pronounced Shure] about  from where the river enters the sea. Practically the entire city is built on the south bank of the river. The "Old town", now the business centre, clusters behind the broad quay-front on a low-lying strip of land left behind by a gentle loop of the river at this point. From this, the land rises sharply to the east and opposite to the west while remaining level in between. The eastern slopes are almost entirely occupied by private residential estates, while the western and southwestern prominences are largely given over to local council housing development. There are corresponding elevations on the north bank eastwards towards Christendom and westwards towards Mount Misery nothing. The rocks which form the base of the city all belong to the Palaeozoic Group – principally Ordovician shales underlying sandstone. On the East side of the city, the rock is crossed by an alluvial bank running N.E./S.W. At the cliffs alongside the banks of the River Suir, above Rice Bridge, inter-stratification of sharply-folded Ordovician Slates and Sandstone conglomerates may be clearly observed.

Barnett Frank, born on March 31, 1940, is a former American politician from Massachusetts who served in the U.S. House of Representatives from 1981 to 2013. As a Democratic Party member, Frank chaired the House Financial Services Committee from 2007 to 2011 and was a significant co-sponsor of the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act. Known for being openly gay, Frank hails from Bayonne, New Jersey, where he attended Bayonne High School, Harvard College, and Harvard Law School. Prior to his political career, Frank worked as a political aide. He was elected to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1972 and to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1980, receiving 52% of the votes. Frank was re-elected every subsequent term with substantial majorities. In 1987, he publicly acknowledged being gay, making him the first openly gay congressman. From 2003 until his retirement, Frank led the Democrats on the House Financial Services Committee and acted as committee chairman during Democratic Party rule from 2007 to 2011. Baked Clams Recipe
Ingredients:

24 littleneck clams
1/3 cup chopped onion
2 tablespoons butter
1/4 cup bread crumbs
1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).

2. In a small bowl, mix together onion, butter, bread crumbs, oregano, salt, and black pepper.

3. Arrange clams in a single layer in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Stuff clam shells with the bread crumb mixture.

4. Bake for 10 minutes, or until clams are opened. (Discard any clams that remain closed.)

5. Serve immediately.

In this work, we tackle the problem of source-free domain adaptation for image segmentation. To this end, we propose a simple and effective approach based on Cycle-Consistency Training (CCT). Our key idea is to train a segmentation model to be cycle-consistent, meaning that it should be able to map an image from the source domain to the target domain and back to the source domain while preserving the segmentation. To encourage this behavior, we design a loss function that penalizes the distance between the input and output images in the feature space as well as the distance between the segmentation masks of the input and output images. We evaluate our approach on two publicly available datasets and show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for source-free domain adaptation.

If you're in the market for a new computer, you may be wondering what to do about the RAM shortages. For the past few months, RAM prices have been soaring, and availability has been constrained. The good news is that there are alternatives to traditional RAM that can provide similar performance.

One option is to use a smaller amount of RAM and supplement it with a large solid state drive (SSD). This will give you the benefit of fast boot times and short load times, without the high price tag of a fully loaded RAM setup.

Another option is to use a hybrid hard drive, which combines a large traditional hard drive with a smaller amount of flash memory. This can give you the best of both worlds in terms of price and performance.

Finally, you could opt for a computer with an integrated graphics processor, which can offload some of the work that would otherwise be handled by the RAM. This can help free up RAM for other tasks, and potentially improve performance.

No matter which route you choose, be sure to do your research and find the best option for your needs. With a little bit of creativity, you can find a computer that will suit your needs without breaking the bank.

This paper introduces the concept of witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes as a way to study the combinatorial structure of simplicial complexes. Witness structures are a generalization of simplicial complexes that allow for the representation of higher-dimensional combinatorial structures. Immediate snapshot complexes are a specific type of witness structure that capture the combinatorial structure of a system at a specific point in time. The paper presents algorithms for constructing witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes, as well as techniques for analyzing their properties. The authors demonstrate the utility of these concepts by applying them to various real-world examples, including social networks and biological systems. Overall, this paper provides a novel framework for studying the combinatorial structure of complex systems and offers new insights into their behavior.

Rediffusion Singapore was a pioneering cable-transmitted, subscription-based radio station in Singapore that broadcasted predominantly in Chinese and English from 1949 to 2012. It is historically noteworthy as one of the earliest examples of subscription-based radio broadcasting. 

Highlighting its beginnings in Singapore back in 1949, Rediffusion began as Associate Rediffusion Services, a British-owned company. Based mainly in the city area, the Rediffusion service comprised of a network of cables that ran across the city linking homes and businesses. It featured daily broadcasts in four different languages: English, Malay, Chinese, and Tamil.

Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, it underwent several significant changes, including a name change from Associate Rediffusion Services to Rediffusion Singapore Pte Ltd in 1963. The next notable development in the company's progression came in the 1970s when Rediffusion underwent a period of localization and transitioned into an entirely Chinese language radio service.

In 1980, Rediffusion was sold to the Singaporean entrepreneur See Hoy Chan and became a wholly local company. During this period, it devoted substantially to the broadcasting of Chinese drama serials along with the sponsoring of several prominent local events, thereby reinforcing its cultural significance in the community. 

Rediffusion Singapore faced a significant challenge with the advent of free-to-air TV and FM radio services in the 1990s that led to a reduction in its subscriber base. The company attempted to reinvent itself by targeting niche listeners through content such as dialect programming, health, and wellness programs. The company underwent additional changes in management over the next few decades, yet continued to face declining subscriptions and financial difficulties. 

Amidst these challenges, Rediffusion decided to bid adieu to the cable radio broadcasting in 2011 after broadcasting for 62 years. The following year, in 2012, the company made its much-awaited return as a digital radio platform, but the revival was short-lived and the station ceased broadcasting permanently later in 2012.

Despite its cessation, Rediffusion Singapore holds a significant place in the history of Singapore's media landscape, having played a crucial role in the development of contemporary radio broadcasting in Singapore. To date, it echoes as an icon of nostalgia for those who recall the golden age of subscription-based radio stations.

The book is set in a large house called Warings near the village of Derne. It was once a grand countryside mansion, but has since fallen into disrepair and decay. Joseph Hooper has inherited the house, and lives with his son Edmund Hooper. They have a cold, formal relationship which lacks compassion. Joseph announces that a housekeeper will be moving in, who will also bring her son who is of a similar age to Edmund. Mrs. Helena Kingshaw, and her son Charles Kingshaw arrive at Warings. Hooper becomes defensive of his house, and instantly takes a disliking to Kingshaw. He mocks him about his social class and father, and a small fight ensues where Kingshaw punches Hooper. Kingshaw then attempts to escape Warings, but is attacked by a vicious crow. The crow is thought to symbolize Hooper, who is very protective of his territory. Animalistic symbolism is used throughout the novel. Hooper proceeds to taunt and bully Kingshaw, who acts as the weak victim in their relationship. They venture to Hang Wood together, where Hooper's weaknesses become apparent and Kingshaw seems to retrieve some kind of power. However, it is apparent that Kingshaw does not have the capacity to be cruel. This pattern of cruelty continues throughout the book within the isolated setting of Warings. Both parents seem oblivious to their fights, and lack an understanding of their children's antics. They travel to Hang Wood on a few more occasions. It appears that Hooper is vulnerable in this setting, away from his home. The family decide to take a trip to Leydell Castle. Here, Kingshaw further exploits Hoopers fears as they climb the ancient monument. Hooper falls by accident, and badly injures himself. Even though Kingshaw tried to save him Hooper accuses Kingshaw of pushing him and is believed by the adults. Kingshaw is convinced that he has killed Hooper. As Hooper recovers, it appears that Kingshaw gains independence and meets a local boy by the name of Fielding. Fielding appears confident and well-rounded, and takes Kingshaw to his farm where he witnesses the birth of a calf. This is in stark contrast to Warings, which is full of death morbidity. Glass cabinets filled with moths are used to symbolize the decay of the Hooper dynasty. Fielding offers Kingshaw hope away from the manipulative clutches of Hooper. However, once Hooper returns to health, the normal regime of taunting resumes. Hooper's cruelty climaxes, and Kingshaw is devastated when he discovers that Helena and Joseph have agreed to marry, and that Hooper and Kingshaw will attend school together. The novel ends with Kingshaw committing suicide by drowning himself in a river in Hang Wood and Mrs. Kingshaw comforting Hooper who is described as feeling a sense of triumph.

Flaky Pastry:
350g all-purpose flour, 250g cold butter, 200g powdered sugar, a scant amount of salt, zest of 1 lemon, 1 beaten egg
Nut Filling:
500g granulated sugar, 500g walnuts, 500ml heavy cream, 50g tablespoons liquid honey, 1 egg yolk

First, make the pastry: Cream together butter and sugar in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, combine flour, lemon zest, salt, and egg; mix on medium speed until a dough forms. Divide dough in half, shape each portion into a disc, then wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Next, prepare the filling: Cook sugar in a large saucepan over medium heat until it turns a pale amber color. Gradually pour in heated cream while constantly stirring. Add honey and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and fold in walnuts. Allow to cool completely before using.

Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Roll out larger pastry disk and press it into the bottom and sides of a greased 24cm springform pan. Pour in cooled nut filling, followed by rolling out and placing the smaller dough disk as the lid. Seal the edges and brush the top with lightly beaten egg yolk. Bake for approximately 50-60 minutes. Let cool completely before removing from the tin. Chill cake thoroughly before slicing and serving to ensure that the filling has set properly.

Most recent semantic segmentation methods adopt a U-Net framework with an
encoder-decoder architecture. It is still challenging for U-Net with a simple
skip connection scheme to model the global multi-scale context: 1) Not each
skip connection setting is effective due to the issue of incompatible feature
sets of encoder and decoder stage, even some skip connection negatively
influence the segmentation performance; 2) The original U-Net is worse than the
one without any skip connection on some datasets. Based on our findings, we
propose a new segmentation framework, named UCTransNet (with a proposed CTrans
module in U-Net), from the channel perspective with attention mechanism.
Specifically, the CTrans module is an alternate of the U-Net skip connections,
which consists of a sub-module to conduct the multi-scale Channel Cross fusion
with Transformer (named CCT) and a sub-module Channel-wise Cross-Attention
(named CCA) to guide the fused multi-scale channel-wise information to
effectively connect to the decoder features for eliminating the ambiguity.
Hence, the proposed connection consisting of the CCT and CCA is able to replace
the original skip connection to solve the semantic gaps for an accurate
automatic medical image segmentation. The experimental results suggest that our
UCTransNet produces more precise segmentation performance and achieves
consistent improvements over the state-of-the-art for semantic segmentation
across different datasets and conventional architectures involving transformer
or U-shaped framework. Code: https://github.com/McGregorWwww/UCTransNet.

A City Remembered

In the valley, a forgotten city:
 discreets of ruined homes,
 fractured domes of marketplaces,
 crumbling statues of heroes.

Once a hive of industry,
 whispers of it stilled by time,
 now just a shell of grandeur,
 engulfed by the pines.

Where once iron elbows bowed,
 now only birdsong fills the air,
 and the murmur of brooks,
 as if nature seeks to repair.

Time's gentle touch, reclaiming brick and mortar,
 once a shield against the world,
 now just a memory of people,
 who lived, loved and endured.

Yet in this tranquil silence,
 I hear the echoes of laughter,
 see the ghosts of children,
 running through the meadows.

In my mind's eye, I can still picture them,
 though their images fade with time,
 I hear the echoes of their voices,
 though the wind has blown away their words.

In this forgotten place, I find a beauty,
 in the solitude and the silence,
 for in this city, now remembered,
 I feel a connection, as if I belonged.

Music downloading, for those that have rejected the free peer to peer services, can be a costly business.
The cost of paying even as little as 70p per track can add up, particularly for those people who own one of the new generation of players that can store thousands of songs. Paying per track for music is becoming as outmoded as paying per minute for internet access and alternative monthly or yearly subscription models are springing up as a more convenient, and ultimately cheaper way of owning music.
"Music fans are moving away from buying the traditional bundled package of a dozen or more songs that we used to call an album to newer ways that fit their lifestyle; either single tracks or subscriptions services," said Paul Myers, chief executive of Wippit, a UK-based music download service. While iTunes is doing good business with its sales of individual tracks to iPod owners, others are questioning whether the concept of owning music is even valid in the digital age. Napster is due to launch a new rental subscription service - dubbed Napster to Go in the UK in the next few months. The service can be used on players that support Microsoft Windows latest Digital Rights Management technology known as Janus. This includes players made by Samsung, Rio and Creative.
Currently on offer in beta-version in the US, the service costs $15 per month for unlimited downloads. The technology ensures that music downloaded to the player only remains playable while the user subscribes to the service. Users need to update their license on a monthly basis or the tunes will no longer play.
This has outraged some digital music lovers, especially as Napster already offers a cheaper service for downloading music to the PC. Napster claims the higher price is a result of record labels charging more for the to-go service and says it also offers "greater value" for customers. Mr Myers is not convinced a rental model will work for consumers. "We've been offering our unlimited music subscription service for more than three years now and our customers know what they want. Format interoperability, excellent value and the reassurance that music purchased from Wippit is theirs to keep and enjoy on whatever device they choose," he said. "Who wants to download a track that won't play next month if you decide to unsubscribe to the service or change portable player for an iPod or the latest mobile phone?" Wippit offers a download subscription service for £4.99 per month or £50 per year. It has a catalogue of around 60,000 songs.

Transitional bilingualism, also known as early-exit bilingualism, is a form of bilingual education where students with a native language different from the language of instruction in school are taught in their native language for a certain period before transitioning to the second language. This approach is designed to help students gradually adapt to the second language while maintaining their academic progress.

The main goal of transitional bilingualism is to ensure that students do not fall behind in their academic subjects while they are learning the second language. This is achieved by initially teaching students in their native language, then gradually increasing the use of the second language in instruction until it becomes the primary language of instruction. 

Transitional bilingualism programs typically last for two to three years. During this period, students receive instruction in their native language for a significant portion of the day, while the rest of the day is spent learning the second language. As students become more proficient in the second language, the amount of instruction in their native language is reduced.

The effectiveness of transitional bilingualism has been a subject of debate among educators and researchers. Supporters argue that it allows students to continue learning academic content while they are still gaining proficiency in the second language, thus preventing them from falling behind. They also argue that it helps students maintain their cultural identity and heritage, as they continue to learn and use their native language.

Critics, on the other hand, argue that transitional bilingualism does not promote long-term bilingualism and biliteracy, as it eventually leads to the replacement of the native language with the second language. They also argue that it may delay students' acquisition of the second language, as they spend a significant portion of their school day learning in their native language.

Despite these debates, transitional bilingualism remains a common approach to bilingual education in many countries, particularly in situations where students are expected to transition to using the second language in their daily lives. It is seen as a practical solution to the challenge of providing quality education to students who are not yet proficient in the language of instruction. 

In conclusion, transitional bilingualism is a form of bilingual education that aims to help students transition from their native language to a second language. While it has its critics, it is widely used and has been shown to be effective in helping students maintain their academic progress while they are learning a second language.

Mita Taupopoki ( – 14 January 1935) was a notable Māori tribal leader of New Zealand. He identified with Ngāti Wāhiao, a hapū (subtribe) of the Tūhourangi iwi of Te Arawa. He was born near Lake Rotorua, New Zealand, probably in 1845 or 1846. His father, Hēmana Te Whareiro of Ngāti Wāhiao, lived mostly at Whakarewarewa. His mother, Kanea II, was of Tūhourangi, and the Ngāti Tūnohopū hapū of Ngāti Whakaue. In 1864 Mita joined other Te Arawa who fought for the government in the wars of the 1860s. He returned to Whakarewarewa in 1874. In 1883 he represented several hapū of Ngāti Wāhiao in the Native Land Court in a case relating to land claimed by Ngāti Whakaue, including Whakarewarewa, and succeeded in claims to the land on the east side of the Puarenga Stream at Whakarewarewa, although other land was won by Ngāti Whakaue. His success in the land court contributed to a recognition of his leadership among the wider Tūhourangi, in addition to within Ngāti Wāhiao. The 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera killed many Tūhourangi, and survivors took refuge with Mita and his people at Whakarewarewa and Ōhinemutu. Mita continued to act in the Native Land Court, representing Tūhourangi, and in 1887 won recognition of their claims of the 211,000-acre Rotomahana–Parekārangi block. In 1910 he toured Australia, England and the United States with Maggie Papakura's cultural group. He died in hospital in Rotorua on 14 January 1935.

Born on January 13, 1972, Mark John Bosnich is a retired Australian goalkeeper who competed in the English Premier League for teams like Aston Villa, Manchester United, and Chelsea, as well as in Australia for Sydney United, Central Coast Mariners, and Sydney Olympic. Representing Australia seventeen times, he netted a solitary goal for his country. Previously, Bosnich joined Manchester United from Australia in 1989, but due to limited playing time and an unsuccessful work visa application, he returned to his homeland. Aston Villa then recruited him in 1990, and he became a top-tier goalkeeper in the Premier League throughout the 1990s. Manchester United re-hired him in 1999 as Schmeichel's replacement, but injuries and reduced game time resulted in a loss of form. He moved to Chelsea in 2001, where he contended for a starting spot and endured recurring injuries. In September 2002, he was dismissed by Chelsea and prohibited from participating in football for nine months after a positive drug test for cocaine.

Ingredients:
- 1 pound rice noodles (bihon)
- 1/2 pound pork belly, sliced into thin strips
- 1/2 pound shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup ground pork
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 onion, minced
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 4 cups shrimp stock (or chicken stock)
- 1/2 cup fish sauce (patis)
- 1/4 cup annatto powder (atsuete)
- 1 cup crushed pork cracklings (chicharon)
- 4 hard-boiled eggs, sliced
- 1/2 cup green onions, chopped
- 1/2 cup fried garlic
- 1/2 cup calamansi or lemon juice
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat the cooking oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and onion, and sauté until fragrant and translucent.
2. Add the ground pork and pork belly to the pot, and cook until browned and cooked through.
3. Pour in the shrimp stock and fish sauce, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for about 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
4. While the broth is simmering, prepare the annatto mixture. In a small bowl, mix the annatto powder with a few tablespoons of water to create a paste. Set aside.
5. Cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions, then drain and set aside.
6. In a separate pan, heat a tablespoon of cooking oil over medium heat. Add the shrimp and cook until pink and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.
7. In the same pan, add the annatto mixture and cook for a minute or two until the color is fully released. Pour this mixture into the simmering broth and stir well to distribute the color evenly.
8. To assemble the pancit palabok, place a serving of rice noodles on a plate. Ladle the broth over the noodles, making sure to include some of the meat and shrimp. Top with crushed pork cracklings, sliced hard-boiled eggs, green onions, and fried garlic.
9. Serve the pancit palabok with calamansi or lemon juice on the side for squeezing over the noodles. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
10. Enjoy your homemade Pancit Palabok!

American singer Stacey Q has released five studio albums, one compilation album, one extended play, thirteen singles, four promotional singles, and six music videos. Born Stacey Swain, she first served as the lead singer of the band SSQ put together by producer Jon St. James. Swain first began to work on solo material in 1985. She continued her collaboration with St. James and SSQ's original line-up. Her self-titled EP was released by On the Spot Records. Shortly after its release, Swain got signed by Atlantic Records and released her debut studio album Better Than Heaven (1986). It debuted at number fifty-nine on the US Billboard 200 and was certified gold in the United States. The first single released from the album was  "Two of Hearts", which was praised by critics and was a commercial success. It peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the highest-selling singles of 1986. The second single, "We Connect" was also successful, peaking at number thirty-five on the Hot 100 chart. "Insecurity" and "Music Out of Bounds" were also released as singles but did not perform as well as its predecessors.

Deep learning approaches for segregating 3D brain vessel images have underperformed compared to other organ and tissue types. This can be attributed to two reasons. Initially, deep learning algorithms struggle with the segmentation of small objects relative to the overall image size. Secondly, the intricacy of vascular networks and the minute scale of vessels pose difficulties in amassing sufficient annotated training data, a prerequisite for deep learning techniques. In response, we suggest a new deep learning framework for annotation-efficient vessel segmentation. This framework abstains from requiring pixel-wise annotations; instead, it uses weak patch-level labels to distinguish between vessel and non-vessel 2D patches in the training dataset. These user-supplied weak annotations serve dual functions: 1) they generate pseudo-pixel labels for vessels and the backdrop in each patch, which are employed to train a segmentation network, and 2) they instruct a classifier network to produce additional weak patch labels, thereby alleviating the annotation workload and acting as a filter for subpar image quality. We apply this framework to the segmentation of the cerebrovascular tree in Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Images (SWI). Our findings indicate that the framework attains top-tier precision, while decreasing the annotation time by approximately 77% compared to learning-based segmentation methods employing pixel-wise labels during training.

Ingredients:

* 1/4 cup granulated sugar
* 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
* 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
* 1 large egg
* 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 1/2 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
* 1/4 cup chopped walnuts (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

7. Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and gently knead it a few times until it comes together.
8. Pat the dough into a circle that is about 1 inch thick.
9. Use a biscuit cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out scones. You should be able to get about 8-10 scones.
10. Place the scones on the prepared baking sheet.
11. Brush the tops of the scones with a little extra yogurt or milk.
12. Bake the scones for 18-20 minutes, or until they are golden brown.
13. Remove the scones from the oven and let them cool on a wire rack

Hey there! If you're a frequent trader on Binance, you already know the importance of using stop loss orders to minimize your losses in a bear market. However, setting the correct stop loss order can be a bit tricky, especially for new traders.

Here are a few tips to help you set up a stop loss order on Binance:

1. Determine your risk tolerance: Before setting up a stop loss order, you need to determine how much you're willing to lose on a trade. This will help you set a realistic stop loss level.

2. Use trailing stop loss: A trailing stop loss order allows you to lock in profits as the market moves in your favor. This type of stop loss order can be adjusted as the price of the asset moves, so you can take advantage of swings in the market.

3. Consider market conditions: Before setting up a stop loss order, take a look at the broader market conditions. If the market is highly volatile, you may want to set a tighter stop loss to minimize your losses.

4. Keep an eye on the order book: Before setting up a stop loss order, take a look at the order book to see if there are any significant orders at the level you're considering. If there are, you may want to adjust your stop loss level.

Overall, using stop loss orders is crucial for minimizing your losses in a bear market. By following these tips, you can set up a stop loss order that will help you manage your risk and protect your profits.

The US economy has grown more than expected, expanding at an annual rate of 3.8% in the last quarter of 2004.
The gross domestic product figure was ahead of the 3.1% the government estimated a month ago. The rise reflects stronger spending by businesses on capital equipment and a smaller-than-expected trade deficit. GDP is a measure of a country's economic health, reflecting the value of the goods and services it produces.
The new GDP figure, announced by the Commerce Department on Friday, also topped the 3.5% growth rate that economists had forecast ahead of Friday's announcement. Growth was at an annual rate of 4% in the third quarter of 2004 and for the year it came in at 4.4%, the best figure in five years. However, the positive economic climate may lead to a rise in interest rates, with many expecting US rates to rise on 22 March. In the January-to-March quarter, the economy is expected to grow at an annual rate of about 4%, economists forecast. In the final quarter of 2004, businesses increased spending on capital equipment and software by 18%, up from 17.5% in the third quarter. Consumer spending grew 4.2% in the final quarter, down from the third quarter's 5.1%.

At the stroke of midnight, a sense of enchantment unfolds. In this captivating film, our hero encounters an extraordinary moment when he recognizes the chance to confront his deepest yearnings and ideals. Initially, he longs to establish a life in the City of Lights, but his aspirations clash with his girlfriend's more conventional perspective. For her, Paris represents a refined elegance, perhaps viewed through aristocratic lenses. Our protagonist, however, seeks inspiration for his artistic pursuits in this dreamland.

One fateful evening, he becomes disoriented in the Parisian labyrinth and is fortuitously saved by a group of elusive night owls, later revealed to be esteemed figures in literary circles. As our screenwriter/aspiring author experiences the realization of one dream, he also uncovers profound revelations about his new companions, their true identities, and their own dreams.

The film unfolds across various timeframes, with Paris exuding an alluring and mesmerizing charm in each era. Its rain-soaked skies, mirrored streets, and stunning architectural wonders capture the heart, while the splendid reenactments of earlier eras beckon with their irresistible allure. Paris' magnetic pull leaves one craving to reveal its hidden depths and embrace the essence of this exceptional film.

The Queers' second live album, titled "Suck," was released in 1995 by Clearview Records. Recorded live at The Jam Room in Columbia, South Carolina, this single-sided picture disc album showcased the American punk rock band's energy. Initially reissued on compact disc in 1998, it marked the only live recording of the Queers featuring Dan Vapid and Dan Panic from Screeching Weasel. Critical response was positive, with Mike DaRonco of AllMusic awarding it 4 out of 5 stars. He commended the improved production quality compared to their previous live album, Shout at the Queers (1994), noting that the tracks seamlessly transitioned from one to the next, save for the brief interlude of "Beer Break." In summarizing the band for Trouser Press, Ira Robbins praised both live albums for encapsulating the exhilarating essence of a Queers performance.

The events of The Bastard Prince span a period of approximately six months, from late May to late December of 928. The novel begins after the invasion of Prince Marek Furstán-Festil, the bastard child of the last Deryni ruler of Gwynedd, King Imre, and his sister, Princess Ariella. Supported by his Torenthi relatives, Marek has occupied the town of Culliecairn and slain Earl Hrorik II of Eastmarch. Word of the invasion is quickly sent to Rhemuth, where King Rhys Michael Haldane has spent the first six years of his reign as an imprisoned puppet of his lords of state. When a Torenthi herald arrives at Rhemuth to challenge the king, the great lords realize that they must permit Rhys Michael to go to Eastmarch and personally respond to the invasion. Disguised as one of Queen Michaela's serving maids, Rhysel Thuryn quickly learns of the king's plans to accompany his army to Eastmarch. Rhysel meets with members of the Camberian Council and attempts to convince them to activate the king's Haldane potential before he leaves the following day. Despite his own objections, Father Joram MacRorie, Rhysel's uncle, eventually agrees to her plan. That night, Joram and Tieg Thuryn, Rhysel's brother, infiltrate the castle and meet with the king. Tieg unblocks the Deryni powers of both Michaela and her brother, Sir Cathan Drummond, and Michaela then assists Tieg, Rhysel, and Joram in activating Rhys Michael's arcane powers. After the ritual, Joram and Tieg capture Master Dimitri, a Torenthi Deryni collaborator who has been working for the great lords. The Camberian Council alters Dimitri's mind with their own set of commands before returning him to Rhemuth. The next day, Rhys Michael departs the capital with army, accompanied by Cathan, Earl Manfred MacInnis, Earl Rhun von Horthy, Lord Albertus, and Father Paulin Sinclair. Before departing the city, Constable Udaut is killed when Dimitri secretly uses his powers to spook Udaut's horse. Later on the journey, a swarm of bees mysteriously attacks the royal party and nearly kills Albertus. Several days later, Albertus questions Rhys Michael about the incidents, concerned about the rumored magical powers of the Haldane family. He orders Dimitri to probe the king's mind, but the Deryni is still under the compulsions of the Camberian Council. To protect the king, Dimitri kills Albertus and later allows himself to be implicated in the death. When Paulin attempts to confine Dimitri, he lashes out with his powers and destroys Paulin's mind before be overcome. Dimitri is tortured for several hours before he is killed by a mental death-trigger in his own mind. The royal army arrives at Lochalyn the next day, where it is joined by the levies of Duke Graham of Claibourne, Earl Sighere of Marley, and Earl Corban Howell of Eastmarch. In a private conversation, Lady Sudrey, Hrorik's Deryni widow, offers Rhys Michael her support and the use of her limited powers. The following morning, Rhys Michael agrees to meet with Prince Miklos of Torenth, who claims to have led the invasion on Marek's behalf. Accompanied by Sudrey, the king parleys with Miklos briefly, but Miklos breaks the peace by attacking Sudrey. Rhys Michael uses his own powers to protect himself and kill Miklos, but Sudrey is killed in the battle and Rhys Michael is wounded when a horse steps on his hand. Afterwards, the king claims that it was Sudrey who used magic in the battle, and later realizes that Miklos' companion was actually Marek himself. After Miklos' death, Marek withdraws his forces and returns to Torenth. Rhys Michael asks the northern lords to help him break free of the great lords, and Graham and Sighere agree to become Regents for the king's son, Prince Owain, if anything should happen to the king. Cathan prepares a codicil to the king's will, and all parties involved succeed in signing it without alerting Rhun or Manfred. The king departs for Rhemuth the next day, but the progress of the army is slowed by the worsening condition of his injury. The army is eventually forced to stop at Saint Ostrythe's Convent when the king becomes too ill to continue. Dom Queron Kinevan rushes to the king's side, but he does not arrive in time and Rhys Michael soon dies from poor medical treatment. As the army returns to Rhemuth with Rhys Michael's body, the Camberian Council informs the northern lords of the king's death and offers their assistance in securing the rights of the new Regents. Unpublished works on semantic segmentation using publicly accessible datasets have yielded impressive results. Nevertheless, they neglected the individualized aspect of segmentation, which holds significance in real-world applications. This study tackles the challenge of customized image segmentation, with the goal of generating more precise segmentation outcomes from unmarked personal images by scrutinizing the distinctive features of the data. To stimulate further exploration in this domain, we amass an extensive collection of users' personalized images termed as PIS (Personalized Image Semantic Segmentation). Moreover, we examine current studies pertaining to this issue and evaluate their effectiveness on our dataset. Additionally, based on the relationship between a user's personalized images, we suggest a baseline approach that integrates inter-image context for selectively segmenting images. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses existing techniques on the presented dataset. The associated code and PIS dataset will be distributed publicly.

Numerous natural decision issues can be translated into constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for reducts $\mathbb{A}$ of homogeneous structures with finite bounds. This category of problems represents a significant expansion of the finite-domain CSP class. Our initial finding is a general polynomial-time transformation of such infinite-domain CSPs into finite-domain CSPs. By employing this reduction, we derive novel polynomial-time tractability criteria that can be articulated through the topological polymorphism clone of $\mathbb{A}$. Furthermore, we examine the subclass $\mathcal{C}$ of CSPs for structures $\mathbb{A}$, which are reducts of structures with a single-element language. Notably, this class $\mathcal{C}$ encompasses all finite-domain CSPs as a subset. We utilize these new tractability conditions to validate the overall tractability conjecture for reducts of finitely bounded homogeneous structures within the class $\mathcal{C}$.

Melt 4 ounces bittersweet chocolate in top of double boiler set over simmering water, stirring chocolate until smooth. Remove melted chocolate from over water. Cool chocolate 10 minutes. Add melted bittersweet chocolate; beat until just combined. Mix in poppy seeds. Using electric mixer fitted with clean dry beaters, beat egg whites in another large bowl until stiff but not dry. Fold half of beaten egg white into chocolate mixture. Fold flour into remaining beaten white. Fold egg white mixture into chocolate mixture. Pour batter into prepared spring-form pan. Ingredients:
- 1 small goat cheese log (4-6 oz)
- 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- Pinch of salt
- 4 cups mixed garden lettuces (such as mesclun or arugula)
- 1/4 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/4 cup sliced cucumber
- 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Place the goat cheese log in a small baking dish or ovenproof ramekin.

2. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, thyme leaves, black pepper, and a pinch of salt. Stir well to combine.

3. Drizzle the olive oil mixture over the goat cheese, making sure to coat the entire log. Gently press the mixture onto the cheese to help it adhere.

4. Bake the goat cheese in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until lightly golden and softened. Remove from the oven and let cool for a few minutes.

5. In the meantime, prepare the garden lettuces. Wash and dry the lettuces thoroughly and place them in a large salad bowl. Add the cherry tomatoes and sliced cucumber.

6. In a small bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar and honey. Drizzle the dressing over the lettuces and toss to coat.

7. Once the goat cheese has cooled slightly, carefully transfer it to a serving plate or individual salad plates.

8. Serve the baked goat cheese alongside the garden lettuces. The warm, creamy cheese can be spread onto crackers or toasted bread, or simply dolloped onto the salad.

Gabriel Oak is a young shepherd. With the savings of a frugal life, and a loan, he has leased and stocked a sheep-farm. He falls in love with a newcomer eight years his junior, Bathsheba Everdene, a proud beauty who arrives to live with her aunt, Mrs. Hurst. She comes to like him well enough, and even saves his life once, but when he makes her an unadorned offer of marriage, she refuses; she values her independence too much and him too little. Gabriel's blunt protestations only serve to drive her to haughtiness. After a few months, she moves to Weatherbury, a village some miles off. When next they meet, their circumstances have changed drastically. An inexperienced new sheep dog drives Gabriel's flock over a cliff, ruining him. After selling off everything of value, he manages to settle all his debts, but emerges penniless. He seeks employment at a work fair in the town of Casterbridge (a fictionalised version of Dorchester). When he finds none, he heads to another fair in Shottsford, a town about ten miles from Weatherbury. On the way, he happens upon a dangerous fire on a farm and leads the bystanders in putting it out. When the veiled owner comes to thank him, he asks if she needs a shepherd. She uncovers her face and reveals herself to be none other than Bathsheba. She has recently inherited the estate of her uncle and is now a wealthy woman. Though somewhat uncomfortable, she hires him. Meanwhile, Bathsheba has a new admirer: the lonely and repressed William Boldwood. Boldwood is a prosperous farmer of about forty whose ardour Bathsheba unwittingly awakens when – her curiosity piqued because he has never bestowed on her the customary admiring glance – she playfully sends him a valentine sealed with red wax on which she has embossed the words "Marry me". Boldwood, not realising the valentine was a jest, becomes obsessed with Bathsheba, and soon proposes marriage. Although she does not love him, she toys with the idea of accepting his offer; he is, after all, the most eligible bachelor in the district. However, she postpones giving him a definite answer. When Gabriel rebukes her for her thoughtlessness, she fires him. When her sheep begin dying from bloat, she discovers to her chagrin that Gabriel is the only man who knows how to cure them. Her pride delays the inevitable, but finally she is forced to beg him for help. Afterwards, she offers him back his job and their friendship is restored. At this point, the dashing Sergeant Francis "Frank" Troy returns to his native Weatherbury and by chance encounters Bathsheba one night. Her initial dislike turns to infatuation after he excites her with a private display of swordsmanship. Gabriel observes Bathsheba's interest in the young soldier and tries to discourage it, telling her she would be better off marrying Boldwood. Boldwood becomes aggressive towards Troy and she goes to Bath to prevent Troy returning to Weatherbury, as she fears Troy may be harmed on meeting Boldwood. On their return, Boldwood offers his rival a large bribe to give up Bathsheba. Troy pretends to consider the offer, then scornfully announces they are already married. Boldwood withdraws humiliated and vows revenge. Bathsheba soon discovers that her new husband is an improvident gambler with little interest in farming. Worse, she begins to suspect that he does not love her. In fact, Troy's heart belongs to her former servant, Fanny Robin. Before meeting Bathsheba, Troy had promised to marry Fanny; on the wedding day, however, the luckless girl goes to the wrong church. She explains her mistake, but Troy, humiliated at being left waiting at the altar, angrily calls off the wedding. When they part, unbeknownst to Troy, Fanny is pregnant with his child. Some months afterward, Troy and Bathsheba encounter Fanny on the road, destitute, as she painfully makes her way toward the Casterbridge workhouse. Troy sends his wife onward with the horse and gig before she can recognise the girl, then gives her all the money in his pocket, telling her he will give her more in a few days. Fanny uses up the last of her strength to reach her destination. A few hours later, she dies in childbirth, along with the baby. Mother and child are then placed in a coffin and sent home to Weatherbury for interment. Gabriel, who has long known of Troy's relationship with Fanny, tries to conceal the child's existence – but Bathsheba, suspecting the truth and wild with jealousy, arranges for the coffin to be left in her house overnight. When all the servants are in bed, she unscrews the lid and sees the two bodies inside – her husband's former lover and their child. Troy then comes home from Casterbridge, where he had gone to keep his appointment with Fanny. Seeing the reason for her failure to meet him, he gently kisses the corpse and tells the anguished Bathsheba, "This woman is more to me, dead as she is, than ever you were, or are, or can be." The next day he spends all his money on a marble tombstone with the inscription "Erected by Francis Troy in beloved memory of Fanny Robin...". Then, loathing himself and unable to bear Bathsheba's company, he leaves. After a long walk he bathes in the sea, leaving his clothes on the beach. A strong current carries him away, though he is rescued by a rowing boat. A year later, with Troy presumed drowned, Boldwood renews his suit. Burdened with guilt over the pain she has caused him, Bathsheba reluctantly consents to marry him in six years, long enough to have Troy declared dead. Troy, however, is not dead. When he learns that Boldwood is again courting Bathsheba, he returns to Weatherbury on Christmas Eve to claim his wife. He goes to Boldwood's house, where a party is underway, and orders Bathsheba to come with him; when she shrinks back in surprise, he seizes her arm, and she screams. At this, Boldwood shoots Troy dead and tries unsuccessfully to turn the gun on himself. Although he is condemned to hang for murder, his friends petition the Home Secretary for mercy, citing insanity. This is granted and Boldwood's sentence is changed to "confinement during Her Majesty's pleasure". Bathsheba, profoundly chastened by guilt and grief, buries her husband in the same grave as Fanny and their child, and adds a suitable inscription. Throughout her tribulations, she comes to rely more and more on her oldest and (as she admits to herself) only real friend, Gabriel. When he gives notice that he is leaving her employ for California, she finally realises how important he has become to her well-being. That night, she goes alone to visit him in his cottage, to find out why he is (in her eyes) deserting her. Pressed, he reluctantly reveals that it is because people have been injuring her good name by gossiping that he wants to marry her. She exclaims that it is "...too absurd – too soon – to think of, by far!" He bitterly agrees that it is absurd, but when she corrects him, saying that it is only "too soon", he is emboldened to ask once again for her hand in marriage. She accepts, and the two are quietly wed.

An important problem in computer vision is to understand the 3D layout of the world from a video or a collection of images. In recent years, there has been significant progress in monocular depth estimation from a single image. However, most approaches focus on depth estimation and do not provide a full 3D reconstruction as an output. On the other hand, 3D object detection methods provide a 3D box around each object instance in a scene, but they do not explicitly reconstruct the 3D geometry of the scene or the surfaces of the objects. In this paper, we attempt to bridge this gap by proposing a new method for joint segmentation and localization in videos and images. Our method combines foreground clustering with a new 3D localization algorithm that uses a set of point-based features to localize objects in a scene. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on the Cityscapes dataset and show that our method can accurately segment and localize objects in a scene, resulting in a full 3D reconstruction of the scene.

Recent advances in generative models and adversarial training have led to a
flourishing image-to-image (I2I) translation literature. The current I2I
translation approaches require training images from the two domains that are
either all paired (supervised) or all unpaired (unsupervised). In practice,
obtaining paired training data in sufficient quantities is often very costly
and cumbersome. Therefore solutions that employ unpaired data, while less
accurate, are largely preferred. In this paper, we aim to bridge the gap
between supervised and unsupervised I2I translation, with application to
semantic image segmentation. We build upon pix2pix and CycleGAN,
state-of-the-art seminal I2I translation techniques. We propose a method to
select (very few) paired training samples and achieve significant improvements
in both supervised and unsupervised I2I translation settings over random
selection. Further, we boost the performance by incorporating both (selected)
paired and unpaired samples in the training process. Our experiments show that
an extremely weak supervised I2I translation solution using only one paired
training sample can achieve a quantitative performance much better than the
unsupervised CycleGAN model, and comparable to that of the supervised pix2pix
model trained on thousands of pairs.

This paper presents an efficient automatic color image segmentation method
using a seeded region growing and merging method based on square elemental
regions. Our segmentation method consists of the three steps: generating seed
regions, merging the regions, and applying a pixel-wise boundary determination
algorithm to the resultant polygonal regions. The major features of our method
are as follows: the use of square elemental regions instead of pixels as the
processing unit, a seed generation method based on enhanced gradient values, a
seed region growing method exploiting local gradient values, a region merging
method using a similarity measure including a homogeneity distance based on
Tsallis entropy, and a termination condition of region merging using an
estimated desired number of regions. Using square regions as the processing
unit substantially reduces the time complexity of the algorithm and makes the
performance stable. The experimental results show that our method exhibits
stable performance for a variety of natural images, including heavily textured
areas, and produces good segmentation results using the same parameter values.
The results of our method are fairly comparable to, and in some respects better
than, those of existing algorithms.

Martin was born in Miami, Florida and raised in Southern California. He attended the University of Southern California, where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in business administration. After graduation, he worked in the hospitality industry for several years before co-founding Playtech in 2001.

Playtech is a leading software provider for online gaming operators. The company develops and licenses gaming software for online casinos, online poker rooms, online bingo halls, and sports betting websites. Playtech is publicly traded on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index.

Martin is also an investor in various other businesses, including in the hospitality and real estate sectors. He is a member of the board of directors of the fashion e-commerce company, Nasty Gal, and also sits on the board of the Las Vegas Sands Corporation.
