The Good Soldier is narrated by the character John Dowell, half of one of the couples whose dissolving relationships form the subject of the novel. Dowell tells the stories of those dissolutions as well as the deaths of three characters and the madness of a fourth, in a rambling, non-chronological fashion that leaves gaps for the reader to fill. The novel opens with the famous line, “This is the saddest story I have ever heard.” Dowell explains that for nine years he, his wife Florence and their friends Captain Edward Ashburnham (the “good soldier” of the book’s title) and his wife Leonora had an ostensibly normal friendship while Edward and Florence sought treatment for their heart ailments at a spa in Nauheim, Germany. As it turns out, nothing in the relationships or in the characters is as it first seems. Florence’s heart ailment is a fiction she perpetrated on John to force them to stay in Europe so that she could continue her affair with an American thug named Jimmy. Edward and Leonora have a loveless, imbalanced marriage broken by his constant infidelities (both of body and heart) and Leonora’s attempts to control Edward’s affairs (both financial and romantic). Dowell is a fool and is coming to realize how much of a fool he is, as Florence and Edward had an affair under his nose for nine years without John knowing until Florence was dead. Florence’s affair with Edward leads her to commit suicide when she realizes that Edward is falling in love with his and Leonora’s young ward, Nancy Rufford, the daughter of Leonora's closest friend. Florence sees the two in an intimate conversation and rushes back into the resort, where she sees John talking to a man she knows (and who knows of her affair with Jimmy) but whom John doesn’t know. Assuming that her relationship with Edward and her marriage to John are over, Florence takes prussic acid – which she has carried for years in a vial that John thought held her heart medicine – and dies. With that story told, Dowell moves on to tell the story of Edward and Leonora’s relationship, which appears normal but which is a power struggle that Leonora wins. Dowell runs through several of Edward’s affairs and peccadilloes, including his possibly innocent attempt to comfort a crying servant on a train; his affair with the married Maisie Maidan, the one character in the book whose heart problem was unquestionably real, and his bizarre tryst in Monte Carlo and Antibes with a kept woman known as La Dolciquita. Edward’s philandering ends up costing them a fortune in bribes, blackmail and gifts for his lovers, leading Leonora to take control of Edward’s financial affairs. She gradually gets him out of debt. Edward’s last affair is his most scandalous, as he becomes infatuated with their young ward, Nancy. Nancy came to live with them after leaving a convent where her parents had sent her; her mother was a violent alcoholic, and her father (it is later suggested that this man may not be Nancy’s biological father) may have abused her. Edward, tearing himself apart because he does not want to spoil Nancy's innocence, arranges to have her sent to India to live with her father, even though this frightens her terribly. Once Leonora knows that Edward intends to keep his passion for Nancy chaste, but only wants Nancy to continue to love him from afar, Leonora torments him by making this wish impossible—she pretends to offer to divorce him so he can marry Nancy, but informs Nancy of his sordid sexual history, destroying Nancy’s innocent love for him. After Nancy's departure, Edward commits suicide, and when she reaches Aden and sees the obituary in the paper, she becomes catatonic. The novel’s last section has Dowell writing from Edward’s old estate in England, where he takes care of Nancy, whom he cannot marry because of her mental illness. Nancy is only capable of repeating two things – a Latin phrase meaning “I believe in an omnipotent God” and the word “shuttlecocks.” Dowell states that the story is sad because no one got what he wanted: Leonora wanted Edward but lost him and marries the normal (but dull) Rodney Bayham; Edward wanted Nancy but lost her; Dowell wanted a wife but has twice ended up a nurse to a sick woman, one a fake. As if in an afterthought, Dowell closes the novel by telling the story of Edward’s suicide. Edward receives a telegram from Nancy that reads, “Safe Brindisi. Having a rattling good time. Nancy.” He asks Dowell to take the telegram to his wife, pulls out his pen knife, says that it’s time he had some rest and slits his own throat. Dowell ends up generally unsure about where to lay the blame but expressing sympathy for Edward, because Dowell thinks himself to be similar to Edward in nature.

Soak 500 ml dried garbanzo beans without using canned alternatives for at least 12 hours but no more than 24 hours. Drain the beans after soaking. Combine the soaked beans, one medium quartered onion, 2-3 minced garlic cloves, 2-3 slices of stale bread, 50 ml chopped parsley, and 1/3 sliced sweet red pepper in a large mixing bowl. Grind the mixture using a meat grinder's fine blade or process in a food processor until it becomes mealy. Next, add 10 ml each of salt, black pepper, cumin, oregano, ground coriander, and hot red pepper flakes, along with 20 ml flour, 10 ml baking powder, and 125 ml water. Form the chickpea mixture into walnut-sized balls, then gently press them into flat, slightly flattened shapes. Deep fry the falafel balls in vegetable oil over medium-high heat until they turn golden brown. Serve these warm, either immediately or after freezing and reheating in an oven.

To make the Tarator Sauce, combine 175 ml tahini, 1 crushed garlic clove, the juice of 1 1/2 to 2 lemons, 175 ml water, and 5 ml salt in a blender. Blend until smooth. Stir in 50 ml finely chopped parsley.

As garnishes, consider adding sliced tomatoes, dill pickles, and chopped parsley. While I strongly recommend including fresh spearmint, it can also be considered optional.

Form 4-5 falafel balls per Arabic pita bread. Press the falafel down the length of the pita using the heels of your hands. Open the pita and fill it with desired garnishes, such as tomato slices, dill pickles, and a generous amount of parsley and fresh spearmint. Drizzle with the Tarator Sauce, roll up, and enjoy a flavorful sandwich wrap.

The story takes place in Northern Europe, in an area inhabited by clans of humans named after different animals. These clans live a hunter-gatherer existence and adhere to a shamanic belief system. Six months after the events of Wolf Brother, Torak, the young male protagonist, is now living with the Raven Clan. One of the clan members, becomes sick and attempts to kill himself and his young nephew, but is stopped by the clan's leader. He is tied up and quarantined. Torak suspects that the sickness has been created by a group of renegade shamans known as the Soul-Eaters. Leaders from other Clans come to the Raven camp and tell them the sickness has been spreading through the forest. Torak realises that a small creature has been stalking him and trying to kill him, and when Oslak escapes and kills himself, Torak discovers that the creature was responsible. Torak sneaks out of the camp and goes into the forest seeking a cure. Wolf, Torak's companion from the previous novel, has been living with a pack in the High Mountains, but becomes unhappy with his life and he goes off to find Torak. Renn, the female protagonist, has encountered the creature at the Raven Camp and the clan's shaman, Sauenn, explains that a it is a Tokoroth: a child who has been stolen from their mother and abused by the Soul-Eaters until he or she does their bidding, the Soul-Eaters then put a demon inside the child. Renn sneaks out of the camp to find Torak and she and Wolf encounter each other. They then both go looking for him. At the seashore, Torak encounters and fights three boys from the Seal Clan: Bale, Detlan and Asrif, but is eventually overpowered. They believe that, by washing his hunting gear in the sea, he has dishonoured the Sea Mother and must be punished, so they take him by canoe to their home in the Seal Islands. Renn and Wolf meet up with some members of the Sea Eagle Clan, who take them both to the Seal Islands to help Torak. The Seal Clan's shaman, Tenris, initially wants to punish Torak until Torak informs him of the sickness. Tenris tells Torak that a cure can be made from a rare plant which grows at the top of a particular cliff: the plant must be gathered on midsummer night, which is only four days away. Torak quickly realises the Tokoroth has followed him to the island. He goes looking for it but is tricked into falling into a seal net, from which he is rescued by Wolf and Renn. They talk and establish that an orca has been killed, breaking a taboo. Only the teeth have been removed from the carcass. Renn informs Torak that she saw one of the Seal Clan near the orca's carcass, but she is unable to persuade Torak that any of the clan would break such a taboo. Torak goes with Bale, Detlan and Asrif to climb the cliff and gather the plant. Asrif climbs up but his climbing harness becomes snagged, and Torak follows him up. He has to unhook himself from his rope to rescue Deltan and to gather the plant. Unable to reach his harness, he realises that the only way back down is to dive into the sea. Under the water, he feels himself taking the form of a fish for a few moments and senses an angry orca approaching, before returning to his body. The boys rush into the water to save Torak as an orca attacks Detlan, causing him a crippling injury. When they return to the island, Torak talks with Tenris about the odd experience he had in the water. Tenris explains that Torak must be a Spirit Walker: a human with the rare ability to drift out of his own body and into the body of any other living creature. Renn is found by some of the Seal Clan and realises that Tenris was responsible for killing the orca, and that he must be a Soul-Eater. Tenris notices a scab on her hand and, mistaking it for a symptom of the sickness, tells Bale to lock her up so the sickness won't spread. On Midsummers night, Torak goes to the crag to make the cure with Tenris, but Tenris overpowers Torak with the help of two Tokoroth. Tenris admits that he is a Soul-Eater, and that he killed the orca. He reveals that he had created the rogue bear which killed Torak's father and, realizing that the bear's killer must be a powerful shaman, had sent the Tokoroth to poison the juniper berries of the forest, knowing that the epidemic will flush him out as he searches for a cure. Tenris intends to eat Torak's heart, in order to assimilate his powers and become the greatest Soul-Eater. Tenris also reveals that Torak's father was his own brother, and had been a Soul-Eater before seeing the error of his ways. Wolf appears and chases away the Tokoroth. Renn, who has persuades Bale to let her go, shoots Tenris through the hand with an arrow, giving Torak the opportunity to escape by diving off the crag. Tenris jumps after him, but the blood from his arrow-wound attracts an orca which has been seeking revenge for the killing of its mate. Before Tenris is killed by the orca, he tells Torak that his adopted father in the Raven Clan knows more about Torak's father. Torak swims to safety, and he, Renn, and Wolf, now armed with the information to save the Clans, return to the Forest.

John Steiner (born 7 January 1941) is an English actor. Tall, thin and gaunt, Steiner attended the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, worked for a few years at the BBC and later appeared mostly in Italian films. Career
Steiner found work primarily in films including Marat/Sade (1967), and the original Bedazzled (1967) with Peter Cook and Dudley Moore. In 1969, Steiner was hired to play a part in the Spaghetti Western Tepepa, and also appeared opposite Franco Nero in White Fang, directed by Lucio Fulci. In 1971 he starred in the television series Hine. In 1979 he featured in the leading role of Leo in a television production of Design for Living by Noël Coward.           
He found himself in demand in Italy and moved there, appearing in a great number of Italian exploitation and B-films including police actioners (Violent Rome), westerns (Mannaja), war films (The Last Hunter), nazisploitation (Deported Women of the SS Special Section), sci-fi adventure films (Yor, the Hunter from the Future), and horror films, such as Mario Bava's Shock, Dario Argento's Tenebrae, and Ruggero Deodato's Body Count. He also became a favourite of famed Italian filmmaker Tinto Brass, featuring in Salon Kitty, the infamous Caligula, Action, and Paprika.
Steiner was in very steady demand until the late 1980s. As the Italian film industry dwindled, Steiner retired from acting in 1991 and moved to California, where he became a real estate agent.

Georgia E. Engelhard Cromwell (November 19, 1906 – September 14, 1986) was an American mountaineer in the Canadian Rockies and the Selkirk and Purcell ranges.  She was the first female climber to ascend many of the peaks in the Rockies and was the leading female amateur climber of her day.  She was also an accomplished painter and photographer. Early life
Engelhard was born in Manhattan on November 19, 1906, the first child of George Engelhard, a lawyer, and Agnes Stieglitz.  She was a niece of Alfred Stieglitz, an American photographer and modern art promoter, and his wife, Georgia O'Keeffe, an American artist considered by many to be the "Mother of American modernism". To avoid confusion of names between the two "Georgias", Engelhard was usually referred to as "The Kid" or "Georgia Minor".  She occasionally posed for photographs by Stieglitz, including nudes. Stieglitz was a close confidant and mentor to Engelhard, and the two corresponded vigorously from the time she was twelve into her early twenties.

La Vendetta is a short work relating the tragic fate of Ginevra Piombo, the daughter of proud Corsican immigrants, who has the misfortune of falling in love with another Corsican Luigi Porta. When it becomes known that Luigi is the sole survivor of a massacre in which the rest of his family were the victims of a bloody vendetta with Ginevra's family, Ginevra's father Bartolomeo is determined to complete the act of vengeance by having him killed. But Ginevra refuses to yield to her father's demands and she and Luigi are married. Over the following years the pair eke out a miserable existence, dogged by hunger and poverty, while Ginevra's wealthy father refuses to lift a hand to support her: it is as much as he can do to refrain from murdering Luigi. Ginevra gives birth to a child, but she and the child die on the very day that Monsieur Piombo finally relents and decides to assist the impoverished couple. Before he can act, however, Luigi visits him and gives him the tresses of his deceased daughter. "Dead! Our two families were doomed to exterminate each other. Here is all that remains of her," he says, laying Ginevra's long black hair upon the table. Ginevra's parents are shaken, as though a stroke of lightning has blasted them. Luigi departs. "He has spared me a shot, for he is dead," says Bartolomeo, slowly, gazing on the ground at his feet.

Quantum computation and communication rely heavily on the reliable storage of quantum information. However, numerous experimental setups for these applications experience significant bias in their noise, compromising their resistance to spin depolarization due to high dephasing rates. This study presents evidence that the memory efficiency of a noisy trapped-ion qubit memory can be significantly enhanced by integrating dephasing error correction via teleportation of information between two repetition codes written on separate qubit registers within the same trap. Despite the demanding technological prerequisites for error correction, our method can be executed using a solitary global entangling phase gate with exceptionally low fidelity, exploiting the dominance of gate errors by dephasing-related processes. By readjusting the logical flip and dephasing error rates, we prove that, under practical conditions, our memory can display error rates that are several orders of magnitude lower than those of unprotected physical qubits, thereby offering an effective solution for enhancing memory performance in trapped ion systems lacking field-insensitive qubits.

Shrimp and Cilantro Shu Mai Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 pound raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tablespoon ginger, minced
- 2 green onions, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup cilantro, chopped
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 package round wonton wrappers
- Water for sealing the dumplings
- Soy sauce or dipping sauce for serving

Instructions:
1. In a food processor, add the shrimp, minced garlic, minced ginger, chopped green onions, chopped cilantro, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper. Pulse until everything is well combined and forms a sticky mixture.
2. Take a wonton wrapper and place a teaspoon of the shrimp mixture in the center.
3. Wet the edges of the wonton wrapper with water and fold it in half, creating a small semi-circular dumpling. Pinch the edges to seal the dumpling. Repeat with the remaining wonton wrappers and shrimp mixture.
4. Place the shrimp shu mai on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
5. Steam the shrimp shu mai in a bamboo steamer for about 8-10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
6. Serve the shrimp and cilantro shu mai with soy sauce or a dipping sauce of your choice.

Note: If you don't have a bamboo steamer, you can also pan-fry the shrimp shu mai in a non-stick skillet with a little oil until they are crisp and golden on the outside. Make sure to cook them in batches and avoid overcrowding the pan.

Ingredients:

- 1 can (395 grams) of condensed milk
- 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter
- 3 tablespoons of coconut milk
- 1 cup of shredded unsweetened coconut
- Granulated sugar for rolling (optional)
- 50 colorful candy paper cups (also called bonbon or truffle cups)
- 50 cloves (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a non-stick pan, add the condensed milk, unsalted butter, coconut milk, and half a cup of shredded coconut. 

2. Cook the mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens and starts to peel off the bottom of the pan. This process will take about 10 minutes. You will know it's done when you scoop some up with a spoon, turn it upside down, and it holds its shape without falling off.

3. Pour the mixture into a greased dish and let it cool to room temperature. 

4. While waiting for the mixture to cool, take the remaining half cup of shredded coconut and spread it out on a flat plate. If you're using granulated sugar, get another plate and spread it out as well.

5. Once the mixture has cooled, apply some butter to your hands and start shaping the candies into small balls, about the size of a cherry. 

6. Roll each candy in the shredded coconut or granulated sugar until well coated, then place each ball into a candy paper cup.

7. To give the candies a traditional Brazilian look, stick a clove into the top of each one (this is optional and the clove is not meant to be eaten).

8. Place the candies in the refrigerator for at least an hour before serving to let them firm up. 

Now you have 50 delicious Brazilian Coconut Beijinhos ready to serve! This sweet treat is a hit at parties and tastes just like the ones you'd get in Brazil. Enjoy!

In the narrative, the setting is Corrientes, a city in northern Argentina, marked by police vehicles bearing the insignia "Policía de Corrientes." Eduardo Plarr, a young English descendant doctor, grew up in Paraguay before relocating to Buenos Aires with his mother. His English father, a political dissident, was left behind. Save for a solitary hand-delivered note, they no longer communicate. Upon settling into the tranquil, subtropical hamlet, Plarr befriends its only two English denizens: Humphries, a disenchanted elderly English teacher, and Charles Fortnum, the Honorary Consul, a divorced, self-absorbed alcoholic who misutilizes his role. Saavedra, a neglected Argentine author of silent macho novels, is also a key contact. During a visit to a local bawdy house with Saavedra, Plarr is smitten with a woman yet another man claims. Years later, he's summoned to treat Fortnum's new spouse. Recognizing her as Clara from the brothel, Plarr finds himself infatuated. Despite striving to maintain emotional detachment, he eventually seduces her, procuring her sunglasses. "Caring is the most perilous act," Plarr muses in the book. "The term `love' was a demand, an obligation, an ultimatum. My mother had often employed it during my childhood; it was like a gun pointed at my head. `Surrender or else ...' Something was always required in exchange: compliance, contrition, a kiss I didn't wish to offer." Clara falls pregnant, and Fortnum reduces his alcohol consumption. Subsequently, some of Plarr's former classmates, including Rivas, a failed priest, arrive at his practice. They bring news of Plarr's father, who has resurfaced after decades.

Objective: This study introduces a liver segmentation approach based on a neural network. The method's effectiveness was assessed utilizing abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans. Methodology: A fully convolutional network was designed to address the challenge of volumetric image segmentation. By employing an adaptive self-supervision strategy, the neural network was intensely supervised to precisely outline the target liver, with the derived essential contour serving as a supportive complement to the overall form. The discriminative contour, shape, and deep features were combined within the segmentation process. Results: One hundred sixty abdominal CT images served as the training and validation datasets. An eight-fold cross-validation was conducted to evaluate the proposed network's performance. The findings indicated that the proposed technique, incorporating the contour feature, outperformed the current state-of-the-art by improving the dice score by 2.13%. Significance: Through this investigation, a novel learning framework was presented to instruct a neural network and acquire supplementary contour characteristics. The suggested neural network reveals that these guided contour features can substantially enhance the segmentation task's efficiency.

In this coming-of-age story, a young girl named Mia discovers she has the ability to manipulate time. She can rewind, fast forward, and even pause the clock, but she soon learns that this power comes with great responsibility.

Mia's small town is filled with people who are struggling to make ends meet, and she decides to use her powers to help them. She uses her abilities to give people extra time to study for exams, to help them finish their work faster, and even to save lives. However, as she continues to use her powers, Mia begins to realize that changing time has unintended consequences.

As Mia becomes more confident in her abilities, she starts to take on bigger challenges. She tries to prevent accidents and disasters before they happen, but she quickly realizes that altering events in the past has a ripple effect that can impact the present in unexpected ways. Mia must grapple with the moral implications of her actions and learn to balance her desire to help others with the potential risks of tampering with time.

Meanwhile, Mia's personal life is also complicated by her newfound abilities. Twitter represents a major player among Online Social Networks, accounting for approximately 20% of the global online population with rapid expansion. The social structure of Twitter has attracted extensive research interest due to its insights into the fundamental characteristics of vast and intricate online groups. Yet, there is a scarcity of information regarding the development of these properties within the social graph over time. Given Twitter's enormous scale (consisting of millions of entities and billions of connections), only a select number of graph attributes can be proficiently analyzed within a practical timeframe. In this study, we introduce a sampling scheme to approximate graph properties in extensive social networks. Applying this approach to a segment of Twitter's social network comprising 13.2 million users, 8.3 billion connections, and spanning the entire Twitter feed (April 2006 to January 2015), we provide estimates for the progression of 24 graph properties, several of which remain unexplored in large-scale social networks. Furthermore, we elucidate how these assessments contribute to a better understanding of Twitter's social network's underlying structure and growth patterns.

With supervised semantic segmentation yielding satisfactory outcomes, current research has shifted towards creating quicker, smaller, and more effective segmentation network structures. This pursuit is crucial for real-time applications, including autonomous vehicles and robotics, as well as real-time video processing in medical imaging.

The standard evaluation metrics for these approaches have been identical to those utilized for image segmentation without time constraints: Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU). However, this metric falls short when considering real-time video since it neglects the network's processing time (latency). In this study, we advocate for an alternative metric, FLAME (Frame Latency for Accurate video-Segmentation Networks), which evaluates the network's output segmentation against the ground truth segmentation of the current video frame at the moment the network completes processing.

Our experiments demonstrate the efficacy of several networks utilizing this metric and introduce a straightforward modification to network training to improve performance based on this new metric.

Remember 'Jaws'? Remember the way you only got to see little glimpses of the shark or just the remains of his victims for nearly half the movie? Instead, you got to meet half the town first and all the main characters while fear and paranoia slowly spread across the whole community, and when the great white guy finally did make his entrance - boy, what an impact he had.

Now, that was 40 years ago - but would it be possible to make that kind of movie today? To show restraint despite a budget of 160+ million dollars and all the latest state of the art CGI-effects the blockbuster factory has to offer?

As it turns out, it's not quite possible; at least not as far as this latest version of 'Godzilla' is concerned - but that's probably not for lack of trying on director Gareth Edwards' part. The young director ('Monsters') has stated many times that 'Jaws' was a huge inspiration for him on this movie, and it is hardly a coincidence that the (human) hero in 'Godzilla' shares the same name with the hero in Spielberg's masterpiece (they're both called Brody).

Edwards made it very clear that he wanted to take an "old school" approach - and as far as the beautiful, haunting build-up of the first half of the movie is concerned, he actually succeeds. The atmosphere of mystery and dread is tangible; the human element is there, the acting and the dialogues are solid, and the production design is breathtaking (especially the apocalyptic images of an evacuated city in Japan which was left to decay for 15 years, overgrown with plants and with packs of wild dogs running in the streets).

The "muto" design - when we do get a first glimpse at a creature - is otherworldly and frightening (as good monsters should be), but as the movie progresses into the second half and the creature-action increases, the quality of the pacing, the dialogues and the acting inexplicably decreases. The movie sadly starts to feel flat, and although there is one great creature scene after another, and although those scenes get more and more intense as the storyline steers towards the inevitable showdown, it's hard to stay invested in the human side of the story.

After the first act (when there was actually still some real acting required from the actors), there are virtually no interesting moments anymore when the human protagonists interact, let alone lingering scenes where the characters get to talk long enough to one another to even try to build such a thing as chemistry. So when the finale does arrive (which looks absolutely beautiful, by the way), you admire its epic scale, but since there is nobody to care about, it's hard to feel thrilled.Sure, you kind of root for Godzilla, but since you only just met the guy, you don't feel too much attached.

Ultimately - despite a great build-up and a fantastic looking finale - 'Godzilla' is a valid effort but only rarely a thrilling one. Unlike in 'Jaws', there are no interesting human characters here who could help create the kind of tension-heavy atmosphere or sense of impending doom the way Chief Brody, Hooper and Quint could 40 years ago.

Trying to show restraint alone is not enough to create a sense of wonder the way seventies cinema did - you also need the kind of character-driven scenes where someone says: "We're gonna need a bigger boat!"

This study presents the Deep LOGISMOS technique for precise 3D tumor segmentation through integrating boundary data obtained from deep contextual learning into the LOGISMOS system - an advanced graph-based image segmentation method for handling numerous objects and surfaces. Precise tumor segmentation is vital for tumor progression analysis and therapy selection. Initially, a fully convolutional network (FCN), specifically UNet, is trained via three adjacent 2D patches positioned around the tumor. This results in contextual UNet segmentation and the generation of a probability map for every 2D patch. Following this, the UNet segmentation undergoes enhancement via Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and morphological procedures. The improved UNet segmentation serves as the foundation for constructing a segmentation graph's initial shape boundary, with node costs determined based on UNet probability maps. Ultimately, a max-flow algorithm is utilized to discover the global optimum, resulting in the complete segmentation. On a collection of 51 CT scans, 30 of which served as training samples and the remaining 21 for testing, the method yielded DICE Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Relative Volume Difference (RVD) scores of 83.2±7.8% and 18.6±17.4%, respectively - improvements that were statistically significant (p<0.05) compared to contextual UNet and/or LOGISMOS individually.

The iOS version of Popcorn Time is no longer maintained.

In a large mixing bowl, combine 1/4 tsp rapid rise yeast and 1 1/2 cups room-temperature water. Add 1 3/4 tsp salt. Gradually beat in 4 cups all-purpose flour using a wooden spoon until a thick, sticky dough forms that separates from the bowl's sides. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it rest in an oven that has been turned off for 12 to 14 hours. The dough should be bubbly and extremely sticky. On a baking sheet, place a silicone baking mat coated with generous amounts of cornmeal. Using a floured spatula, move the dough from the bowl to a well-floured work surface, then dust it with more flour. Pat it into a rectangle, divide it into 4 equal parts, and shape each part into a log measuring about 10 inches long and 1 1/2 inches wide. Transfer one log to the prepared baking sheet. If preferred, remove excess cornmeal from the sheet with a damp paper towel. Perform the same steps with the remaining dough, reserving the remaining portion to prepare later or using two baking sheets to cook all four loaves simultaneously. Lightly dust the loaves with flour. Coat a large sheet of plastic wrap with flour, then loosely cover the baking sheet with it, cornmeal side down. Allow the loaves to rise, covered, until they have doubled in size, which takes approximately 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Adjust the oven racks to the lower and middle positions and preheat the oven to 500°F (260°C) or its maximum temperature. Put a baking dish filled with water into the bottom rack of the oven. Use kitchen shears to make 4-5 angled incisions on the top of each loaf. Press down the dough tips created by the shears. Spritz the loaves with water using a spray bottle. Cook the loaves in the heated oven until they turn golden brown, which takes roughly 15 minutes. Re-make (also remake) and re-model (also remodel) are synonyms that refer to refresh or update an existing thing. Although the term "remake" originally referred only to film adaptations of existing stories, its meaning has expanded to other types of creative works.

A remake is technically identical in theme and plot to the original work, but with different characters, settings, dialogue, and/or visuals. It is distinct from a sequel or a prequel, as remakes generally serve as a revision of the original work or as a vehicle for a new cast. Multiple remakes of the same work may vary in how closely they stick to the original. Although official remakes are based on previous works, unofficial remakes are held in different regard and are generally derivative works.

Remodeling, on the other hand, denotes an overhaul of something, rather than a simple update. It is a popular term in the interior design and home improvement industries, where it is used to refer to the process of updating a room's decor, functionality, or layout. It may include changing the layout, replacing fixtures and appliances, or updating the aesthetics. It can also refer to changing the functionality or appearance of a software program or adding new features to it.

The term "remodel" is also sometimes used to refer to a remake of a movie or television show, with changes being made to the plot, characters, settings, dialogue, or visuals. However, this usage is less common than "remake."

The difference between "remake" and "remodel" is that "remake" refers to creating something new from an existing work, while "remodel" refers to overhauling something existing to create a new and improved version. However, the terms are often used interchangeably.

Net users are being told to avoid a scam website that claims to collect cash on behalf of tsunami victims.
The site looks plausible because it uses an old version of the official Disasters Emergency Committee webpage. However, DEC has no connection with the fake site and says it has contacted the police about it. The site is just the latest in a long list of scams that try to cash in on the goodwill generated by the tsunami disaster.
The link to the website is contained in a spam e-mail that is currently circulating. The message's subject line reads "Urgent Tsunami Earthquake Appeal" and its text bears all the poor grammar and bad spelling that characterises many other phishing attempts. The web address of the fake site is decuk.org which could be close enough to the official www.dec.org.uk address to confuse some people keen to donate. Patricia Sanders, spokeswoman for the Disaster Emergency Committee said it was aware of the site and had contacted the Computer Crime Unit at Scotland Yard to help get it shut down. She said the spam e-mails directing people to the site started circulating two days ago shortly after the domain name of the site was registered. It is thought that the fake site is being run from Romania. Ms Sanders said DEC had contacted US net registrars who handle domain ownership and the net hosting firm that is keeping the site on the web.
DEC was going to push for all cash donated via the site to be handed over to the official organisation. BT and DEC's hosting company were also making efforts to get the site shut down, she said.
Ms Sanders said sending out spam e-mail to solicit donations was not DEC's style and that it would never canvass support in this way. She said that DEC hoped to get the fake site shut down as soon as possible. All attempts by the BBC News website to contact the people behind the site have failed. None of the e-mail addresses supplied on the site work and the real owner of the domain is obscured in publicly available net records. This is not the first attempt to cash in on the outpouring of goodwill that has accompanied appeals for tsunami aid. One e-mail sent out in early January came from someone who claimed that he had lost his parents in the disaster and was asking for help moving an inheritance from a bank account in the Netherlands. The con was very similar to the familiar Nigerian forward fee fraud e-mails that milk money out of people by promising them a cut of a much larger cash pile. Other scam e-mails included a link to a website that supposedly let people donate money but instead loaded spyware on their computers that grabbed confidential information. In a monthly report anti-virus firm Sophos said that two e-mail messages about the tsunami made it to the top 10 hoax list during January. Another tsunami-related e-mail is also circulating that carries the Zar worm which tries to spread via the familiar route of Microsoft's Outlook e-mail program. Anyone opening the attachment of the mail will have their contact list plundered by the worm keen to find new addresses to send itself to.

Creamy Tarragon Chicken Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 tablespoon butter
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 1 cup heavy cream
- 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
- 1 tablespoon fresh tarragon leaves, chopped
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper on both sides.
2. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken breasts and cook for about 5-6 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion is translucent and the garlic is fragrant.
4. Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing the broth to reduce slightly.
5. Stir in the heavy cream, Dijon mustard, and chopped tarragon leaves. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, until the sauce has thickened slightly.
6. Return the chicken breasts to the skillet, along with any juices that have accumulated. Spoon the sauce over the chicken to coat.
7. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.
8. Stir in the lemon juice and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
9. Serve the creamy tarragon chicken hot, garnished with extra tarragon leaves if desired. This dish pairs well with rice, pasta, or roasted vegetables. Enjoy!

In the 15th century, the duke of Löwenstein built a residence next to it for his wife Elzbieta von Ochsenhausen. She was a wealthy heiress who made significant donations during her lifetime to religious charities throughout Europe. It was this generosity that earned the hill its name, which means "holy mount."

Over time, the site underwent several renovations and additions, eventually becoming a grand palace in Renaissance style. The outer walls were painted with frescoes depicting scenes from biblical stories. During World War II, Schloss Heiligenberg suffered damage, but it survived mostly intact thanks to the protective dome that covered part of the complex. After the war, the foundation conducted extensive restorations to repair the damage caused by fighting. Today, the castle attracts tourists from all over the world seeking panoramic views of the surrounding area.

Artificial intelligence's spatial-temporal domain encompasses computational sciences, cognitive sciences, and cognitive psychology. The objective on the cognitive side is to model and process spatial-temporal knowledge within intelligent systems. On the computational side, the aim is creating advanced automata control systems capable of comprehending and traversing temporal and spatial dimensions. Cognitive psychology's findings have significantly impacted this field: newborn infants initially grasp the concept of the connection relation, followed by orientation and distance concepts. The internal connections among these spatial relations can be systematically and computationally described using the cognitive prism theory: (1) connection relations are fundamental, (2) orientation relations are a type of comparison of distances: being in front of someone means being closer to their front side than their others, and (3) distance relations are connection relations involving a third object: one meter separation between individuals can be understood as a one-meter-long object linking both parties.

12 teaspoon ground allspice
freshly grated nutmeg, a pinch

1 cup sugar

Position oven rack in the middle of oven; preheat to 350. Line a standard 12-cup muffin pan with paper or foil liners. A little girl was playing in the garden 'round her home,
Mischief sparkled in her dark eyes and her curly hair was blond.
Innocent joy rang in the laughter of her happy, playful song:
'Dandelions are as pretty as the flowers that grow high.
I have picked some for you, Mommy, and I want to show you why.
They make tassels on our slippers; we can wear them, you and I.'
Into that happy garden crept a serpent black and long,
Shining sinister in the sunlight as he flicked a jeweled tongue.
Captivatedly she listened to his strange inviting song:
'Stolen candies can be sweeter than the ones your parents buy.
Taste how sweet they are, like honey, as I coil about your thigh.
It will be our little secret as we eat them, you and I.'
Secrets growing in a garden, in among the pretty blooms,
Rob children of their laughter; so that it was very soon
That a mother's heart was sighing a sad, foreboding tune:
'Oh, my daughter was so pretty, and I wish that I knew why
Such a change has come about her that it makes my spirit cry.
Her eyes have lost their glitter and she has not told me why.'
Little girls will always grow up; that, in life, has been decreed,
While secrets locked in childhood are concealed in history.
Yet the scars they are concealing will be sung in misery:
'Why do candies taste so bitter? Why does laughter make me cry?
Why do I have a feeling happiness has passed me by?
I'm living with a memory that will haunt me 'til I die.
Within me lives a memory that will haunt me 'til I die.'

Whole Wheat Ricotta Gnocchi Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1 cup ricotta cheese
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg (optional)
- 1/4 cup additional whole wheat flour (for dusting)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, ricotta cheese, egg, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg (if using). Mix well until all the ingredients are fully incorporated.

2. Sprinkle a clean surface with some additional whole wheat flour. Transfer the dough onto the floured surface and knead it gently for a few minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour, but be careful not to add too much as it can make the gnocchi dense.

3. Divide the dough into four equal portions. Take one portion and roll it into a long rope, about 1/2 inch in diameter. Cut the rope into small pieces, about 1 inch long. Repeat this process with the remaining dough portions.

4. To shape the gnocchi, you can either use a gnocchi board or the back of a fork. Hold the fork or gnocchi board at a slight angle and press each piece of dough against it with your thumb. As you press, the dough will curl around the fork or board, creating ridges on one side and a small indentation on the other. Place the shaped gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet or tray.

5. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Carefully drop the gnocchi into the boiling water, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pot. Cook the gnocchi for about 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked gnocchi to a plate or colander.

6. Serve the whole wheat ricotta gnocchi with your favorite sauce, such as marinara, pesto, or browned butter with sage. Garnish with additional grated Parmesan cheese and fresh herbs, if desired.

Enjoy your homemade whole wheat ricotta gnocchi!

Different approaches have been used to tackle semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentations, although they share fundamental links. This paper introduces a unified framework, referred to as K-Net, which harmoniously handles instances and semantic categories via a set of learnable kernels. Each kernel generates a corresponding mask for an instance or a semantic class. To address the challenge of separating distinct instances, we propose a kernel updating strategy, allowing each kernel to adapt dynamically based on its significant cluster in the input image. K-Net can be taught through end-to-end training using bipartite matching, and its training and evaluation processes are inherently free from non-maximum suppression (NMS) and bounding boxes. K-Net achieves superiority over prior art in panoptic segmentation on MS COCO (52.1% PQ) and ADE20K (54.3% mIoU), as well as competitive instance segmentation accuracy on MS COCO compared to Cascade Mask R-CNN with inference speeds improved by 60%-90%. The code and models will be accessible at <https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection>.

This paper presents a novel graph-based framework called Affinity Fusion Graph (AFG) for natural image segmentation. The AFG model integrates both the color and texture features of an image to enhance the discriminatory power. The scheme employs the fusion of multiple affinity matrices to form a comprehensive graph portraying an image’s structural and feature information. Utilizing a spectral clustering approach, the proposed framework exhibits improved segmentation by avoiding over-segmentation or under-segmentation that is common in other models. Experimental results on several datasets validate the effectiveness of AFG in comparison to other state-of-the-art methods in terms of achieving better segmentation accuracy and visual quality. The study opens up new avenues for the integration of different image features and multiple affinity graphs in natural image segmentation tasks.

Egypt and Israel have recently signed a trade accord with the US, enabling Egyptian merchandise produced in conjunction with Israeli businesses to be imported duty-free into American markets. This agreement, sealed in Cairo, will instate "certified industrial areas" in Egypt. For merchandise originating from these zones to qualify for preferential treatment, they must comprise a minimum of 35% Israeli-Egyptian collaborative content. The US characterizes this arrangement as the most significant economic pact between Egypt and Israel in over twenty years.

Negotiations on the zone creation have been delayed for extended periods. Egypt's diplomatic ties with Israel have been strained due to ongoing impasses in the Palestinian peace process. However, in the last few weeks, a noticeable thawing has emerged in the relationship between the two nations. They have reciprocally released prisoners; Egypt returned an Israeli man who had spent eight years imprisoned for espionage.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has commended Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon as the most promising figure for Palestinian reconciliation. The Egyptian administration now perceives Sharon shifting towards the political center and distancing himself from the hardline factions. Furthermore, they anticipate the US, under pressure from Europe, to be increasingly committed to resolving the conflict. Nevertheless, compelling economic motivators compel Egypt to pursue this commercial deal. It will significantly bolster Egyptian textile exports, which face imminent decline due to forthcoming US regulations effective January 1st.

The abstract of the academic paper "Baer and Baer *-ring characterizations of Leavitt path algebras" could be something like this:

In this paper, we present new characterizations of Leavitt path algebras using Baer and Baer *-ring techniques. Leavitt path algebras are a class of algebraic structures that have been studied extensively in recent years due to their connections to various areas of mathematics, such as algebraic geometry, symbolic dynamics, and operator algebras.

Our main result provides a new characterization of Leavitt path algebras in terms of their Baer *-ring structure. Specifically, we show that a *-ring is isomorphic to a Leavitt path algebra if and only if it satisfies certain identities, which we describe explicitly. This result gives a new way to recognize Leavitt path algebras and provides a new tool for studying their properties.

In addition, we also prove a Baer *-ring version of the classical Frobenius reciprocity theorem, which relates the *-ring structure of a Leavitt path algebra to its underlying graph structure. This result has important implications for the study of Leavitt path algebras and their applications.

Our work builds on previous research in the field and provides new insights into the structure and properties of Leavitt path algebras. It also demonstrates the power and flexibility of Baer and Baer *-ring techniques in the study of algebraic structures.

Overall, our paper contributes to the development of the theory of Leavitt path algebras and provides new tools and techniques for studying these important algebraic structures.

USS Indiana (BB-58) was the second of four  fast battleships built for the United States Navy in the 1930s. The first American battleships designed after the Washington treaty system began to break down in the mid-1930s, they took advantage of an escalator clause that allowed increasing the main battery to  guns, but refusal to authorize larger battleships kept their displacement close to the Washington limit of . A requirement to be armored against the same caliber of guns as they carried, combined with the displacement restriction, resulted in cramped ships, a problem that was exacerbated as wartime modifications that considerably strengthened their anti-aircraft batteries significantly increased their crews. Indiana entered service in April 1942, by which time the United States was engaged in World War II, and the ship was immediately pressed into action in the Pacific War against Japan. Her first combat came in late 1942 when she supported marines fighting during the Guadalcanal campaign. Over the next three years, she was occupied with two primary roles: naval gunfire support for amphibious assaults across the Pacific and anti-aircraft defense for the fast carrier task force. She shelled Japanese positions during the Battle of Tarawa in November 1943 and the Battle of Kwajalein in February 1944. During the latter operation, she collided with the battleship  and was forced to withdraw for repairs.

A limestone cliff extended from left-center to center field, presenting challenges for outfielders and enhancing the thrill of baseball games. Accessible solely via a goat trail in left-center field, the cliff became infamously known as "Billy Goat Hill." Atop this hill stood a scoreboard near the fence, adding to the unpredictability of ball trajectories for outfielders. The Longhorns derived significant home-field advantage due to these peculiarities. For instance, the Longhorns frequently achieved inside-the-park home runs when balls were hit towards the cliff, as visiting outfielders grappled with the erratic bounces and uncertain play strategies. Longhorn outfielders profited from their intimate knowledge of the cliff, often limiting opponents to doubles or triples. Reportedly, half of the team's outfielders preferred to station themselves atop the cliff while the other half positioned themselves in front.

Here, as in childhood, Brother, no one knows us.
And someone has died, and someone is not yet
born, while our father walks through his church at night
and sets all the clocks for spring.  His sleeplessness
weighs heavy on my forehead, his death almost
nothing. in the only letter he wrote to us
he says, No one can tell how long it takes a seed
to declare what death and lightning told it
while it slept.  But stand at a window long enough,
late enough, and you may some night hear
a secret you'll tomorrow, parallel to the morning,
tell on a wide, white bed, to a woman
like a sown ledge of wheat.  Or you may never
tell it, who lean across the night and miles of the sea,
to arrive at a seed, in whose lamplit house
resides a thorn, or a wee man, carving
a name on a stone, at afluctuating table of water,
the name of the one who has died, the name of the one
not born unknown.  Someone has died.  Someone
is not yet born.  And during this black interval,
I sweep all three floors of our father's house,
and I don't count the broom strokes; I row
up and down for nothing but love: his for me, and my own
for the threshold, as well as for the woman's name
I hear while I sweep, as though she swept
beside me, a woman who, if she owns a face at all,
it is its own changing; and if I know her name
I know to say it so softly she need not
stop her work to hear me.  But when she lies down
at night, in the room of our arrival, she'll know
I called her, though she won't answer, who is on her way
to sleep, until morning, which even now,
is overwhelming, the woman combing her hair opposite
the direction of my departure.
And only now and then do I lean at a jamb
to see'if I can see what I thought I heard.
I heard her ask, My love, why can't you sleep?
and answer, Someone has died, and someone
is not yet born.  Meanwhile, I hear the voices
of women telling a story in the round,
so I sit down on a rain-eaten stoop, by the saltgrasses,
and go on folding the laundry I was folding,
the everyday clothes of our everyday life, the death
clothes wearing us clean to the bone, to the very
ilium crest, where my right hand, this hand, half
crab, part bird, has often come to rest on her,
whose name I know.  And because I sat down,
I hear their folding sound, and know
the tide is rising early, and I can't hope
to trap their story told in the round.  But the woman
whose name I know says, Sleep, so I lie down
on the clothes, the folded and unfolded, the life
and the death.  Ages go by When I wake, the story
has changed the firmament into domain, domain
into a house.  And the sun speaks the day,
unnaming, showing the story, dissipating the boundaries
of the telling, to include the one who has died
and the one not yet born.  Someone has died
and someone is not yet born.  How still
this morning grows about the voice of one
child reading to another, how much a house
is house at all due to one room where an elder
child reads to his brother, and that younger
knows by heart the brother-voice.  How darker
other rooms stand, how slow morning comes, collected
in a name, told at one sill and listened for
at the threshold of dew What book is this we read
together, Brother, and at which window
of our father's house?  In which upper room?
We read it twice: Once in two voices, to each
other; once in unison, to children,
animals, and the sun, our star, that vast office
of love, the one we sit in once, and read
together twice, the third time bosomed in
the future.  So birds may lend their church, sown
in air, realized in the body uttering
windows, growing rafters, couching seeds.

Denbigh, a heritage-listed property situated at 421 The Northern Road in Cobbitty, a suburb of southwestern Sydney within the Camden Council area in New South Wales, Australia, was established in 1818. Originally, it functioned as a vineyard, Clydesdale horse stud, Ayrshire cattle stud, and dairy farm, and later transformed into a Hereford stud. Built by Charles Hook, Thomas and Samual Hassall, and Daniel Roberts, this privately-owned estate was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on December 22, 2006.

Charles Hook, the initial proprietor of Denbigh, acquired the land grant in 1812 after being released from imprisonment due to his support for Governor Bligh's endeavors to manage the military in New South Wales. In his late fifties, Hook obtained the land in the Parish of Cook, which lies between Cowpasture Road and Bringelly Road (now Northern Road) at Cobbitty. While residing at Macquarie Grove nearby, Hook oversaw the construction of his home, Denbigh house, which was completed and saw him commence the process of cultivating the surrounding lands. He passed away in 1826.

½ cup chopped onion
½ cup chopped green bell pepper
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 tablespoon butter
1 teaspoon dried basil
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon dried thyme
½ teaspoon black pepper
½ cup dry white wine
2 cups beef broth
1 link (3½ ounces) sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, browned and crumbled
1/3 cup chopped pitted green olives

Preparation
1. Cook pasta according to package directions.
2. In a large skillet, cook the mushrooms, onion, and green pepper in hot olive oil and butter over medium heat until tender. Add the basil, salt, oregano, thyme, and black pepper. Cook and stir for 1 minute.
3. Stir in wine and simmer for 2 minutes. Add the beef broth and sausage. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
4. Stir in olives. Cook and stir for 1 minute more.
5. Drain pasta. Serve with sausage mixture.

A prominent Japanese businessman, Yoshiaki Tsutsumi, was apprehended on Thursday for allegedly fabricating shareholder records and peddling shares founded on false data. Previously recognized as the world's wealthiest individual, Tsutsumi headed a conglomerate encompassing hotels, railways, infrastructure, and a baseball team. His detention marks another instance of high-ranking executive arrests in Japan due to business misdeeds. The incident unfolded outside one of his Prince hotels in Tokyo, where he was escorted away in a vehicle.

At one point, Tsutsumi appeared invulnerable. In the 1960s, he inherited a substantial real estate business from his father and rose to become one of Japan's formidable industrialists, boasting ties to numerous influential politicians. Through his affluence and sway, he successfully brought the Winter Olympics to Nagano in 1998. However, last year, he was compelled to relinquish all positions within his corporate domain following accusations of manipulating Seibu Railways' ownership structure - one of his corporations - by concealing the true extent of the top 10 shareholders' holdings. According to Japanese securities regulations, no publicly traded firm can exceed an 80% stake by its 10 major investors. Consequently, Tsutsumi now confronts potential criminal prosecution and imprisonment for deceiving the public regarding the actual shareholding proportions. Seibu Railways has since been de-listed, its stock value has cratered, and it stands vulnerable to a buyout attempt.

Tsutsumi's downfall mirrors that of several other senior Japanese executives as law enforcement endeavors to quell the unscrupulous business tactics prevalent in past Japanese firms. His single-minded drive to maintain supremacy may trace back to his youth. Born an illegitimate third son to a prosperous father who amassed his fortune through land acquisitions during post-WWII Japan, Tsutsumi recounted the harsh criticisms from his father in a 1987 weekly publication. "Dining with him was nothing but agony," Tsutsumi admitted. "His reprimands were nothing but torment."

For a long time it was believed that Pirehūrehu (also known as Tūmanako) could lift canoes up into the sky, as he did when he killed his grandfather Āpiro and fled to Uruao in Te Ika-a-Māui - this story does not come down in the oral tradition though [citation needed]. It became very popular later on though after the introduction of Western canoeing technology which allowed much bigger hulls to be easily built at Hastings and Gisborne - these vessels were referred to colloquially as 'piri poutama' or 'piripou'. In actual fact they differed only slightly from whaling boats such as sloops with deep keels being necessary for local conditions so that they would plane off over breaking waves well before reaching shore at speed [2].
Hokianga has always been famous around Te Tai Rawhiti, i.e., east coast North Island New Zealand Maori because it produces very large specimens of pipi, locally called kai moana. A local proverb goes:"Ngati Kuri he tangata o te waka tuna e karakia mai ano ki uta; Ngatitoa he taua o tu ma roro no te whenua". That is: Ngati Kuru are men who raise their dug out canoes right on dry land while the Ngati Toarangatira raised them on rafts close enough to be washed by sea spray! This may seem unbelievable now but during World War II two huge 80 ft. timber clinker dugouts made here ended up travelling all over the Pacific islands including Guadalcanal carrying cargo.
Other examples include the warship Te Watewate, the training ships RA Maui and Mt Cook plus many other coastal yachts and dory workboats all built here even more recently using traditional hand tools. These craft frequently sail into the South Seas in good weather without fuel consumption while also having excellent wave piercing ability combined with seaworthiness for open ocean passage. Japanese electronics giant Hitachi has developed what it says is the world's fastest industrial robot, capable of moving at 10 metres per second (22mph).

The company said its new machine was able to move faster than any other on the market and could be used in factories for tasks such as welding or painting.

It can also handle heavy loads - up to 35kg (77lb) - which means it could be used to lift car parts into place during assembly.

"We believe this will help us win orders," said Yasuhiro Kawamura, head of Hitachi's factory automation division.

He added that the firm had already received several enquiries about the product since announcing it last week.

## Faster robots

Industrial robots are typically used by manufacturers to perform repetitive jobs more quickly and accurately than humans.

They have been around for decades but their speed has increased significantly over time.

In 2014, Japanese firm Fanuc launched an industrial robot called CR-35iA/L that could travel at speeds of up to nine metres per second.

But Hitachi claims its latest model, known as HS16iD/85, is even quicker. It can reach top speeds of 10 metres per second when carrying light objects weighing less than one kilogramme (two pounds), according to the BBC's Tokyo correspondent Rupert Wingfield-Hayes.

However, he adds that the robot slows down considerably if it needs to carry heavier items. For example, it takes just under two seconds to accelerate from zero to five metres per hour while holding something weighing 35kg.

Mr Kawamura told Reuters that the robot would cost between $90,000-$100,000 (£65,000-£72,000). He expects sales to start next year.

A remote-controlled target system that behaves like a moving human-sized target is helping sharpen the marksmanship of soldiers in the British Army.

The £215,000 ($279,000) system, known as i-Fire, has been introduced at the Army's Pirbright training range in Surrey.

It allows soldiers to practice against moving targets from close range, in a safe, virtual battlefield.

The i-Fire system has been introduced as part of a £1.5m investment in the training facility by the Ministry of Defence.

The aim is to ensure the soldiers' marksmanship and battlefield skills are kept up to date.

Mita Taupaki (approximately 1845-1846 – 14 January 1935), a prominent Maori tribal leader in New Zealand, belonged to the Ngati Wahiao hapu (subtribe) of the Tuhourangi iwi from Te Arawa. He was likely born near Lake Rotorua. His father, Hemanathe Whareiro, was a member of Ngati Wahiao, and his mother, Kanea II, was of Tuhourangi and the Ngati Tunohopu hapu of Ngati Whakaue. In 1864, Mita joined other Te Arawa warriors fighting for the government during the 1860s conflicts. He resettled at Whakarewarewa in 1874. In 1883, he advocated for several Ngati Wahiao hapu in the Native Land Court against Ngati Whakaue's claim to land, which included Whakarewarewa, and successfully secured ownership of the land on the eastern side of the Puarenga Stream. This victory granted him prestige not only within Ngati Wahiao but also among the broader Tuhourangi community. The 1886 Mount Tarawera volcanic eruption resulted in significant losses for Tuhourangi, leading survivors to seek shelter with Mita and his people at Whakarewarewa and Ohinemutu. Throughout the 1880s, Mita continued representing Tuhourangi in the Native Land Court, ultimately achieving recognition of their claims to the 211,000-acre Rotomahana–Parekarangi block in 1887. In 1910, he embarked on an Australian, English, and American tour alongside Maggie Papakura's cultural group. He passed away in a Rotorua hospital on 14 January 1935.

Ross Lee McKay (born March 3, 1964) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender who played in one National Hockey League game for the Hartford Whalers during the 1990–91 season. The rest of his career, which lasted from 1988 to 1991, he played in various minor leagues. Career
From 1981 to 1984 McKay played major junior hockey for the Calgary Wranglers of the Western Hockey League. He then played for the University of Saskatchewan for four years before signing a professional contract with National Hockey League team the Hartford Whalers in 1988. He split the following two season between the Indianapolis Ice of the IHL, the Knoxville Cherokees of the ECHL and the Binghamton Whalers of the AHL. During the 1990-91 season McKay made his NHL debut, playing 35 minutes of relief against the Buffalo Sabres and he helped the Whalers AHL affiliate the Springfield Falcons win the Calder Cup.

Computer giant Microsoft has launched a pilot scheme to replace counterfeit versions of Windows XP with legal ones.
The first-time initiative is restricted to the UK and to users with pre-installed copies of the operating system in PCs bought before November. Until December Microsoft said software can be sent to it for analysis if there are doubts about its legitimacy. The company aims to detect illegal traders and turn users of fake versions of Windows into legitimate ones.
The Windows XP Counterfeit Project will mean that software that is found to be counterfeit will be replaced for free, subject to certain conditions, until the end of the year. It is the first time Microsoft has launched a counterfeit product replacement scheme in the world, the company told the BBC News website. In June, the software giant said that the major security update to Windows XP, Service Pack 2, would not work with the most widely pirated versions of its operating system. The upgrade closed security loopholes in XP and added features that made it easier to keep machines safe from viruses and other types of malicious computer code.
The US company invited anyone who had suspicions about their version of Windows XP to submit it for testing as soon as possible. The procedure consists of a series of computer checks, collating documents, and filling out a witness statement. "This is a great opportunity for users to confirm the authenticity of Windows XP software whilst helping gather vital information about illegal traders", said Alex Hilton, licence compliance manager at Microsoft. The scheme has also been welcomed by the technology and commerce industry. "It is important that users ensure that they are legally licensed to avoid the risks of purchasing and using counterfeit products", said David Frost, director general of the British Chambers of Commerce. The plan would enable Microsoft to gather intelligence about illegal traders in a prompt way, which would allow it to take action against software pirates. Microsoft said it would evaluate the results of the UK programme before setting up similar schemes in other countries.

Normally, supervised semantic segmentation assumes that test data aligns with the training data's data domain. Yet, domain disparities between training and unseen data can result in substantial performance decline. Labeling pixels accurately for images in distinct domains is time-consuming and demanding, particularly for histopathology images. In this study, we suggest a dual adaptive pyramid network (DAPNet) for histopathological gland segmentation, enabling adaptation from one stain domain to another. We handle domain adaptation at two levels: 1) the image level deals with color and style discrepancies; 2) the feature level tackles spatial inconsistencies between domains. Both components are designed as domain classifiers utilizing adversarial training. Our method's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments and an ablation study using two gland segmentation datasets featuring H&E and DAB-H stains. Results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms other leading methods in domain adaptive segmentation tasks.

Unsupervised deep learning methods often face the challenge of insufficient labeled data in medical image segmentation, which can be expensive and time-consuming to acquire. In this study, we introduce an uncertainty-guided semi-supervised learning method based on a student-teacher approach. This technique enables effective use of minimal labeled samples and an extensive collection of unlabeled images for training a segmentation network. Initially, a teacher segmentation model is developed utilizing Bayesian deep learning from the available labeled data. Subsequently, this trained model generates soft segmentation labels and corresponding uncertainty maps for the unlabeled dataset. Next, the student model undergoes updates via the softly labeled samples and the estimated segmentation reliability derived from the teacher model's uncertainty through a novel loss function. Our experimental findings from a retinal layer segmentation task indicate that our suggested method surpasses the fully supervised approach and matches the level of expertise provided by human annotators. The presented semi-supervised segmentation framework is a significant contribution, as it holds applicability for biomedical image segmentation across diverse imaging modalities where obtaining annotated medical images proves difficult.

Deep learning has seen significant achievements in the realm of powerful classification and made strides in semantic segmentation. Several researchers hold the view that deep learning is the leading method for pixel-precise image segmentation. However, can deep learning match the pixel-level precision of conventional image segmentation techniques through transforming object features into a non-linear function? This paper provides an overview of the accuracy levels attained by deep learning in image classification and segmentation to date. In contrast to the impressive classification accuracies of deep learning in international vision contests, its segmentation accuracies in the same events lag behind by approximately 20 percentage points. Conversely, segmentation accuracies in international biomedical challenges approach ninety-five percent. What accounts for such a substantial disparity? Given that competitor methods' accuracies are assessed solely based on their reported outcomes rather than by reproducing results via code or software submission, are these achievements valid or inflated? To shed light on this question, we will scrutinize the underlying mechanisms of deep learning. Ultimately, we compared the performance of cutting-edge deep learning approaches against a threshold selection method numerically. Our findings revealed that the threshold selection method surpassed deep learning methods in terms of accuracy for image segmentation.

3/4 cups Unsalted Butter, Room Temperature
1/2 cups Granulated Sugar
1/2 cups Dark Brown Sugar (packed)
1/4 cups Unsulphured Molasses
1 whole Large Egg
1/2 teaspoons Pure Vanilla Extract
2 cups Unbleached All-purpose Flour
1/2 teaspoons Baking Soda
1/4 teaspoons Salt
1-1/2 teaspoon Ground Cinnamon
2 teaspoons Ground Ginger
1/2 teaspoons Ground Cloves
1 cup Granulated Sugar, For Rolling
In a large mixing bowl combine the butter and sugars until light and fluffy. Add the molasses, egg and vanilla. Gently mix until incorporated. In a separate medium size mixing bowl whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt and spices. Slowly add the flour mixture to the creamed butter and sugar and mix until incorporated. For a crisper cookie, bake a minute or two longer. When done, remove the pans from the oven and let the cookies sit for on the pan for a couple minutes. Then remove them from the pans to cool completely on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container. Makes about 4 dozen cookies. (Recipe adapted from a recipe on Joy of Baking.)

To My Dear Sister Mrs. C. P. On Her Nuptial

Why do you, my dear Sister, now disclose
A bosom where all softly bowed before?
Why doth your cheek with gladness overflow,
And raise a glance too gay for woe?

'Tis Nature, stern mistress of our fate,
Commands the heart to love, and stamps it true:
With thrills of sweet emotion you are moved,
And must obey her mighty law.

In vain you offer to my searching eye
Your placid brow and cheek of roseate hue;
In vain you seek to still my anxious fear,
And whisper of a joy too great to bear.

I see you tremble; I behold your heart
 tumultuously beating as you start;
And through a sea of troubled emotions wide
I see love dawning in your timid eye.

You are about to be united in ties
Of holy wedlock, close and indissoluble;
And with a breast brimming with anguish deep
I see you leaving sisterly love's sunny steep.

Oh, do not fancy that I question thy choice,
Or that I doubt the worth of the one thou didst choose;
I but behold in thee a woman thro' and thro',
And own thee trembling, trembling at love's pow'r.

In the calm strength of that eternal love
I see thee standing, none may overthrow;
Nor evil tongue his subtle venom spray
On thee, dear sister, as thou wilt pass away.

I kiss thee as thou layest trembling there,
And bless thy choice, as I bid thee farewell;
And when in after time thou resemblest me
Call up a smile, thinking of thy sister.

Using elastic collisions, the linear momentum of a swift neutron can be determined from as few as two sequential recoil ion trails and the location of the third impact point. In some cases, the interval between the initial two sequential ion trails can be quantified, allowing for a reduction in the number of ion trails needed to just one and a half. The precision of the angle and magnitude measurements is restricted by ion range dispersion to roughly ten percent. For tracking fast neutrons, multi-wire proportional counters and light-field imaging are suggested. A single-charge or single-photon identification capability is essential in both methods. While light-field imaging does not encounter charge diffusion-induced image smear, the scarcity of available photons may pose difficulties. $^1$H, $^2$H, and $^3$He can potentially serve as the foundation for developing fast neutron trackers using light-field imaging.

Religions are expressions of the human spirit. they encapsulate our waking consciousness and subconscious thoughts, emotions, instincts, and natural gestures into a single cohesive entity: a poetic manifestation. Nothing holds significance until it is brought to life through language, and what exists solely in words is devoid of truth. A poem, in comparison to a formalized religion, may resemble a transient moment of connection between two individuals, yet a full-fledged religion is the grand poem that endures through loving repetition. Like a poem, it must be infinite and comprehensive, offering moments of introspection where we question the reasoning behind the poet's choices. As Huckleberry Finn once stated, "You can't fake a prayer"; similarly, you cannot fabricate a genuine poem. This mirror reflects our deepest thoughts and emotions, and we refer to it as poetry when it is mobile and elusive, and as a religion when it is fixed and central. The essence of deity resides within this reflection, not as a prisoner but as an allure that draws us in, existing in the world just as poetry is embedded within the fabric of a poem, defying the possibility of closure. Religion will persist as long as there is poetry or a void of it, much like the behavior of birds - such as the crested pigeon and rosella parrot - that fly with closed wings, then fluttering and open again.
