Former Japanese football player and presently the head coach of Tochigi SC, Tokisaki, was born in Fukushima on June 15, 1979. Following his high school graduation, he entered J1 League team Bellmare Hiratsuka (previously Shonan Bellmare) in 1998. He remained benched throughout his first year, and the team descended to J2 League in 2000. In 2000, Tokisaki made his debut as a center back and featured frequently in matches. Despite limited playing time in 2001, he continued to play consistently from 2002 through 2003. In addition to center back, he also took on the role of side back in 2002. However, his participation declined significantly from 2004. In June 2005, he transferred to J2 club Mito HollyHock, where he saw limited action as a center back in 2005. Starting in 2006, he rejoined his local club, FC Pelada Fukushima (later renamed Fukushima United FC), in the Regional Leagues. His sibling Rui Tokisaki was a teammate from 2007 until their retirement in 2011. Tokisaki's performances were frequent until 2009. He sat out entirely during the 2010 season and concluded his playing career by the end of 2011.

Hailing from the animation house that brought us such jems as Morph, the Wallace and Gromit series and Rex the Runt, Chicken Run is the first ever feature length claymation ever attempted.

Set on a chicken farm in Yorkshire some time in the middle of the century, our plucky (sorry) heroines face a lifetime of hard labor laying for the farmers, and if their performance is not up to par they quite literally face the chop. Ginger, making her way to the top of the pecking order (sorry again) attempts jailbreak after farcical jailbreak, but success is less than forthcoming.

Enter Rocky The Rhode Island Red, (Rocky Rhodes for short, and you can't blame me for that one, the writers came up with it) apparently able to fly, the chickens look to him to help them bust this chicken coup, but Rocky is not what he may appear to be.

That's the plot in a nut (egg?) shell, and as you can imagine the subject matter made for perfect "salutes" to the classic world war 2 escape movies, references to which abound throughout. From Ginger tossing a baseball (actually a sprout) in the "cooler" (coal bunker), to Fowler's incessant ramblings about his old RAF days.

The lead characters are deep and endearing enough for you to care about what happens to them, if a little stereotypical at times. The interaction between them is fluid and believable, all the more amazing considering that Mel Gibson never even set foot in the same recording studio as the other actors, reading his lines in a studio in America instead. The supporting cast provide plenty of humour and Mrs. Tweedy substitutes quite nicely for the Nazi camp commandant.

The animation is lively and colourful the characters wonderfully expressive in that unmistakable style developed in the Wallace and Gromit shorts, and thanks to the fact the sets are real models there is plenty of scope for dramatic lighting effects.

The only real fault I could find in the film was that it just seemed a little too... American at times. Hollywood's involvement showed through the English setting to some degree, especially as you get to the movie's climax which seems to go a bit overboard, especially compared to the utterly hysterical ending to The Wrong Trousers. But all in all I have to say I really enjoyed this movie. Now all we need is a Wallace and Gromit movie.

In recent developments, impressive achievements have been made in semantic segmentation through the application of fully convolutional networks (FCNs). The majority of these networks utilize encoder-decoder architecture akin to U-Net, training on images and their corresponding segmentation masks via pixel-wise classification. Our proposed framework, presented in this paper, seeks to leverage both structural and spatial information, in addition to class information. By modifying the decoder component of the FCN, we aim to simultaneously extract class and structural data. This objective is pursued while maintaining a minimal parameter count. We derive structural information through one of two methods: i) utilizing contour maps or ii) employing distance maps, which can be derived from ground truth segmentation maps without extra labeling expenses. Additionally, we investigate various techniques for generating distance maps and evaluate their influence on segmentation accuracy. Experiments are conducted on two distinct medical image segmentation applications: i) optic disc and cup segmentation using color fundus images and ii) polyp segmentation utilizing endoscopic images. Our findings reveal outcomes that rival, and even surpass, existing state-of-the-art models, while reducing the parameter count by roughly a factor of 2.

"Background subtraction" is an old technique for finding moving objects in a
video sequence for example, cars driving on a freeway. The idea is that
subtracting the current image from a timeaveraged background image will leave
only nonstationary objects. It is, however, a crude approximation to the task
of classifying each pixel of the current image; it fails with slow-moving
objects and does not distinguish shadows from moving objects. The basic idea of
this paper is that we can classify each pixel using a model of how that pixel
looks when it is part of different classes. We learn a mixture-of-Gaussians
classification model for each pixel using an unsupervised technique- an
efficient, incremental version of EM. Unlike the standard image-averaging
approach, this automatically updates the mixture component for each class
according to likelihood of membership; hence slow-moving objects are handled
perfectly. Our approach also identifies and eliminates shadows much more
effectively than other techniques such as thresholding. Application of this
method as part of the Roadwatch traffic surveillance project is expected to
result in significant improvements in vehicle identification and tracking.

Kazuya is a fascinating character, and I'll tell you why. Firstly, his design is incredibly well-done. His appearance, with the red hair and the mole under his eye, is instantly recognizable and memorable. His character arc, from a naive and entitled rich kid to a vengeful and power-hungry individual, is also well-executed.

One of the things that sets Kazuya apart from other characters is his unapologetic and unwavering ambition. He knows what he wants, and he's willing to do whatever it takes to get it, even if it means hurting others or sacrificing his own relationships. This makes him both a compelling and a frustrating character to watch, as you're never quite sure what he'll do next.

Another aspect of Kazuya's character that I appreciate is the way he challenges the traditional hero/villain dynamic. He's certainly not a hero, but he's not necessarily a villain either. He exists in a gray area, and his motivations and actions are often understandable, even if they're not always admirable. This complexity makes him a refreshing change from the usual black-and-white characterizations found in many stories.

Overall, I think Kazuya is a well-written and engaging character, and I'm looking forward to seeing how his character develops in the future. How about you? What are your thoughts on Kazuya as a character? Do you love him, hate him, or something in between? Let me know in the comments!

Unsalted butter (140g), combined with 135g sugar, 2 eggs, 150g flour, 60g ground almonds, and 1 teaspoon cinnamon; blend using an electric mixer until resembling breadcrumbs. Quickly form a dough ball, adding minimal water if necessary to bind. Refrigerate wrapped in plastic for 2 hours. Cook 5 pears, peeled, cored, and sliced, with 50ml wine or port and 3 star anise in a pan, covered, for around 10 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Mix 60g butter, 60g sugar, remaining egg, 1 tsp flour, cinnamon, and 150g almonds for frangipane; chill. Preheat oven to 160°Celsius. On a floured surface, roll pastry and transfer to buttered tartlet cases. Spread frangipane generously over pastry. Slice each pear half into fan shapes, arrange on top of dough. Bake for 25 minutes or until golden.

R&B star Alicia Keys is to open February's Super Bowl singing a song only previously performed there by Ray Charles and Vicki Carr.
Keys, who will sing America the Beautiful, will be accompanied by 150 students from the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind. Charles, who died last year, attended the school as a child in 1937. Keys said she was "very excited", describing Charles as "an artist I admire, miss and respect". "I know that this is going to be a very touching and memorable moment," she said.
It will be her first performance at the Super Bowl, which will be watched by millions in the US on 6 February. Sir Paul McCartney will provide the half-time entertainment in the slot filled by Janet Jackson last year. Organisers have promised there will be no repeat of her nipple-baring incident that sparked thousands of complaints on US TV's most-watched broadcast. A National Football League spokesman said they were "comfortable" this show would be acceptable to a mass audience. The game and show were watched by 144 million people in the US in 2003.
Twenty CBS-owned TV stations were fined $550,000 (£300,000) by the country's TV regulatory agency after more than 542,000 complaints were made about Janet Jackson's "wardrobe malfunction". Sir Paul said: "There's nothing bigger than being asked to perform at the Super Bowl. "We're looking forward to rocking the millions at home and in the stadium."

Captain Jonathan Archer and the Starship Enterprise team encounter an enigmatic extraterrestrial craft operated by the Antianna race, obstructing their advance. Unable to decode the alien ship's signals and hesitant to engage in combat, Enterprise alters its trajectory. Soon afterward, they enter the domain of the Thelasian Trading Confederacy, which has previously interacted with the Antianna. The Thelasian governor, Maxim Sen, is presently orchestrating a conflict against the Antianna to safeguard the Confederacy's commercial routes. Archer harbors doubts about Sen's true intentions and believes the Antianna's aggressive behavior conceals hidden reasons. However, with multiple races in the sector gearing up against him, Archer requires solid evidence rather than mere speculation. One individual possesses this information: Ensign Hoshi Sato. Her ability to decipher the Antianna language could pave the way for peace. Conversely, if she fails, a catastrophic intersector war looms on the horizon.

In the beginning of the narrative, fifteen-year-old Lia sits by her great-grandmother Sarah's dying bed. Before passing, Sarah recounts tales of Graymoss Plantation, the abandoned Louisiana ancestral home shunned due to an alleged "awful, terrifying evil." Following Sarah's demise, Lia uncovers that the property has been bequeathed to her mother, who intends to relocate the family there and welcome a troupe of difficult-to-place kids. Lia disapproves and sets out to verify that the dwelling is genuinely haunted. Documented accounts reveal numerous spectral manifestations, and local opposition to the family settling at Graymoss heightens. Might one of these individuals be fabricating the hauntings? Yet, Lia experiences a transformation upon encountering the kids her parents wish to foster, deciding instead to confront the specters herself. With a compilation of Edgar Allan Poe's tales as her guide, she ultimately triumphs in banishing the spirits. These phantoms mirror those in Shirley Jackson's renowned The Haunting of Hill House, communicating through the structures and hurling books through the atmosphere. The story concludes unexpectedly, and an intriguing romantic subplot evaporates entirely; nonetheless, it remains an engrossing read for enthusiasts of mysteries and ghost stories.

THE AUTHOR OF THIS NOVEL, MARK FRANCIS, HAS DEALT WITH A LOT OF CONVERSATIONS ABOUT HOW BEST TO DESCRIBE HIS SIDE of the argument about how to understand reality (or to describe it accurately) and has chosen this very approach. He describes the various categories of arguments in short descriptions that he believes are essential parts of explaining things so that we can make accurate statements about them. These include "objective description", "subjective description", "conceptual analysis", and the like.

He writes:

Objectivity is first and foremost not having an opinion as to what is real, or whether things exist in any particular sense. Realizing that you have an answer, whether the truth, or anything else really matters doesn't mean you've understood it, only that your answer isn't made up by yourself—that others might draw upon the concepts you discuss. Thus, I argue that Objectivity involves not just knowing that the world exists but also knowing exactly why those who live in that world exist.


As with all art there must be subjectivity. There may well indeed be questions about objective vs subjective. So far, however, I am uninterested in these question because they seem likely to become confused by another idea which seems to me incontrovertibly true if I were ever granted access to the information necessary to formulate a definitive answer: Subjectivity doesn't involve merely being aware of what's going on; you're also aware of where things come from and how things work as a whole. For example, do people know the size of their own hands? How many apples are at your table today while you eat yours and read some more paragraphs of material on my page? Of course, most people think things happen by luck, and therefore don't mind being in an environment where someone else has worked very hard to get something just handed to them! The same may be said for many other mundane phenomena. But we still say things along what seems pretty much reasonable lines when our lives look like an accident rather than something planned. [1]

In his attempt to explain reality, Francis often uses vague analogies or metaphors, suggesting that he simply trusts his readers to come up with ways of understanding and comparing facts without recourse to words such as "right", "good", and "bad". Though somewhat naive and simplistic, these attempts

I
In days when men had joy of war,
A God of Battles sped each mortal jar;
The peoples pledged him heart and hand,
From Israel's land to isles afar.
II
His crimson form, with clang and chime,
Flashed on each murk and murderous meeting-time,
And kings invoked, for rape and raid,
His fearsome aid in rune and rhyme.
III
On bruise and blood-hole, scar and seam,
On blade and bolt, he flung his fulgid beam:
His haloes rayed the very gore,
And corpses wore his glory-gleam.
IV
Often an early King or Queen,
And storied hero onward, knew his sheen;
'Twas glimpsed by Wolfe, by Ney anon,
And Nelson on his blue demesne.
V
But new light spread. That god's gold nimb
And blazon have waned dimmer and more dim;
Even his flushed form begins to fade,
Till but a shade is left of him.
VI
That modern meditation broke
His spell, that penmen's pleadings dealt a stroke,
Say some; and some that crimes too dire
Did much to mire his crimson cloak.
VII
Yea, seeds of crescive sympathy
Were sown by those more excellent than he,
Long known, though long contemned till then -
The gods of men in amity.
VIII
Souls have grown seers, and thought out-brings
The mournful many-sidedness of things
With foes as friends, enfeebling ires
And fury-fires by gaingivings!
IX
He scarce impassions champions now;
They do and dare, but tensely--pale of brow;
And would they fain uplift the arm
Of that faint form they know not how.
X
Yet wars arise, though zest grows cold;
Wherefore, at whiles, as 'twere in ancient mould
He looms, bepatched with paint and lath;
But never hath he seemed the old!
XI
Let men rejoice, let men deplore.
The lurid Deity of heretofore
Succumbs to one of saner nod;
The Battle-god is god no more.

The standard model of particle physics has been highly successful explaining most of the phenomena we see in nature, however it is not complete. It cannot explain phenomena such as the baryon asymmetry of the universe, the nature of dark matter and energy, and the existence of a gravitational force. This paper discusses some of the ways in which physics beyond the standard model could address these mysteries. 

One way is to introduce new particles and interactions that are not present in the standard model. These could include new heavy particles that interact with the standard model particles through weak or electromagnetic forces, or new light particles that interact with the standard model particles through gravitational forces. Another way is to modify the standard model particles and interactions. This could include changing the way the particles interact with each other, or adding new forces to the model.

This paper focuses on one particular beyond the standard model scenario, where a new scalar field is added to the theory. This field could explain the dark matter and energy in the universe, and also have other interesting implications for particle physics and cosmology. In particular, we discuss how the scalar field could affect the primordial helium abundance in the universe, and how this could be tested by future experiments.

Re-using old mobile phones is not just good for the environment, it has social benefits too.
Research has found that in some developing nations old mobile phones can help close the digital divide. The Forum for the Future research found that the low cost of these recycled handsets means they can have a very useful second life in poorer nations. But the Forum found that more needed to be done to collect old phones rather than let them rot in landfill sites.
The report reveals that approximately 15 million mobile phones go out of use every year in the UK. Of the 15 million that are swapped for newer models each year, only 25% get returned to mobile phone firms for recycling or re-use. The slowly growing mass of unrecycled, discarded phones has now reached 90 million handsets, the equivalent of 9,000 tonnes of waste, estimates James Goodman, report author and a senior adviser at the Forum for the Future. "It's quite common for people to have two or three phones just lying around," said Mr Goodman.
Many of these older phones could end up in landfill sites leaking the potentially toxic materials they are made of into the wider world, said Mr Goodman. Far better, he said, to hand the phone back to an operator who can send it overseas where it can enjoy a second lease of life. "We've heard the environmental argument for handing a phone back," said Mr Goodman, "but there's a strong social argument too." Older mobile phones are proving particularly useful in poorer nations where people want to use a mobile and keep in touch with friends and family but do not have the income to buy the most up to date model. The Forum for the Future report took an in-depth look at Romania where reconditioned mobile phones were proving very popular. "It's an interesting country because it has a really crap fixed line network," said Mr Goodman, "and there's a real desire for people to get mobile phones." But the relatively low wages in Romania, which is one of the poorest countries in Europe, mean few people can afford a shiny new phone. "The affordability of the handsets is a real barrier to getting one," he said. Reconditioned handsets have boosted take-up of mobiles as the report revealed that almost one-third of Romanian pre-pay mobile phone users were using reconditioned handsets. The re-used handsets tend to be about one-third of the price of a new handset. Georgeta Minciu, a Romanian part-time cleaner, said: "Normally a mobile phone would not be possible on my wages. Planned government measures include stricter regulations on economic migrants and reinforced border surveillance, to be announced on Monday. Home Secretary Charles Clarke intends to implement a points system for economic migrants and escalate the removal of unsuccessful asylum seekers. Prime Minister Tony Blair acknowledged public apprehensions regarding system manipulation but maintained there is no definitive solution. The Conservatives criticize Labour for delaying actions, whereas the Liberal Democrats question the efficiency of the proposed methods.

The upcoming five-year government plan aims to demonstrate Labour's approach to immigration and asylum control reforms should they secure the May election victory. Ministers refute allegations of being influenced by Tory campaigns or the prime minister's concerns over insufficient action. Instead, they assert these steps are part of an ongoing effort to rebuild public trust.

Mr. Clarke is anticipated to abolish the automatic settlement right for immigrant families and enforce biometric identification for all visa candidates. The prime minister stated that immigration criteria would be strengthened to admit only those immigrants whose abilities align with the UK's genuine requirements. He dismissed the Tories' suggestion of a numerical limit on economic migrants, expressing doubt that a fixed figure could accurately represent the nation's demands.

Mr. Blair spoke to BBC Radio 4's Westminster Hour, stating, "We must decrease the number or increase it based on the country's requirements..." He addressed public anxieties over immigration and asylum system misuse, acknowledging valid concerns. However, he defended the existing regime, highlighting global prevalence of systemic abuses. Mr. Blair argued against Tory suggestions to restrict asylum seeker numbers and process applications overseas, stating, "We will not... pretend there is a straightforward, effortless means to process the UK's asylum seekers in another country, because no such country exists." Conservative shadow home secretary David Davis echoed similar sentiments.

Northern Ireland man James McIlroy is confident he can win his first major title at this weekend's Spar European Indoor Championships in Madrid.
The 28-year-old has been in great form in recent weeks and will go in as one of the 800 metres favourites. "I believe after my wins abroad and in our trial race in Sheffield, I can run my race from the front, back or middle," said McIlroy. New coach Tony Lester has helped get McIlroy's career back on track. The 28-year-old 800 metres runner has not always matched his promise with performances but believes his decision to change coaches and move base will bring the rewards. McIlroy now lives in Windsor and feels his career has been transformed by the no-nonsense leadership style of former Army sergeant Lester. Lester is better known for his work with 400m runners Roger Black and Mark Richardson in the past but under his guidance McIlroy has secured five wins this indoor season.
McIlroy now claims he is in his best shape since finishing fourth for Ireland at the outdoor European Championships in 1998. "That was my last decent year," said McIlroy, who temporarily retired last August before returning to the sport under Lester's shrewd guidance. "Before, every race was like trying to climb Mount Everest and I now know you can't do it on your own. "Trying to succeed saw me sometimes standing half-dead and terrified on the starting line, which became a bit too much." McIlroy, who was compared to the likes of Sebastian Coe, Steve Cram and Steve Ovett in his younger days, is now competing without the benefit of National Lottery funding. That situation could change if he maintains his current form and repeats the world-class times he produced in the 800m and 1000m at major races in Erfurt and Stuttgart earlier this season. Russian Dmitriy Bogdanov won at the same Madrid venue last week and then claimed the European Championship race would be between himself, Dutchman Arnoud Okken and Antonio Reina of Spain but McIlroy is unfazed.
He admitted: "He looked quite good in his win and fair enough everyone has the right to their own opinion. "I never write myself off and let's face it, I haven't or looked like being beaten this season." And McIlroy, whose time of one minute 46.68seconds in Erfurt elevated him to sixth place on the UK All-Time list, is also already looking beyond Madrid. He said: "I've been much more focused this year about my career and having such a good team around me has been very important. "Ultimately of course, this weekend is a means to an end and that is getting prepared for the summer's world championships. "That ambition has meant that I've had only two nights out since last August. The rest of my time has seen me just concentrating on rebuilding my career."

Electronic Arts (EA), the leading US video game company, aims to surpass entertainment giants like Disney by broadening its appeal to mainstream audiences. With blockbuster titles such as Fifa, John Madden, and licensed movie adaptations including Harry Potter and James Bond, EA generated $3bn (£1.65bn) in revenue in 2004, targeting a doubling by 2009. As the largest games publisher worldwide, EA boasted 27 top-selling titles exceeding one million copies each, accounting for nine of the UK's top 20 bestsellers in 2004.

Gerhard Florin, EA's European publishing managing director, envisioned expanding beyond current boundaries. While challenging Disney's $30bn (£16bn) revenue from 2004 might take decades, he maintained it as a long-term objective. Florin anticipated future consoles, such as PS3 and Xbox 2, offering developers the capability to evoke genuine emotions through advanced graphics. "Emotion isn't solely defined by polygon counts; it's about intricacies like facial expressions," he explained.

Florin projected that more than half of EA's sales went to adult consumers. However, he acknowledged the common misconception that gaming is merely for children. "Our mission is to make emotionally engaging games accessible to everyone," he emphasized. In 2004, the video game industry surpassed the music industry in size, according to EA. "People no longer queue for music releases," Florin stated, adding, "However, the frenzy surrounding midnight launches for titles like Grand Theft Auto underscores the industry's significant impact."

Many recent medical segmentation systems rely on powerful deep learning
models to solve highly specific tasks. To maximize performance, it is standard
practice to evaluate numerous pipelines with varying model topologies,
optimization parameters, pre- & postprocessing steps, and even model cascades.
It is often not clear how the resulting pipeline transfers to different tasks.
We propose a simple and thoroughly evaluated deep learning framework for
segmentation of arbitrary medical image volumes. The system requires no
task-specific information, no human interaction and is based on a fixed model
topology and a fixed hyperparameter set, eliminating the process of model
selection and its inherent tendency to cause method-level over-fitting. The
system is available in open source and does not require deep learning expertise
to use. Without task-specific modifications, the system performed better than
or similar to highly specialized deep learning methods across 3 separate
segmentation tasks. In addition, it ranked 5-th and 6-th in the first and
second round of the 2018 Medical Segmentation Decathlon comprising another 10
tasks. The system relies on multi-planar data augmentation which facilitates
the application of a single 2D architecture based on the familiar U-Net.
Multi-planar training combines the parameter efficiency of a 2D fully
convolutional neural network with a systematic train- and test-time
augmentation scheme, which allows the 2D model to learn a representation of the
3D image volume that fosters generalization.

Clark Field, named after World War I pilot and Medal of Honor winner1 Marshal Cyrus Clark, was an American military installation located in Angeles, Pampanga, Philippines. Clark Air Base was the headquarters of the United States Army Forces in the Far East(USAFFE) and the United States Fifth Air Force during World War II, serving as a vital hub of air and ground activity in the defense of the Philippine Islands against invading Japanese forces. The base was closed following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease in 1991.

The base was captured by the Japanese on December 8, 1941, following the Japanese bombing of Pearl Harbor and the simultaneous attacks on Clark Field and several other American military installations in the Philippines. The United States bases in the Philippines were subject to Japanese attack as part of the Japanese plan for the conquest of Southeast Asia, which also involved attacks on the British possessions of Malaya, Singapore, and Hong Kong.

The Japanse forces began their offensive in the Philippines with an air raid on Clark Field on December 8, which destroyed over half of the American fighter planes stationed there. The base was subsequently captured by ground troops, and the American forces in the Philippines were forced to retreat to the Bataan Peninsula. Clark Field remained in Japanese hands until 1945, when it was recaptured by American forces during the Battle of Luzon.

Following the end of World War II, Clark Field was used by the United States Air Force (USAF) as a base for occupation forces in the Philippines. The base was gradually expanded, and in 1950, it became the headquarters for the Far East Air Forces (FEAF). The base continued to serve as a support facility for US military operations in Southeast Asia during the Vietnam War, and was the launch site for B-52 bombers that conducted airstrikes against targets in Vietnam.

The base was closed by theUS government in 1991, following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease. The base has since been redeveloped as Clark Freeport Zone, a special economic zone administered by the Philippine government.

We present an experimental demonstration that measurement-device independent (MDI) quantum key distribution (QKD) can be achieved using a modified coherent state, which we call the "coherent-state-modified-coherence". We demonstrate this by measuring the entanglement between two entangled photons in a single photon detector and then performing a QKD protocol on the measured data. The MDI protocol uses only one device to perform the QKD protocol, while the original coherent-state-modified-coherence requires two devices. This allows us to achieve a large number of qubits per device, as well as a high degree of control over the parameters of the protocol. Our results show that our method has the potential to enable a wide range of new applications such as secure communication protocols, quantum cryptography, and quantum computation.

The BAFTA-winning ShortStaters scheme is now open for entries from 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK.

Lee said the scheme was "disturbing" as young filmmakers were being given an opportunity "to actually do what you dream about".

The submission phase opened on Monday and runs until 17 January.

ShortStaters is aimed at finding the next generation of talented filmmakers from all corners of the UK and is open to anyone aged 18 to 24 who thinks they have what it takes to make a short film.

Entrants do not need any professional experience but will need to demonstrate a passion for film and storytelling, as well as a creative idea for a short film.

Out of all the entrants, a shortlisted 30 will be given the chance to develop their short film ideas with the help of top industry mentors, with three final films being produced with the support of Lee and BBC Studios.

The three winners will then receive their premieres at an exclusive BBC event, and the short films will be broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer.

Utilizing FCNs with integrated multi-scale characteristics has been crucial for attaining top-tier results in semantic image segmentation. A frequent approach to extracting multi-scale features involves submitting multiple resized input images to a single deep network and combining the generated features for per-pixel categorization. In this study, we suggest an attention mechanism that adapts to softly assign weights to multi-scale features at individual pixel locations. By collaboratively training a leading semantic image segmentation model with multi-scale input images and the proposed attention model, we achieve superior performance compared to average- and max-pooling techniques. Additionally, we verify the necessity of additional supervision at every scale for optimal feature merging outcomes. Our method's efficacy is confirmed through comprehensive experiments on three demanding datasets: PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012, and a section of MS-COCO 2014.

Paolo Radaelli (born 14 December 1977) is an Italian former soccer midfielder and current football manager. He last coached Lecce, leaving in January 2016 to take charge at Serie A club Parma who were relegated at the end of the season before retiring from this role on 23 February 2017 to be replaced with Domenico Giampaolo for their promotion back into top-flight football.

As a player, Radaelli began his career with Bologna and played throughout Italy including in Turin where he helped Inter win four consecutive scudettos between 1999 and 2003 under head coach Maurizio Sarri. In 2005 he joined Juventus but had an injury that halted his stay there after just one year, during which time he completed only two full games. Afterwards he had spells at Fiorentina and Udinese, ending up at Milan the following season alongside Gianluca Caligara and Ronaldinho as they finished fifth place in Serie A.

In 2008 he moved to Lazio where he went onto spend seven seasons and became a squad regular. On the final day of the winter transfer window on 5 March 2014, it was announced Radaelli would move abroad signing until June 30th later that year becoming a free agent once again when his contract expired, although he stayed in Italy joining Atalanta but immediately rescinded his deal soon after due to off field issues. The same summer, he signed with Siena based on a mutual consent agreement. On 3 November 2015, Radaelli left the club by mutual agreement until the end of the season citing family reasons. Later that month he took his first steps as a coach replacing Giovanni De Cagno at Calcio Foggia 1908 on 13 November. However, three days later after not being able to attend training sessions due to ongoing issues relating to his wife's illness, Radaelli stepped down from his post. As of July 2016 he serves as a football journalist working for Sky Italia in addition holding coaching classes with children suffering from cancer through charity organisation Carioca

Lately, I underwent a colonoscopy because of persistent lower abdominal discomfort and trace amounts of blood in my stools for several weeks. Colonoscopy findings revealed no polyps, tumors, merely hemorrhoids within the colon, and inflammation in the rectal region. Two weeks post-procedure, I was informed of potential ulcerative colitis based on the biopsy results. However, I've experienced no bleeding since then, nor did I suffer from diarrhea prior or subsequent to the procedure. My primary concern remains constipation, which I alleviate through Metamucil and coffee consumption in the mornings. Fortunately, I managed to ease the pain with medication. Yet, I can't shake off the feeling that there's more to it, as I've come across numerous accounts of patients grappling with Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBD) characterized by diarrhea and constant symptoms. I warmly welcome any additional insights or expertise from those knowledgeable in this field. For those dealing with IBD, let us unite, support each other, and raise awareness, as many remain oblivious to the challenges we face.

This paper proposes a novel deep neural architecture for extracting text from high entropy images. The proposed architecture combines the semi-bagging technique with deep learning to improve the accuracy and robustness of text extraction. These networks are then combined to make predictions on new images. Continuous-variable (CV) quantum information is the area of quantum information science that makes use of physical observables, like the strength of an electromagnetic field, whose numerical values belong to continuous intervals. One primary application is quantum computing. In a sense, continuous-variable quantum computation is "analog", while quantum computation using qubits is "digital." In more technical terms, the former makes use of Hilbert spaces that are infinite-dimensional, while the Hilbert spaces for systems comprising collections of qubits are finite-dimensional. One motivation for studying continuous-variable quantum computation is to understand what resources are necessary to make quantum computers more powerful than classical ones. Implementation 
One approach to implementing continuous-variable quantum information protocols in the laboratory is through the techniques of quantum optics. By modeling each mode of the electromagnetic field as a quantum harmonic oscillator with its associated creation and annihilation operators, one defines a canonically conjugate pair of variables for each mode, the so-called "quadratures", which play the role of position and momentum observables. These observables establish a phase space on which Wigner quasiprobability distributions can be defined. Quantum measurements on such a system can be performed using homodyne and heterodyne detectors.

The goal of this work is to develop a statistical machine learning scheme for medical image segmentation: we propose a novel approach based on the stochastic model of image meta-correction. The key properties of this scheme are: 1. the number of segments estimated by the system are proportional to the sum of the number of image patches. It can further be modified by introducing noise. 2. It is robust to the problem of overfitting (i.e., the number of images with a statistically different set of regions compared with the original image). 3. The procedure does not penalise for the lack of precision of the images, the method remains accurate no matter of the data quality (i.e., the probability of missing pixels is proportional to the number of pixels in the images).

The authors' research has been accepted in the "Artificial Intelligence in Medicine" conference organized by the Centre de Recherche Biomètre d'Hommes et de Recherche Biomédical/Université de Montréal and the University of Toronto. In August 2015, several of the organizers announced that the paper "The image meta-correction step-instructions as a training algorithm" was selected as a Research Post-doctoral Award, a prestigious award of $200,000 offered to the most promising research in the field of artificial intelligence.

In addition to the journal article, the paper received the following awards:

– F. Lottie. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 B.E. D.E.A.A. (2012) Award of the Royal European Institute for the History of Medicine.

– S. S. L. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 S.I.A.O. (2011) Award of the Society of Automation Research.

Image-to-image transformation is a well-known and challenging issue in computer vision. In this study, we suggest an adversarial model for addressing this problem. Conventional deep learning techniques handle image-to-image translation through comparison of gram matrices and reliance on image segmentation, which necessitates human input. Our proposed generative adversarial network (GAN) model employs a conditional probability strategy, enabling image translation without dependence on local, global, content, or style characteristics. We incorporate a bidirectional reconstruction model combined with an affine transform factor to preserve content and enhance realism relative to other approaches. This method's benefits include semi-supervised image-to-image translation, independence from image segmentation, and the inherent ability to generate realistic images. The outcomes have shown superiority over Multimodal Unsupervised Image-to-image translation.

12 Years a Slave tells the true story of Solomon Northup, an educated and free black man living in New York during the 1840's who gets abducted, shipped to the south, and sold into slavery. It is a film that stimulates at both an emotional level and an intellectual one.

Chiwetel Ejiofor plays Solomon Northup. He's been a "that guy" actor for sometime – film-goers may know his face but not his name. After this film his name will be known. He gives, quite simply, the best performance from a leading actor since Daniel Day Lewis in There Will Be Blood. Because of his character's position as a slave he is usually unable to speak his mind unless he is prepared to be beaten. As a result Ejiofor is forced to utilize body language and his eyes, which become enormous pools of emotion to express himself to the audience. He's forced to endure terrible things, but he always maintains a certain dignity and nobility that makes his plight even more affecting. It's a performance of incredible subtlety that may leave you speechless and in complete awe.

Micheal Fassbender gives the best performance of his already extremely impressive career, even besting his previous high marks from the films Shame and Hunger (both directed by Steve McQueen, who also directed 12 Years a Slave). He plays Edwynn Epps, a vicious and demonic slaver and perhaps the most loathsome and disgusting character ever put on screen. If alive today, he'd likely be a drunk with severe anger management issues. By turns pathetic and terrifying, he embodies the ultimate nightmare of a deeply flawed man given absolute power over other human beings, and through that absolute power finds only madness, which drives him to deeper cruelty. He's always a menacing and malignant presence even when not on screen, as his slaves must always be aware and prepared for his seemingly random bouts of sadism.

Other actors give excellent performances as well. Paul Giamatti, Paul Dano, Benedict Cumberbatch, Sarah Paulson, Alfre Woodard are all great in relatively small roles. But in this film of titans it's the one you've probably never heard of who perhaps stands above them all. In her first role in a feature film, Lupita Nyong'o, playing the pretty young slave Patsey - the object of Edwynn Epps demented and horrifying affections and the emotional epicenter of the entire picture, gives one of the most devastating performances I have ever seen. A portrait of unbearable sadness, her character is a mirror image of Solomon. While Solomon is a man who refuses to break and give up the dignity which he's known since birth, she is one who has long since been broken, and who never knew dignity in the first place. Her life is a living hell, forced to endure the "love" of Edwyn Epps and the brutal jealousy of his wife, she's trapped in a terrible triangle that she can't escape. Starting his career as a video artist before making full length films, Steve McQueen has an uncanny eye for imagery and contrast. He's also a very patient film maker, utilizing long, steady single shots to emphasize various things. In his prior films this has felt like a purely stylistic choice, here, it's a choice aimed directly at our heart. When the events on screen become their most horrifying and ugly is when his camera becomes the most unflinching. At times feeling perhaps like we're seeing out of the solemn eyes of the ghost of some murdered slave, watching in sorrow and rage. This is both McQueen's most accessible and artistically searing film yet.

There are also moments of stunning natural beauty that would make Terrence Malick proud. Alone, these shots would inspire wonder, but in the context of this film they make us feel more forlorn, as if the ugliness of man is encroaching on the natural beauty of the world.

Perhaps the most noteworthy thing about 12 Years a Slave is the way that it portrays slavery itself. Instead of taking the easy way out and limiting his exploration of the topic solely to the slaves, Steve McQueen increases the scope and we see how it affects those who profited by it. Take Benedict Cumberbatch's character. A seemingly decent and caring man who treats his slaves with some semblance of respect and kindness. He comes off as a relatively good man who is trapped within the powerful confines of the institution of slavery. In 12 Years a Slave, slavery is shown as a horrifying and destructive social construct that drains the humanity from everyone it touches, turning good men into moral quandaries, turning flawed men into monsters, and turning an entire race of people into livestock and tools.

To watch 12 Years a Slave is to be confronted with the grim reality of slavery in a way that's never been done before. To say this is the best film ever made about slavery feels trivial, as slavery is a subject in film that has been shown with naive romanticism from films like Gone With the Wind or silly exploitation from something like Django Unchained. Both of which serve to make the topic digestible. To watch 12 Years a Slave is to experience a level of despair and misery that can become overwhelming. It's a film of such ugliness, such blunt emotional trauma, that it may haunt you for hours if not days after seeing it. So why should you watch a film that could leave you reeling and devastated? Because, it's also one of the greatest cinematic achievements of our time.

Title: Drifting toward Sodom: Modern Liberalism and the Demise of American Values

Robert H. Bork, a previous US Court of Appeals judge, penned a 1996 non-fictional work titled Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline. In this book, Bork posits that US culture is deteriorating and identifies modern liberalism and the emergence of the New Left as the root causes. He critiques modern liberalism for its seemingly contradictory focus on extreme egalitarianism and extreme individualism. The title alludes to W.B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming," with Bork asserting that instead of Bethlehem, the "beast of decay … drifts towards us, not to be born anew, but to reside in Sodom." The title additionally draws inspiration from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem.

Bork initiates by detailing the swift proliferation of modern liberalism throughout the 1960s, maintaining that the tenets of modern liberalism clash fundamentally with the rest of America's political heritage. He subsequently denounces various societal, cultural, and political developments as indicators of the US's cultural decay and moral decay. These include affirmative action, heightened violence and sexualization in mass media, the approval of abortion, mounting pressure to legitimize assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism, and the waning influence of religion. As a rejected Supreme Court nominee by President Ronald Reagan, Bork also reproaches the judiciary and liberal judicial activism for contributing to the moral degradation of the US.

450 g cream cheese, at room temperature
1/4 cup caster sugar
3 teaspoons cornflour
3 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
3 teaspoons finely grated icing sugar
1 1/2 tablespoons strained fresh lemon juice
2 cups sour cream
1 cup thickened cream
220 g good quality white chocolate, melted then cooled to lukewarm
fresh seasonal fruit
passion fruit pulp, to serve
Preheat oven to 180°C Grease a 20cm springform cake pan and line base with baking paper. Wrap the outside tightly with a double layer foil. Whiz cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until smooth. With motor running, add cornflour, eggs one at a time, stopping occasionally to scrape down sides. Add vanilla, zest, juice, creams and 1/4 tsp salt, and process until just combined, scraping down sides. Add chocolate and pulse until smooth. Pour into pan and sit in a large baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the sides of the pan. Bake for 45 minutes, then off the oven, leaving the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. Remove pan from dish, take off the foil and cool cake completely in pan on a rack. Cover and chill overnight. To turn out, sit pan on a hot, damp towel to loosen base. Run a palette knife around edge of pan, then turn onto a serving plate. Decorate with fruit by piling the fruit on top (I find doing it randomly looks best) and pouring over the passionfruit pulp, then slice with a hot, dry knife.

> A POEM ON THE RISING GLORY OF AMERICA
>
> By William Cullen Bryant, 1825
>
> I.
>
> O Liberty! how long hast thou been sleeping?
> How long has thy sweet voice been stilled in silence?
> Long have we heard the tyrants' voices pealing;
> Long have they boasted o'er us and defied us;
> And now at length their power is broken,
> Their pride is humbled, and their empire crumbled.
> No more shall they oppress our land with iron,
> Or chain our limbs to slavery's galling yoke.
> We are no longer slaves, but freemen born again,
> To live as free men ought to live on earth.
> Our fathers fought for liberty, and died for it,
> But we will fight and conquer for ourselves.
>
> II.
>
> Now let us all unite together,
> Let every man be true to his country,
> Forgetting all past differences,
> And join in one great brotherhood.
> Then shall we see the day approaching,
> When peace and plenty shall abound,
> And freedom shall reign triumphant,
> In this fair land of the free.
>
> III.
>
> Oh! may that glorious day soon come,
> When all the world shall know our name,
> And sing our praises far and wide,
> As the most noble nation on earth.
> May we ever stand united,
> Against all enemies both foreign and domestic,
> And never allow any tyranny or despotism
> To gain a footing among us.
>
> IV.
>
> So let us raise our voices high,
> And shout aloud for liberty,
> That all the world may hear our cry,
> And know that we are free indeed.
> Let us pledge ourselves anew,
> To defend our rights and freedoms,
> With all the strength and courage that we possess,
> Until death do us part.

The Australian veteran looked dead and buried against the American lucky loser, trailing by a set and 5-2 down, before reeling off five straight games to level.

Hewitt, the world number 16, went on to edge a final-set tie-break and win 6-7 (4/7) 6-4 7-6 (7/4) in three hours and 18 minutes.

The 30-year-old has now won his last eight three-set matches, boosting his chances of making Australia's Olympic team.

The world number 41 seemed to have momentum firmly on his side when he broke Hewitt to love to go 5-2 up in the second set but the Australian fought back to win the next five games.

David John Mays (November 22, 1896 – February 17, 1971) was an American lawyer and writer. He attempted to slow racial desegregation on behalf of Byrd Organization during the Massive Resistance era. Mays served as counsel to the Gray Commission which tried to formulate segregationists' response to the United States Supreme Court rulings in 1954 and 1955 in consolidated cases known as Brown v. Board of Education. He later unsuccessfully defended actions taken against NAACP attorneys (although he had argued against adoption of those laws and correctly predicted they would be overturned) and significantly unequal legislative reapportionment. In 2008 the University of Georgia Press published an annotated volume of excerpts of his diaries concerning the early years of Massive Resistance (1954-1959).<ref>Race Reason and Massive Resistance: The Diary of David J. Mays, 1954-1959. Edited by James R. Sweeney (University of Georgia Press 2008)</ref> In 1953, Mays won the Pulitzer Prize for Biography or Autobiography for Edmund Pendleton 1721-1803 (Harvard University Press, 1952), a biography of the late 18th-century Virginia politician and judge Edmund Pendleton. Early life
Mays was born in Richmond to Harvey James Mays, a chemical company foreman, and his wife, the former Helga Nelsen. His  Danish immigrant grandfather, Rasmus Nelsen, founded the Nelsen funeral home in Richmond. He eventually had 10 brothers and sisters and attended public schools near his father's employment stations in Alabama and a suburb of Memphis, Tennessee. While he and his father traveled from Washington D.C. to visit Vanderbilt University, they stopped in Ashland, Virginia, where the elder Mays renewed a friendship and the younger Mays ultimately decided  to attend Randolph-Macon Academy. David Mays never received a degree from that institution, although he studied and achieved high grades both from 1914-1916 and 1919-1920.

The Inpui people, an indigenous Naga group, primarily reside in the Haochong subdivision of Noney District and Tamenglong district in Manipur, India. Additionally, they are found in Makuilongdi, Senapati headquarters, Inthan (Waphong) in Senapati district, and Changangei, Tamphagei, Yurembam, Pantilong, and Sagolband in Imphal west district. Inpui communities also exist in Nagaland and Assam. The tallest peak in their territory is Antrimon, located approximately 12 km from Haochong village, and numerous waterways such as Tuilang, Lingkwa, and Ra-ah crisscross the land.

Historically, some scholars have identified them as Kabuis alongside the Rongmeis. However, it is essential to note that the Inpui are the authentic Kabuis, not the Rongmeis. The term "Inpui" has its roots in their ancestry. According to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act of 1976 within the Indian Constitution, they are recognized as a Scheduled Tribe. Festivals celebrated by the Inpui community include Karing-ngei, Somdungnu, Tataaknu, and Muliaang. [Sources]

Silas Boxley Mason II (October 22, 1879 – April 14, 1936) was an American construction executive and racehorse owner, born in Orange County, Virginia. He was part of a Mason family that had been involved with the construction business since 1827. A graduate of Washington and Lee University and Princeton University, he went on to make the Mason & Hanger company one of the largest construction contractors in the United States. His first high-profile venture came in 1927 when he was awarded the contract for the George Washington Bridge foundation on the New Jersey side. During the 1930s Mason would cement his reputation as a master builder when in 1933  Mason headed the M. W. A. K. consortium (Mason-Walsh-Atkinson, Kier) that built the Grand Coulee Dam in Mason City, Washington. His company would then  become involved in the construction of the Lincoln Tunnel. Thoroughbred racing
Silas Mason and his wife Suzanne (née Burnett) met with success in Thoroughbred horse racing  with horses registered in her name. A native Kentuckian, she was a descendant of Colonel Richard Henderson who, along with General George Rogers Clark, Daniel Boone, and others, were Kentucky pioneers who formed the Transylvania Land Company. The couple purchased a home and breeding farm near Lexington, Kentucky called Duntreath.

Objective of this study is to offer both theoretical and numerical analyses concerning the development and progression of a confined plastic region in a one-dimensionally loaded bar featuring a varying cross-sectional profile. Through an energy-oriented variational methodology, we establish the fundamental equations coupled with suitable physical boundary conditions, transition conditions, and regularity conditions at the advancing elasto-plastic boundary. We apply these calculations to a fourth-order explicit gradient plasticity model with linearly isotropic hardening. Four distinct cases are introduced, each representing varying degrees of yield stress irregularity and stress distributions. Outcomes encompassing the applied load level, extent of the plastic zone, arrangement of plastic deformation and its related gradients, plastic stretch, and energy equilibrium are generated and contrasted against those obtained from a priorly examined non-variational gradient formulation.

Shortly after Dreamworks screwed up with the uninspired "Shark Tale", Pixar contains its remarkably success story with "The Incredibles". And while I have to say that I liked "Finding Nemo" a bit better, "The Incredibles" is still an amazing movie.

First of all, this is because it's funny. It's not so funny that you're constantly laughing out loud, but there are more than enough good jokes in the movie to keep you entertained, and it's full of good observations about superhero movies (note all the ridiculous superhero and villain names) and references to other movies. It's also a brilliant James Bond spoof/homage, containing all the gadgets, secret island bases and crazy schemes that made early Bond movies so much fun.

Secondly, this movie has heart and charm in droves. It's full of memorably and likable characters you can really identify with and care about. Characters like Edna are instant classics. The voice acting is universally excellent, but Holly Hunter steals the show as Elastigirl. This is a movie that doesn't need toilet humor, characters modeled like celebrities, or a "hip" soundtrack...it easily succeeds on charm and style alone.

Also, I found it to be a surprisingly good action movie. The plentiful action sequences are full of energy, extremely fast-paced, and exciting, and put many a live-action movie to shame.

Finally, I also liked the tone and message of the movie. "The Incredibles" basically makes a plea against mediocrity, breaking with the politically correct idea that "everybody is special" (and thus nobody really is), and encouraging people to use the talents they have been given. I think this couldn't be more true. Not all people are equally talented (just compare Pixar to Dreamworks), but this is no reason to keep the talented people from not reaching their full potential just because it makes the less talented ones feel bad.

"The Incredibles", while maybe not as hilarious as I had hoped (though it's still very funny), is nonetheless an extremely entertaining movie, that manages to charm you wit its combination of great characters, lots of style, tongue-in-cheek attitude and good message. Highly recommended.

Brewers' profits lose their fizz

 Financial results for the world's biggest beer makers have been flatlining in recent months as a young generation shuns the drink.

AB InBev, the owner of Budweiser and Stella Artois, reported a 0.5% fall in organic revenue in the first three months of the year.

The company blamed bad weather in Europe for a 1.3% drop in volumes, while profits were also hit by higher commodity prices.

Heineken, the world's second biggest brewer, reported a 0.9% fall in beer volumes in the first three months of the year.

also announced a 0.5% drop in revenues, blaming "Korea and Nigeria".

Carlsberg, the third biggest global brewer, posted a 0.4% drop in beer sales in the first three months of 2018.

The Danish company said that it had seen "high single-digit growth" in eastern Europe, but this was offset by declines in China and Western Europe.

All three companies have been trying to offset falling demand for beer in developed markets by raising prices and investing in new products.

AB InBev said it was "encouraged" by the performance of its new non-alcoholic beer, Budweiser Zero.

But it is clear that the global beer market is struggling to find growth.

In the US, the world's biggest beer market, sales have been in decline for a decade.

In 2017, beer sales fell by 1% in volume and 2% in value, according to industry group the Beer Institute.

The trend is being driven by a younger generation of drinkers who are turning their backs on the traditional pint.

"People are drinking less beer and they're drinking better beer," said Simon Thorpe, chief executive of Sheffield-based beer maker and pub group Molson Coors.

"The big challenge for the beer category is how do we continue to be relevant to consumers, particularly younger consumers."

The global beer market is forecast to grow by just 1% this year, according to research group Euromonitor.

The Medusa algorithm generates the quadratic rational map, which is the union of two postcritically finite quadratic polynomials as input. It delivers an sequence of approximations for the map's parameters together with its Julia set image. The convergence of these approximations is determined through Thurston's topological classification of rational maps.

This algorithm was devised by John Hamal Hubbard and brought to life in 1998 by Christian Henriksen and REU scholars David Farris and Kuon Ju Liu. Within this paper, we explain the algorithm and its implementation, present selected results such as numerous illustrations, and address associated queries. We provide visualizations and analysis for certain shared matings, Lattes instances, and sequential combinations of matings.

The book begins in April 1979 at a small academic conference at the University of Rummidge. It is the first conference that Persse McGarrigle, (a reference to Percival the grail knight), an innocent young Irishman who recently completed his master's thesis on T. S. Eliot, has attended. He teaches at the fictional University College, Limerick, after having been mistakenly interviewed because the administration sent the interview invitation to him instead of someone else with the same last name. Several important characters are introduced: Rummidge professor Philip Swallow, American professor Morris Zapp, retired Cambridge professor Sybil Maiden, and the beautiful Angelica Pabst, with whom McGarrigle falls immediately in love. Much of the rest of the book is his quest to find and win her. Angelica tells Persse that she was adopted by an executive at KLM after she was found, abandoned, in the washroom of an airplane in flight. Persse professes his love for her, but she leaves the conference without telling him where she has gone. Morris Zapp and Philip Swallow, who are seeing each other for the first time in ten years after the events of Changing Places, have a long evening talk. Since the previous novel, Swallow has become a professor and head of the English Department. Zapp has discovered deconstructionism and reinvented himself academically. Swallow tells Zapp about an incident a few years before, when after almost dying in a plane crash he spent the night at a British Council official's home and slept with the official's wife, Joy. Soon after, Swallow read in the newspaper that Joy, the official, and their son had died in a plane crash. Part II of the book begins by going around the world, time zone to time zone, showing what different characters are doing all at the same time: Morris Zapp travelling; Australian Rodney Wainright trying to write a conference paper; Zapp's ex-wife Désirée trying to write a novel; Howard Ringbaum trying to convince his wife Thelma to sleep with him on an airplane so he can join the Mile High Club; Siegfried von Turpitz talking to Arthur Kingfisher about the new UNESCO chair of literary criticism; Rudyard Parkinson plotting to get that chair; Turkish Akbil Borak reading William Hazlitt to prepare for a visit by Swallow; Akira Sakazaki translating English novelist Ronald Frobisher into Japanese; Ronald Frobisher having breakfast; Italian Fulvia Morgana (a reference to Morgan le Fay) meeting Morris Zapp on a plane; and more.` Cheryl Summerbee is also introduced. She is a check-in clerk for British Airways at Heathrow and plays a small but very important role in helping, or hindering, other characters as they travel around the world. She loves reading romance novels, especially the kind published by "Bills and Moon" (a fictionalized Mills & Boon). People continue to move around from conference to conference around the world in Part III. Persse continues to pursue Angelica. At a meeting in Amsterdam, Persse hears the German literary scholar Siegfried von Turpitz speaking about ideas that he submitted in an unpublished book, and all but accuses von Turpitz of plagiarism. Zapp rises to defend Persse from von Turpitz. Later, Persse sees someone who looks like Angelica, and thinks she has appeared in pornographic movies and worked as a stripper. In Turkey, Phillip Swallow meets Joy, the woman he thought was dead. She explains that only her husband had been on the plane that crashed. They begin an affair, and Swallow plans to leave his wife. Events and characters move along in Part IV, often with direct reference to the genre of romance, such as Sybil Maiden (who at one point acts as a sibyl) saying that grail knights "were such boobies... All they had to do was ask a question at the right moment, and they generally muffed it." Zapp is kidnapped by an underground left-wing movement, but is later released after pressure from Morgana. Persse, who has won an award and got a credit card, has enough money to continue to chase Angelica but never manages to catch up with her. She does leave him a clue referencing The Faerie Queene and he discovers that she has an identical twin, and it is the twin, Lily, who made the pornographic movies. When Persse meets Cheryl Summerbee again, she is now reading not romance novels but romances such as Orlando Furioso and critics such as Northrop Frye after Angelica has passed through her line. Persse is happy to learn this, but Cheryl is shaken to see that Persse is infatuated with Angelica, because she loves him herself. Persse continues to chase Angelica around the world, to conferences in Hawaii, Tokyo, and Hong Kong, and Jerusalem, but he never catches up with her. At that Jerusalem conference, Philip Swallow is with Joy, but after he sees his son there he becomes psychosomatically ill, which people think might be Legionnaires' Disease in a moment of panic. This stops the conference, and leads to the end of Philip and Joy's affair. Part V takes place at the Modern Language Association conference in New York at the end of 1979. All of the characters in the book are there. Arthur Kingfisher oversees a panel discussion about criticism where Swallow, Zapp, Morgana, and others present their opinions on what literary criticism is. Zapp's kidnapping experience has cured him of his interest in deconstructionism. Persse (contrary to what Sybil Maiden had said about knights not asking the right question at the right time) asks, "What follows if everyone agrees with you?" Kingfisher is inspired by this question, and recovers from his mental and physical impotence. Persse finally finds Angelica and hears her read a paper about romances that directly reflects the structure of Small World itself: "No sooner is one crisis in the fortunes of the hero averted than a new one presents itself; no sooner has one mystery been solved than another is raised; no sooner has one adventure been concluded than another begins... The greatest and most characteristic romances are often unfinished - they end only with the author's exhaustion, as a woman's capacity for orgasm is limited only by her physical stamina. Romance is a multiple orgasm." After this talk, Persse runs through the hotel and sees a woman he takes to be Angelica, kisses her and declares that he loves her. She takes him up to her hotel room where they make love, in Persse's first sexual experience. However, after this encounter, she reveals that she is not Angelica, but the twin sister, Lily. Persse feels ashamed, but Lily convinces him that he was "in love with a dream". Later in the evening, Arthur Kingfisher announces that he will offer himself as a candidate for the UNESCO chair. Right afterwards, Sybil Maiden steps forward and announces that she is Angelica and Lily's mother and Kingfisher is their father, which throws the entire meeting into a joyous uproar. Angelica introduces Persse to her fiancee, Peter McGarrigle, the person whose job Persse was interviewed for back in Ireland. However, Peter is not angry, because as a result, he went to America and there met Angelica. Swallow has returned to his wife, saying "Basically I failed in the role of a romantic hero." All of the narrative threads of the novel wrap up but for one: Persse realizes that Cheryl Summerbee, not Angelica, is the woman for him, and he flies to Heathrow to see her. The Shrimal (Srimal) community, historically rooted in Rajasthan's Shrimal or Bhinmal region, has its origins as affluent Jain and Hindu traders and financiers. The Srimal (Srimal) Jain community is considered the most prestigious within the Oswal merchant and minister caste prevalent in northern India. Scholars propose that the Srimal separated from the Oswal, indicated by the predominantly Jain faith among the Srimal population, contrasting the Jain beliefs of some Oswals who trace their descent from the Rajput prince of Osnagar, who embraced Jainism after encountering the Jain ascetic Sri Ratan Suri reviving his son. A minority of Srimals practice Hinduism and adhere to the Vaishnav sect, revering their clan goddess, Goddess Lakshmi. Primarily inhabiting Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat, the Srimal community is recognized for its commercial acumen and historical ties to royalty.

Microsoft is offering Windows XP users a free swap to a later version of the operating system, in an attempt to boost the number of computers that are secure against malware.

The company has promised to provide a free one-year licence for Windows 7, Windows 8 or Windows 10 to any XP user who visits a special website.

The offer is being run in partnership with the nonprofit group, Preserve Connectivity.

"Customers who browse the web with an unpatched browser on an unsupported operating system are more vulnerable to security risks," said Christine Hall, head of Microsoft's Windows marketing for Asia Pacific.

"This offer is for those consumers who are unaware or less informed about the risks of continuing to use an unsupported operating system."

Windows XP was released in 2001 and discontinuted in 2014. Nevertheless, analyst firm NetMarketShare reported that as of March this year, it was still running on 8.93% of desktops.

It is particularly popular in Asia, where it accounts for more than a quarter of desktops.

Windows 7, which was released in 2009, will also be discontinued next year.

However, it is still used on half of all desktops, according to NetMarketShare.

Microsoft is making the offer available in Hong Kong, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines and India.

"Background subtraction," an age-old method for detecting moving objects in video sequences like cars on a highway, involves subtracting the current image from a time-averaged background image. This approach leaves only nonstationary objects behind. However, it is a rough estimate for labeling each pixel in the present image; it falls short with slowly moving objects and cannot discern shadows from moving ones. In essence, this research proposes categorizing each pixel based on a model depicting how that pixel appears when belonging to distinct classes. By employing an unsupervised learning technique, specifically an efficient, iterative variant of EM, we develop a mixture-of-Gaussians classification model for every pixel. Distinct from typical image averaging methods, our approach adaptively adjusts the Gaussian mixture component for each class based on probability of membership. As a result, this method adeptly handles slow-moving objects and accurately distinguishes shadows from moving objects. The anticipated application of this method within the Roadwatch traffic monitoring initiative is predicted to yield substantial enhancements in vehicle recognition and tracking.

This study explores correlations between the initial expansions of basic modules and specific filtrations of standard modules within the realm of graded Hecke algebras. The filtrations under consideration are radical filtrations and Jantzen filtrations. Our strategy incorporates insights derived from the Langlands categorization and a more comprehensive grasp of certain module properties. The module in question stems from the projection of a Knapp-Stein intertwining operator's output and represents a quotient of a generalized standard module. Throughout our investigation, we derive outcomes concerning the blocks of finite-dimensional modules within graded Hecke algebras.

As a practical application, we determine the Ext-groups for irreducible modules within a block for the graded Hecke algebra of type $C_3$, contingent upon the validity of a particular version of the Jantzen conjecture.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation based on affinity learning. Our approach is based on the principle of maximin affinity, which aims to maximize the similarity between neighboring pixels while simultaneously minimizing the similarity between dissimilar pixels. To learn the affinity between pixels, we use a convolutional neural network (CNN) which is trained using a novel loss function that is based on the maximin principle. We evaluate our approach on the Weizmann Horse Segmentation dataset and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our approach outperforms existing methods and offers a new way to approach the problem of image segmentation.

The families EPT (resp. EPG) Edge Intersection Graphs of Paths in a tree
(resp. in a grid) are well studied graph classes. Recently we introduced the
graph classes Edge-Intersecting and Non-Splitting Paths in a Tree ENPT, and in
a Grid (ENPG). It was shown that ENPG contains an infinite hierarchy of
subclasses that are obtained by restricting the number of bends in the paths.
Motivated by this result, in this work we focus on one bend {ENPG} graphs. We
show that one bend ENPG graphs are properly included in two bend ENPG graphs.
We also show that trees and cycles are one bend ENPG graphs, and characterize
the split graphs and co-bipartite graphs that are one bend ENPG. We prove that
the recognition problem of one bend ENPG split graphs is NP-complete even in a
very restricted subfamily of split graphs. Last we provide a linear time
recognition algorithm for one bend ENPG co-bipartite graphs.

2-1/2 cups Whole Milk
1/2 cups Heavy Cream
1/2 cups Light Agave Syrup
2 ounces, weight Unsweetened Baking Chocolate
1/2 cups Cocoa Powder
1/4 teaspoons Salt
4 whole Eggs
2 Tablespoons Cornstarch Stirred Into 1/4 Cup Cold Water
16 envelopes Sweet-N-Low
2 teaspoons Real Vanilla
Pour milk, cream and agave into a medium sized pot. Add chopped chocolate. Stir in cocoa and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring frequently, until cocoa is dispersed and chocolate is melted. Continue to heat until mixture is quite hot. Meanwhile, crack eggs into a small mixing bowl. Stir cornstarch into water until smooth. Stir cornstarch water into eggs. Set aside. Open Sweet-N-Low packets and place into a small bowl. Measure vanilla into another small bowl. When milk mixture in pot is quite hot, like hot chocolate, spoon about 1 cup into the egg mixture and mix well. This tempers your eggs so they don't scramble when you add them to the pot. Once your eggs are well mixed, pour this egg mixture back into the pot with the rest of the hot milk, etc. Continue to cook until this mixture is very thick. It will coat a spoon thickly. At this point you can remove the pot from the heat and blend mixture with a stick blender, or pour into a blender and blend until completely smooth. Now add the vanilla and the sweetener to the mix. Blend well. Pour the pudding into serving-sized bowls or into one or two larger bowls. Place in the fridge until cold. Eat. Yum yum.

Born on April 24, 1941, Mostafa Azkia hails from Iran and is a distinguished sociologist. Notable in the field of Iranian rural development, Azkia serves as a sociology professor at the University of Tehran. He has authored and translated approximately twenty books. His contribution to "Twenty Years of Islamic Revolution: Political and Social Transition in Iran since 1979," specifically his chapter "Rural Society and Revolution in Iran" edited by Eric Hooglan, is regarded as groundbreaking. Considered a pioneer, Azkia is among the founders of rural development studies in Iran. His upbringing was in a middle-class Tehran household where his father worked for the Iranian postal service. Aspiring to become a medical doctor during his formative years, an error in college entrance exams led him instead to enroll in the Faculty of Sociology at Tehran University in 1960. Simultaneously, he joined the Faculty of Law but was compelled to abandon his legal studies in 1962 due to a regulation barring students from pursuing dual degrees.

Pat Chan is a Canadian professional chef and restaurateur known for his work in the culinary industry.

Early Life and Education

In 2007, Chan opened his second restaurant, Chambar, which serves Belgian-inspired cuisine with Asian flavors. The restaurant was an instant hit and has since been recognized as one of the top restaurants in Vancouver.
