Scaling properties of time series are usually studied in terms of the scaling
laws of empirical moments, which are the time average estimates of moments of
the dynamic variable. Nonlinearities in the scaling function of empirical
moments are generally regarded as a sign of multifractality in the data. We
show that, except for the Brownian motion, this method fails to disclose the
correct monofractal nature of self-similar L\'evy processes. We prove that for
this class of processes it produces apparent multifractality characterised by a
piecewise-linear scaling function with two different regimes, which match at
the stability index of the considered process. This result is motivated by
previous numerical evidence. It is obtained by introducing an appropriate
stochastic normalisation which is able to cure empirical moments, without
hiding their dependence on time, when moments they aim at estimating do not
exist.

"Ingredients: 1/2 cup butter, softened 4 cups shredded Cheddar cheese 3 tablespoons chopped green onions 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce 1 loaf French bread Directions Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). In a medium bowl, mix together the butter, cheese, green onion and Worcestershire sauce until well blended. Cut the top off the loaf of bread, leaving about an inch at the bottom. Hollow out the inside of the bread, leaving a shell with about 1-inch thick walls. Fill the hollowed out center with the cheese mixture. Place the lid back onto the filled bread. Wrap in aluminum foil and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes."

1 large onion, chopped
100 g smoked bacon lardons
2 tablespoons olive oil
500 g lean stewing beef, cubed
2 tablespoons plain flour
3 parsnips, cubed
500 ml brown ale
300 ml beef stock
2 tablespoons cranberry jelly or 2 tablespoons red currant jelly
4 fresh thyme sprigs
greens, to serve (optional)
butter, for greasing
300 g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
2 teaspoons English mustard powder
140 g shredded suet
Heat a large pan and cook the onion and lardons together for 5 mins until golden. Scoop out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Add the oil to the pan, dust the beef with the flour, then evenly brown over a high heat. Add the parsnips, ale, stock, jelly, thyme and lardon mixture to the pan. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hrs until the meat is tender. Generously butter a 1.5-litre pudding basin. To make the pastry, mix together the flour, mustard powder, suet and 1/2 tsp table salt. Add enough cold water, about 150ml, to make a soft dough. Remove one-quarter of the dough and set to one side. On a heavily floured surface, roll out the remaining dough to make a large round, big enough to line the basin. Carefully lay the pastry in the basin (aim to have 1cm of pastry overhanging the rim), then press the edges of the join together to seal. Roll out the remaining one-quarter into a circle big enough to cover the top. Pour off the cooking liquid from the filling into a small pan and set aside. Discard the thyme stalks. Spoon the filling into the lined basin and pour over 100ml of the cooking liquid. Fold over the overhanging pastry and brush with water. Place the lid on top, pressing firmly around the edges to seal. Butter a sheet of baking parchment, fold in a large pleat and lay, butter-side down, on top of the pudding. Cover with a pleated layer of foil and finally tie with string, making a loop for the handle so you can lift the pudding easily. Sit a small trivet or a large cookie cutter in the bottom of a deep saucepan that's big enough to take the basin easily. Half-fill the pan with water and bring to the boil. Lower in the pudding, cover and simmer for 2 hrs, topping up with boiling water when necessary. Reheat the cooking liquid, bubbling it down a little so it reduces into a tasty gravy. Carefully lift out the pudding. Run a knife around the rim, then turn out and serve with gravy and greens, if you like.

This is a topic that I've been grappling with a lot recently and I wanted to bring this discussion to the wider Reddit community to gain a balanced perspective. 

Culture appropriation is a sensitive issue and rightly so, as it involves taking elements from a less dominant culture by a more dominant one, often without understanding, acknowledgment or respect. This can include traditional clothing, language, music, dances, and even religious symbols. 

However, I am wondering where we draw the line between appreciating and borrowing from a culture and appropriating it. If one genuinely has an interest in a culture different from their own, appreciates it and borrows certain aspects of it, should it be seen as appropriation or appreciation? 

For instance, if I, as an individual with a deep admiration of Japanese culture adopt elements of it in my daily life, such as clothing or language, would that be considered appropriation? Is there a 'right way' for me to express my admiration for this culture? What guidelines should one follow to ensure they are not disrespecting or trivializing the values of a culture they admire?

Also, another question that keeps me awake at night revolves around global fusion. As our world becomes more interconnected and cultures meld together naturally, doesn't this open up a space for shared cultural elements? 

It would be great to hear your thoughts. Please remember to keep all responses respectful and understanding of differing viewpoints. Let's make this dialog a safe space for everyone who chooses to participate.

We build on recent works on Stein's method for functions of multivariate
normal random variables to derive bounds for the rate of convergence of some
asymptotically chi-square distributed statistics. We obtain some general bounds
and establish some simple sufficient conditions for convergence rates of order
$n^{-1}$ for smooth test functions. These general bounds are applied to
Friedman's statistic for comparing $r$ treatments across $n$ trials and the
family of power divergence statistics for goodness-of-fit across $n$ trials and
$r$ classifications, with index parameter $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ (Pearson's
statistic corresponds to $\lambda=1$). We obtain a $O(n^{-1})$ bound for the
rate of convergence of Friedman's statistic for any number of treatments
$r\geq2$. We also obtain a $O(n^{-1})$ bound on the rate of convergence of the
power divergence statistics for any $r\geq2$ when $\lambda$ is a positive
integer or any real number greater than 5. We conjecture that the $O(n^{-1})$
rate holds for any $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.

Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) has great potential for medical imaging
applications. Most of the existing FSS techniques require abundant annotated
semantic classes for training. However, these methods may not be applicable for
medical images due to the lack of annotations. To address this problem we make
several contributions: (1) A novel self-supervised FSS framework for medical
images in order to eliminate the requirement for annotations during training.
Additionally, superpixel-based pseudo-labels are generated to provide
supervision; (2) An adaptive local prototype pooling module plugged into
prototypical networks, to solve the common challenging foreground-background
imbalance problem in medical image segmentation; (3) We demonstrate the general
applicability of the proposed approach for medical images using three different
tasks: abdominal organ segmentation for CT and MRI, as well as cardiac
segmentation for MRI. Our results show that, for medical image segmentation,
the proposed method outperforms conventional FSS methods which require manual
annotations for training.

US oil prices have fallen by 6%, driven down by forecasts of a mild winter in the densely populated northeast.
Light crude oil futures fell $2.86 to $41.32 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange (Nymex), and have now lost $4 in five days. In this paper, we present a theoretical analysis of active contours on graphs, which are a generalization of traditional active contour models that operate on graph-structured data. We propose a new formulation of active contours on graphs, based on a probabilistic framework that allows for efficient inference and learning. Our approach enables the integration of domain knowledge into the segmentation process, leading to improved accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods.

We derive a set of algorithms for active contour evolution on graphs, including a novel iterative algorithm that converges to an optimal solution under certain conditions. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical bound on the convergence rate of our algorithm, providing insights into its performance.

Our analysis also covers the case where the graph structure is uncertain or noisy, in which case we propose a robust variant of our algorithm that can handle such scenarios. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on several real-world datasets, showcasing its ability to accurately segment complex objects in various domains.

Overall, our work provides a solid foundation for understanding and improving active contour models on graph-structured data, opening up new possibilities for applications in computer vision, machine learning, and related fields.

Tumor detection in biomedical imaging is a time-consuming process for medical
professionals and is not without errors. Thus in recent decades, researchers
have developed algorithmic techniques for image processing using a wide variety
of mathematical methods, such as statistical modeling, variational techniques,
and machine learning. In this paper, we propose a semi-automatic method for
liver segmentation of 2D CT scans into three labels denoting healthy, vessel,
or tumor tissue based on graph cuts. First, we create a feature vector for each
pixel in a novel way that consists of the 59 intensity values in the time
series data and propose a simplified perimeter cost term in the energy
functional. We normalize the data and perimeter terms in the functional to
expedite the graph cut without having to optimize the scaling parameter
$\lambda$. In place of a training process, predetermined tissue means are
computed based on sample regions identified by expert radiologists. The
proposed method also has the advantage of being relatively simple to implement
computationally. It was evaluated against the ground truth on a clinical CT
dataset of 10 tumors and yielded segmentations with a mean Dice similarity
coefficient (DSC) of .77 and mean volume overlap error (VOE) of 36.7%. The
average processing time was 1.25 minutes per slice.

Fig and Peach Salad Recipe

Ingredients:
- 6 fresh figs, quartered
- 4 ripe peaches, sliced
- 1/2 cup of walnuts or almonds (or both!), chopped
- 4 oz. crumbled goat cheese or feta cheese 
- 2 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- The juice of half a lemon
- Fresh mint leaves, chopped
- Arugula or baby spinach for serving 

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine the quartered figs, sliced peaches, chopped nuts, and crumbled cheese.
2.In a small bowl mix together the honey, lemon juice, and mint leaves.
3. Pour the dressing over the fruit mixture and gently toss to coat.
4. Serve immediately over a bed of arugula or baby spinach leaves.
5. Enjoy your sweet and healthy Fig and Peach Salad!

In this study, we report findings from an experiment demonstrating subpar iris recognition results for individuals with cataract-impacted eyes versus healthy eyes. The literature on this subject is scant, with limited resources featuring insufficient representations of multiple diseases. We assembled our proprietary database consisting of 1288 eye images sourced from 37 patients at the Medical University of Warsaw. This collection includes various common ocular diseases, including cataracts, as well as less frequent conditions like altered iris patterns caused by illness or injury. Photos were taken using near-infrared light (utilized in biometrics) and, in certain instances, visible light (employed in ophthalmological diagnoses). Given the prevalence of cataracts within our database, we exclusively concentrate on this condition in this investigation. We evaluate the degree of performance decline by applying three distinct iris recognition techniques to determine genuine match scores for both healthful and cataract-affected eyes. Our results reveal a substantial decrease in iris recognition accuracy, evidenced by a rise in genuine scores across all three matching algorithms used in the study (an enhancement of 12% for an academic matcher, and a maximum increase of 175% for a commercial matcher). These enhanced genuine scores led to heightened false non-match rates in two of the matchers. For example: if I am taking care of anything around the house (laundry, dishes, yard work), I play games that allow me to multi-task while doing so. The only issue is, sometimes I feel bad about completing a game knowing there are more levels to explore or more quests to complete. The satisfaction I get from achieving goals keeps me coming back for more. However, this also means I can never fully experience everything the game has to offer unless I force myself to move forward and push through to a story end.

Am I alone here? Or do you guys also find yourself getting stuck in your gaming habits? Weighing enjoyment vs progression - both equally important! Let me know what you think in the comments below. 😊

A 5- to 6-pound pork shoulder or Boston butt roast, seasoned with 2 teaspoons of salt, should be refrigerated for 30 minutes after salting. Light half of a 10-pound charcoal load in the grill, allowing it to burn for 15 to 20 minutes until ashed over. Arrange the coals into two piles on opposite sides of the grill. On top of each pile, place 2 hickory wood chunks. The food rack goes on the grill next, followed by the pork, meatier side down, in its center. Secure the lid, ensuring all ventilation holes remain unobstructed. Prepare another charcoal fire using 12 briquettes in a separate grill or firebox, and wait for it to ash over. Once ashed, incorporate 6 briquettes into each pile and add an additional 2 hickory chunks. Repeat this process every 30 minutes. Maintain a cover and cook for approximately 5 hours and 30 minutes, checking the internal temperature with a meat thermometer every 30 minutes until it reaches 165° in the thickest part. (Cooking the pork to 165° facilitates easier bone removal.) Allow the pork to rest briefly before chopping and serving with Cider Vinegar Barbecue Sauce or Peppery Vinegar Sauce.

1/4 teaspoon rapid rise yeast
1 1/2 cups water at room temperature
1 3/4 teaspoons salt
4 cups all-purpose flour, or as needed
1/2 teaspoon cornmeal, or as needed
Place yeast into the bottom of a large mixing bowl and stir with water; mix in salt. Beat flour into yeast mixture with a wooden spoon until dough is thick and sticky and pulls flour from the side of the bowl, 5 to 10 minutes. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let stand in a turned-off oven until doubled in size, 12 to 14 hours. Dough will be bubbly and very sticky. Place a silicone baking mat onto a baking sheet and dust generously with cornmeal. Use a floured spatula to scrape dough out onto a well-floured work surface and dust dough with flour. With well-floured hands, pat dough into a rectangle and cut into 4 equal-size pieces. Dust a piece of dough with flour and use your floured fingers to gently roll and stretch it out into a log about 10 inches long and 1 1/2 inches around. Gently transfer to prepared baking sheet. If desired, wipe off excess cornmeal with a damp paper towel. Repeat with another piece of dough. (Reserve remaining dough to bake later or prepare 2 baking sheets to bake all 4 at once). Dust loaves lightly with flour. Dust a large piece of plastic wrap with flour and drape plastic lightly over the baking sheet with floured side down. Let loaves rise, covered, until doubled, 1 to 1 1/2 hour. Move oven racks to the bottom and middle positions. Preheat oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C) or as high as your oven will go. Place an oven-safe baking dish full of water into bottom rack of the oven. Use a sharp kitchen shears to cut 4 or 5 angled slashes into the top of each loaf. Poke down the little sharp tips of dough left by the scissors. Spray loaves with water, using a spray bottle. Bake in the preheated oven until baguettes are browned, about 15 minutes, spraying loaves with water after 5 minutes and 10 minutes. Turn the pan around on the second spraying. Transfer baguettes to a cooling rack and let cool to room temperature before slicing with a serrated knife.

When Sara's mother is killed in a car accident she comes to live in a predominately black area in Chicago. She is befriended by black Chenille and starts to fall for her brother Derek. Derek teaches her the latest hip-hop dances to help her fit in and together they begin to fall for each other. However a white girl seeing a clever black man is never going to be popular and the couple must overcome many obstacles to see their dreams and be true to themselves.

Did someone say `a black Dirty Dancing?' Essentially that's what this is, although the story is naturally a bit more urban than that film. The story is about overcoming to reach your dreams, and it does it quite well  better than I expected. The love story is nice without being too romanticised. The obstacles are the usual things in an `urban' film  the challenge of mixed race relationships, the temptation to back up your crew instead of getting out etc. These are quite cliched but are still well done.

My main problem came with the strength of black culture in the filmnot every black person (even in a poor area) talks like a gangstaand not everyone says `aiiiirite'  and why did Sara only become accepted when she started to imitate black culture and speak in that way. It may be realistic, but I felt that Sara should have been allowed to be herself rather than be seen to be assimilated into the hip-hop culture (I don't mean that she shouldn't have got involved with the scene  but did she have to lose part of herself to get there?). However these are minor side issues that many people won't even think about.

The cast are good for MTV teens. Julia Stiles is cool and Thomas is cute and charming. The rest of the cast fall into so many black stereotypes  we have gangsta friend, baby mothers galore, useless baby father, jealous bitchy ex-girlfriends etc. However they are just what you expect so I wasn't too upset. Fredro Starr was cool as Malakai  even if the character was just one big hood cliché.

The soundtrack is hot and the dance scenes are sexy  I wish I could do it! They are much more enjoyable than Dirty Dancing's scenes  although some day this will feel dated too! Overall I expected another piece of MTV teen tat, but I was pleasantly surprised by a story that, despite being ridden with clichés, is actually very involving and enjoyable.

We introduce a new light-field dataset of materials, and take advantage of
the recent success of deep learning to perform material recognition on the 4D
light-field. Our dataset contains 12 material categories, each with 100 images
taken with a Lytro Illum, from which we extract about 30,000 patches in total.
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mid-size dataset for
light-field images. Our main goal is to investigate whether the additional
information in a light-field (such as multiple sub-aperture views and
view-dependent reflectance effects) can aid material recognition. Since
recognition networks have not been trained on 4D images before, we propose and
compare several novel CNN architectures to train on light-field images. In our
experiments, the best performing CNN architecture achieves a 7% boost compared
with 2D image classification (70% to 77%). These results constitute important
baselines that can spur further research in the use of CNNs for light-field
applications. Upon publication, our dataset also enables other novel
applications of light-fields, including object detection, image segmentation
and view interpolation.

Bill Conti's job of musical director of the Oscars show is not for the faint-hearted since conducting the orchestra is the ultimate plate-spinning assignment.
This year marks Conti's 17th turn at the helm of the Academy Awards orchestra. "The excitement is a live performance as a musician," he says. "All of your colleagues, everyone in the film industry is in the theatre. All the important people. "I guess it's just a television show but we always think it's a bit more.' The orchestra strikes up more than 110 times during the average Oscars show. As well as playing the presenters and winners on and off stage, it also performs during the commercial breaks to entertain the live audience in the house.
"It's a very busy evening, it takes a certain amount of preparation of music, orchestrating, sketching rehearsing, before the show. But you don't know what the unexpected will be and as the musical director, it's exciting," explains Conti. And much of the preparation goes into mastering scores that will never be performed. "We don't know who the winners will be. So when they say, 'the winner is', we have five different pieces of music in front of us, they say the name, we play the appropriate one immediately," adds Conti.
The orchestra is often called upon to play when the winners ramble on too long during their acceptance speeches, despite being told to be brief by the show's producers.
The decision to drown out or 'kill' the offending star with music is relayed from the director's box to the orchestra via Conti's earpiece. "I don't feel good about it at all. It's not my call though," he says. "When the director says 'music' the orchestra plays and he takes a long shot of the hall. We don't usually see the person speaking while his microphone is cut off. "The person that's been cut off, who's 10 feet from me, is glaring at me like it's death time." On occasions, some stars have taken it upon themselves to send a warning shot across the bows of the musical director before they start to speak. "Julia Roberts, when she came on, she asked me to not get ready to play because she had so much to do," he says. Conti received an Oscar in 1983 for the original score of The Right Stuff. He also received two nominations in the original song category in 1976 for Gonna Fly Now from Rocky and in 1981 for the title song from For Your Eyes Only.
"It's a moment in the sun," he says. "When people get up there, some people, this is hard to believe, people that spend their lives in front of the camera or audiences entertaining, might get a little flustered. "But there's this moment in time when the biggest award that they could possibly get in their life has been handed to them and they're either not in control or they want to thank everyone that they ever met."
The image of the Oscars telecast is one of slick presentation and smooth transitions between performances and the award categories. Behind the scenes, the key players, such as Conti, have a bewildering array of technical props to deal with. "There's a big script and video monitors you have to watch and there are also audio controls. I can control hearing in my ears, the left ear or the right ear - different things at different times.
"I have to communicate with the director. I have a little microphone that's attached to my headset. To open up that microphone, I have a footswitch," he explains. Conti's most nerve-wracking moment came during his first Oscars show as musical director, in 1977, when a member of the orchestra alerted him that they could smell smoke. Conti immediately told the show's director: "I start cursing and screaming, I tell him we're not going to die for this show - you must do something or I'm going to climb out of this pit with 60 musicians and we're going to be home in 10 minutes. "'Oh no Bill don't do anything," came the response. "Imagine these elegantly dressed ladies and gentlemen of the orchestra, 60 or so of them in the pit and while we're playing, firemen with their helmets and their hatchets crawling among us trying to find the reason for the smoke." The smell turned out to be new paint smouldering on the music stands. "No one died, it's not a big story, but it was scary at the time," laughs Conti. When the ceremony is over, the music director attends the annual Governor's Ball with his family. "I have a drink and relive the show," he says. "I'm not for too much carousing. I go home and unwind. It takes me about a day."

In the aftermath of her mother's death in a car crash, Sara moves to a predominantly African American community in Chicago. There, she forms a friendship with Chenille and becomes attracted to her brother, Derek. To help Sara adjust, Derek instructs her in the latest hip-hop dance moves. As they grow closer, they develop feelings for one another. Nevertheless, their interracial relationship faces numerous challenges, compelling them to surmount various hurdles to pursue their dreams and remain true to themselves.

This tale can be likened to a contemporary, urban take on "Dirty Dancing." While the narrative excels in conveying themes of perseverance and self-realization, it does so effectively, surpassing my initial expectations. The love story is well-balanced and authentic, devoid of excessive sentimentality. The challenges confronted in the film, such as racial prejudice and the lure of conformity, though predictable, are competently portrayed.

My primary issue lies with the representation of African American culture in the film. Not all residents of impoverished neighborhoods adopt the vernacular commonly associated with hip-hop culture, and it seemed unrealistic that Sara would only gain acceptance once she adopted this mannerism. Although I acknowledge that assimilation might be a realistic aspect of certain social environments, I believe that Sara should have been allowed to maintain her individuality rather than being perceived as having sacrificed part of herself to fit in. Nonetheless, these concerns may be overlooked by many viewers.

In a sign of a thaw in relations between Egypt and Israel, the two countries have signed a trade protocol with the US, allowing Egyptian goods made in partnership with Israeli firms free access to American markets.
The protocol, signed in Cairo, will establish what are called "qualified industrial zones" in Egypt. Products from these zones will enjoy duty free access to the US, provided that 35% of their components are the product of Israeli-Egyptian cooperation. The US describes this as the most important economic agreement between Egypt and Israel in two decades.
The protocol establishing the zones has been stalled for years. There has been deep sensitivity in Egypt about any form of co-operation with Israel as long as its peace process with the Palestinians remains blocked. But in recent weeks an unusual warmth has crept into relations between the two countries. Both exchanged prisoners earlier this month, with Egypt handing back an Israeli who has served eight years in prison after being convicted for spying.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has described Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon as the best chance for the Palestinians to achieve peace. The government in Cairo now believes Mr Sharon is moving towards the centre and away from the positions of right wing groups. It also believes the US, pressed by Europe, is now more willing to engage seriously in the search for a settlement. But there are also pressing economic reasons for Egypt's decision to enter into the trade agreement. It will give a huge boost to Egyptian textile exports, which are about to suffer a drop after new regulations come into force in the US at the beginning of the year.

Born on 14th March 1909, at North Shields, Northumberland, Horace Cedric Lee was an English cricketer. A right-handed batsman, he bowled with his right arm at medium-fast speed. Lee's cricket career began in 1929 when he represented Northumberland in the Minor Counties Championship against Durham. Prior to World War II, Lee appeared in 67 games for Northumberland in the Minor Counties Championship. In 1935, Lee made his first-class debut for a combined Minor Counties side against Oxford University at the University Parks. The Minor Counties scored 251 runs in their first innings, but lost all wickets for 294 runs in the second. Lee contributed 45 runs in the first innings before being dismissed by Whitehouse. Oxford University scored 23 runs without loss in their second innings, leading to a drawn match. Lee's second first-class appearance came against Ireland in the next season at Observatory Road, Dublin. The Irish team was dismissed for 102 runs, and the Minor Counties managed only 69 runs in response, with Lee scoring 5 runs before being dismissed by James Graham. Ireland scored 179 runs in their second innings, setting the Minor Counties a target of 213 for victory. The Minor Counties could only manage 133 runs, losing all wickets with Lee scoring a single run before being dismissed by the same bowler. After the war, Lee made one more appearance in the Minor Counties Championship for Northumberland against Staffordshire.

Ingredients:

1 cup whole wheat flour

1 cup ricotta cheese

1 egg

1/4 teaspoon salt

1 tablespoon olive oil

1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese

Directions:

2. On a lightly floured surface, roll dough into a 1-inch-thick rope. Cut rope into 1-inch pieces.

3. In a large pot of boiling water, add gnocchi. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, or until they float to the top.

A Spanish football hooligan who stabbed a police officer to the death on the Spanish town of Fuengirola in April has admitted to detectives that he killed and had his victim decapitated.

Rios Romero Gomez, who was known as "Gomez the Jackal", was on Wednesday accused of killing 24-year-old Elisabeth Lopez at Fuengirola, and then "having her head shaved and put into a suitcase in a nearby garden", according to a statement released by prosecutors.

The 31-year-old spent three months in a psychiatric hospital and has since been released and is seeking legal action.

In the four-minute video Gomez admitted to throwing a stone to the officer's face that killed Lopez on April 23 in an incident that resulted in her death. He also said he "honestly believed".

In the video, when asked if he had killed Lopez Lopez answered: "Yes."

Lopez had fallen asleep on a sofa, then woke up, screaming and falling headfirst onto the carpet. Gomez allegedly rushed over and stabbed her several times.

After he was arrested he said she had been a "pig" who stole from others. He claimed he had been trying to clean a sink when the knife got stuck in a piece of metal on the floor.

After the stabbing, he went to the garden where he was joined by three other Fuengirola men. There they threw Lopez' head into the garden and sawed a plastic bag back together – only for Gomez to see them doing the same to a plastic bag containing a dead monkey, and to conclude that he should have used it to wash his hands before going out.

> Abstract: We study magnetic reconnection in two dimensions using resistive MHD simulations with an imposed guide field and periodic boundary conditions. In this configuration, we find that large scale effective potentials can be generated during the early stages of reconnection which reduce ion heating significantly compared to the case without such potentials. These potentials are created due to the presence of a strong guide field and are found to have a characteristic length scale comparable to the system size. This effect is not observed when the guide field is weak or absent. Our results suggest that the generation of these potentials may play an important role in reducing ion heating during magnetic reconnection in astrophysical systems where there is a significant guide field present.

* Olive oil for drizzling

* 1 small lemon, juiced then ½ zested
* 3 tbsp tahini
* 1¼ tsp salt, plus a pinch
* ¼ tsp black pepper
* 2 tbsp pastrami, very finely chopped

Recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have greatly advanced medical image segmentation, an essential requirement for various clinical applications. Yet, CNNs encounter limitations when modeling long-range relationships explicitly. Previous approaches, which involve constructing deep encoders accompanied by forceful downsampling procedures, result in needlessly complex networks and the loss of fine-grained details. To enhance the ability to model global contexts while retaining precise low-level details, there is a need for a more effective segmentation solution. This study introduces a new parallel-in-branch architecture called TransFuse, which integrates Transformers and CNNs concurrently. By employing this design, both global interconnections and intricate spatial details can be effectively captured using shallower structures. Furthermore, a novel fusion method named BiFusion module is introduced to seamlessly merge multi-level features derived from both branches. The experiments conducted demonstrate that TransFuse delivers state-of-the-art performance on multiple 2D and 3D medical image datasets, such as polyps, skin lesions, hips, and prostates. These achievements come with substantial reduction in parameters and enhanced inference speeds.

British-Canadian figure Constance Eaton Hamilton (1862–1945) made history as a government official and advocate. In Winnipeg, she championed for refugees and women's rights before relocating to Toronto. There, she headed the Equal Franchise League, becoming Toronto City Council's inaugural female member and Ontario's first woman holding elective office at the federal, provincial, or municipal levels. Following two tenures, she left to focus on immigrant resettlement, refugee concerns, and gender equality. In 1979, Toronto City Council introduced the Constance E. Hamilton Award for Women's Status. Born in Yorkshire, England, in 1862, she was the daughter of Dr. George Fowler Bodington (1829-1902) and Caroline Mary Eaton (1825-1873). Educated through private tutors, she mastered German and attended the Leipzig Conservatory, excelling as a pianist. Her youth included farming work. Hamilton emigrated to Canada in 1887 with her family, settling in Vancouver. There, she encountered Lauchlan Hamilton, an elder businessman, whom she wed the next year.

The study of data leakage through the connection between confidential info and detectable data falls under the field of information security. Given that total elimination of this correlation isn't achievable, measuring the leakage becomes crucial. Primarily, popular methods for establishing suitable metrics lie within information theory. Among these, an effective approach is the recent $g$-leakage framework, encompassing various information-theoretic techniques. However, a drawback of $g$-leakage is its definition as a minimization problem, which can lead to significant computational complexity in complex systems. In this research, we investigate instances where the system's channel can be broken down into simpler channels, often observed when observables consist of numerous components. Our key contribution involves deriving limits on the (multiplicative variant of) $g$-leakage for the entire system using the component-wise $g$-leakages. We further examine specific cases of min-entropy leakage and parallel channels, extending and unifying prior findings. We validate the efficacy of our methodology and assess the accuracy of our bounds via illustrative examples.

The graphs formed by the edge intersections of paths in a tree (respectively, a grid), namely EPT (EPG), have received significant attention. More recently, we introduced the graph classes Edge-Intersecting and Non-Splitting Paths with one bend in a Tree (ENPT) and in a Grid (ENPG). It was demonstrated that ENPG admits an infinite hierarchy of subclasses derived from limiting the number of bends in the paths. In this study, we concentrate on one-bend ENPG graphs. The graph Laplacian, a crucial instrument in data science, machine learning, and image processing, derives its intricate structure from the underlying network. In specific applications, this matrix is densely populated, leading to challenging computations, particularly matrix-vector products. A common usage involves calculating its eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Traditional techniques become impractical when the graph's node count becomes excessive. We suggest utilizing the fast summation method based on the nonequispaced fast Fourier transform (NFFT) to accomplish sparse dense matrix-vector multiplication with the graph Laplacian efficiently, without constructing the entire matrix. The adaptability of the NFFT algorithm enables us to integrate the expedited multiplication into Lanczos-based eigenvalue routines or iterative linear system solvers and even explore non-standard Gaussian kernels. We demonstrate the viability of our strategy on various test issues, ranging from image segmentation to semi-supervised learning through graph-based PDEs. Notably, we contrast our technique with the Nyström method and introduce and evaluate an advanced, hybrid variant of the Nyström method that employs the NFFT internally.

Quantitative image analysis often depends on accurate classification of
pixels through a segmentation process. However, imaging artifacts such as the
partial volume effect and sensor noise complicate the classification process.
These effects increase the pixel intensity variance of each constituent class,
causing intensities from one class to overlap with another. This increased
variance makes threshold based segmentation methods insufficient due to
ambiguous overlap regions in the pixel intensity distributions. The class
ambiguity becomes even more complex for systems with more than two
constituents, such as unsaturated moist granular media. In this paper, we
propose an image processing workflow that improves segmentation accuracy for
multiphase systems. First, the ambiguous transition regions between classes are
identified and removed, which allows for global thresholding of single-class
regions. Then the transition regions are classified using a distance function,
and finally both segmentations are combined into one classified image. This
workflow includes three methodologies for identifying transition pixels and we
demonstrate on a variety of synthetic images that these approaches are able to
accurately separate the ambiguous transition pixels from the single-class
regions. For situations with typical amounts of image noise, misclassification
errors and area differences calculated between each class of the synthetic
images and the resultant segmented images range from 0.69-1.48% and 0.01-0.74%,
respectively, showing the segmentation accuracy of this approach. We
demonstrate that we are able to accurately segment x-ray microtomography images
of moist granular media using these computationally efficient methodologies.

"Story of O" is an intriguing novel that revolves around the life of a young Parisianne named 'O', who lives a relatively normal life by day but indulges in the world of BDSM and submission at night. Introduced to this alternative lifestyle by her boyfriend René, O embarks on a journey of self-discovery as she learns to navigate and derive pleasure from the pain in a consensual BDSM relationship that eventually leads to her deep transformation.

As the story unfolds, O's experiences become more extreme as she is taken by René to Roissy, a chateau where women are trained in submission through methods ranging from bedroom games, sensory deprivation to physical torment. They are treated as objects for pleasure, with their own desires dismissed or considered secondary. 

The narrative showcases a stark contrast between the sophisticated life O leads as a respected photographer in French society and her enslaved existence in the chateau. As her engagement in submission intensifies, O begins to question her identity and societal norms, getting used to the complexity of her dual life.

The climax sees O fully submitting not only to her master René but also to Sir Stephen, a more dominant figure who places stricter demands on her. O's unflinching surrender to her own desires and choice to devalue societal standards encapsulates the core essence of the novel.

"Story of O" is a gripping exploration of polarizing themes such as power dynamics, human eroticism, sexuality, and depravity. The novel ends with a profound question about the extremities one can go to for love and desire, leaving readers reflecting on the subjective boundary line separating passion and obsession.

Jung considers the Book of Job a landmark development in the "divine drama", for the first time contemplating criticism of God (Gotteskritik). Jung described the book as "pure poison", referring to the controversial nature of the book (Storr, 1973). He did, however, feel an urge to write the book. The basic thesis of the book is that as well as having a good side, God also has a fourth side - the evil face of God. This view is inevitably controversial, but Jung claimed it is backed up by references to the Hebrew Bible. The book, has however, been criticised. For example, it assumes that the John who wrote the fourth Gospel was the same John who wrote The Book of Revelation - which most Bible scholars today dispute. Jung saw this evil side of God as the missing fourth element of the Trinity, which he believed should be supplanted by a Quaternity. However, he also discusses in the book whether the true missing fourth element is the feminine side of God. Indeed, he saw the dogmatic definition of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary by Pope Pius XII in 1950 as being the most significant religious event since the Reformation.

Chelsea have sacked Adrian Mutu after he failed a drugs test.
The 25-year-old tested positive for a banned substance - which he later denied was cocaine - in October. Chelsea have decided to write off a possible transfer fee for Mutu, a £15.8m signing from Parma last season, who may face a two-year suspension. A statement from Chelsea explaining the decision read:"We want to make clear that Chelsea has a zero tolerance policy towards drugs." Mutu scored six goals in his first five games after arriving at Stamford Bridge but his form went into decline and he was frozen out by coach Jose Mourinho. Chelsea's statement added: "This applies to both performance-enhancing drugs or so-called 'recreational' drugs. They have no place at our club or in sport. "In coming to a decision on this case, Chelsea believed the club's social responsibility to its fans, players, employees and other stakeholders in football regarding drugs was more important than the major financial considerations to the company. "Any player who takes drugs breaches his contract with the club as well as Football Association rules. "The club totally supports the FA in strong action on all drugs cases." Fifa's disciplinary code stipulates that a first doping offence should be followed by a six-month ban. And the sport's world governing body has re-iterated their stance over Mutu's failed drugs test, maintaining it is a matter for the domestic sporting authorities. "Fifa is not in a position to make any comment on the matter until the English FA have informed us of their disciplinary decision and the relevant information associated with it," said a Fifa spokesman. Chelsea's move won backing from drug-testing expert Michelle Verroken. Verroken, a former director of drug-free sport for UK Sport, insists the Blues were right to sack Mutu and have enhanced their reputation by doing so. "Chelsea are saying quite clearly to the rest of their players and their fans that this is a situation they are not prepared to tolerate. "It was a very difficult decision for them and an expensive decision for them but the terms of his contract were breached and it was the only decision they could make. "It is a very clear stance by Chelsea and it has given a strong boost to the reputation of the club." It emerged that Mutu had failed a drugs test on October 18 and, although it was initially reported that the banned substance in question was cocaine. The Romanian international later suggested it was a substance designed to enhance sexual performance. The Football Association has yet to act on Mutu's failed drugs test and refuses to discuss his case.

WMH, or white matter hyperintensity, is frequently identified in older adults and linked to various neurological conditions. The U-net architecture, a popular convolutional network utilized extensively in biomedical image segmentation, has effectively been implemented for WMH segmentation. Traditionally, the U-net's weights are initialized randomly. Although this approach allows the model to explore diverse local optima, it may result in inconsistent segmentations due to varying randomly initialized weights. Our research indicates that an ensemble of U-nets with distinct random initializations significantly enhances WMH segmentation accuracy by combining their outputs through thresholding and averaging. To elaborate, we transform the U-net score maps into binary masks using thresholding, then merge these masks by averaging to generate the ultimate WMH segmentation. Our findings, validated through both quantitative evaluation (using the Dice similarity coefficient) and qualitative assessment (through visual inspections), demonstrate the superiority of this method. Importantly, this post-processing strategy is agnostic to the specific U-net implementation. Consequently, it can be adopted in scenarios where alternative deep learning models are employed, particularly when random initialization is selected and pre-training is absent.

Low-quality or incomplete image segmentation is a complex issue. Incorporating statistical information regarding the expected shapes can enhance segmentation outcomes substantially. The majority of shape-based segmentation techniques minimize an energy functional and yield a single estimation of the object to segment. However, this approach lacks the ability to convey the level of certainty in the result or suggest alternative possibilities based on available data and priors. Adopting a probabilistic perspective would necessitate handling the challenge of determining the posterior densities of the objects' shapes. To tackle this, we suggest a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method for image segmentation using statistical shape priors. Besides improving the understanding of the statistical structure of the problem, this strategy could also alleviate concerns related to reaching local optima encountered by current shape-based segmentation techniques. Our approach enables the assessment of the posterior probability density in the shape domain via its samples and offers multiple solutions, possibly representing distinct modes of a multimodal probability distribution, as observed during segmenting objects belonging to various shape categories. We report encouraging findings across numerous datasets. Additionally, we introduce an extension to accommodate segmenting objects with parts undergoing independent shape modifications. This enhancement incorporates local shape priors on object components and fortifies resistance against constraints in shape training data size.

Freddie Threepwood, still trying to persuade his Aunt Georgiana of the benefits of Donaldson's Dog-Joy, hears that his cousin Gertrude has become infatuated with Orlo Watkins, a weedy tenor invited to the castle by Lady Constance. While visiting his friend Beefy Bingham to borrow his dog Bottles, Freddie learns that she has indeed all but "handed him the bird". Freddie tells this to Lady Georgiana, while giving a rather poor demonstration of Dog-Joy's powers, during which Bottles is scared off by Susan, one of Lady Georgiana's Pekes. He later tries to reason with his cousin, but to no avail; the glamour of the singer has taken her over. That evening, while the household take after-dinner coffee in the drawing room, Freddie enters with Bottles and a sack of rats, intending to demonstrate the Dog-Joy reared mongrel's ratcatching prowess; Orlo Watkins, observed by Gertrude, cringes somewhat at the sight. The family protest, and Beach is called to take the bag of rats away. Bottles remains, however, and when one of Lady Georgiana's Airedales comes in, a mighty battle commences. First Minister Jack McConnell has ordered a report on the decision to allow a paranoid schizophrenic knife attacker to go on a visit unguarded.
Michael Ferguson, 36, escaped after being allowed out of the high-security Carstairs unit. The SNP's Nicola Sturgeon has demanded to know who was responsible for signing off the leave. The Scottish Executive said ministers would be notified but it would "not be common practice" to sign approval. An executive spokesman said the health department and the state hospital itself would work together on preparing the report. Ministerial responsibility for Carstairs rests with Rhona Brankin, the deputy health minister. Ms Brankin said: "The first minister has called for a review of what has happened, we need to talk to the state hospital and we need to reflect on this." Ms Sturgeon has written to Mr McConnell asking for clarification on the move to allow the prisoner out. She said questions must be answered about his escape, if the public is to be reassured about safety. Police are still searching for Ferguson, who failed to return after a trip to East Kilbride on Monday.
The Scottish National Party's parliamentary leader argued that under the law, authorisation of Ferguson's leave of absence would have come directly from ministers. She said: "The Scottish Executive seemed to indicate yesterday that the escape of Mr Ferguson was a matter for Carstairs. "However, my understanding is that, under the mental health legislation, the decision to grant this patient - and any restricted patient - leave of absence, would have required direct and specific authorisation by Scottish ministers." She added: "I have written to the first minister today asking for confirmation of that fact. I have also asked him to confirm which minister would routinely take decisions of this nature and what information they are based on. "This is not an attempt to apportion blame, but to ensure a better understanding of the decision making process in such important and sensitive cases."
Police said Ferguson posed a danger to the public. BBC Scotland political correspondent Glenn Campbell said the first minister had ordered an urgent report into the situation. He said: "We understand from the executive that in this case no individual minister signed off the approval for Michael Ferguson to be released unescorted from Carstairs. "The executive concedes that it is up to Scottish ministers, they have a legal responsibility for approving this sort of leave, but they say routinely it is specialised officials that make that decision and simply inform ministers that they have taken it. "But at that stage presumably ministers can ask hard questions and can ask for reassurances that the patient is not a serious danger to the public or that any risk has been minimised." Scottish Conservative leader, David McLetchie, said earlier it was "almost beyond belief that this has been allowed to happen".
The executive spokeswoman said the recommendation for leave was agreed by a psychiatric advisor "in conjunction with officials on behalf of ministers". She said: "Ministers were told of that, notified of it, but it would not be common practice for them to sign it off. "They do have statutory responsibility, but the common practice has been that people who work with the patient and have the best knowledge about risk would make that decision." Ferguson, who slashed a man in a doctors' surgery in Coatbridge in 1994, had been out to see his fiancée Annabella Holmes, 47, whom he met when she was a patient at the high security complex in South Lanarkshire. He is described as being 5ft 9ins tall, slim, with blond hair, blue eyes and a fair complexion. Ferguson was wearing a black jacket, grey jeans, black jumper and black shoes when he was last seen. He has multiple fading tattoos on his left hand and a very faded tear tattoo under his left eye. Ms Holmes is not missing but there have been no sightings of Ferguson since Monday. Strathclyde Police asked anyone who spots Ferguson to contact Sergeant Keith McDonald on
.

A middle-aged man named Paul undergoes a leg amputation after being struck by a careless motorist's vehicle while riding his bicycle. Subsequently, he withdraws into seclusion at his apartment, receiving assistance from various nurses. None manage to connect with him until Marijana arrives; they had both spent their formative years in Europe (her in Croatia, his in France). As Paul's emotions toward Marijana and her adolescent son Drago evolve, complications arise when Marijana's spouse grows wary of Paul's financial support for Drago's education. Consequently, family tensions escalate, leading Drago to leave his father's household and live with Paul. Paul's intricate sentiments towards Marijana and his bitterness about his own post-accident existence are finally addressed upon the arrival of renowned author Elizabeth Costello, who unexpectedly visits Paul without warning. Perplexed by her presence, Paul suspects that she intends to utilize him as a character in her upcoming novel. The narrative may be interpreted as a metafictional exploration of the intricacies shared between the literary creator and fictional characters, as well as reality.

In a small bowl, combine 3/4 cup beer, 1/2 cup Dijon mustard, 7 tbsp honey, 1/3 cup olive oil, 1 tbsp dried rosemary, 3-4 tbsp chopped fresh garlic, and 1 small onion, sliced. Marinate a 2-3 lb boneless pork loin roast in a heavy-duty zip-top plastic bag with this mixture for at least 12 hours in the refrigerator, turning occasionally. Preheat oven to 425°F. Remove roast from marinade, season with salt and pepper, and sear in a roasting pan at 425°F for 20 minutes. Lower oven temperature to 350°F and cook until internal temperature reaches 150°F, approximately 1-1/2 hours. Let rest for 15 minutes before slicing. In a medium saucepan, reduce reserved marinade by simmering with 1/2 cup unwhipped whipping cream. Season with salt and pepper. Serve sliced pork roast on a large platter with a drizzle of sauce, passing the remaining sauce at the table.

We show that, contrary to simple predictions, most AGNs show at best only a
small increase of lags in the J, H, K, and L bands with increasing wavelength.
We suggest that a possible cause of this near simultaneity of the variability
from the near-IR to the mid-IR is that the hot dust is in a hollow bi-conical

Steven Speilberg once asked a friend of mine, "Why didn't anyone like this movie?" Well, I think that I can answer that - "1941" is a gigantic in-joke. The people who are in on the joke are people who, like myself, have an oversized love and knowledge of the city of Los Angeles and it's history. I think that in the vast, world-wide movie-going public, this group probably comprises 1%. For that group, "1941" has a wonderful nostalgia value. And for the people in that 1% that have a twisted sense of humor and enjoy seeing nostalgic L.A. blown to bits, this movie really delivers. By the way, the folks with that twisted sense of humor probably account for about 1% of the original 1%.

I don't know why, but having grown up in L.A. and being an aficionado of it's history, I find it funny to see planes in a dogfight over Hollywood Blvd, the ferris wheel rolling off the end of Santa Monica Pier, and aircraft crashing into the La Brea Tarpits. But for non-locals and people unfamiliar with the paranoia that gripped Southern California in the wake of Pearl Harbor, this movie will likely seem confusing and silly. To the history buff with a twisted sense of humor (like me, proud member of the 1% of the 1%), the movie is not only amusing, but sometimes surprisingly accurate, historically. Robert Stack plays General Joseph Stillwell - a very real historical figure in L.A. history. Stack even bears a striking resemblance to the real General Stillwell. The whole movie is based upon a few real-life incidents of panicky anti-aircraft fire that occurred over L.A. in 1941/1942, as well as a Japanese sub that actually shelled an oil refinery near Santa Barbara. Like "Chinatown" (a film mistakenly thought to be an accurate account of L.A. water politics in the 1930s), "1941" borrows from real-life history and distorts it into pure fabrication. The difference is that while "Chinatown" is a noir drama, "1941" is an over-the-top comedy. Both films appeal to the historian, but as it is often said, comedy is much harder to pull off than drama. You either love "1941", or sit though it, saying, "huh?".

In the central, hilly region of Ghana's Volta Area lies the Siwu language. This language falls under the Niger-Congo family's Kwa subgroup, specifically the Ghana-Togo Mountain languages, also known as the Togorestsprachen or Togo Remnant languages. The Mawu people, who speak Siwu, refer to themselves and their land as Kawu.

Geographical and demographic information
The Siwu language is spoken across eight villages nestled among the mountains, approximately north of Hohoe. The estimated speaker count ranges between 10,000 and 23,000 individuals. The territory of Kawu is split into Akpafu (to the west) and Lolobi (to the east), reflecting a dialectal division. Akpafu's five towns include Tɔdzi, Ɔdɔmi, Mempeasem, Sɔkpoo, and Adɔkɔ. These settlements are situated close to one another, with the first three being positioned on the western side of the Akpafu range, and the last two on the eastern side. The Lolobi towns of Kumasi, Ashiambi, and Huyeasem are more densely populated and are situated in the flatter ground northeast of Hohoe.

Richard "Racehorse" Haynes (April 3, 1927 – April 28, 2017)  was a Texas criminal defense attorney. He became a star of the legal world after prevailing in a series of seemingly impossible murder trials in Texas in the 1970s and 1980s. Time magazine named him one of the top defense attorneys in the nation. Law practice
A native of Houston, Texas, Haynes graduated from the University of Houston Law Center in 1956, and was admitted to the State Bar of Texas on April 23, 1956. He was involved in landmark cases such as The State of Texas v. John Hill (a basis for journalist and author Thomas Thompson's 1976 book Blood and Money), and the notorious T. Cullen Davis murder and later solicitation of murder trials in Fort Worth, Texas, both of which ended in acquittals. He also represented Morganna, a.k.a. "The Kissing Bandit,"  and Vicki Daniel, who was the wife of Price Daniel Jr. His successful defense of Vicki Daniel established battered woman syndrome as a legal defense in the state of Texas.

Their cause is not clear and I can't help

Though I feel an undeniable sense of compassion

For some of them, I do want to do something about it;

But I'm too selfish and I don't feel ready to give

To others, because I know that it's a crime

To be poor. I am convinced that the cause of

That very poverty lies not in our greed, but in

Our stupidity.I want to change this and do something;

But first I'll have to go away and think about it first;

Though I'm already so busy that I haven't a chance

To visit a poor person, I am looking forward to

That day when I do visit. And for that reason

I want to have some time to reflect.

When I look into my mirror every day

And consider myself, I see a thin, dirty face.

You can see every line of that face is stretched tight.

It's hard for me to think of who I used to be

When I look into that mirror. I'm too old to do it

Any more. There's no one left, only this one

Still trying to survive.I can't help but think that I

Could have done more, given this life more time.

I know I'm too much of a coward

To take any action, this one has no life now;

But after I've left it here, then maybe

If I see it again, then I'll be forced to act

I'd give anything to change this and do something;

I have to change my life and make some change.

I'm too old, I can't do that any more,

But I know I'll have to leave it out here;

Perhaps if I can see it again, then

My children can see it too. You think my children are

Poor? No, they've got everything they need.

They must be better off than I was

When I was young.

Born circa 1898 as Gwendolyn Hinton Perry to first cousin parents Irma Perry (née Hinton) and Roland Hinton Perry, Gwen Le Gallienne spent her formative years in America before relocating to England to establish herself as a painter and sculptor. Notable for defying societal conventions and garnering attention since the 1920s, Gwen's unconventional lifestyle set her apart, even within the Montparnasse bohemian community.

A California-based defense and telecommunications company, Titan Corporation, has consented to pay $28.5m following its acknowledgment of bribery in Benin, West Africa. The firm admitted to channelling over $2m into President Mathieu Kerekou's 2001 re-election campaign during negotiations for a higher telecommunications project price. No evidence implicates Mr. Kerekou personally in any misconduct. Titan confessed to account falsification and breaching US anti-bribery regulations. The corporation will pay $13m in criminal fines and an additional $15.5m to resolve a civil lawsuit initiated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The SEC alleged that Titan paid $2.1m to an intermediary in Benin claimed to have connections to President Kerekou. Some funds were reportedly utilized for producing election campaign T-shirts bearing slogans prior to the 2001 elections. Post-election, Benin authorities granted Titan a fourfold increase in management fees. United States Attorney Carol Lam stated, "US companies must understand that endeavoring to bribe foreign officials constitutes illicit activity and will be subjected to prosecution." Titan declared its intolerance towards such behaviors. As per the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, it is illegal for American enterprises to offer bribes to foreign officials.

18 ounces milk chocolate, finely chopped
10 ounces semisweet or bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped
1 1/2 cups sugar
2 1/4 cups heavy cream
1/2 tablespoon fine sea salt
1 1/2 sticks room temperature unsalted butter, cut into cubes
1 Chocolate Cake recipe, recipe follows
Sea salt flakes (recommended: Maldon)
2 sticks unsalted butter, softened, plus more for greasing pan
2 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda
1/2 teaspoon sea salt
1 1/4 cup packed light brown sugar
1/2 cup granulated sugar
4 eggs, at room temperature for 30 minutes
1/3 cup semisweet chocolate, melted and cooled
2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
1 1/2 cups well-shaken buttermilk (or 1 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice)
Put your chocolates in a big bowl. Put the sugar and 1/2 cup water in a saucepan and place over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves and bring up to a boil. As soon that happens, stop stirring and let it boil until it turns an amber color, 8 to 10 minutes or so. (If you think that it needs another stir, brush down the sides of the pan with a wet pastry brush, and stir the entire mixture, picking up the pot itself by the handle, being careful not to touch the caramel or else it could crystallize.) Once the mixture reaches that dark amber color, turn the heat down. Stand back from the pot and add the cream very slowly, stirring with a heatproof spatula. (If you are nervous about the steam, wear a kitchen glove to protect your hand.) Continue to stir until all is incorporated. Once the mixture is smooth, stir in the fine salt. Take off the heat and pour the caramel over the bowl of chocolate. Whisk to combine, making sure all the chocolate melts. Pop in the fridge for about 1 hour until completely chilled. Take the frosting out of the fridge and beat it with a hand mixer just until it becomes spreadable. Add the butter in pieces and mix until it's all combined. Pop back into the refrigerator for another hour. Place 1 cake layer on a cake platter, flat-side up. (You want the cake flat-side up so when you get into it you'll have nice and even layers.) Evenly spread 2 cups of the frosting over the top. Sprinkle with sea salt flakes, then put the other cake layer on top, flat-side up. Spread the rest of the frosting over the top and on the sides of the cake. Sprinkle the top with more salt flakes. Put a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Butter 2 (9 by 2-inch) nonstick round cake pans. Line the bottom of each with a round of parchment paper, and then butter the paper. Sift the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt together onto parchment paper. With an electric mixer on medium-high speed, cream the butter and sugars until light and fluffy, 4 or 5 minutes. Add your eggs, 1 at a time, mixing until completely incorporated before adding each additional egg. Mix in the chocolate and vanilla, making sure to combine really well. Turn the mixer to low and slowly add the dry ingredients, alternating with the buttermilk, in 3 batches, starting and ending with the flour mixture. Make sure to let it mix thoroughly. Pour half the batter in each pan and spread it evenly with a spatula or butter knife. Bake until a toothpick comes out clean, 25 minutes. Remove the pans to racks and allow the cakes to cool for 10 minutes or so. Loosen the edges of the cake from the pan with a knife, then turn them onto the racks. Remove the paper and let the cakes completely cool. Yield: 2 (9-inch) cake layers

Foulk Road, identified as DE 261 in Delaware and PA 261 in Pennsylvania, serves as a state highway traversing both states. DE 261 originates in New Castle County, Delaware, starting from an intersection with US 202 and DE 141, north of I-95 in Fairfax, and extends to the Pennsylvania state boundary. This road passes through the residential districts of Brandywine Hundred as a four-lane highway below DE 92 and as a two-lane road above it. Upon entering Pennsylvania, Foulk Road transforms into PA 261 and proceeds through Bethel Township in Delaware County. It intersects PA 491 in Booths Corner and concludes at an interchange with US 322. DE 261's history can be traced back to the 1930s when it was initially marked along Foulk Road. During the 1960s, the majority of the route underwent expansion into a four-lane highway. The southern terminus at US 202 was rebuilt as an interchange during the 2000s. PA 261 was first established in 1928, following Foulk Road from the Delaware border to PA 61 and PA 161 in Chelsea. By 1940, the route had been extended northward along Valley Brook Road to US 1 in Chester Heights. The present northern terminus of PA 261 was established by 1980.

The UK's first ever banning of a AI-powered chatbot has occurred, with the High Court ordering that the chatbot "Collins" cannot be used in court proceedings. This landmark decision sets a precedent for how AI technology is to be used in the future. The case, which was brought by the Bar Council, argued that the use of AI in court proceedings risked undermining the public's trust in the justice system. 

The ban on Collins, which was developed by the company ROSS Intelligence, Inc., stems from the concern that allowing AI to participate in legal proceedings may threaten the integrity of court proceedings. The judge argued that allowing Collins to contribute alongside humans creates an errant hybrid of human and AI participation, and that this goes against the core of legal proceedings in the UK. 

While this decision marks a turning point in the use of AI in the UK, it's unclear what the future holds for AI technology in the country. With this decision, the UK has set a standard for the legal industry, but it's unclear if other industries will follow suit. While AI offers unprecedented potential and advancement, clearly defining the boundaries and regulations of AI technology is becoming increasingly more urgent.
