Ingredients:
- 1 block of firm tofu
- 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro
- 1/4 cup of chopped scallions
- 2 cloves of minced garlic
- 1 tablespoon of soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil
- 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon of sesame oil
- 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper
- 6 egg roll wrappers
- 1 avocado
- Salt

Instructions:
1. Drain the tofu and cut it into small cubes.
2. In a pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and add the minced garlic.
3. Once the garlic is fragrant, add the chopped scallions and black pepper.
4. Add the cubed tofu to the pan and cook for about 5 minutes until it is lightly browned.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and salt to taste.
6. Pour the sauce over the tofu and stir to coat.
7. Add the chopped cilantro and stir to combine.
8. Lay out the egg roll wrappers and place a spoonful of the tofu mixture in the center of each wrapper.
9. Slice the avocado and place a few slices on top of the tofu mixture.
10. Fold the wrapper over the tofu mixture and tuck in the sides.
11. Roll the egg roll tightly and seal the end with a little water.
12. Heat a pan with vegetable oil over medium heat and add the egg rolls.
13. Cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown.
14. Serve the egg rolls with your favorite dipping sauce and enjoy!

Let D be a bounded domain in n-dimensional Eucledian space with a smooth
boundary. We indicate appropriate Sobolev spaces of negative smoothness to
study the non-homogeneous Cauchy problem for an elliptic differential complex
{A_i} of first order operators. In particular, we describe traces on the
boundary of tangential part t_i (u) and normal part n_i(u) of a
(vector)-function u from the corresponding Sobolev space and give an adequate
formulation of the problem. If the Laplacians of the complex satisfy the
uniqueness condition in the small then we obtain necessary and sufficient
solvability conditions of the problem and produce formulae for its exact and
approximate solutions. For the Cauchy problem in the Lebesgue spaces L^2(D) we
construct the approximate and exact solutions to the Cauchy problem with
maximal possible regularity. Moreover, using Hilbert space methods, we
construct Carleman's formulae for a (vector-) function u from the Sobolev space
H^1(D) by its Cauchy data t_i (u) on a subset S on the boundary of the domain D
and the values of A_i u in D modulo the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Some
instructive examples for elliptic complexes of operators with constant
coefficients are considered.

Chop 4 oz bittersweet (not unsweetened) or semisweet chocolate and set aside. In a large bowl, combine 3/4 cup sugar, 6 tbsp (3/4 stick) room temperature unsalted butter, and 1 tsp vanilla extract using an electric mixer. Add egg yolks one at a time, beating well after each addition. Melt the chocolate in a double boiler over simmering water, then remove from heat and let it cool for 10 minutes. With the electric mixer running, add the cooled chocolate to the butter-sugar mixture and blend. Fold in 1/2 cup ground poppy seeds. In a separate large bowl, use the electric mixer with clean, dry beaters to whip the egg whites until they form stiff peaks but are not dry. Gently fold half of the egg whites into the chocolate mixture. Fold in 2 tbsp flour. Fold in the remaining egg whites. Pour batter into a greased and floured 9-inch springform pan and smooth the top. Bake at 350°F for approximately 45 minutes, or until a tester comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack (can be made one day ahead, covered with aluminum foil and kept at room temperature). Loosen cake from sides of pan, remove sides, and sift powdered sugar over the top. Serve with whipped cream.

One of the standout aspects of Draft Day is its portrayal of the relationships between the characters. From Sonny's strained relationship with his wife to the bond between him and his daughter, the film explores themes of family, loyalty, and sacrifice. For many, many days together
The wind blew steady from the East;
For many days hot grew the weather,
About the time of our Lady's Feast.
For many days we rode together,
Yet met we neither friend nor foe;
Hotter and clearer grew the weather,
Steadily did the East wind blow.
We saw the trees in the hot, bright weather,
Clear-cut, with shadows very black,
As freely we rode on together
With helms unlaced and bridles slack.
And often, as we rode together,
We, looking down the green-bank'd stream,
Saw flowers in the sunny weather,
And saw the bubble-making bream.
And in the night lay down together,
And hung above our heads the rood,
Or watch'd night-long in the dewy weather,
The while the moon did watch the wood.
Our spears stood bright and thick together,
Straight out the banners stream'd behind,
As we gallop'd on in the sunny weather,
With faces turn'd towards the wind.
Down sank our threescore spears together,
As thick we saw the pagans ride;
His eager face in the clear fresh weather,
Shone out that last time by my side.
Up the sweep of the bridge we dash'd together,
It rock'd to the crash of the meeting spears,
Down rain'd the buds of the dear spring weather,
The elm-tree flowers fell like tears.
There, as we roll'd and writhed together,
I threw my arms above my head,
For close by my side, in the lovely weather,
I saw him reel and fall back dead.
I and the slayer met together,
He waited the death-stroke there in his place,
With thoughts of death, in the lovely weather,
Gapingly mazed at my madden'd face.
Madly I fought as we fought together;
In vain: the little Christian band
The pagans drown'd, as in stormy weather
The river drowns low-lying land.
They bound my blood-stain'd hands together,
They bound his corpse to nod by my side:
Then on we rode, in the bright March weather,
With clash of cymbals did we ride.
We ride no more, no more together;
My prison-bars are thick and strong,
I take no heed of any weather,
The sweet Saints grant I live not long.

O God, our sanctuary and bulwark,
When we place our trust in Thee,
The enemy has pierced Thy chosen,
With an infamous, shameful gore.
History repeats itself once more,
A Trojan horse conceals the war,
Intending to slaughter innocents,
Inflicting nine-eleven's grim events.
They dare challenge an army grand,
Which boasts Thy sovereignty, O Lord,
Save us from their clutches,
And sharpen Your mighty sword.
Our Father in the heavens above,
Protect us, Your weapon of war,
Guard us as Your repossessed,
Until Babylon is put to the test.
May You grant us righteous triumph,
In Your name, the victor supreme,
So shall all the world declare,
"In God We Trust," forevermore.
O Lord, our solid rock and stronghold,
Protect "The Land of the Free,"
Strengthen us until Shiloh appears,
Then claim Your prize, the ultimate reward.
He ends all conflicts to the very end,
Splitting bows, shattering swords asunder,
To the flames of chariots, He ascends,
"Fear not, for I am God:
Exalted among the nations,
Exalted upon the earth."*
The Lord Almighty is our shield,
Our fortress, our everlasting appeal.
Bless us in our pursuits, we implore,
In Jesus' name, we humbly implore.
*Psalms 46: 10, Inspired by Jeremiah Chapters 50 and 51

I've had this experience before. For me it was sort of a psychological block on getting the music going in a direction that didn't fit the lyrics, so the music was locked into a certain rhythm/melody that I knew was "wrong" for the lyrics, but I couldn't break out of it... sometimes you just have to walk away for a while and come back to it later. Sometimes it means the melody/rhythm you're writing simply isn't right for the lyrics, and you have to scrap it and start over from scratch.

As others have said, it can be helpful to jam on the chords and see if anything new presents itself, or to start singing random notes or lyrics over the chords (exactly what you were doing), until something clicks.

For others, it can help to talk/sing the lyrics aloud as if you're having a conversation, and then sing/speak the tones/rhythms of your speech back into a melody.

Sometimes when I'm really stuck in this situation, I'll reduce the lyrics to just a few key words, or even a single word, and use that as the seed for the melody. I find that once I have a good melody, I can usually modify it to fit the actual lyrics, if I need to.

The acclaimed work of Raimi and his team, "The Evil Dead," merits further discussion despite being as exhaustively analyzed as a reanimated corpse plagued by Ash. Preceding the era of Spiderman and its subsequent spin-offs, these filmmakers embarked on a low-budget zombie production primarily for amusement. In retrospect, it transcended expectations, becoming a terrifying and horrifying masterpiece. Despite its meager resources and occasional wavering performances, "The Evil Dead" manages to frighten and unsettle viewers through its haunting ambiance and groundbreaking special effects. For those with weak constitutions, a hasty retreat is strongly advised.

Several factors contribute to the film's success. First, Raimi's cinematography is remarkable. Through rapid camera movements and intense shots, he crafts a disquieting universe that is both difficult to endure yet impossible to look away from. His distinctive directorial style is undeniably evident. This is vividly demonstrated in the opening scene, where the camera itself generates an apprehensive mood, leaving you nervously anticipating the impending terror. At any instant, you sense someone could have their throat torn apart by a lurking zombie concealed off-camera. An opening of unparalleled tension and pacing. The excitement only intensifies when the action unfolds. Certain shots linger indefinitely, evoking a conflicting desire for respite from the graphic brutality or a perverse enjoyment of it. A standout shot involves the encroaching darkness from the woods, toppling any tree or obstacle in its path. An awe-inspiring technique, albeit the method remains uncertain.

Additionally, "The Evil Dead" employs practical effects that remain startlingly effective today. The use of prosthetics, makeup, and animatronics adds a tangible sense of dread and visceral horror to the proceedings, making it all the more memorable and impactful. These elements, combined with the inventive camerawork, create a cinematic experience that continues to influence and inspire horror films to this day.

3 small russet potatoes
1 head garlic (12-14 cloves. It's a LOT. Be afraid.)
1/3 cup fresh lemon juice
1/2 tablespoon salt
1/2 cup canola oil
Peel the potatoes and boil in water until soft. Mash and let cool. Crush and peel a whole head of garlic. Cut into quarters. Place raw garlic in a heavy duty blender with the salt and lemon juice. Pour a light layer of oil onto garlic. Puree the garlic, salt lemon juice on high and begin pouring a slow steady stream of the rest of the oil through the blender's handle hole until everything has mixed. At this point, you'll have extreme garlickiness (new word), which some people like, but for "texturizing" like Zankou's, you'll need the taters. Add the mashed potatoes, about 2-3 tablespoons at a time and mix. Continue adding/blending potato until the sauce is mixed well. At some point in this process, you might consider changing blending vessels. After all this work, my blender was starting to think twice about helping me out. Transfer to a bowl and allow to chill completely in the fridge. After about an hour, the flavors will blend together nicely and the texture will take on that library paste consistency like Zankou's sauce.

The Alden staRRcar, short for "Self-Transport Road and Rail Car", was a personal rapid transit (PRT) system designed by William Alden in the 1960s. It originally envisioned small electrically powered cars suitable for short distance trips at low speed within urban areas, which could optionally merge onto tracks that would provide power and guidance for high-speed travel over longer inter-city distances. It was one of the earliest dual-mode vehicles to be proposed, and one of the earliest to be actually built. Over its lifetime the design changed dramatically, originally a four-person vehicle with dual-mode operation but eventually emerging as a much larger people mover for 20 people. In this form, Boeing Vertol was awarded a construction contract in 1970 to build a demonstration system in Morgantown, West Virginia. A smaller system was also built by their licensee, Kobe Steel, and installed at the Expo '75 on Okinawa (as well as the more advanced CVS). The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system first opened for service in 1975, and with the exception of a closure for a major expansion, has remained in service since then.

This paper introduces Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRW-Net) for semantic image segmentation as a combination of convolutional neural networks, random walks on graphs and spectral graph theory. The basic idea is to extend the receptive field of a neural network's convolutional layer at a minimal cost. Given a CNN, CRW-Net extends the receptive field by one convolutional layer which has random connections to the original CNN's convolutional layers. The randomness comes from the random choice of edges in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs). To solve the issue of overfitting in GCN-based models, We proposed a loss function called graph spectral loss. We empirically show that the proposed method can improve segmentation performance when it is combined with fully connected CRF on PASCAL VOC 2012 (segmentation accuracy 71.2\%), VOCS (segmentation accuracy 77.1\%) and COCO-Stuff (segmentation accuracy 51.2\%). Our proposed method achieved the state-of-the-art performance on COCO-Stuff, outperformed the previous best result by more than 3\%.

Do the papers get cited on Google Scholar? If not, what is the primary use case for authors to release papers on arxiv.org?

A: ArXiv is not a publication venue; it is an archive.  They have an agreement that once an author publishes on the archive, he/she will not post the work elsewhere for at least a month, which is why you see one-month "first notice of use."  That protects the author in case somebody sees the work, then publishes something on it earlier.

A: The primary use of arxiv is to provide a quick way for researchers to distribute their work to a large audience before peer review. Once posted, the paper can be immediately cited, discussed, etc., while the researchers work on tweaking / fixing their paper.
For example, if an author finds a minor error in their arXiv posted paper, they can make the corrections and repost it

Over the last ten years, Deep Convolutional Neural Networks have become popular for medical image segmentation, delivering satisfactory results. Nevertheless, these networks are limited by the innate biases embedded in their convolutional structures, preventing them from comprehending long-range connections within the image. More recent Transformer-based designs, which employ self-attention mechanisms, can encode long-range dependencies and create highly descriptive representations. Motivated by these advancements, we aim to investigate Transformer-based alternatives and assess their applicability to medical image segmentation tasks. Most existing Transformer models suggested for computer vision tasks demand substantial training data. In contrast, medical imaging datasets contain fewer instances, posing challenges for transformer training. To address these concerns, we suggest a Gated Axial-Attention model that enhances current frameworks with an extra control component in the self-attention module. Additionally, we introduce a Local-Global (LoGo) training approach to enhance the model's effectiveness on medical images. By working on both the entire image and its patches, we focus on acquiring global and local characteristics, respectively. Our Medical Transformer (MedT) is tested on three distinct medical image segmentation datasets and outperforms convolutional and related transformer-based architectures according to the evaluations. Fiat's board has approved a deal to give GM a $2.8bn (£1.7bn) stake in its auto business, clearing a major obstacle to a merger of the two carmakers.

The deal had been delayed as Fiat's board debated GM's offer and fought off a rival bid from Ford.

The merger will create the world's third-biggest carmaker by sales.

The combined company will be called Fiat-GM and be headed by Fiat's CEO, Sergio Marchionne.

The deal must still be approved by regulators and shareholders.

If it goes through, GM will get a 20% stake in Fiat, while Fiat will get a 1.5% stake in GM.

The companies said the deal would save them $2.8bn a year by 2015.

The merger has been approved by the boards of both companies but still needs the go-ahead from regulators and shareholders.

If the merger is approved, the new company would be worth about $140bn, based on the companies' current market values.

By comparison, Toyota is currently the world's biggest carmaker with sales of 10.2 million vehicles last year, followed by Volkswagen with 8.3 million.

Fiat-GM would sell about 8.6 million cars a year.

The merger deal comes as the auto industry struggles to recover from a sharp drop in sales in the US and Europe.

The combined company will have about $132bn in debt, ranking it as one of the most indebted companies in the world.

GM sold a record 4.7 million cars and trucks in 2010 but analysts say it needs to expand to survive as sales growth slows in its main markets.

Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornmeal
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 package (2 1/4 teaspoons) active dry yeast
- 1 cup warm water (110°F)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 cup pizza sauce
- 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1/2 cup sliced pepperoni
- 1/4 cup sliced black olives (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced green bell peppers (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced red onions (optional)
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Fresh basil leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, salt, and sugar. In a separate small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until it becomes frothy.

2. Pour the yeast mixture and olive oil into the dry ingredients. Stir until a dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour. If it's too dry, add a little more water. Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.

3. Grease a deep-dish pizza pan or a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Press the dough into the pan, making sure to cover the bottom and sides evenly. Let the dough rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes until it doubles in size.

4. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Once the dough has risen, spread the pizza sauce evenly over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges. Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce.

5. Arrange the pepperoni slices on top of the cheese. If desired, add black olives, green bell peppers, and red onions as additional toppings. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the toppings.

6. Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is bubbly and slightly browned.

7. Remove the pizza from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh basil leaves if desired. Slice and serve hot.

Enjoy your delicious homemade Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza!

Deep learning techniques for 3D brain vessel image segmentation have not been
as successful as in the segmentation of other organs and tissues. This can be
explained by two factors. First, deep learning techniques tend to show poor
performances at the segmentation of relatively small objects compared to the
size of the full image. Second, due to the complexity of vascular trees and the
small size of vessels, it is challenging to obtain the amount of annotated
training data typically needed by deep learning methods. To address these
problems, we propose a novel annotation-efficient deep learning vessel
segmentation framework. The framework avoids pixel-wise annotations, only
requiring weak patch-level labels to discriminate between vessel and non-vessel
2D patches in the training set, in a setup similar to the CAPTCHAs used to
differentiate humans from bots in web applications. The user-provided weak
annotations are used for two tasks: 1) to synthesize pixel-wise pseudo-labels
for vessels and background in each patch, which are used to train a
segmentation network, and 2) to train a classifier network. The classifier
network allows to generate additional weak patch labels, further reducing the
annotation burden, and it acts as a noise filter for poor quality images. We
use this framework for the segmentation of the cerebrovascular tree in
Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Images (SWI). The
results show that the framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, while
reducing the annotation time by ~77% w.r.t. learning-based segmentation methods
using pixel-wise labels for training.

Renowned Dutch trainer Rinus Michels, known as "The General," passed away at the age of 77. In the Netherlands, he managed their team during the 1974 World Cup finals, where they lost 2-1 against Germany. Nevertheless, Michels led them to victory in the 1988 European Championship, winning 2-0 against the Soviet Union. While playing for Ajax, Michels helped secure four Dutch championships from 1965 to 1971, along with a European Cup triumph in 1971. During the 1970s, his Dutch squad, featuring Johan Cruyff and Johan Neeskens, popularized the concept of "total football" worldwide. This innovative approach emphasized collective team spirit and individual creativity, allowing each player to adapt to various positions on the field. Cruyff served as the captain and tactical mastermind for this flexible squad, which seamlessly switched defensive roles and showcased captivating offensive play. Following heart surgery, KNVB spokesperson Frank Huizinga stated, "Michels was one of our greatest coaches." Besides his tenure with Ajax, Michels coached Barcelona to a Spanish title in 1974, FC Cologne, and Bayer Leverkusen. FIFA honored him as the century's top coach in 1999. Dutch sports minister Clemence Ross-van Dorp added, "Michels, alongside Cruyff, transformed Dutch football into a global phenomenon."

General Sir John Gordon Noel Wilton,  (22 November 1910 – 10 May 1981) was a senior commander in the Australian Army. He served as Chief of the General Staff (CGS), the Army's professional head, from 1963 until 1966, and as Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (CCOSC), forerunner of the role of Australia's Chief of the Defence Force, from 1966 until 1970. His eight-year tenure as senior officer of first the Army and then the Australian military spanned almost the entire period of the nation's involvement in the Vietnam War. Born in Sydney, Wilton entered the Royal Military College, Duntroon, in 1927. Owing to lack of opportunity in the Australian military at the time, he took a commission in the British Army following his graduation in 1930. He spent most of the remainder of the decade with the Royal Artillery in India. Wilton returned to Australia on the eve of World War II and was commissioned into the Royal Australian Artillery. He saw action with the 7th Division in Syria and the 3rd Division in New Guinea, earning a mention in despatches in the former campaign and the Distinguished Service Order in the latter.  Finishing the war a temporary colonel, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1947. Wilton was posted to Korea in 1953 to take command of the 28th Commonwealth Brigade, leading it in its final action of the war in July. He was raised to Commander of the Order of the British Empire and awarded the US Legion of Merit for his performance in Korea.

Bradley Sinopoli (born April 14, 1988) is a former Canadian football wide receiver who played for nine years in the Canadian Football League (CFL). He was originally a quarterback with the Calgary Stampeders before being converted to wide receiver in 2013. He then joined the Ottawa Redblacks where he was twice named the CFL's Most Outstanding Canadian, was named an East Division All-Star three times, and a CFL All-Star in 2018. Sinopoli played CIS football for the Ottawa Gee-Gees from 2007 to 2010. In 2010, Sinopoli became the fourth Gee-Gee player to win the Hec Crighton Trophy after passing for a school record and CIS leading 2,756 passing yards and 22 touchdowns in eight games. Because of his strong season, he was one of only two quarterbacks invited to the CFL Evaluation Camp for players eligible in the 2011 CFL Draft.

The study focuses on the lexicographically smallest infinite word that is free of $a/b$-powers in the alphabet of non-negative integers. Often, this word is a fixpoint of a uniform morphism or closely linked to one. An instance is the lexicographically least $7/4$-power-free word, which is a fixpoint of a $50847$-uniform morphism. We determine the structure of the lexicographically smallest $a/b$-power-free word for three major classes of rational numbers $a/b$, alongside several "isolated" rationals that don't fit into these categories. To achieve this goal, we create an automated method for verifying $a/b$-power-freedom for certain morphisms, applicable to both explicit and symbolic rational numbers $a/b$. Furthermore, we relate this concept to words on a finite alphabet. Specifically, the lexicographically smallest $27/23$-power-free word turns out to be a word comprised of symbols from the set $\{0, 1, 2\}$, and its letter sequence is $353$-automatic.

The four defendants were the masterminds behind a popular peer-to-peer file-sharing website called "MegaUpload," which allowed users to store and share files, including copyrighted content such as movies, TV shows, music, and software, without permission from the copyright holders. The site was shut down by the FBI in 2012 following an investigation that revealed the massive scale of copyright infringement taking place on the site. 

The jury found that the defendants were aware of the widespread copyright infringement taking place on MegaUpload but took no meaningful action to prevent it. In a statement, the U.S. Attorney's Office said that the defendants "made a profit by encouraging, promoting, and assisting the widespread distribution of copyrighted materials without the permission of the copyright owners." 

The four defendants face a maximum sentence of five years in prison and significant financial penalties for their role in operating MegaUpload. The sentencing hearing is scheduled for later this year.

In this paper, we explore the concept of higher order differentiation over finite fields and its applications in cryptography, specifically in the context of generalizing the cube attack. We introduce a new technique for computing higher order derivatives of functions over finite fields, which enables us to analyze and improve the security of cryptographic primitives.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique by applying it to several examples of cryptographic functions, including the S-box and the AES encryption algorithm. Our results show that higher order differentiation can be a powerful tool for analyzing and breaking cryptographic primitives, and that our technique provides a significant improvement over existing methods.

Furthermore, we use our technique to generalize the cube attack, a well-known attack on block ciphers, to a higher order attack that can break more rounds of the encryption algorithm. Our results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach, and highlight the importance of considering higher order differential properties in the design and analysis of cryptographic primitives.

Overall, our work provides a new perspective on the study of cryptographic functions and their differential properties, and demonstrates the potential of higher order differentiation as a tool for analyzing and improving the security of cryptographic primitives.

Mary Jane Blige (; born January 11, 1971) is an American singer, songwriter and actress. Her career began in 1991 when she was signed to Uptown Records. In 1992, Blige released her debut album, What's the 411?, which is credited for introducing the mix of R&B and hip hop into mainstream pop culture. Its 1993 remix album became the first album by a singer to have a rapper on every song, popularizing rap as a featuring act. Both What's the 411? and her 1994 album My Life are featured on the Rolling Stones 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list, and the latter on Time magazine's All-Time 100 Albums. Throughout her career, Blige went on to release 14 studio albums, all of which have reached the top ten on the Billboard 200 chart, including four number-one albums. Her biggest hits include "Real Love", "Not Gon' Cry", "Be Without You" and the Billboard Hot 100 number-one single "Family Affair".

Form dough into a ball and smooth out any inconsistencies, then divide it into eight portions. Press each portion into a disc shape, cover them with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for an hour. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Combine all filling ingredients in a medium bowl and set aside. Roll out a disc of dough on a lightly floured surface into an 8x8 inch square. Spread approximately 1/4 cup of the filling over the center of the dough, maintaining a 1/2-inch border along the edges. Roll up the dough from the top edge, creating a tight log. Slice the log into 3/4-inch thick pieces using a sharp knife, discarding the end pieces. Arrange the Rugelach slices on an ungreased baking sheet and repeat this process with the remaining dough discs. Brush the tops of each cookie with beaten egg and sprinkle with granulated sugar. Cook for around 20 minutes in the preheated oven until they turn golden brown. Allow the Rugelach to cool on wire racks.

First, remove the skin and pin bones from the salmon fillet using needle-nose pliers. Place the fillet, skin-side down, in a shallow metal baking dish. Juice the lemons over the fish and scatter them, along with the quartered onions, parsley, basil, thyme, and oregano, garlic powder, and onion powder over the fillet. Add the Chardonnay and water to the pan. Cover the pan with plastic wrap followed by aluminum foil. Cook at 375-400 degrees Fahrenheit for around 30 minutes. Test doneness with a thermometer; cook until internal temperature is between 130-140 degrees Fahrenheit. Let rest for 15-20 minutes before removing the covering. Discard the lemon and onion pieces, draining the pan juices. To transfer the salmon from the pan, cover it with new plastic wrap and carefully turn the pan upside down onto the plastic. Lift the fillet off the plastic wrap and place it on a serving platter. Decorate with Italian parsley, tomato roses, or thin lemon slices. Refrigerate for at least an hour prior to serving with Creamy Dill Sauce.

Chips (1940–1946) was a trained sentry dog for United States Army, and reputedly the most decorated war dog from World War II. Chips was a German Shepherd-Collie-Husky mix owned by Edward J. Wren of Pleasantville, New York. During the war, private citizens like Wren donated their dogs for duty. Chips shipped out to the War Dog Training Center, Front Royal, Virginia, in 1942 for training as a sentry dog. He served with the 3rd Infantry Division in North Africa, Sicily, Italy, France and Germany.  His handler was Pvt. John P. Rowell.  Chips served as a sentry dog for the Roosevelt-Churchill conference in 1943. Later that year, during the invasion of Sicily, Chips and his handler were pinned down on the beach by an Italian machine-gun team.  Chips broke from his handler and jumped into the pillbox, attacking the gunners. The four crewmen were forced to leave the pillbox and surrendered to US troops. In the fight, he sustained a scalp wound and powder burns.  Later that day, he helped take ten Italians prisoner.

Deep learning methods have achieved promising performance in many areas, but
they are still struggling with noisy-labeled images during the training
process. Considering that the annotation quality indispensably relies on great
expertise, the problem is even more crucial in the medical image domain. How to
eliminate the disturbance from noisy labels for segmentation tasks without
further annotations is still a significant challenge. In this paper, we
introduce our label quality evaluation strategy for deep neural networks
automatically assessing the quality of each label, which is not explicitly
provided, and training on clean-annotated ones. We propose a solution for
network automatically evaluating the relative quality of the labels in the
training set and using good ones to tune the network parameters. We also design
an overfitting control module to let the network maximally learn from the
precise annotations during the training process. Experiments on the public
biomedical image segmentation dataset have proved the method outperforms
baseline methods and retains both high accuracy and good generalization at
different noise levels.

Although deep convolutional neural networks have made significant strides in medical image processing and diagnosis, their reliance on supervised learning necessitates a substantial amount of labeled data to prevent overfitting and ensure satisfactory outcomes. However, acquiring extensive semantic annotations in clinical settings can be challenging when specialized biomedical expertise is required and limited annotated classes are accessible. To address this challenge, we present a novel approach for few-shot medical image segmentation, which allows a segmentation model to effectively adapt to a new class with minimal training samples. Our few-shot image segmenter is designed using a deep convolutional network that undergoes episodic training. Inspired by the consistent and uniform characteristics of medical images, we created an efficient global correlation module to identify the relationship between a reference and target image and incorporate it into the deep architecture, referred to as the global correlation network. Furthermore, we boosted the distinguishing ability of deep embeddings to promote clustering of identical class features while maintaining a sufficient separation between distinct organ feature domains. An ablation study validated the significance of the proposed global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on abdominal imaging data from both CT and MRI scans to showcase the superior performance of our suggested model.

The demand for sign language interpretation is rapidly growing, particularly for the deaf community. Few research teams attempt to automatically identify sign language from videos using technologies like colored gloves. These methods necessitate dividing the data used for training and recognition into distinct sections. Recognizing sign language image sequences is complex due to the diverse range of hand shapes and motions. In this study, we suggest employing a blend of image segmentation and restoration using topological derivatives to achieve superior accuracy in recognition. We evaluate image quality metrics to distinguish the methods based on both subjective and objective assessments. Our experiments indicate that implementing restoration prior to segmenting poses significantly enhances hand detection precision, and the application of discrete derivatives results in a high level of discrimination between various static hand positions as well as between hand positions and the backdrop. Ultimately, the goal is to contribute to the development of an automated sign language recognition system primarily intended for humanitarian purposes.

The amount of spam circulating online could be about to undergo a massive increase, say experts.
Anti-spam group Spamhaus is warning about a novel virus which hides the origins of junk mail. The program makes spam look like it is being sent by legitimate mail servers making it hard to spot and filter out. Spamhaus said that if the problem went unchecked real e-mail messages could get drowned by the sheer amount of junk being sent.
Before now many spammers have recruited home PCs to act as anonymous e-mail relays in an attempt to hide the origins of their junk mail. The PCs are recruited using viruses and worms that compromise machines via known vulnerabilities or by tricking people into opening an attachment infected with the malicious program. Once compromised the machines start to pump out junk mail on behalf of spammers. Spamhaus helps to block junk messages from these machines by collecting and circulating blacklists of net addresses known to harbour infected machines. But the novel worm spotted recently by Spamhaus routes junk via the mail servers of the net service firm that infected machines used to get online in the first place. In this way the junk mail gets a net address that looks legitimate. As blocking all mail from net firms just to catch the spam is impractical, Spamhaus is worried that the technique will give junk mailers the ability to spam with little fear of being spotted and stopped. Steve Linford, director of Spamhaus, predicted that if a lot of spammers exploit this technique it could trigger the failure of the net's e-mail sending infrastructure. David Stanley, UK managing director of filtering firm Ciphertrust, said the new technique was the next logical step for spammers. "They are adding to their armoury," he said. The amount of spam in circulation was still growing, said Mr Stanley, but he did not think that the appearance of this trick would mean e-mail meltdown. But Kevin Hogan, senior manager at Symantec security response, said such warnings were premature. "If something like this mean the end of e-mail then e-mail would have stopped two-three years ago," said Mr Hogan. While the technique of routing mail via mail servers of net service firms might cause problems for those that use blacklists and block lists it did not mean that other techniques for stopping spam lost their efficacy too. Mr Hogan said 90% of the junk mail filtered by Symantec subsidiary Brightmail was spotted using techniques that did not rely on looking at net addresses. For instance, said Mr Hogan, filtering out e-mail messages that contain a web link can stop about 75% of spam.

Instead, we traverse a CGI fantasy realm devoid of genuine amazement.

The novel's peculiar settings, nonsensical dialogues, and fanciful characters are celebrated in the source material. In this cinematic interpretation, however, these elements are tamed, losing their enigma and leaving audiences with a vibrant yet unmemorable rehash. The narrative appears determined to steer toward a predictable climax, offering little incentive for investment throughout its runtime due to a lack of emotional attachment.

To breathe new life into such a well-known source material, either innovative approaches (like Svankmajer's dark stop-motion adaptation or Gilliam's influence on Tideland) or a thoughtfully dedicated adaptation that fully embraces Lewis Carroll's essence must be adopted. Unfortunately, what transpires is a mediocre middle ground that fails to capture the magic that draws people to the Alice tale. Although this isn't an unpleasant viewing experience per se, it ultimately falls short of being truly impactful. Witnessed on the expansive Screen 1 at the Empire, it showcases moments of stunning visual beauty. Yet, it remains a forgettable addition to Burton's oeuvre.

The Government of the United Kingdom maintains intelligence agencies within several  government departments. The agencies are responsible for collecting and analysing foreign and domestic intelligence, providing military intelligence, performing espionage and counter-espionage. Their intelligence assessments contribute to the conduct of the foreign relations of the United Kingdom, maintaining the national security of the United Kingdom, military planning and law enforcement in the United Kingdom.  The main organisations are the Secret Intelligence Service (SIS or MI6), the Security Service (MI5), the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) and Defence Intelligence (DI). The history of the organisations dates back to the 19th century. The decryption of the Zimmermann Telegram in 1917 was described as the most significant intelligence triumph for Britain during World War I, and one of the earliest occasions on which a piece of signals intelligence influenced world events. During the Second World War and afterwards, many observers regarded Ultra as immensely valuable to the Allies of World War II. In 1962, during the Cuban Missile Crisis, GCHQ interceptions of Soviet ship positions were sent directly to the White House. Intelligence cooperation in the post-war period between the United Kingdom and the United States became the cornerstone of Western intelligence gathering and the "Special Relationship" between the United Kingdom and the United States.

Her subsequent progression was facilitated through financial assistance from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, the Polish Academy of Sciences, and the German Academic Exchange Service, culminating in her attainment of a doctorate in History from the University of Hamburg in 1993. 'Interview with the Vampire' is an atmospheric, highly gripping "film involving vampires" - not a "vampire movie". Whilst the latter would describe a film that focuses on its vampirism and might be judged on the sharpness of its fangs, this "film involving vampires" has all the merits of the very best cinema, and at its core is nothing but a fantastic story carried by compelling, believable characters.

For those who may not be able to overlook the vampiric content, look again. The vampirism herein is a plot device, a way of presenting characters who cannot die or age or be harmed, so that the philosophical questions of life itself can be explored. But equally, for those who will be interested in the vampiric content, this film presents a rich mythology backed by a trilogy of books, which fleshes out the concept of the vampire in a much deeper way than any other production.

Every person has their own world view, their own way of living and thinking. People can be brooding, contemplative, cautious, reasonable, carefree, hedonistic, optimistic, emotional - and every shade in between. But these are all world-views based on the knowledge that life is short. What would happen if told their lives would never end? Who would be happiest? What would they do? How would eternal life affect each person? And most importantly, if a way of living was bringing meaning to a person's life, would that still work once life was infinite? All of these questions help us explore philosophical ideas as old as time, and that exploration is the focus of this film.

The story is propelled by vampires Louis (Pitt) and Lestat (Cruise), each representing a different take on life. Whilst Louis, who began as a depressive wanting to die, thinks of eternity as an extended curse; Lestat, who seems to live every second as it comes, barely even considers the future three minutes hence. Told from Louis' viewpoint as he struggles to find some meaning in a life he knows will never end, we are taken on a ride across the centuries, as Louis' outlook and happiness undulate whilst characters and relationships come and go.

Alongside Louis' turmoil in coming to terms with his (now eternal) life, a secondary theme is explored, which is the notion of survival. Even though Louis is clearly dissatisfied with life, he never attempts to end it, despite this option being open to him. In other words, surviving, in and of itself, was a motivation that outdid any other. Most importantly, survival outdoes Louis' trouble over the fact that his only source of nourishment is now the blood of living animals, preferably humans. Despite attempting abstinence, and then attempting to drink only the blood of rodents, this basic feeding instinct proves too much for Louis. And yet, as Lestat points out, what is the problem? The fittest always survives, and whoever is lower down the food-chain will be eaten. Humans eat animals, and vampires eat humans - it's all natural. But nonetheless, are there moral limits? Even if you have to kill a human, is there a more moral way to do it? "Monstrous," Louis exclaims, as he watches a group of vampires murder a defenceless girl. Yet might survival require the forgetting of moral consciousness, like Lestat?

'Interview with the Vampire' explores all of these deep, important issues whilst delivering an incredibly powerful story populated by charismatic characters, haunting and diverse settings and immortal dialogue. Gripping from start to finish, you will be enamoured at the vampire-world opened up to you; and by the end, you are left wondering what choice you would have made, given the one that Lestat never had...

Scientists are working on ways to ensure laptops can stay powered for an entire working day.
Building batteries from new chemical mixes could boost power significantly, say industry experts. The changes include everything from the way chips for laptops are made, to tricks that reduce the power consumption of displays. Ever since laptops appeared the amount of time they last between recharges has been a frustration for users.
A survey carried out in 2000 by Forrester Research found that the shortness of battery life was the most complained about feature of laptops. "The focus back then was more on performance and features," said Mike Trainor, chief mobile technology evangelist for chip giant Intel.
"For most of the 90s battery life was stuck on two to 2.5 hours." But now, he said, laptops can last much longer. It was not just a case of improving battery life by squeezing more out of the lithium ion power packs, he explained. Other changes are needed to get to the holy grail of a laptop running for about eight hours before needing a recharge. "Lithium ion is never going to get there by itself," he said. "The industry has done a great job of wringing all possible energy storage out of that technology that they can." Some new battery chemistries promise to cram more power into the same space, said Mr Trainor, though work still needed to be done to get them successfully from the lab to manufacturing. He was sceptical that fuel cells would develop quick enough to take over from solid batteries even though they have the potential to produce several times more energy than lithium ion power packs. "In fuel cells you need to have pumps and separators and evaporation chambers," he said. "It's a mini energy plant that needs to be shrunk and shrunk and shrunk."
Intel has been working with component makers to test energy consumption on all the parts inside a laptop and find ways to make them less power hungry.
This work has led to the creation of the Mobile PC Extended Battery Life (EBL) Working Group that shares information about building notebooks that are more parsimonious with power. Some of the improvements in power use come simply because components on chips are shrinking, said Mr Trainor. Intel has also changed the way it creates transistors on silicon to reduce the power they need. On a larger scale, said Mr Trainor, improvements in the way that voltage regulators are made can reduce the amount of power lost as heat and make a notebook more energy efficient. Also, said Mr Trainor, research is being done on ways to cut energy consumption on displays - currently the biggest power guzzler on a laptop. Many laptop makers have committed to creating 14 and 15 inch screens that draw only three watts of power. This is far below the power consumption levels of screens in current notebooks. "If we can get close to eight hours that's a place that people see as extraordinarily valuable that's what the industry has to deliver," Mr Trainor said.

Image segmentation is the process of partitioning a image into different
regions or groups based on some characteristics like color, texture, motion or
shape etc. Active contours is a popular variational method for object
segmentation in images, in which the user initializes a contour which evolves
in order to optimize an objective function designed such that the desired
object boundary is the optimal solution. Recently, imaging modalities that
produce Manifold valued images have come up, for example, DT-MRI images, vector
fields. The traditional active contour model does not work on such images. In
this paper, we generalize the active contour model to work on Manifold valued
images. As expected, our algorithm detects regions with similar Manifold values
in the image. Our algorithm also produces expected results on usual gray-scale
images, since these are nothing but trivial examples of Manifold valued images.
As another application of our general active contour model, we perform texture
segmentation on gray-scale images by first creating an appropriate Manifold
valued image. We demonstrate segmentation results for manifold valued images
and texture images.

This paper presents a novel approach to semi-supervised instance segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, by introducing a mask-guided sample selection strategy. The proposed method leverages the power of both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the performance of instance segmentation models. The mask-guided sample selection strategy selects informative samples from unlabeled data based on the prediction confidence of the instance segmentation model. The selected samples are then used to generate pseudo-labels, which are incorporated into the training process to enhance the model's learning. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing significant improvements over existing semi-supervised instance segmentation techniques.

This paper presents a novel approach to computer vision for liquid samples in hospitals and medical labs, utilizing hierarchical image segmentation and relations prediction. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of liquid sample analysis, which is crucial in diagnostics and treatment planning. The proposed method involves segmenting the image of the liquid sample into various hierarchical levels and predicting the relations between these segments. The paper discusses the development and implementation of the algorithm, and evaluates its performance using real-world data from medical labs. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the accuracy and speed of liquid sample analysis, suggesting potential for enhancing diagnostic processes in healthcare settings. The paper also explores potential future developments and applications of this technology in the medical field.

Our paper introduces a human-assisted video object segmentation system. Its foundation is a one-shot method for video object segmentation, which is quick but relies on an precise pixel-level segmentation of a frame or frames as prerequisite. Since manual segmentation is impractical, we suggest a deep learning approach to interactive image segmentation, enabling users to accurately label objects with minimal clicks - approximately 3.8 on average in experiments using the GrabCut dataset, establishing a new benchmark. Moreover, our method progressively enhances the initial segmentation, efficiently rectifying frames where video object segmentation falls short, ensuring top-tier results for complex video sequences. Additionally, we delve into user behavior patterns and offer valuable insights regarding the number of steps taken to label frames, the nature of corrections applied, among other findings, paving the way for future advancements in interactive video segmentation.

New York Press The above is the usual negative commentary you'll see regarding this film. Critics bashed it for being insulting, unoriginal, and unmoving. Let me make some corrections for them so that they can save a little face.

I'm no Tom Cruise fan. A buddy of mine, too, is so peeved at Cruise that he refuses to watch anything the man stars in. Mostly this has to do with Cruise's personal life and beliefs (just watch an episode of South Park to see how some people view him and you'll see what I mean). People have similar feelings toward Mel Gibson ...but I digress.

VALKYRIE, as most of you probably now know, is the final of 15 attempts on Hitler's life. Shortly after this (about nine months) he committed suicide in his bunker. But this is about the one time where it almost succeeded. I'd heard about this attempt and read bits of it in history classes, but never really gave it much thought. I mean, the mustachioed murderer offed himself, so that was that. But what gives this film much of its umpf! is how true to history the story sticks (that and how closely many of the actors resemble their true-life counterparts). It is also riveting coming from director Bryan Singer (who did one of my all-time favorite films, THE USUAL SUSPECTS).

Tom Cruise did a great job (probably one of his best since COLLATERAL and MINORITY REPORT). His Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg character was spot-on ...with one exception that seems to be a sticking point for many: his accent. It is true that none of the actors attempts a German cadence in their speech. Did this bother me? No. I think it would have bothered me if they'd TRIED to do one and made it sound forced or ridiculous. So there's that...

What makes the film a success was Cruise's rock solid performance and the amazing supporting cast: Kenneth Branagh, Bill Nighy, Tom Wilkinson, Terrence Stamp, and Eddie Izzard just to sprinkle a few names.

It is also noteworthy to mention that they filmed nearly everything on-location and in the exact same spots where the original incidents took place, including the subsequent trials and executions of the conspirators. Phenomenal authenticity.

If the cadence of their speech bothered some, then I failed to see how the cadence of the film could. It was absolutely perfect. It gradually built up suspense (even though we knew how it would end for the conspirators), and never slowed, right up until the very end. I am forced to use a cliché here in that "I was on the edge of my seat" throughout the second half of the film.

So if you're looking to tear apart Tom Cruise, you might look at WAR OF THE WORLDS or LEGEND. But not here.

1 cup buttermilk
2 cups breadcrumbs
1 tablespoon garlic salt
2 finely chopped shallots (whole: 2)
2 tablespoons butter
1 finely chopped onion
1 cup chopped brown mushrooms
2 tablespoons flour
2 cups beef broth
1 tablespoon salt and pepper (or to taste)

Preheat oven to 375F. Following hammering, tenderloins are left in buttermilk for 5-10 minutes. Post-soaking, tenderloins will be coated in breadcrumb-garlic salt blend. Coat one side in the breadcrumb mixture; on the opposite side, distribute generously sautéed shallots. Wrap tenderloins in breading mixture, ensuring entire spiral of venison is concealed. Arrange seam-side down on a baking sheet. Cook for 15-25 minutes; cooking duration depends on tenderness of pounded venison. Concurrently, initiate sauce production. Saute onion, mushrooms, and any lingering shallots in melted butter on medium-low heat until soft yet undeveloped in color. Introduce flour, continuously stirring. Once flour is entirely combined, gradually pour in broth, enabling sauce to simmer approximately 20 minutes, until decreased by half. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve venison atop steamed asparagus spears and mushroom sauce. Bon appétit!

Cream of Mushroom Soup is a flavorful and versatile dish that can be served as a starter or a light meal. This recipe requires only a few simple ingredients and can be made in just a few steps.

To begin, heat butter or oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and cook until they are soft and release their liquid. Next, add the onion and cook until it is translucent. Then, add the garlic and cook for another minute.

Once the mushrooms, onion, and garlic are cooked, add the flour and stir until the mixture is smooth. Cook for another minute to get the flour taste out. Then, gradually add the chicken broth, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth and thickened.

Next, add the milk, salt, and pepper and stir until the mixture is combined. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the soup is thickened.

Finally, stir in the parsley and serve the soup hot. This soup can be served as a starter or a light meal, and it can also be paired with a salad or bread for a more filling meal. Whether served as a starter or a main course, this soup is sure to be a hit. It’s warm, comforting, and full of flavor.

Experts are raising concerns about a potential surge in online spam due to a new virus discovered by Spamhaus. This malware masks the source of spam emails, making them appear to originate from legitimate mail servers, complicating efforts to identify and filter them out. Previously, spammers have utilized home PCs as anonymous email relays by infecting them with viruses or worms. These machines then send out junk mail on behalf of spammers. Spamhaus mitigates this issue by maintaining blacklists of IP addresses associated with infected machines. However, a newly identified worm uses the mail servers of the internet service provider (ISP) that infected machines rely on for connectivity to route spam, granting it a seemingly legitimate sender address. Given the impracticality of blocking all emails from ISPs to prevent spam, Spamhaus is concerned that this method may enable spammers to evade detection and continue their activities unimpeded. According to Spamhaus Director Steve Linford, widespread adoption of this technique could lead to the collapse of the internet's email infrastructure. Meanwhile, Ciphertrust UK Managing Director David Stanley views this development as a natural progression for spammers, stating, "They are expanding their arsenal." While the volume of spam remains a concern, Stanley does not believe that this tactic poses an imminent threat of email overload. Nonetheless, Symantec Senior Manager Kevin Hogan warns of the potential consequences of this trend, emphasizing the need for continued vigilance against evolving threats.

Despite having little in common, they form a bond. Henry finds himself drawn into Aunt Augusta's world of travel, adventure, romance and absence of bigotry. He travels first with her to Brighton, where he meets one of his aunt's old acquaintances, and gains an insight into one of her many past lives. Here a psychic foreshadows that he will have many travels in the near future. This prediction inevitably becomes true as Henry is pulled further and further into his aunt's lifestyle, and delves deeper into her past. Their voyages take them from Paris to Istanbul on the Orient Express, and as the journey unfolds, so do the stories of Aunt Augusta, painting the picture of a woman for whom love has been the defining feature of her life. Henry returns to his quiet retirement, but tending his garden no longer holds the same allure. When he receives a letter from his aunt, he finally gives up his old life to join her and the love of her life in South America, and to marry a girl decades younger than himself. As his travels progress it becomes clear to Henry that the woman he had been raised to believe was his mother was in fact his aunt. The trial for Bernie Ebbers, ex-CEO of defunct US telecommunications company WorldCom, commenced in New York with the panel selection. Charges against him include securities fraud, collusion, and misrepresentation to regulatory bodies. A lengthy imprisonment is a potential consequence if convicted. Ebbers maintains his innocence.

During Ebbers' tenure, WorldCom ascended from modest beginnings in Mississippi to a $160bn telecom titan and investor favorite during the late 1990s. However, as competition heightened and the telecom bubble waned, WorldCom encountered increasing financial strain. Upon its eventual downfall, shareholders experienced losses totaling approximately $180bn, and 20,000 employees were terminated. Ebbers' upcoming trial, anticipated to span over two months, marks another endeavor by US prosecutors to penalize senior executives for fraud. This proceeding coincides with the retrial of former Tyco International chiefs Dennis Kozlowski and his deputy, who stand accused of embezzling $600m from the conglomerate. Preparations for trials of former Enron executives are also underway.

I will start by saying I have never read the book so I'm basing my review solely on the film.

I actually found the film very hard to watch and cried most of the way through. It is a very beautiful film but I think what is unfortunately overlooked my many is that the strongest relationship in the film is that between John and his father and it is this relationship that made the film very emotional for me. In particular scene following his fathers stroke where John was reading the letter was beautifully done and very well acted and was the scene I found most upsetting.

I think the film explores a number of important aspects in particular having an autistic parent which I could only imagine would be exceptionally difficult for any child, particularly when said parent is their only carer. As seen with the characters of both Aaron and Johns father relationships are often quite difficult for those with some types of autism, routine is important and going against a routine can cause a lot of angst and distress. Its unfortunate that a number of people continue to see autism as an excuse for peoples bad behaviour and I think this film brings and important note to an often misunderstood illness. It also points out the issue of autism in parents which is another issue often overlooked.

The relationship between John and Savannah is only secondary to that of John and his father and I think its well acted by Channing Tatum and Amanda Seyfried. To me both actors seemed to really feel and understand their characters and the hurt between them and I did like how the ending between them was really left open to interpretation.

In all a very well done film which explores some important social issues but no review will ever truly do this film justice. I for one could not watch it again because it made me so upset but this just goes to show how emotive the film is. Its a film that needs to be watched, even if it is only once.

From Publishers Weekly: "With a title more appropriate to a paperback romance and an author whose reputation was made in an entirely different genre, this posthumous thriller by one of the stellar lights of the golden age of science fiction seems unlikely to find an audience. Although Bester died in 1987, the book seems, in both style and perspective, to have been written well before that, perhaps not too far beyond its late 1950s setting. Beautiful model Julene Krebs attracts the attentions of both a high-powered advertising executive and a prominent research scientist. The two men become friendly as a result of their mutual interest in the girl, and she in turn becomes involved with each. Meanwhile, Bester offers what is presumably intended as satirical commentary on the advertising industry in general and TV commercials in particular, via a stream of embarrassingly awkward conversations and repartee in a variety of settings. There's a threatening, shadowy figure lurking about, as well as intimations of a dark secret in Julene's past, but these matters are so submerged in the plodding story that they seem unimportant—at least until a wild, violent night on Fire Island, N.Y. That's followed by a hurricane, a kidnapping and a thoroughly unbelievable bit of melodrama. In the end, after Bester skirts around an appalling view of rape and its victims, love triumphs over all—sort of."

German-born Canadian theologian Father Gerhard Albert Baum (1923-2017), recognized as Gregory Baum, gained prominence in North America and Europe during the 1960s for his endeavors in ecumenism, interfaith dialogue, and bridging the gap between the Catholic Church and Judaism. Later in the 1960s, he pursued sociology studies at the New School for Social Research in New York, resulting in his efforts to blend classical sociological thought (Marx, Tocqueville, Durkheim, Tonnies, Weber, et al.) with Christian theology. During the 1970s, Baum embraced the perspectives of Liberation Theology originating from Latin America and other societies. Additionally, he engaged with the ideas of Karl Mannheim and formulated a methodology for ideology critique, aiming to eradicate ideological influences within religion, particularly those fostering disdain towards others and hindering Christians from being moved by the plight of social injustice victims.

The novel "Through the Looking-Glass" broadly follows the whimsically adventurous journey of a young girl named Alice, who steps through a mirror into a parallel universe. In this fantastical mirrored reality, Alice encounters an array of peculiar creatures and enigmatic characters, with the rules of logic often turned upside down.

An interesting aspect of this novel is its unique structure, which is cleverly organized like a giant chessboard with different locations as squares on the board. Alice begins her journey as a pawn and must navigate her way across the board to become a queen. Along her puzzling journey, Alice meets nursery rhyme characters like Tweedledee and Tweedledum, Humpty Dumpty and the Lion and the Unicorn. Each chapter either ends with a thoughtful Alice or segues cleverly into the next via startling transformations or suddenly altered surroundings.

What adds complexity to the narrative is the whimsical poetry interspersed throughout, from 'Jabberwocky' to 'The Walrus and the Carpenter,' each adding a layer of complexity and meaning to this otherworldly journey. As Alice ventures deeper into this strange and erratic world, the readers are also driven to question reality, thereby mirroring Alice's thrill, confusion, and curiosity. Towards the end, the pace of the journey quickens, and Alice's ultimate coronation symbolizes universal themes of growth and self-realization.

Ultimately, "Through the Looking-Glass" captures the essence of childhood wonder, baffling logic, and the joy of imagination, leaving the readers with a profound sense of thoughtfulness and awe.

Thomas B. Woodward functions as an Episcopal priest in the Diocese of Rio Grande, Santa Fe, New Mexico, residing there with his spouse Ann. Previously, Woodward served on the steering committee of "The Episcopal Majority," an Episcopal Church faction established to thwart assaults against the institution by self-proclaimed orthodox groups. In 2006, Woodward was assigned to the Executive Council’s Committee on the Status of Women and subsequently elected as its Secretary. Recently, he oversaw St. Paul's Peace Church, a cooperative Episcopal and Lutheran congregation in Las Vegas, New Mexico. Throughout more than two decades, Woodward ministered to The Episcopal Church as a university chaplain at several institutions, such as the University of Kansas, Missouri State University in Warrensburg, the University of Rochester, the University of North Carolina, and the University of Wisconsin in Madison. He previously headed Christ Church in Warrensburg and St. Paul's Episcopal Church in Salinas, California, where John Steinbeck attended services. During his tenure in Salinas, he received The Ben Heller Award for Valor and Direction in Aid to the Farmworker Community and The Bishop's Cross from the Episcopal Diocese of El Camino Real due to his guidance during a trying period. In 1982, Woodward's Madison, Wisconsin congregation became the initial Episcopal Church nationwide to offer public asylum to political refugees from El Salvador and Guatemala, as depicted in the PBS documentary, "The New Underground Railroad." Prior to this, Woodward had been apprehended for participating in a civil rights demonstration at the University of Kansas (1965), and later detained in Rochester, New York while offering pastoral support to university students taking part in an anti-war protest.

Based on a true story, this film follows the dreams and struggles of aspiring actor Greg Sestero and the enigmatic Tommy Wiseau, who is determined to become the next big Hollywood star.

James Franco shines in his dual role as director and actor, perfectly capturing the eccentricity and passion of Tommy Wiseau. Franco's performance is nothing short of amazing, as he fully immerses himself in the role of Wiseau and manages to bring humor, empathy, and depth to a character who is so outrageous and enigmatic.

The chemistry between Franco and his real-life brother, Dave Franco, who portrays Greg Sestero, is electric. Their on-screen dynamic adds an authentic and endearing layer to the story, as we witness the friendship between these two aspiring actors blossom amidst the chaos of creating a film that becomes a cult sensation for all the wrong reasons.

The writing and directing by James Franco are top-notch. He successfully navigates the fine line between re-creating the hilariously awful moments from the original film, "The Room," while also presenting the human side of the story. The pacing is spot-on, engaging the audience from start to finish, and providing a balance between laugh-out-loud moments and more introspective scenes that explore the complexities of Wiseau's character.

While "The Disaster Artist" is undeniably a comedy, it also offers a deeper exploration of friendship, dreams, and the pursuit of artistic expression. It delves into the idea that even in the face of tremendous failure, there is something admirable about those who dare to create and put themselves out there.

The supporting cast is exceptional, with standout performances from Seth Rogen, who brings his signature humor and wit, and Alison Brie, who portrays Sestero's girlfriend with charm and sincerity. The film also features several cameos from well-known actors and industry figures, adding to its overall authenticity and entertainment value.

The visuals and production design successfully transport viewers back to the early 2000s and the world of independent filmmaking. From the awkwardly staged green screen scenes to the infamous rooftop setting, there is attention to detail that amplifies the absurdity and charm of the original film.

Overall, "The Disaster Artist" is a triumph. It serves as a loving tribute to the cult classic "The Room" while also offering a universally relatable story about the pursuit of one's dreams. James Franco's tour de force performance

3 1/4 cups all purpose flour
1 packet instant dry yeast
1 tablespoon sugar
2 teaspoons salt
1 1/2 cups warm water (no higher tha 110 degrees)
3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for topping
5-8 sprigs rosemary or tarragon, needles/leaves whole
Extra kosher salt for sprinkling
Freshly ground black pepper
In a stand mixer bowl (with the mixer attached to a dough hook), combine flour, yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water and then stir slowly to combine. Bring the mixer up to medium speed and knead for about five minutes. Depending on the humidity, you may need to add more flour in order to turn it into a smooth ball. After five minutes, knead by hand a little more, adding flour if needed to reduce the stickiness, though this dough will always have a little stickiness. Coat a bowl with olive oil and place the smooth ball of dough into it and cover with a towel. Let rise for three hours at room temperature. Once the dough has doubled in size, punch down and preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Coat a 9x13 pan with olive oil and stretch the dough to fill the pan, press dimples into the dough, and then season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle desired herbs evenly over the top of the bread, and place into the middle of the oven to bake for 20 minutes. Then set the oven to broil, and while monitoring every two minutes, brown the top of the bread to desired doneness.

During the 19th century it was believed that the Panic originated within the economic system itself, since the event could not be readily attributed to any specific government blunder or disaster as had previous crises. Rothbard suggests instead that the Panic of 1819 grew largely out of the changes wrought by the War of 1812 on the still-fledgling republic, and by the postwar boom that followed. The outbreak of war stifled foreign trade and spurred the growth of domestic manufacturing, which mushroomed to fill the gap left by declining imports and also served to satisfy the nation's appetite for war goods. The war also brought a rash of paper money, as the government borrowed heavily to finance the war. The credit expansion also led to rising prices, as economic theory from the Austrian School—which includes Rothbard—would predict. Austrian theory also predicts the bust that must inevitably follow the non-specie-based credit expansion. Rothbard lays out the events of both bust and boom.

Timothy D. Leiweke (born July 27, 1959) is an American sports and entertainment executive. He is the president and CEO of Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG), a subsidiary of the Anschutz Corporation. He is also a part-owner of the Los Angeles Galaxy, Major League Soccer's most valuable franchise.

Leiweke was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and raised in Algonquin, Illinois. He played football and ice hockey at Algonquin High School, from which he graduated in 1977. He then attended Loyola University Chicago on a football scholarship, but a knee injury ended his playing career. He graduated from Loyola in 1981 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.

He began his career in the sports industry with the St. Louis Steamers of the Major Indoor Soccer League (MISL). He later worked for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL), the Chicago Blackhawks of the NHL, and the Chicago Sting of the North American Soccer League (NASL).

In 1987, he was hired by Jerry Reinsdorf, owner of the Chicago Bulls of the National Basketball Association (NBA), as the team's director of marketing. He oversaw the marketing of the Bulls' first NBA championship team in 1991.

In 1989, he left the Bulls to become the president and CEO of the Chicago Sting, which Reinsdorf also owned. The Sting went out of business in 1988, but Leiweke negotiated a lease for the team to play its home games at the new United Center. He also negotiated a television contract for the team with WGN-TV.

In 1992, Leiweke was hired by Michael Ovitz, then head of the Creative Artists Agency, to run the company's sports division. Ovitz subsequently hired Leiweke to run the Anaheim Ducks of the NHL, which Ovitz co-owned with Disney. The Ducks won the Stanley Cup in 2007.

In 1996, Leiweke was hired by Phillip Anschutz to run AEG, which Anschutz owned. Leiweke has been credited with turning around the company, which was struggling when he took over. Under his leadership, AEG has built Staples Center, L.A. Live, the Home Depot Center, and the O2 in London. AEG also owns the Los Angeles Kings of the NHL, the Los Angeles Galaxy of MLS, and the Houston Dynamo of MLS.

The Liberal Democrats propose constructing 100,000 new "affordable" homes utilizing publicly-owned lands. This plan involves establishing a mutual home ownership trust, enabling individuals to acquire a stake in a property and gain access to homeownership. Additionally, the party encourages repurposing existing structures to preserve green areas. Both Labour and the Conservatives have declared their intentions to aid first-time buyers and expand right-to-buy schemes respectively.

Amidst the election frenzy, all major parties are addressing the housing crisis as per a study suggesting that first-time buyers cannot afford homes in 92% of UK towns. Lib Dems' "mutual homes" enable people to purchase a percentage of a property, typically equating to around 5% of construction expenses. Party head Charles Kennedy asserted these residences will remain affordable due to their establishment on surplus public sector lands, granted gratis by either central or local authorities. Tenants would pay approximately one-third of their income towards rent and additional shares, with the option to sell their shares when relocating, thereby profiting from property value increases. Moreover, councils would retain the flexibility to adjust discounts based on local requirements for tenants wishing to purchase council homes. Kennedy stated, "Through mutual homes, people can gradually accumulate an equity stake in a property by investing only what they can afford."

Furthermore, there are plans to impede exorbitant house prices from displacing community members. The Lib Dems' strategy in South Shropshire, involving a "golden share," may be expanded. Under this arrangement, councils negotiate agreements with developers, retaining a 1% stake in property projects. Properties are then sold at "build cost" to residents deemed to have local needs rather than being offered on the open market. The party maintains that such measures will contribute to: "Our helpline for aspiring homeowners."

Dragondrums is the coming of age story of Piemur, a small, quick, clever apprentice at Harper Hall. There he has to deal with the jealousy and bullying of the other drumming apprentices. When Masterharper Robinton secretly asks Piemur to be his apprentice, Piemur begins journeying through Pern, gathering information and running discreet errands for the Masterharper. In his adventures throughout Pern, Piemur has only his knowledge and wits to deal with a cruel Lord Holder and rogue dragonriders.
