Despite losing the top spot, Meet The Parents 2 had a strong second week, taking $31.3m (£19.1m).
But its figures mark a 46.4% fall on its first weekend.
The top two films were followed by Smith, starring Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, ($30.2m (£18.9m) and King Kong ($23.8m (£14.4m).
Stiller, who plays the lead in the Fockers series, said it was "great" for his family to be back together again.
He said: "It's great when the family all get along - it really is.
"I play a character in this film that is essentially what I thought I would be when I grew up. I'm a stay-at-home dad - and my character in the movie can't actually work. He's a pot-head."
Mr & Mrs Smith was a surprise hit, taking third spot behind the second Focker movie.
The film - starring the Mr & Mrs Smith couple in starring roles - has made $30.2m.
It is directed by Doug Liman, whose recent movies include The Bourne Identity and is produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, who made the Pirates of the Caribbean series.
Inspiration for the comedy came from news that Drew Barrymore's then-husband Tom Green had been caught smoking a "blunt" - a pipe - full of marijuana.
That has sparked a series of gags suggesting that he and Ben Stiller have a pot-smoking club together.

Three upcoming Radio 1 DJs, Huw Stephens, Ras Kwame, and Rob Da Bank, will take over the mid-week, late-night slot beginning in February, featuring diverse, non-commercial music and UK talent in honor of the late John Peel. Peel's legacy won't be directly replaced, but these DJs will strive to maintain his influence by showcasing unpredictable music. Peel passed away from a heart attack in October. These DJs were selected for their extensive musical knowledge across various genres. Rob Da Bank has filled in for The John Peel Show since Peel's passing and co-hosts The Blue Room. Huw Stephens co-hosts the Radio 1 Thursday night show in Wales and focuses on new music, particularly emerging Welsh acts. Ras Kwame hosts 100% Homegrown on Radio 1's digital station 1Xtra, dedicated to the best of UK black music and providing live sessions for new artists. All three DJs will continue their current Radio 1 roles. Radio 1 acknowledged that John Peel cannot be replaced, promising support for both established and unsigned talent. They will focus on artists creating music for artistic reasons rather than commercial gain and nurture emerging genres and styles. One Music, already present as a Radio 1 website offering industry advice, will expand into radio programming. Radio 1's controller, Andy Parfitt, stated, "By having a group of DJs hosting multiple shows under the One Music umbrella, we aim to foster and promote a wide range of musical genres and talent."

In Tarzan and the Ant Men, Tarzan encounters a race of miniature people who live in a lost city deep in the African jungle. The Ant Men are a peaceful people who have developed a sophisticated civilization, complete with an advanced system of writing and a form of government. They are also experts in the art of warfare, and are able to defeat their enemies by using their small size to their advantage.

Tarzan befriends the Ant Men and helps them to defend their city against a group of marauders who are intent on plundering its treasures. In the process, Tarzan learns the Ant Men's language and comes to understand their culture and way of life. He also discovers that the Ant Men are being threatened by a race of giant ants who live in the nearby jungle.

Tarzan rallies the Ant Men to fight the giant ants, and together they are able to defeat them. In the process, Tarzan earns the respect and admiration of the Ant Men, and he is welcomed into their society as one of their own.

In the field of multi-organ segmentation using abdominal CT scans, most current fully supervised deep learning techniques rely heavily on labor-intensive and costly voxel-wise annotations. However, vast amounts of unlabeled 3D CT data are generally readily available. While numerous graph-based approaches dominate the solution to the semi-supervised biomedical image segmentation challenge, there has been limited exploration of deep learning methods based on neural networks for this purpose. This study introduces Deep Multi-Planar Co-Training (DMPCT), which offers two key contributions: 1) A deep learning model that learns collaboratively across different planes such as sagittal, coronal, and axial planes; 2) Multi-plane fusion is employed to produce more dependable pseudo-labels, thereby minimizing the errors present in these labels and enabling the development of superior segmentation networks. Our research is supported by a newly compiled extensive dataset consisting of 100 unlabeled cases and 210 labeled cases, featuring 16 distinct anatomical structures meticulously annotated by four radiologists and verified by a seasoned expert. The findings indicate that DMPCT surpasses the fully supervised approach by over 4%, particularly when dealing with minimal annotation sets.

Neil O'Donnell, born July 3, 1966 in Morristown, New Jersey, enjoyed a 14-year career in the National Football League (1990-2003) with Pittsburgh Steelers, New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, and Tennessee Titans. His collegiate football days were spent at Maryland.

Growing up, O'Donnell attended Madison High School in Madison, New Jersey. His four elder brothers, coached by Ted Monica, achieved state championship titles. Among them was Stephen O'Donnell, a standout quarterback who later represented Duke. Although Monica had retired before Neil's arrival at Madison High School, he continued to guide and inspire him throughout his formative years in football.

As a sophomore and junior, Neil Kennedy O'Donnell excelled as the star quarterback for the Dodgers varsity team, but they managed only three victories during that period. In his senior year, leading the team as their quarterback, O'Donnell steered them to a more commendable 4-2-3 record in 1985. Despite the absence of impressive statistics and accolades compared to other high school phenoms, Bobby Ross recognized his potential and extended a recruitment offer from the University of Maryland.

Deep learning has been successfully applied to a wide range of medical image analysis tasks. However, the application of deep learning to cardiac image analysis has been limited by the lack of large-scale annotated datasets. In this paper, we propose a multi-planar deep segmentation network (MPSNet) for cardiac substructures segmentation from MRI and CT. The proposed MPSNet is a fully convolutional network that takes multi-planar images as input and outputs the segmentation of the left ventricle (LV), right ventricle (RV), and myocardium (MYO). The proposed MPSNet is trained on a large-scale dataset of cardiac MRI and CT images. The dataset contains over 1,000 cardiac MRI and CT images with manual annotations of the LV, RV, and MYO. The proposed MPSNet is evaluated on a separate test set of cardiac MRI and CT images. The results show that the proposed MPSNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in cardiac substructures segmentation from MRI and CT.

As the story opens, Lia, 15, is at her great-grandmother Sarah's bedside. Delirious, the old woman begins to speak of Graymoss Plantation, the Louisiana family estate left unoccupied for decades because of a "terrible, fearful evil." After the woman's death, Lia discovers that the house has been willed to her mother, who plans to move the family in and adopt a group of hard-to-place children. Lia is against this idea and vows to prove to her mother that the house is truly haunted. She learns that the ghostly occurrences are well documented and that several locals oppose the family taking up residence at Graymoss. Could one of these people be staging the hauntings? Lia has a change of heart, however, after she meets the children her parents want to care for and resolves to take on the ghosts herself. Aided by a collection of Edgar Allan Poe's stories, she eventually succeeds in driving the spirits away. The ghosts are reminiscent of those in Shirley Jackson's classic The Haunting of Hill House, whispering through the walls and sending books flying through the air. The novel ends somewhat abruptly, and a potentially interesting romantic relationship fizzles out completely, but this is still a page-turner that will satisfy mystery and ghost story fans.

2 tablespoons olive oil
1 large green bell pepper, seeded and diced
1 large red bell pepper, seeded and diced
2 medium yellow squash, diced (about 2 cups)
2 medium zucchini, diced (about 2 cups)
1 medium eggplant, diced (about 2 cups)
1 small onion, diced (about 1 cup)
2 cups sliced mushrooms
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano
Salt and pepper
2 cups shredded part-skim mozzarella
1 15-oz. container fat-free ricotta
1/2 cup grated Parmesan
1 10-oz. box frozen chopped spinach, defrosted and squeezed dry
1 large egg, beaten
2 24-oz. jars marinara sauce
12 no-cook lasagna noodles
In a large skillet, warm oil over medium heat. Add peppers, squash, zucchini, eggplant, onion and mushrooms and cook, stirring, until vegetables are crisp-tender, 12 to 14 minutes. Add garlic and saute 2 minutes longer. Transfer to a bowl, stir in herbs and season with salt and pepper. In a bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups mozzarella, ricotta, 1/4 cup Parmesan, spinach and egg; mix well. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a large baking sheet with foil and mist a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with cooking spray. Spread 1 cup sauce over bottom of baking dish. Place 4 noodles over sauce; do not allow noodles to overlap (break up noodles if necessary). Spread 1 cup sauce over noodles. Spread 1/2 ricotta mixture on top. Using a slotted spoon, spread 1/2 vegetable mixture on top. Repeat layers, ending with noodles. Spread remaining marinara on top of noodles; sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and Parmesan. Lightly mist a large piece of foil with cooking spray and carefully cover dish with foil. Place dish on baking sheet and bake for 45 minutes. Remove foil and bake until cheese has melted and filling is bubbling, about 15 minutes longer. Remove lasagna from oven and let stand for at least 10 minutes before serving.

In a small bowl, mix onion and water. Let stand 10 minutes or until onion is softened. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water. A tale of bonding sisterhood, this novel is set in Syai, an imaginary Chinese kingdom. Jin-shei is a pledge given by one woman to another, and once accepted can never be broken. This declaration of loyalty transcends social class and normal customs. Through jin-ashu, a unique language passed on from generation to generation of women (inspired by a real example of secret women's writing, Nü Shu), the lives within the sisterhood continue to intertwine throughout time. The story begins with Tai, daughter of a court seamstress, who becomes jin shei bao of the Little Empress Antian. An earthquake claims the lives of the royal family, leaving an obstinate Liudan, Antian's younger sister, as the unexpected new Empress. Antian, during her dying moments, binds Tai to look after her sister. Tai is comforted by Yuet, an apprentice healer. A new pledge is made, and Tai finds herself with a new jin shei bao who works tirelessly to bridge the gap between Tai and Liudan. The initial moves are tentative, for Liudan remains insecure throughout her lonely life in the imperial court. During her time of sorrow, Tai is also consoled by her childhood friend Nhia. A club-footed young girl, Nhia grew up in the vicinity of the great temple, and has learned much about the Way. She is a sage with a pure heart who later becomes Syai Chancellor. It is also at the temple that Nhia meets Khailin, to whom she pledges sisterhood. A restless soul, Khailin is actively seeking knowledge about the Way. However, her thirst for information leads her down the path of darker forces. Khailin secretly marries the Ninth Sage Lihui. Within Liudan’s court, an exceptional young Guard trainee named Xaforn is injured and Yuet is summoned to heal her. Xaforn is jin shei bao to Qiaan, binding their lives beyond adoptive sisterhood. Xaforn is protective by nature, while Qiaan is nurturing. Through a series of events, the circle of sisterhood between these young ladies will test their loyalty, determination, courage and bravery. Liudan, in her quest for absolute rule over her empire, declares herself to be Dragon Empress. However, when the existence of Tammary, the late Emperor’s illegitimate daughter with a Traveller, comes to light, Liudan becomes obsessed by her need to maintain her power. In order to protect Tammary, Tai pledges sisterhood and tries to act as the peacemaker. Qiaan is then discovered to be the daughter of Cai, the Ivory Emperor's concubine, and becomes a pawn of Lihui, who wants to rule as Emperor and overthrow Liudan. An increasingly insecure Liudan resorts to extraction of duties of sisterhood despite mistrusting her sisters who try fervently to bring her back to their fold, to a life with some sense of calm and peace. They fail, and their failure comes with a huge price, as one sister after another dies. The story ends with Tai in her old age, looking back to her youth and reminiscing that her life was joyful yet marred by occasions of unhappiness, a life that was changed by a single promise - Jin-Shei.

In the city, a group of con artists led by Volpone, a cunning and greedy old man, devise a plan to trick a wealthy and gullible young nobleman named Corvino into believing that Volpone is dying and needs his wealth to pay for a grand funeral. Volpone's accomplices, Mosca and Corvino's own servant, Bonario, pretend to be religious figures and convince Corvino to give up his wealth. However, Volpone's plan is foiled when Corvino's love interest, Celia, discovers the truth and outsmarts the con artists. In the end, Volpone and his associates are exposed and punished for their deceitful ways, while Corvino and Celia are able to find true love and happiness together.

Lanre Oyebanjo (born 27th April 1990), a professional football defender, previously featured for Welling United. He participated in the Football League with York City and Crawley Town. Despite failing to secure first-team opportunities with Brentford, Oyebanjo descended to the Conference Premier with Histon in 2008. In his inaugural term, he aided Histon to reach the play-off semifinals. Following their demotion to Conference South in 2011, Oyebanjo continued to compete in the Conference Premier with York City. In the 2011-12 season, he contributed York's second objective in their FA Trophy Final triumph and took part in their subsequent Conference Premier play-off Final win, propelling them to League Two. Post being named York's Clubman of the Year during the 2013-14 tenure, he enlisted for League One outfit Crawley Town in 2014. Their relegation to League Two ensued in the 2014-15 term, leading to his release. He rejoined York, now in the National League, in 2016 but was released once more the following year.

We propose an end-to-end learning framework for segmenting generic objects in
both images and videos. Given a novel image or video, our approach produces a
pixel-level mask for all "object-like" regions---even for object categories
never seen during training. We formulate the task as a structured prediction
problem of assigning an object/background label to each pixel, implemented
using a deep fully convolutional network. When applied to a video, our model
further incorporates a motion stream, and the network learns to combine both
appearance and motion and attempts to extract all prominent objects whether
they are moving or not. Beyond the core model, a second contribution of our
approach is how it leverages varying strengths of training annotations.
Pixel-level annotations are quite difficult to obtain, yet crucial for training
a deep network approach for segmentation. Thus we propose ways to exploit
weakly labeled data for learning dense foreground segmentation. For images, we
show the value in mixing object category examples with image-level labels
together with relatively few images with boundary-level annotations. For video,
we show how to bootstrap weakly annotated videos together with the network
trained for image segmentation. Through experiments on multiple challenging
image and video segmentation benchmarks, our method offers consistently strong
results and improves the state-of-the-art for fully automatic segmentation of
generic (unseen) objects. In addition, we demonstrate how our approach benefits
image retrieval and image retargeting, both of which flourish when given our
high-quality foreground maps. Code, models, and videos are
at:http://vision.cs.utexas.edu/projects/pixelobjectness/

I first saw this film (one of my top ten favorites) in 1995 on the big screen, as part of the commemorations for the 50th anniversary of the end of WWII. It had an impact that was so strong that it's never left me--I've seen it many times since, and with each viewing the film seems to reveal new artistic richness and spiritual depth.

William Wyler's direction is breathtaking. One of the most moving scenes occurs early on in the film, when Homer, the young disabled Navy veteran, arrives at his family home and stands for a moment on the front lawn. For that one second there is an exquisite stillness that communicates a depth of emotion that can't be expressed physically. Then, just as the tension becomes almost unbearable, Homer's little sister Louella comes to the front door and runs out to greet him. In a similar way, the scene where Al Stephenson comes home to his wife and children is so finely directed you can almost feel that you're in the apartment with them--that it's your husband or father come home to you from the war--and you're experiencing the sheer elation of their physical nearness.

This aspect of the film--its portrayal of the joys and hardships of post-war readjustment and the veterans' experience--is what makes it so enlightening, honest and powerful. As a young woman, I have never experienced wartime or had my father, brothers or friends go off to fight. The film moves swiftly but seamlessly from the initial joy of homecoming and reunion to the problems, anxieties and humiliations that the three veterans encounter as they attempt to build a new life for themselves and their families.

I found it interesting how the film tries to give a picture of the different socio-economic backgrounds of the three men, and show the emergence of an affluent, market-driven economy. While this in itself is not bad, different episodes in the film show how this economic approach can conflict sharply at times with enduring human values such as integrity and justice. Al's dealings with the young veteran Mr Novak, who comes to him for a service loan to buy a farm, and his later (slightly tipsy) speech to a business gathering show this. Al declares at the end of his speech that when the bank lends money to poor veterans it will be a financial gamble but "we'll be gambling on the future of this country".

The film's interweaving of the characters and their struggles never falters and is deeply satisfying. Even as Al and Milly, Homer and Wilma gradually move towards a happy resolution of their difficulties this positive strand of the film is counter-balanced by the focus on Fred, the courageous Air Force captain who, in the eyes of the commercial world is "unqualified", suitable only for a job at a soda fountain, and in the eyes of his war bride, Marie, is only wonderful when he's dressed up in his officer's uniform. Fred's situation seems only to deteriorate and at one point in the film, after he farewells his elderly father to leave town and look for work, the father finds the citations for Fred's medals and sits down to read them. As he reads the words describing Fred's bravery and dedication to duty while he was terribly wounded in his aircraft, Pat Derry's voice nearly breaks with pride and love for his son. The film beautifully juxtaposes Fred's unselfish conduct and willingness to make the ultimate sacrifice with the cold indifference of a country in peacetime that does not want him and seemingly has no place for him.

The actors are uniformly impressive and really make their characters come alive. Dana Andrews is especially outstanding together with two young actors making their debut, Harold Russell and Cathy O'Donnell, as Homer and Wilma. Personally, I loved Homer and Wilma's story the best among those of all the characters,and the resolution is a simple, sensitively shot scene that lifts the whole film to a new point of happiness, gratitude and release. Both Cathy O'Donnell and Teresa Wright are lovely, gifted actresses with a slightly understated style, that is perfectly suited to the film's restrained but powerful tenor. This is demonstrated especially well in the tense scene where Wilma tries to talk to Homer in the shed, and in the scene where Peggy confides her heartache to her parents.

One feature that adds significantly to the film's quality is Hugo Friedhofer's score. The music is remarkably fresh and undated, has a strong, classic sound, and is poignant without being too romantic or sentimental (a flaw often found in other 1940s film scores).

The producer, Samuel Goldwyn, reportedly said of this film: "I don't care if it doesn't make a nickel...I just want every man, woman and child in America to see it". Although I'm not American (I am Australian) I found this film, with its universal human themes and its portrayal of post-war readjustment, speaks to anyone who shares in this heritage of WWII. Tell others about this film--it is breathtaking, beautiful and brave. See it and remember.

Toward the close of WWI in 1918, this narrative recounts the tale of timid Milwaukeean Paul Peachy, an unassuming railway worker and amateur thespian. Discovering his spouse's lost affection, Paul volunteers as a private in the US Army and embarks on a vessel bound for France's battlefields. Amidst the war's atrocities, Peachy locates transient refuge in camaraderie. However, his respite is short-lived as he is seized by the enemy Germans in No Man's Land. To ensure his survival, the bilingual Paul feigns the identity of a renowned German spy, Harry Stroller. Enthralled by Peachy's charade, high-ranking Germans celebrate him as a hero and grant him access to a hitherto unexperienced realm of opulence. Yet, this fresh persona compels Paul to draw upon hidden reservoirs of bravery and resourcefulness. Suspicion mounts, compelling Paul to devise increasingly audacious deceits. In this cloak-and-dagger setting, Paul Peachy pursues a romantic entanglement with Belle, a stunning French courtesan, who appears to penetrate his intricate masquerade. The denouement offers a succession of unexpected twists and cunning plot manipulations.

Mountview House, a heritage-listed detached property located at 37 Leichhardt Street, Spring Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, was initially constructed in the 1860s as a two-story stone dwelling for Brisbane foreman carpenter Daniel McNaught. In 1882, a two-story red-brick extension was incorporated into the design by architect Andrea Stombuco, transforming the house into a preparatory school for boys. England prop Phil Vickery is staying positive despite a broken arm ruling him out of the RBS Six Nations.

Isaac M. Barr's origins were in Hornby, Canada West (presently part of Halton Hills, Ontario, Canada). His father, William Barr (b. 1816 in Ireland), was a Presbyterian Minister, while his Irish-born mother, Catharine (Baird) Barr, passed away when Isaac was ten. Young Isaac received his initial education at a humble rural school, where his father served as the teacher, augmenting his meager ministerial earnings. Mirroring his father's ministerial demeanor, Isaac often assumed the role of a preacher during childhood amusements. From 1868 to 1870, Barr pursued his Anglican clergy aspirations at Huron College in London, Ontario. He later transferred to the University of Toronto for further study (1870-1872). Post-graduation, Barr embarked on his ecclesiastical journey, starting as a curate in Exeter and Woodstock, Ontario.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to perform deep neural networks
layer-wise weight initialization using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA).
Typically, the weights of a deep neural network are initialized with: random
values, greedy layer-wise pre-training (usually as Deep Belief Network or as
auto-encoder) or by re-using the layers from another network (transfer
learning). Hence, many training epochs are needed before meaningful weights are
learned, or a rather similar dataset is required for seeding a fine-tuning of
transfer learning. In this paper, we describe how to turn an LDA into either a
neural layer or a classification layer. We analyze the initialization technique
on historical documents. First, we show that an LDA-based initialization is
quick and leads to a very stable initialization. Furthermore, for the task of
layout analysis at pixel level, we investigate the effectiveness of LDA-based
initialization and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art random weight
initialization methods.

The proposed model is designed to maintain high segmentation accuracy while significantly reducing computational complexity and memory footprint, making it suitable for real-time applications. The light-weight RefineNet is based on a multi-path refinement network that exploits the capabilities of modern hardware for efficient parallel processing. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, while being significantly faster and requiring less memory. This work opens up new possibilities for real-time semantic segmentation in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and embedded systems.

A member of the Graphidaceae family, Leucodecton canescens is a lichen species indigenous to Sri Lanka. In 2014, it was identified and named as a new species by lichen experts Gothamie Weerakoon, Robert Lücking, and Helge Thorsten Lumbsch. The type sample was sourced from the Maussakanda Tea Estate in Matale, Central Province, at an elevation of approximately 1800 meters. This lichen, found in various sites within the Central Province, thrives in semi-exposed, disrupted environments at high altitudes. The term canescens derives from its grey-toned thallus covering. Leucodecton canescens boasts a slick, grey thallus, measuring between 70-100 µm in thickness, and a slim (5-10 µm) cortex. The ascomata exhibit round shapes, are embedded in the substrate, and range from 0.2-0.3 mm in diameter. The ascospores possess muriform structures, with dimensions of 25-30 by 10-12 µm. Chemically, this lichen contains stictic acid, constictic acid, acetylconstictic acid, and hypostictic acid. Leucodecton fissurinum shares some resemblance in shape, but it features a yellowish thallus and more restricted ascomata pores that obscure the disc.

One 14-ounce can sweetened condensed milk
Finely grated zest and juice from 1 lemon, preferably Meyer lemon
1/2 vanilla bean, split lengthwise and seeds scraped
1/8 teaspoon ground cloves
Kosher salt
3 cups full-fat plain Greek yogurt
1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries, halved
1/4 cup sugar
1/2 cup finely diced tart green apple, such as Granny Smith
1/4 cup finely diced fennel
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
Preheat the oven to 325. In a bowl, whisk the condensed milk with the grated lemon zest, vanilla bean seeds, cloves and 1/4 teaspoon of kosher salt. Whisk in the yogurt until smooth. Arrange eight 8-ounce ceramic or glass ramekins in a large roasting pan and pour about 1/2 cup of the yogurt mixture into each ramekin. Add enough boiling water to the roasting pan to reach halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Bake for about 12 minutes, until the custards are set but slightly loose in the centers. Transfer the ramekins to a rack and let cool to room temperature. Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, cook the lemon juice, cranberries, sugar and 1 cup of water over high heat until the cranberries are just tender, about 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and let cool to room temperature, about 20 minutes. Drain the cranberries; save the syrup for another use. In a bowl, toss the apple and fennel with the olive oil and season lightly with salt. Spoon the cranberries and the apple salad over the custards and serve.

3 eggs
2 cups water
3 cups low sodium chicken broth
2 boneless chicken breasts
11 garlic cloves
1 teaspoon salt
2 bay leaves
1 teaspoon olive oil
6 tablespoons grated parmesan cheese
6 thin slices of a country-style French bread
1 tablespoon herbes de provence
1/2 teaspoon dried lavender
1/2 teaspoon dried rubbed sage
dried parsley
ground black pepper
olive oil, for toasting
Pour the water and the broth into a deep pot with the salt. Peel and crush 10 of the garlic cloves (I used the base of my glass measuring cup), then put into the broth. Add the bay leaves and the 1st teaspoon of olive oil. Cook for 15 minutes over medium-high heat. Cut the chicken into pieces, and stir into the soup along with all of the herbs (except the parsley). Peel and finely dice the last garlic clove, and add to the pot. Cook about 10 more minutes until the chicken is cooked through. In the meantime, brush both sides of the bread slices with olive oil, and then fry over medium heat until golden brown. (Or you can bake them, I suppose!). Set the toast to the side, and fry each egg one at a time. Sprinkle with parsley and ground black pepper. Set these to the side too. Bring the soup to a boil for 5 minutes, and then strain the soup into a bowl, and then return the broth to the pot. Rinse any clinging herbs from the chicken pieces, and put the chicken back into the soup. Discard all other solids. To serve, place 2 slices toast into the bottom of each (wide and shallow) bowl. Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of Parmesan cheese over each bowl. Ladle the soup over the bread and cheese, and top with an egg. Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot. (Eat this right away, or the bread will become soggy). Serve with fresh apple slices and lightly steamed broccoli or asparagus tips.

My window reveals the traveling clouds,
Discarded leaves, new seasons, altered sky,
Crowds forming and dissolving: The entire world evolves; I remain still.
They don't squander allotted time,
But men and leaders strategize and construct: I witness their towers' triumphs,
And fulfilled promises take flight.
Perhaps, had my intentions held sway,
In prehistoric times, my efforts might have reached such heights,
But now, before the crucible can gleam
With undiscovered treasures,
The bellows will eventually cease to blow,
The forge will grow cold.
Yet it's too late to rectify
The debilitating and burdensome disgrace,
Which renders me powerless amidst men,
More so than the blind or lame.
No, I would scorn the city less,
Even than this unappreciative knowledge;
But I crave the wilderness,
Or rugged coastlines and shores.
I traverse my breezy vantage point,
To observe the waning western sun,
I notice the city pigeons shift,
I observe the tower swallows dart
Between the rooftop and the earth,
Beneath me in the open sky;
Then I discern within the horizons' expanse

Or ancient hills concealing remains,
Or cliffs where rockdoves gather,
And trees of terebinth, and stones,

The controversial sell-off of a Ukrainian steel mill to a relative of the former president was illegal, a court has ruled.
The mill, Krivorizhstal, was sold in June 2004 for $800m (£424m) - well below other offers. President Viktor Yushchenko, elected in December, is planning to revisit many of Ukraine's recent privatisations. Krivorizhstal is one of dozens of firms which he says were sold cheaply to friends of the previous administration.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko said as many as 3,000 firms could be included on the list of firms whose sale was being reviewed.
Mr Yushchenko had previously said the list would be limited to 30-40 enterprises. More than 90,000 businesses in all, from massive corporations to tiny shopfronts, have been sold off since 1992, as the command economy built up when Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union was dismantled. Analysts have suggested that the government needs to avoid the impression of an open-ended list, so as to preserve investor confidence.
Thursday's ruling by a district court in Perchesk overturned a previous decision in a lower court permitting the sale. The consortium which won the auction for the mill was created by Viktor Pinchuk, son-in-law of former-President Leonid Kuchma, and Rinat Akhmetov, the country's richest man. The next step is for the supreme court to annul the sale altogether, opening the way for Krivorizhstal to be resold. Mr Yushchenko has suggested a fair valuation could be as much as $3bn. One of the foreign bidders who lost out, steel giant LNM, told BBC News that it would be interested in any renewed sale.

Omri, a young lad, obtains a cabinet from his sibling, Gillon, as a birthday gift. Utilizing a supposedly magical key inherited from his great-grandmother, Omri animates a Native American figurine made of plastic within the cabinet. The revived figure introduces himself as Little Bear (alternatively named Little Bull), an Iroquois native from the 18th century. As word spreads, Omri's pal, Patrick, learns of the enchanted cabinet and summons a cowboy, Boone, to the present. Amid squabbles and disagreements between the miniature men, Patrick declines to return them until it's too late - during a viewing of an ancient western film on TV, Little Bear injures Boone with an arrow. Although Omri possesses a World War I medic action figure capable of healing Boone, the figure remains inanimate due to the missing key. Following a short escapade involving Gillon's runaway rodent, the key is located and Boone recovers. However, Little Bear proves to be a capricious character, compelling Omri to secure a spouse for him, named Bright Stars (alternatively known as Twin Stars). Believing it prudent to return Little Bear, Bright Stars, and Boone (with Patrick's consent) to their respective eras, Omri hands over the key to his mother to resist the temptation of reactivating them.

rarely broken by clear, piercing blue

to see naked trees
Naked truth...

when seasons run together a blur
so you have to check a calender

weather as metaphor for mediocrity.

who deliver their products
on the evening news

A British Muslim organization, the Muslim Council of Britain, has voiced disapproval towards the upcoming series of US drama 24 airing on Sky One, asserting that it presents an unjust depiction of Islam. The group has lodged a complaint with media regulatory body Ofcom, alleging a violation of editorial standards. After assessing previews of the initial five episodes, Muslim Council of Britain members convened with Sky executives on Tuesday. The series, currently in its fourth installment, premieres on Sunday night. In this latest adaptation, a Muslim family is portrayed as a covert terrorist cell. The Muslim Council of Britain issued a statement expressing their worry: "We are deeply troubled by the one-sided and prejudicial representation of Muslims in this season of 24, based on our observation of the first five episodes." "Notably absent from the narrative thus far is a positively depicted Muslim character. Amidst the escalating unfavorable perceptions of Muslims, we believe Sky, as a prominent UK broadcaster, should assume a proactive stance in counteracting such detrimental perspectives rather than perpetuating them." However, Sky refuted the accusation of guideline infringement. A representative stated: "Sky held a constructive dialogue with council delegates yesterday. Sky maintains that the episodes under review do not contravene Ofcom's programming code." Fox TV, which telecasts the series domestically in the US, is countering criticism by airing public service advertisements showcasing Muslims in a favorable light following objections to the program.

A US banking institution, Riggs Bank, has announced over $8 million in contributions towards victims of the Augusto Pinochet regime in Chile through a Madrid court settlement. These funds will be administered by the Madrid-based Salvador Allende Foundation, which supports those who have endured mistreatment. Previously, accusations against Riggs Bank included the unlawful hiding of General Pinochet's assets. An official record states that more than 3,000 individuals met their demise due to political reasons during Pinochet's rule from 1973 to 1990. In a recent US court hearing, Riggs Bank acknowledged failing to report questionable transactions related to Pinochet and Equatorial Guinea's government, resulting in a $16m penalty. Despite numerous human rights violation cases against Pinochet, he has yet to face trial. Presently, he is under investigation for the murder of a single Chilean and the disappearance of nine others, as well as tax evasion, tax fraud, and misappropriation of public funds.

Supporters of Pinochet's adversaries celebrated the settlement reached in Madrid's courts. Lawyer for the victims, Eduardo Contreras, informed Reuters news agency, "This illustrates that the atrocities of the Pinochet dictatorship are no enigma, and the entire world acknowledges the deserving nature of compensation for his victims." Riggs Bank representative Mark Hendrix stated that the settlement, with specifics to be revealed next week, would facilitate closure on the issue. "This allows the institution to leave this matter in the past," Hendrix conveyed to Reuters. The settlement transpired after a grievance was lodged against the bank by Spanish Judge Baltasar Garzon, accusing it of asset concealment. The bank consented to establish a fund for the victims, yet the charges were subsequently dismissed.

Apocalypse now is not only the best war film ever made but it's also one of the best films of all time as it won the prestigious Palme d'Or at Cannes and it's constantly recognized as a benchmark in cinematic history. Based on the novel "Hearts of darkness" by Joseph Conrad this film is not so much about the Vietnam war, it is about war in general and serves as a deep study into the dark places of the human soul and how war can affect the individual. Apocalypse now depicts a timeless story about a universal human struggle, the duality of man, consisting of morality, the savage primordial instinct and what every person chooses to base his actions upon.

The film has a simple premise, US Army Captain Benjamin Willard (Martin Sheen) is ordered on a dangerous mission into Cambodia through a river, to assassinate a renegade, Colonel Kurtz (Marlon Brando), who has gone insane and set himself up as a god among the local native tribe. It's an accessible premise, allowing for the film to be consumed by even the most casual movie watchers, and yet this film is anything but shallow. It's a journey into madness and hysteria, an observation into the darkness of humanity. I could write a book analyzing this film, there's just so much to talk about. My interpretation is that the river is not only the passage to find Kurtz but also the descent into madness and a reflection to the character's inner journey towards evil that is accomplished through the main theme of the movie, dehumanization. The journey through the river is also reminiscent of Dante's perilous journey through unspeakable surroundings and horrors. There are three major stops before Kurtz and each stop on the river furthers the dehumanization that war has brought, as well as implanting a new type of evil to the characters.

The first stop is with lieutenant Kilgore. That stop shows that Kilgore and his soldiers have been consumed by the love of war after they dehumanized the enemy. Their love of war has blinded them so much that they see no negative and can't comprehend the consequences the war will bring. In one scene of the movie, the "heroic" marching of the helicopters to lay wrath upon their enemies, Captain Kilgore uses Wagner's Ride of the Valkyries to pump his soldiers and scare his enemies and like the mythical creatures Valkyries, he is the decider of who lives and who dies on the battle. At this stage, although everyone has removed any shred of humanity from the enemy, they still understand the innocent.

The second stop is the USO show where we see the loss of morality as well as the dehumanization of the innocent. At this stop we see that a soldier dehumanized everyone aside from himself, becoming very selfish and losing any compassion for anyone but themselves. The soldiers that have passed through this stop would be willing to put anyone at risk for their instant gratification. Now as the characters go deeper into the river metaphorically they go deeper into themselves to explore their own evils which are becoming more apparent. The last stop before Kurtz is the Do-long Bridge and it's at this point that a soldier has gone too far, he's experienced so much trauma and so much evil that he lost grip with his own sanity and thus he dehumanized himself and can't return to a normal state of mind.

The final stop on the journey is Kurtz, at this point only Willard and Kurtz have passed the madness stage and they are competing for the heart of darkness, the ultimate evil that we all have the capacity to have. Kurtz is in possession of the heart of darkness as he associates evil with strength. Bypassing the madness stage he's able to see the world for what it truly is, filled with hypocrites and he decides to bury his hatred and simply act on instinct. Willard at the end of the film rises from the river reborn as a new man ready to obtain the heart himself. He kills Kurtz and leaves the compound with his heart corrupted. In the end Willard has a choice, succumb to evil and stay in the compound having taken Kurtz's place as the leader of the savages or abandoning them into their fates...throwing his weapon, he emerges from the bottomless pit he had fallen through the heart of darkness and by saving Lance and choosing not to exterminate the tribe, he has completed his personal journey and tested his soul to the very limit. Both of them at any point could have just stopped but they didn't, they wanted to explore the depths of their souls and just how much further they could go.

The film presents this study of the human psyche through Carmine Coppola's eerie score, hypnotic images, and some haunting scenes, essentially taking the viewer into the depths of hell. It's here where Coppola succeeds the most. His ability to create a living "hell" is so amazing, and it perfectly captures the mindset of the soldiers. It provides a commentary on war and religion, making the subtext even vaster. The film is weirdly beautiful and a true picture of the evil and hell from within ourselves.

The cinematography by Vittorio Storaro is phenomenal and it provides a hallucinatory feeling throughout the film's runtime - from the faces of the losing minds covered in endless sweat, and the sight of figures within the shadows to a dark trenched riverbank - everything is captured in a stunning manner, conveying the hellish imagery and still taking the viewer's breath away. Coppola's direction transcends itself, the camerawork is at its absolute best when it comes to the use of lighting and shadows, most notable during Col. Kurtz's first appearance. The troubled production obviously didn't hurt the film at all, and most likely increased the dark quality it portrays. Apocalypse Now is beautifully haunting, utterly hellish, terrifyingly intelligent, and magnificently wrought, it slowly pushes you into the horror and absurdity of war, but also its meaningfulness and beauty. Not only is this one of the best films ever made, it's a psychoanalytical journey into places none of us would dare to venture to on our own. It is Francis Ford Coppola's magnum opus as he sacrificed everything to make it work. Rightfully deserving its place as one of the greatest on the cinematic pantheon, immortal for its contribution to cinema, and a truly unforgettable experience, Apocalypse Now is cinema at its most complete, crystalline and pure.

Ulster clung on for a morale-boosting Celtic League win over bottom club Borders at Netherdale on Friday night.
A late try by Borders substitute Jonny Weston had set up a dramatic finish, but the Scottish side could not complete the fightback. Ulster had led 20-6 with tries from Paul Steinmetz and Bryn Cunningham. But the Irish province failed to add to the tally in the second half and ended up relieved to get the win to lift them to eighth place in the table. Borders had edged ahead with a sixth-minute penalty by Charlie Hore - only to hand the visitors the initiative via a gift try. Calum MacRae surrendered possession before centre Steinmetz sent a chip into the danger zone. Substitute Joe Pattison - who had come on for the injured Gareth Morton - wrongly thought the ball was trickling out of play and eased up on the chase.
The speedy Steinmetz had other ideas and he raced up to get the vital touch in the nick of time, giving Adam Larkin an easy conversion. Ally Warnock clawed back three points for Borders, but they were soon hit by another double-blow. First, Mark Blair was yellow carded for killing the ball on the ground and then full-back Cunningham bagged the second touchdown in the wake of fine work by skipper Andy Ward. Larkin again added the extras. Even worse was to come for Borders when Larkin kicked two more penalties just before the break, the second of which also led to Kelly Brown being sin-binned. The hosts gave themselves a glimmer of hope immediately after the restart, however, when Warnock struck a penalty at the other end. And he repeated the feat to set up the tense finale. Ulster coach mark McCall said he was delighted to get the victory. "Borders are a tougher proposition this year in spite of the fact that they have not had a victory in some time," said McCall. "In the first 20 minutes we were edgy but in the second 20 minutes we played some of our best rugby this season and scored two good tries."

Leading US bank JPMorgan Chase has issued an apology after disclosing that two of its predecessor banks had accepted thousands of slaves as collateral prior to the Civil War. This unsettling revelation means that, at the time, these organisations were indeed seemingly involved in the slave trade and played a role in maintaining this abusive system.

The banks - Citizen's Bank and Canal Bank in Louisiana - were part of JPMorgan's heritage. Both these institutions served plantations from the mid-19th century and accepted enslaved persons as collateral on loans. When plantation owners defaulted on loans, the banks took ownership of these slaves.

Documents also revealed that the banks occasionally sold off slaves to raise funds. They owned a total of 1,250 slaves and accepted at least 13,000 as collateral before the Civil War.

JPMorgan said it apologises "to the African-American community, particularly those for whom slavery is not merely an historical fact but a personal tragedy". The bank went on to recognise that people in America still face harsh realities under the long shadow of slavery.

The bank's revelation, initially disclosed in a memo to its employee was picked up by the Chicago Sun-Times. This apology comes amid a backdrop of increased scrutiny of American institutions and their historical ties to the abhorrent trade of enslaved people.

The bank stated that this acknowledgment is "a statement of fact", not an attempt to compensate or make reparation. It is a painful acknowledgment of how deeply the roots of slavery are entwined within the American financial system.

This revelation, nonetheless, could lead to further inquiry into the banking industry's historical ties to slavery, which remains a deeply sensitive issue in the US. In the past, companies such as insurer Aetna and bank Wachovia (now part of Wells Fargo) have also admitted their historic organisational links to slavery and have issued apologies.

The bank's disclosure highlights just how entangled the institution of slavery is in the United States' history. Despite the progress made since then, the lingering effects of this traumatic past remain visible in the persistent racial inequalities and systemic racism that is observed today. 

JPMorgan has not detailed any plans to provide reparations or support to the African American community following their admission. However, this step of admission and apology is seen by some as the first towards atonement and fostering open discussions around systemic racism and institutional responsibility.

Sweetest love, I do not go,
For weariness of thee,
Nor in hope the world can show
A fitter love for me;
But since that I
Must die at last, 'tis best
To use myself in jest
Thus by feign'd deaths to die.
Yesternight the sun went hence,
And yet is here today;
He hath no desire nor sense,
Nor half so short a way:
Then fear not me,
But believe that I shall make
Speedier journeys, since I take
More wings and spurs than he.
O how feeble is man's power,
That if good fortune fall,
Cannot add another hour,
Nor a lost hour recall!
But come bad chance,
And we join to'it our strength,
And we teach it art and length,
Itself o'er us to'advance.
When thou sigh'st, thou sigh'st not wind,
But sigh'st my soul away;
When thou weep'st, unkindly kind,
My life's blood doth decay.
It cannot be
That thou lov'st me, as thou say'st,
If in thine my life thou waste,
That art the best of me.
Let not thy divining heart
Forethink me any ill;
Destiny may take thy part,
And may thy fears fulfil;
But think that we
Are but turn'd aside to sleep;
They who one another keep
Alive, ne'er parted be.

Micki Grant (born January 1, 1952) is an American actress and singer. She was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania to parents who were both musicians. Her father played saxophone with The Ink Spots and her mother sang with The Chordettes.

Grant began performing at an early age, singing with her family's band. After graduating from high school, she attended Temple University where she studied music and theater. While there, she appeared in several productions including "The Wiz" and "Ain't Misbehavin'."

After college, Grant moved to New York City and began working as a professional singer and actress. She made her Broadway debut in the musical "Dreamgirls," which starred Jennifer Hudson. She also appeared in the revival of "Hair" and the Off-Broadway production of "Soul Food."

In addition to her work on stage, Grant has appeared in numerous television shows and films. Some of her notable roles include:

* "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit"
* "ER"
* "The Sopranos"
* "The Wire"
* "The Good Wife"
* "Chicago Fire"

Grant has also released two albums, "I Am...Micki Grant" and "Love Is My Thing."

Today, Grant continues to perform live and appears regularly on stage and screen.

Medical image segmentation is crucial for various clinical applications like diagnosis and treatment planning. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) deliver top-notch performance, they fall short in terms of clinically acceptable precision and adaptability in intricate scenarios. Interactive segmentation thus emerges as a viable alternative. However, conventional interactive segmentation techniques necessitate an extensive number of user inputs, whereas contemporary CNN-based methods display subpar performance when handling new entities. In order to surmount these challenges, we put forth a fresh deep learning-approach to interactive segmentation. This method not only ensures high productivity due to minimal user clicks as inputs but also exhibits versatility in dealing with a spectrum of hitherto unencountered objects. Initially, we encode user-designated internal boundary markers using our suggested exponential geodesic distance, empowering the CNN to generate satisfactory primary segmentations for both familiar and novel objects. Subsequently, we employ a novel data fusion technique that merges the initial segmentation with just a few extra user clicks to swiftly yield a polished segmentation. Our research confirmed the efficacy of this approach via comprehensive tests on 2D and 3D medical image segmentation tasks incorporating a broad assortment of unseen objects that did not feature in the training dataset. The findings revealed that our proposed system 1) delivers precise outcomes with reduced user interactions and time compared to current interactive systems, and 2) adapts effectively to newly encountered objects.

Recipe: Sin-Free Squash & Pepper Stacks

Ingredients:
- 2 medium-sized yellow squash
- 2 medium-sized zucchini
- 1 red bell pepper
- 1 yellow bell pepper
- 1 green bell pepper
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried basil
- 1 teaspoon garlic powder
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: grated Parmesan cheese for topping

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).

2. Wash and dry the yellow squash, zucchini, and bell peppers. Slice the squash and zucchini into 1/4-inch thick rounds. Cut the bell peppers into 1/2-inch wide strips.

3. In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, dried oregano, dried basil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Mix well.

4. Add the sliced squash, zucchini, and bell peppers to the bowl with the seasoning mixture. Toss until all the vegetables are evenly coated.

5. Take a baking dish and lightly grease it with olive oil or cooking spray.

6. Begin stacking the vegetables in the baking dish, alternating between layers of squash, zucchini, and bell peppers. You can create a pattern or simply stack them randomly.

7. Once all the vegetables are stacked, drizzle any remaining seasoning mixture over the top.

8. Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and place it in the preheated oven.

9. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.

10. Remove the foil and sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the top, if desired. Return the dish to the oven for an additional 5 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and slightly golden.

11. Remove from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.

12. Serve the Sin-Free Squash & Pepper Stacks as a side dish or as a main course with a side of rice or quinoa.

Enjoy your guilt-free and delicious Sin-Free Squash & Pepper Stacks!

I dwell in a lonely house I know
That vanished many a summer ago,
And left no trace but the cellar walls,
And a cellar in which the daylight falls,
And the purple-stemmed wild raspberries grow.
O'er ruined fences the grape-vines shield
The woods come back to the mowing field;
The orchard tree has grown one copse
Of new wood and old where the woodpecker chops;
The footpath down to the well is healed.
I dwell with a strangely aching heart
In that vanished abode there far apart
On that disused and forgotten road
That has no dust-bath now for the toad.
Night comes; the black bats tumble and dart;
The whippoorwill is coming to shout
And hush and cluck and flutter about:
I hear him begin far enough away
Full many a time to say his say
Before he arrives to say it out.
It is under the small, dim, summer star.
I know not who these mute folk are
Who share the unlit place with me--
Those stones out under the low-limbed tree
Doubtless bear names that the mosses mar.
They are tireless folk, but slow and sad,
Though two, close-keeping, are lass and lad,--
With none among them that ever sings,
And yet, in view of how many things,
As sweet companions as might be had.

Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
- 1/4 to 1/2 cup ice water

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and salt.
2. Add cold cubed butter to the dry ingredients and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
3. Gradually stir in ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until dough comes together in a ball.

5. Wrap each disk tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or until ready to use.
6. When ready to use, roll out the dough on a floured surface to your desired thickness and transfer to a pie dish.
7. Fill the pastry with your desired filling and bake according to your recipe instructions.

Sportswear giant Nike has reported strong quarterly growth, exceeding market expectations. The company's revenue for the quarter ending in May reached $12.3 billion, a 96% increase compared to the same period last year. This remarkable growth can be attributed to several factors, including the reopening of economies worldwide and the increasing demand for athletic apparel and footwear.

Nike's digital sales played a significant role in driving the company's success, with a staggering 147% increase in online sales. As consumers turned to online shopping during the pandemic, Nike's robust e-commerce platform proved to be a valuable asset. The company's direct-to-consumer sales also saw a remarkable surge, rising by 73% compared to the previous year.

Furthermore, Nike's strong performance was not limited to its home market. International sales soared by 88%, with particularly impressive growth in China, where revenue increased by 17%. This growth in China is a testament to Nike's ability to tap into the country's booming consumer market and capitalize on the rising popularity of sports and fitness.

Nike's success can also be attributed to its ability to adapt and innovate. The company has been quick to respond to changing consumer preferences, focusing on sustainability and inclusivity. Nike's commitment to sustainability is evident in its efforts to reduce its carbon footprint and increase the use of recycled materials in its products. Additionally, the company's collaborations with diverse athletes and celebrities have helped it resonate with a broader audience and drive sales.

Looking ahead, Nike remains optimistic about its future prospects. The company expects continued growth in the coming quarters, driven by the return of sports events and the ongoing shift towards athleisure wear. Nike's strong brand reputation and innovative product offerings position it well to capitalize on these trends and maintain its market dominance.

Despite the positive outlook, Nike acknowledges potential challenges, including supply chain disruptions and rising raw material costs. However, the company remains confident in its ability to navigate these obstacles and continue delivering strong results.

In summary, Nike's strong quarterly growth reflects its ability to adapt to changing consumer preferences, capitalize on digital sales channels, and expand its international presence. With a focus on sustainability and inclusivity, the sportswear giant is well-positioned to maintain its market leadership and drive further growth in the future.

The explosion in consumer technology is to continue into 2005, delegates at the world's largest gadget show, in Las Vegas, have been told.
The number of gadgets in the shops is predicted to grow by 11%, while devices which talk to each other will become increasingly important. "Everything is going digital," Kirsten Pfeifer from the Consumer Electronics Association, told the BBC News website. The Consumer Electronics Show (CES) featured the pick of 2005's products. "Consumers are controlling what they want and technologies like HDTVs [high-definition TVs], digital radio, and digital cameras will remain strong in 2005. "All the products on show really showed the breadth and depth of the industry." Despite showing diversity, some delegates attending complained that the showcase lacked as much "wow factor" as in previous years.
The portable technologies on show also reflected one of the buzzwords of CES, which was the "time and place shifting" of multimedia content - being able to watch and listen to video and music anywhere, at any time. At the start of last year's CES, the CEA predicted there would be an average growth of 4% in 2004. That figure was surpassed with the rise in popularity of portable digital music players, personal video recorders and digital cameras. It was clear also that gadgets are becoming a lot more about lifestyle choice, with fashion and personalisation becoming increasingly key to the way gadgets are designed. Part of this has been the rise in spending power of the "generation X-ers" who have grown up with technology and who now have the spending power and desire for more devices that suit them. More than 57% of the consumer electronics market is made up of female buyers, according to CEA research. Hybrid devices, which combine a number of multimedia functions, were also in evidence on the show floor. "A lot of this is driven by just the ability to do it," said Stephen Baker, a consumer electronics analyst with retail research firm NPD Group. "Some of these functions cost next to nothing to add."
As well as the show floor showcasing everything from tiny wearable MP3 players to giant high-definition TVs, several keynote speeches were made by industry leaders, such as Microsoft chief Bill Gates. Despite several embarrassing technical glitches during Mr Gate's pre-show speech, he announced several new partnerships - mainly for the US market. He unveiled new ways of letting people take TV shows recorded on personal video recorders and watch them back on portable devices. He disappointed some, however, by failing to announce any details of the next generation of the Xbox games console. Another disappointment was the lack of exposure Sony's new portable games device, the PSP, had at the show. Sony said the much-anticipated gadget would most likely start shipping in March for the US and Europe. It went on sale in Japan before Christmas. There were only two PSPs embedded in glass cabinets at the show though and no representatives to discuss further details. A Sony representative told the BBC News website this was because Sony did not consider it to be part of their "consumer technology" offering.
Elsewhere at the show, there was a plethora of colour and plasma screens, including Samsung's 102-inch (2.6 metre) plasma - the largest in the world. Industry experts were also excited about high-definition technologies coming to the fore in 2005, with new formats for DVDs coming out which will hold six times as much data as conventional DVDs. With so many devices on the move there were a lot of products on show offering external storage, like Seagate's 5GB pocket sized external hard drive, which won an innovation for engineering and design prize. More than 120,000 trade professionals attended CES in Las Vegas, which officially ran from 6 to 9 January.

The Epipalaeolithic, also known as the Late Stone Age or Mesolithic, is a period in human prehistory that falls between the end of the Paleolithic period and the beginning of the Neolithic period. It is characterized by the transition from a nomadic, hunter-gatherer lifestyle to a more settled, agricultural way of life.

The Epipalaeolithic period is generally dated from around 20,000 to 10,000 years ago, although these dates can vary depending on the region. It is a time of significant cultural and technological developments, as humans began to adapt to changing environmental conditions and exploit new resources.

During the Epipalaeolithic, the climate was gradually warming after the last Ice Age, leading to the retreat of glaciers and the expansion of forests. This created new opportunities for human populations, as they could now exploit a wider range of plant and animal resources. As a result, there was a shift towards a more sedentary lifestyle, with the establishment of semi-permanent settlements and the development of more complex social structures.

One of the key innovations of the Epipalaeolithic period was the development of new tools and technologies. Stone tools became more specialized and efficient, with the introduction of microliths – small, finely crafted stone blades that could be hafted onto wooden handles or used as projectile points. These microliths were used for a variety of purposes, including hunting, fishing, and woodworking.

The Epipalaeolithic period also witnessed the emergence of early forms of agriculture and animal domestication. While hunting and gathering remained the primary means of subsistence, there is evidence of early cultivation of wild cereals and the domestication of animals such as dogs. This laid the foundation for the later transition to full-scale agriculture and the development of settled farming communities during the Neolithic period.

Archaeological evidence from Epipalaeolithic sites provides valuable insights into the lives of these early human populations. Excavations have revealed evidence of dwellings, storage pits, and hearths, indicating the establishment of semi-permanent settlements. Artifacts such as pottery, bone tools, and personal ornaments have also been found, suggesting the development of more complex social and cultural practices.

Troubled insurance broker Marsh & McLennan is facing a formal investigation by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The SEC is looking into whether the company misled investors about the way it conducted business and the fees it charged clients.

The probe is the latest setback for Marsh, which has been struggling to recover from a scandal over the way it allegedly rigged bids for insurance contracts.

The company has already agreed to pay $850m (£470m) to settle civil charges brought by New York Attorney General Eliot Spitzer.

Mr Spitzer accused Marsh of taking kickbacks from insurers in return for steering business their way.

The SEC's investigation is at an early stage and it is not clear if any action will be taken against the company.

A Marsh spokesman said the company was co-operating with the SEC.

The SEC probe is the latest in a string of problems for Marsh, which is the world's largest insurance broker.

Last month, the company announced that it was axing 1,700 jobs, or 5% of its workforce, in a bid to cut costs.

And in October, Marsh ousted its chief executive, Jeffrey W. Greenberg, in an attempt to draw a line under the scandal.

Two cups of finely grated sharp Cheddar cheese, combined with:
1 teaspoon of dried thyme or 1 tablespoon of finely chopped fresh thyme
1 teaspoon of dried sage or 1 tablespoon of finely chopped fresh sage
1/2 teaspoon of dried oregano or 1 1/2 teaspoons of finely chopped fresh oregano
1/4 teaspoon of cayenne pepper
Salt, to taste
1 box (17.3 oz) of thawed frozen puff pastry (two sheets)
Two large baking sheets, lined with parchment paper
In a mixing bowl, blend together the cheese, herbs, and cayenne pepper. Add salt to taste. On a lightly floured work surface, unfurl one sheet of pastry and shape it into a 16x9 1/2 inch rectangle. Spread half of the cheese mixture on the lower half of the pastry sheet. Fold the upper half over the cheese-covered portion, forming an 8x9 1/2 inch rectangle. Press down to seal the edges and expel trapped air. Roll out again into an 8x16 inch rectangle. Transfer to a baking sheet and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Repeat this process with the second pastry sheet and the remaining cheese mixture. Chill both for 20 minutes. Set the oven temperature to 425°F. Current deep learning models based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) lead the field in supervised medical image segmentation, delivering superior results across diverse imaging modalities and tasks. However, these models can produce anatomically incorrect segmentations with gaps or inaccuracies close to object edges. To counteract this issue, contemporary studies have concentrated on integrating spatial data or expertise to ensure physiologically viable segmentation. Although the application of prior knowledge in image segmentation is not a novel concept in traditional optimization methods, it has gained traction in CNN-driven segmentation, as evidenced by the expanding body of research on the subject. In this review, we explore high-level priors integrated into the loss function. We classify articles based on the kind of prior: object shape, size, topology, and inter-region constraints. We examine the advantages and disadvantages of existing techniques, discuss challenges related to designing and implementing prior-based losses, and propose optimization strategies, and suggest potential areas for future investigation.

David Zimmer (born January 19, 1946) is a Canadian politician, who served in the Legislative Assembly of Ontario from 1995 to 2014 as a member of the Liberal Party. He served in the cabinet of Premiers Dalton McGuinty and Kathleen Wynne, and was the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario from 2014 to 2018.

Zimmer was born in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and raised in Toronto. He attended the University of Toronto, graduating with a bachelor's degree in Political Science and Economics in 1968. He later attended Osgoode Hall Law School, receiving an LL.B. in 1972. After graduating, he worked as a lawyer and became a partner in the firm of Goldblatt, Fryer, and Zimmer.

Zimmer was first elected to the Ontario legislature in the 1995 provincial election, defeating Progressive Conservative incumbent Bill Saunderson in the riding of Ottawa South. He was re-elected in the 1999, 2003, 2007, and 2011 provincial elections.

Zimmer served in a variety of cabinet positions in the government of Premier Dalton McGuinty. On January 18, 2001, he was appointed Minister of Intergovernmental Affairs. He held this position until September 25, 2001, when he was appointed Minister of Education. On February 25, 2003, he was also appointed Minister of Colleges and Universities. On November 25, 2003, he was appointed Minister of Health and Long-Term Care. On July 30, 2007, he was appointed Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

On February 4, 2008, Zimmer was elected as Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario by his peers. He served as Speaker until October 5, 2011, when he was appointed Minister of Environment.

Zimmer served as Minister of Environment until the defeat of the McGuinty government in the 2011 provincial election. The incoming Premier, Kathleen Wynne, appointed him as Minister of Aboriginal Affairs on February 11, 2013. On July 24, 2015, he was appointed Minister of Health and Long-Term Care.

Zimmer did not re-offer in the 2014 provincial election. After the election, he was elected Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario on November 5, 2014. He served as Speaker until 2018.

The most advanced technique for isolating white matter bundles in diffusion-weighted MRI through automated means is achieved via tractography combined with streamline clustering. This procedure consists of intricate sequences of computational stages, which are both expensive and challenging to configure, as well as time-consuming when it comes to ensuring high-quality outcomes. Traditional segmentation methods directly tackle this issue as an ordinary image segmentation problem. Although they have yet to match the competition, they may alleviate several of the cited difficulties. We introduce a new supervised method for direct tract segmentation that yields significant improvements. Based on a stacked U-Net architecture, it utilizes manual bundle segmentations from Human Connectome Project subjects for training. Our method is assessed both in real life and in simulation using the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge phantom dataset. We attain human-level segmentation performance and a substantial enhancement over preceding workflows. We demonstrate how these acquired spatial biases effectively steer the segmentation even at reduced image qualities with minimal degradation.

The Almshouse is an historic almshouse located at 45 Matignon Road in Cambridge, Massachusetts.  It is now the site of the International School of Boston's main campus.  It was built in 1850 and is a prominent example of institutional residential architecture in stone, resembling prisons of the era.  The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982, where it is incorrectly listed at 41 Orchard Street. Description and history
The former Cambridge Almshouse is located in the northwestern corner of Cambridge, on the north side of Matignon Road between Matignon High School and the St. Sava Serbian Orthodox Church.  It is a large three-story stone structure with modest Greek Revival styling, set partly across the city line between Cambridge and Somerville.  It has a central octagonal administrative section from which four wings of varying sizes radiate.  It is built mostly out of slate blocks that were quarried from a ledge on site, with dressed dark granite corner quoining, and granite belt courses between the floors.  The rooflines are pierced by rows of gabled dormers.

Recent advancements in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have led to impressive outcomes in numerous computer vision projects. Nevertheless, their usage in tasks featuring substantial input and output dimensions, including high-resolution image and video segmentation, as well as 3D medical imaging, has been hindered by several factors. Principally, during the training phase, retaining network activations for backpropagation necessitates vast storage capacity. In instances where memory demands for preserving activations outstrip existing hardware capabilities, particularly for 3D-related challenges. In this study, inspired by the transmission of signals through physical networks, which conform to the hyperbolic Telegraph equation, we present a fully conservative hyperbolic network tailored to high-dimensional input and output scenarios. We propose a downsampling process involving a trainable Discrete Wavelet Transform and its inverse to both decrease and enhance the network condition and modify the number of channels. Our findings demonstrate that entirely reversible networks yield comparable performance to current benchmarks in 4D time-lapse hyperspectral image segmentation and complete 3D video segmentation, while maintaining a consistent memory footprint that remains constant regardless of network depth. Furthermore, we apply these networks to Variational Auto Encoders with elevated resolution input and output.

In this study, we offer a comprehensive relativistic analysis of the recorded galaxy count data in the linear regime. Our findings reveal that apart from density fluctuations and redshift-space distortions, several relativistic influences influence observations at vast scales. These impacts stem from the deformation of our reference frame, specifically the galaxy redshifts and the approaching photon directions, caused by inconsistencies within our universe. Subsequently, we examine the implications of these relativistic effects on the angular power spectrum and the two-point correlation function in real space. We demonstrate that the latter is an effective tool for distinguishing relativistic effects due to its inherent utilization of the distinct symmetries of the various components. Particularly, we discuss methods to differentiate the Doppler effect and gravitational redshift distortions through investigation of a dipole pattern in the cross-correlation function between a luminous and a faint sample of galaxies.

Interpreting scribbles through semantic segmentation holds appeal yet poses difficulties: (i) hand-drawn sketches exhibit significant differences in portraying objects due to varying drawing styles and abilities; (ii) skewed lines on touchscreens complicate recognition; (iii) sophisticated image segmentation using advanced deep learning techniques necessitates substantial labeled sketch databases for training. This study introduces the Sketch-target Deep FCN Segmentation Network (SFSegNet), designed for automated identification of free-hand sketches, assigning each sketch a single object with multiple components. SFSegNet comprises two primary sections in its end-to-end network structure: (i) a customized deep Fully Convolutional Network (FCN), incorporating a reweighting approach to disregard background pixels and determine which segment each pixel falls into; (ii) affine transform decoders aiming to normalize unsteady brushstrokes. Our network is conditioned on a dataset of 10,000 labeled sketches, aiming to produce a versatile model capable of recognizing stroke semantics within a sole ground truth. Experiments demonstrate superior performance compared to existing top-tier networks.

Fairfield is a borough in Adams County, Pennsylvania, United States. The population was 507 at the 2010 census. History
During the Gettysburg Campaign in the American Civil War, the Battle of Fairfield played an important role in securing the Fairfield pass and the Hagerstown Road,  enabling Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia to retreat through Fairfield towards the Potomac River. The actual fighting near Fairfield was between elements of the 6th United States Cavalry under Major Samuel Starr, and elements of General "Grumble" Jones' Brigade of Virginia Cavalry. The Union casualties were treated in the town of Fairfield, specifically in the homes of Mrs. Sarah Amanda Blythe, Rufus Christian Swope, and in what is now St. John's Lutheran Church. For more information on the town of Fairfield, see Fairfield In the Civil War, by Sarah Sites Thomas, Tim Smith, Gary Kross, and Dean S. Thomas.

T-Mobile said it was the first mobile operator to offer such a deal.

It said that by combining its HotSpot service - which offers access to wireless networks at airports, hotels and cafes - with Skype, it could provide an alternative to traditional fixed line telephony services.

Users can download the Skype application onto their handsets via the web and then connect to any of T-Mobile's hotspots to start making calls.

They are also able to receive incoming calls while they are away from home or work.

Callers do not need to have Skype installed on their own computers but must have a microphone attached to their PC.

A spokesman for T-Mobile said that the company had already seen a surge in demand for its HotSpot service since announcing the new partnership last week.

Ingredients:
2 lbs mirabelle plums (about 20-25 plums)
2 cups sugar
1/2 cup fresh rosemary leaves
1/4 tsp kosher salt

Instructions:
1. Rinse the mirabelle plums and pat them dry with a paper towel. Remove the stems and cut the plums in half. Remove the pits.
2. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, combine the sugar, rosemary, and salt. Add the plums and stir to combine.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture has thickened and the plums have broken down, about 30-45 minutes.
4. Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture cool for 5 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
5. Transfer the jam to a clean jar and let it cool to room temperature. Cover and refrigerate for up to 1 month.
