Verizon has won a takeover battle for US phone firm MCI with a bid worth $6.8bn (£3.6bn), reports say.
The two firms are expected to seal the deal on Monday morning, according to news agency reports, despite what was thought to be a higher bid from Qwest. The US telecoms market is consolidating fast, with former long-distance giant AT&T being bought by former subsidiary SBC earlier this year for $16bn. MCI exited bankruptcy in April, having gone bust under previous name WorldCom. The bankruptcy followed its admission in 2002 that it illegally booked expenses and inflated profits.
Shareholders lost about $180bn when the company collapsed, while 20,000 workers lost their jobs. Former Worldcom boss Bernie Ebbers is currently on trial, accused of overseeing an $11bn fraud. Qwest has itself come under suspicion of sub-standard behaviour, paying the Securities and Exchange Commission $250m in October to settle charges that it manipulated its results to keep Wall Street happy.
MCI is the US's second-biggest long distance firm after AT&T. Consolidation in the US telecommunications industry has picked up in the past few months as companies look to cut costs and boost client bases. A merger between MCI and Verizon would be the fifth billion-dollar telecoms deal since October. Last week, SBC Communications agreed to buy its former parent and phone trailblazer AT&T for about $16bn. Buying MCI would give either Qwest or Verizon access to MCI's global network and business-based subscribers. The rationale is similar to the one underpinning SBC's AT&T deal. Verizon is by far the bigger company and has its own successful mobile arm - factors which may have swung the board in its favour since both suitors are offering a mixture of cash and shares.

12 oz flank steak, devoid of extra fat and connective tissue
1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
1.5 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp cornstarch
1 tsp peanut or veg oil
1 tsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
0.25 tsp kosher salt
0.25 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp oyster sauce
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
2 tbsp peanut or veg oil
1.5 C sugar snap peas (approx 7 oz), stringless
1 C thinly sliced carrots (approx 2 small)
4 medium scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 2-inch lengths
0.25 C pickled ginger slices (approx 1 oz), chopped if large
Cook rice as base, serve alongside
Slice flank steak against the grain into 2-inch wide strips, then slice each strip crosswise into 1/4-inch thick pieces. Combine beef with remaining ingredients in a medium bowl and mix evenly. Set aside. In a small bowl, blend oyster sauce and Shaoxing wine or sherry. Set aside. Heat a 14-inch flat-bottomed wok over high temp until a droplet of water evaporates upon contact. Coat wok edge with 1 tbsp oil, add beef in a single layer. Sear undisturbed till browning starts, roughly 1 min. Stir-fry for 30 secs till lightly browned but not fully cooked. Transfer to plate. Coat wok edge with remaining oil, add sugar snaps and carrots. Quickly cook till heated through, approx 1 min. Reunite beef with veggies and wok, add oyster sauce blend, scallions, and pickled ginger. Stir-fry till beef is done and ginger dispersed, about 30-60 secs. Serve with rice.

We present a generalized and scalable method, called Gen-LaneNet, to detect
3D lanes from a single image. The method, inspired by the latest
state-of-the-art 3D-LaneNet, is a unified framework solving image encoding,
spatial transform of features and 3D lane prediction in a single network.
However, we propose unique designs for Gen-LaneNet in two folds. First, we
introduce a new geometry-guided lane anchor representation in a new coordinate
frame and apply a specific geometric transformation to directly calculate real
3D lane points from the network output. We demonstrate that aligning the lane
points with the underlying top-view features in the new coordinate frame is
critical towards a generalized method in handling unfamiliar scenes. Second, we
present a scalable two-stage framework that decouples the learning of image
segmentation subnetwork and geometry encoding subnetwork. Compared to
3D-LaneNet, the proposed Gen-LaneNet drastically reduces the amount of 3D lane
labels required to achieve a robust solution in real-world application.
Moreover, we release a new synthetic dataset and its construction strategy to
encourage the development and evaluation of 3D lane detection methods. In
experiments, we conduct extensive ablation study to substantiate the proposed
Gen-LaneNet significantly outperforms 3D-LaneNet in average precision(AP) and
F-score.

Independence Day is the sort of film that's best appreciated on a big screen, preferably a massive great plasma television that is so huge you had to cut the roof off your house and get airlifted in by helicopters just to get it in the living room. You should also have the most state of the art surround sound possible, with bass pickups so deep they cause earthquakes on the Eastern seaboard. Not because Dean Devlin and Roland Emmerich's alien invasion flick is a masterpiece of cinematic art or anything, but because it's loud. Very loud. And if the windows in your house don't shatter when the spaceship flies over New York then well, you're just not experiencing it properly.

Taking the 1950's invasion narratives and pro-tooling them for 90's audiences, Independence Day is an absolute blast of visual flare and gung ho heroism. The plot is so straightforward as to be superfluous (aliens invade, fights ensue) but even so, it remains an invigorating watch purely because of the spectacle it provides. Back in 1996, the sight of that giant blue laser tearing apart lower Manhattan made jaws drop and while it's unlikely to do the same to today's overstimulated audiences, it's still an incredible visual feast. What's more, the ensemble cast makes it surprisingly unpredictable - we all know that the aliens will be defeated at the end, but what isn't so obvious is which characters are going to be alive to see it. Except for the kid and the dog. They're relatively safe bets.

Watching it now though, it does possess a cheerful naivety in the face of world politics. After all, this was 1996, the Cold War was over and 9/11 a long way off, so the entire world uniting against a common foe without being bogged down with petty arguments and personal agendas still seemed believable. Hell, even the gun-toting Arabs that briefly appear on screen are more than happy to rally behind Uncle Sam in the name of freedom. That's right folks, it's an Americans Save The World movie, complete with a snapshot of British officers drinking tea in the desert and waiting for those silly yanks to get a bally move on and show us what to do.

Needless to say, this is blockbuster entertainment through and through. The aliens are apparently here to strip mine the planet of all her natural resources, but they're quite happy to put that off for a bit in order to blow things up for the entire running time. Fans of in-depth characterisation, intelligent story telling and emotional engagement with the protagonists are wasting their time, but if you want to watch tourist attractions, jet planes and space craft exploding for three hours, you can't really go wrong. That business about a computer virus bringing down the mother-ship is a bit daft though, not once did they try switching everything on and off again.

Omi's "Cheerleader," a composition penned and produced by the Jamaican artist himself together with Clifton Dillon, Mark Bradford, and Ryan Dillon, emerged from his creative process initiated in 2008. Its melody took shape during this period, undergoing refinement in collaboration with renowned Jamaican producer, Clifton Dillon. The initial recording sessions featured veterans Sly and Robbie and Dean Fraser. Originally released on independent label Oufah, the track garnered popularity in Jamaica, reaching the top spot on local charts, as well as gaining traction in Hawaii and Dubai.

Upon securing a deal with Ultra Records, two DJs were enlisted to create remixed versions of the original piece. The label and producers favored the interpretation crafted by a young German DJ, Felix Jaehn, which transformed the tune into a deep house rendition characterized by a trumpet, conga beat, and prominent piano notes. An EP of remixes was issued by Ultra in May 2015, marking the beginning of significant commercial success. In 2015, "Cheerleader" surged in popularity worldwide, reaching number one in 20 countries such as the US, UK, Australia, Canada, France, Mexico, Ireland, Sweden, and Germany.

The scaled complex Wishart distribution, a commonly utilized model for multilook full polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, is validated by numerous studies. Various classification, segmentation, and imaging methods based on this model exist, and they often incorporate dissimilarity measures. In this study, we provide analytical expressions for four stochastic distances between general and specific forms of relaxed scaled complex Wishart distributions. Utilizing these distances, we establish inequalities that result in novel approaches for computing the Bartlett and revised Wishart distances. We evaluate the effectiveness of the four analytical distances based on parameter variations. Subsequently, these distances are employed to generate new test statistics, which are proven to follow an asymptotic chi-square distribution. By considering test size as a benchmark, we conduct a sensitivity analysis via Monte Carlo simulations, indicating that the Bhattacharyya statistic excels over other options. We further examine the power of the tests. Real-world applications demonstrate the discriminatory and homogeneity recognition abilities of these distances.

I reside in an abandoned house
Once taken by the summer's fleeting tide,
Leaving behind mere cellar foundations,
A cellar bathed in sunlight's soft descensions,
Where wild raspberries with purple stems hide.
Beside overgrown fences, the vines sprawl,
Reclaiming the mowed meadow's verdant trail;
The gnarled orchard tree bears new and old,
Where woodpeckers tap and the old tales told;
The healed path leads to the crystal pool.
My heart aches oddly within that lost dwelling,
Solitary, on that long-neglected road,
No longer graced by the toad's dusty load.
Nightfall brings black bats that dance and soar,
The whippoorwill begins to sing and shout,
To hush, to cluck, and flit about,
His melody carried on the night airway,
Echoing through the stillness of the day.
I ponder those silent beings near,
Residing in the darkness with me here,
Underneath the tree whose branches droop low,
Perhaps their names, if they had names at all,
Are hidden beneath the mosses' gentle call.
They are tireless creatures, though slow and sorrowful,
Two together, a lass and a lad, never vocal,
Yet, despite their silence, incomparably dear.

12 tablespoons (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature
2/3 cup (packed) brown sugar
1/2 cup chopped macadamia nuts
1/4 cup dried tart cherries*
2 tablespoons minced peeled fresh ginger
1/2 medium pineapple, peeled, quartered lengthwise, cored, cut crosswise into 1/4-inch-thick pieces
1 3/4 cups all purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
1/4 teaspoon salt
3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons finely grated orange peel
3 large eggs, separated
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
2/3 cup buttermilk
Whipped cream
Preheat oven to 350F. Melt 6 tablespoons butter in 9-inch-diameter cake pan with 2-inch-high sides set atop burner on medium-low heat. Stir in sugar, nuts, cherries and ginger. Cook until sugar mixture bubbles, stirring often, about 6 minutes. Cool slightly. Arrange pineapple pieces, overlapping slightly and in concentric circles, over sugar mixture. Set aside. Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in medium bowl. Using electric mixer, beat 3/4 cup sugar and orange peel in large bowl until fragrant. Beat in 6 tablespoons butter until light. Beat in yolks 1 at a time. Beat in lemon juice and vanilla. Beat in flour mixture alternately with buttermilk. Using clean dry beaters, beat egg whites in another large bowl until soft peaks form. Add 2 tablespoons sugar and beat until firm peaks form. Fold into batter. Spoon into pan atop pineapple. Bake cake until tester inserted into center comes out clean, about 1 hour. Transfer to rack; cool 5 minutes. Invert onto platter. Serve with whipped cream.

Use a fork to scrape out "noodles" from the squash and place them on plates. Spoon the Bolognese sauce on top of the noodles and serve. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for 1 week.

Bill Conti's role as musical director for the Oscars involves an intense amount of orchestra conduction, akin to juggling numerous plates. With this being his 17th stint at the Academy Awards, Conti expresses the thrill of performing live for the film industry's elite. "The atmosphere is electric," he remarks. "Everyone in the industry is there, making it more than just a TV show." During an average Oscars broadcast, the orchestra plays approximately 110 times, accompanying presenters and winners both on and off stage, as well as entertaining the live audience during commercial breaks.

Conti elaborates on the event's demanding nature, stating, "It's a bustling night with extensive music preparation – composing, arranging, rehearsing – prior to the ceremony. Yet, the unforeseen occurs, adding an element of excitement." Much of this preparation entails perfecting music that may never be performed. "Since we don't know who the victors will be, we prepare five distinct pieces for each potential win. Upon announcement, we instantly perform the corresponding piece," Conti shares.

When winners extend their speeches beyond acceptable limits, the orchestra steps in to maintain the program's pace. Conti recounts the process, "Instructions from the director to silence the prolonging speaker reach me via an earpiece. While I find it unsettling, it's not my decision. When the director signals 'music,' the orchestra responds, capturing a wide shot of the hall instead of showing the speaker whose microphone has been muted. The speaker, mere feet away from me, may glare menacingly." Occasionally, some performers attempt to warn the musical director beforehand.

I approached the orb, which responded by moving away, accelerating its pace. My cat pursued it, following it down the hallway. The orb entered my bedroom with an open door, collided with the wall, and vanished. My cat continued its pursuit and struck the wall as well. Some attribute this occurrence to "ball lightning," but it appeared to acknowledge my presence and awareness of being watched. Have you encountered a comparable event or hold relevant information on this phenomenon? I harbor a secret hope that this orb may one day become my future ghost, enabling me to witness the experience from its perspective.

On Abarrach, Xar is attempting to learn the secret of necromancy, but he needs a corpse to test it on. He interrogates the lazar Kleitus about the location of any living Sartan, and Kleitus reveals that Haplo lied to Xar about all the Sartan dying at the hands of the dead; Balthazar and his group remain living. Kleitus drops a hint about the Seventh Gate, and reveals that it's where the Sundering took place and that Haplo's corpse would know its location. Xar dismisses this idea, as well as the lazar, and is quickly becoming obsessed with the Seventh Gate when receives word that two Sartan have been captured: Zifnab, for one, whose pleas on Haplo's behalf go unheeded; and, as quite a prize, Samah, ruler of the Council of Seven. Xar is initially excited since Samah is the very person who would know the Seventh Gate's location, and he interrogates Samah for it to no avail. Sang-drax— the one who actually captured Samah and Zifnab— is summoned by Xar to mentally torture Samah to death; even before he dies, Samah does not reveal anything useful. Xar succeeds in turning him into a far-more-complacent lazar, but too much of Samah's will remains, and he still won't talk. Even worse, when Xar turns his back to investigate Zifnab's disappearance, Jonathan walks in and teaches Samah how to let go; the leader of the Council of Seven is now well and truly dead. Xar is soon told by Sang-drax of Haplo's "treachery"; he has helped the mensch start the Kicksey-winsey and given control of Arianus over to the mensch, instead of reserving it for Xar himself. Party to this conversation is the loyal servant who informed Xar of the capture and has already been ordered to investigate the Arianus situation: Marit, the woman Haplo loved, the mother of his child. Xar marries her in traditional Patryn fashion of rune-joining, both to ensure her loyalty and because it gives them an unblockable way to communicate, and then orders her to kill Haplo. Haplo rests on Arianus and tries to heal his heart-rune, a job that truly needs two people (most rune-healing is accomplished by "circling" and allowing strength from one person to flow to the other.) Prince Rees'ahn and King Stephen's deputy, the wizard Trian, have come to Drevlin to talk with High Froman Limbeck Bolttightener in the hopes of hammering out some sort of true alliance between all three races of mensch (the mysteriarchs having folded into the human race after their leader Sinistrad's death.) Haplo gives the Kenkari book to Limbeck, and the three races together reactivate the Kicksey-winsey, which realigns the scattered islands of Arianus and starts a constant flow of water through the sky. Then Haplo enters his dragonship and prepares to leave for the last time. Hugh, under contract to kill Haplo, retraces his own steps. He goes from the Cathedral of the Albedo back to the Fortress of the Brotherhood, where Ciang gives him a cursed knife: ugly, badly made, capable of self-movement... and covered in Sartan runes. It is the only weapon the Brotherhood has that might even possibly be capable of killing Haplo. As payment for it, Ciang orders him to never return or further payment will be taken in his blood. Hugh, in the end, doesn't even use his new Cursed Blade— its main advantage, suppressing Haplo's warning runes and a good amount of his magic, allows Hugh to sneak up on him in his ship and capture him, but the tables turn and Hugh accidentally ends up with Haplo's knife in his gut... only to lurch back from the grave, Alfred's necromancy rune having evidently condemned him to eternal life. Haplo circles with Hugh to calm the human's distress at returning from the dead yet again, and the two begin to plan how to find Alfred when they are interrupted. Marit appears and fights both Haplo and Hugh. The first time they engage their Patryn rune-magic, however, the Cursed Blade reacts, transmuting itself into various threats, and the three break off their conflict periodically to quiet it down (they can't really make it stop;) they also struggle over the ship's steering-stone. Eventually Haplo takes the ship to Chelestra, hoping to douse the Cursed Blade in seawater, but the knife, instead of transforming into another weapon or creature, summons a dragon-snake that destroys the ship. As Haplo drifts in the sea, he hears a voice and looks up to see... Alfred. At Sang-drax's misleading suggestion, Xar has gone to Pryan with the pretext of taming the tytans, and he is frustrated with his inability to reach Marit. His real reason for being there is his hope of finding the Seventh Gate in the citadel that Haplo visited, but he finds little to encourage him. The five mensch— Paithan, Rega, Aleatha, Roland, and Drugar— aren't much help, nor is Zifnab, who has somehow gotten here after escaping from Abarrach. Shortly after Xar and Zifnab have arrived, Sang-drax says he knows now that Zifnab is "one of them;" after a battle with Zifnab's dragon, he takes on Xar's form and steals the ship, claiming that he will search for Haplo while Xar is on Pryan. It is revealed during Xar's stay that Zifnab is actually one of the dissenting Sartan who refused to go along with Samah's plan; he was among the mensch on Earth during the Sundering, and was the first of either race to escape the Labyrinth. It was he who penned many of the books Xar educated himself with. (With all that Zifnab has seen, his total dementia seems a bit more understandable.) Xar decides to leave Pryan in a ship he spotted outside the citadel, covered in Sartan runes, but to do that he needs to get past the tytans. He decides to need to kill off the mensch and revive them with necromancy to serve as distractions. The mensch are having their own problems. Paithan is obsessed with a room in the center of the citadel that he calls the Star Chamber, a room with seven huge seats and an apparatus that generates blinding light. Roland and Aleatha are mostly not on speaking terms; the elf maiden finds herself spending more time with Drugar, who may be the last of his race. But Drugar has discovered a delightful illusion: at a certain clearing in the garden maze, at certain times of the day, he can see ghostly shadows of people from all the mensch races, walking around and talking to each other. Aleatha is there when he uses his amulet to activate the platform, teleporting him instantly to a different citadel— where, as it turns out, there are other survivors. Marit finds herself in a Sartan prison. On a bench in the middle of the room, Haplo recovers from injuries caused by the Cursed Blade. Across from it, Hugh the Hand and the dog watch her with unblinking eyes. Their "jailer": none other than Alfred, who rescued them from Chelestra. After some discussion, Haplo realizes that they are in the Vortex, the one-way gate at the very center of the Labyrinth. It was here that the Patryns were initially imprisoned and chose to live for generations, until people calling themselves Nexus runners started trying to escape. (It's unknown when they abandoned the Vortex and all moved out into the Labyrinth.) Haplo decides to enter the Labyrinth in search of his daughter, whom Marit named Rue. Hugh agrees to go with him, as does Marit at Xar's command; he has told Marit to hold off on killing Haplo to report back any conversations Alfred and Haplo have about the other worlds. It is only Alfred who balks. He has nothing left— Orla "saw" Samah's death and chose a peaceful death to be with him— but fear of the unknown. The Labyrinth itself, however, refuses to let him return to the Vortex by unceremoniously dropping a mountain on top of the exit back into it. To Haplo, the Labyrinth seems afraid of Alfred, though he can't for the life of him figure out why; what is Alfred, besides a bumbling, useless Sartan? ...who can turn into a dragon and bring people back from the dead? The group is about to be overrun by tiger-men when, surprisingly, a Patryn raiding party comes to save them. This party comes from Abri, the one and only city inside the Labyrinth (anathema to the lone-wolf Patryns). While camping overnight, Alfred admits his true name to Haplo: Coren, a Sartan word that can mean "to choose" or perhaps "chosen." Many Sartan children were named that, in hopes of a self-fulfilling prophecy, but (as Haplo points out) Alfred did not feel particularly amused when he awoke, the last living Sartan on Arianus. Clearly Alfred was Coren, was chosen—but for what? Marit, however, betrays them by revealing that Alfred is a Sartan. Haplo, Hugh, and Alfred are jailed by the city's leader, Headman Vasu, to await Lord Xar— Marit accused Haplo of being a traitor and plotting against their people— but are freed again just as quickly after Marit overhears the disguised Sang-drax plotting to kill them. Sang-drax and his cronies are also gathering a huge army of the Labyrinth's native monsters, with which to destroy the city of Abri and seal the Final Gate; they allowed Marit to overhear them to feed off the emotions that would come from it. Abri's occupants prepare for its defense, while Haplo and Marit, prodded by the dog, finally find their love for each other. Alfred feels out of place; though few seem to begrudge him his Sartan heritage, he is still out-of-place here, a clumsy pacifist in a city preparing for war. Talking with Headman Vasu, however, he eventually discovers that the city was not made by Patryns (who do not build cities,) or at least not by Patryns alone— the Sartan "heretics" who were expelled into the Labyrinth were accepted by the Patryns, eventually integrating completely into the society; Vasu himself is half-and-half, supplementing his Patryn tattoos with Sartan magic. The Patryns taught them the value of family; the Sartan, in return, taught the Patryns the value of banding together. Here, at the heart of the Labyrinth, rises Abri, the city that symbolizes the best in both cultures. Alfred also finds out why he is called the Serpent Mage: it is a title from a Sartan hierarchy of strength in magic, whose levels are named after animals. Serpent is very near the top. Alfred has found the meaning of his name: to choose his power, and all the responsibility it comes with... or to choose Alfred, who would rather faint than have to use his magic. Back on Pryan, Drugar returns from the other citadel with knowledge: he knows how to stop the tytans. Aleatha has fled the maze, though; pushed into hysterics by his sudden (and literal) disappearance, she ran back to her brother, and the four are now at a "party" of Xar's, at which he hopes to kill them with poisoned wine so that their bodies will be undamaged. Zifnab, however, saves them by drinking all of it himself and saying that it was poisoned, faking his death once again. The mensch are horrified at the revelation that Xar means to kill them. Aleatha escapes the room, while the other three are sealed inside by Xar... until Zifnab's dragon discovers Zifnab's "death" and tears the room apart. Aleatha has fled once again into the maze, where Xar can't pursue her because of protective Sartan runes covering its path. She runs into Drugar and he tells her they have to let the tytans inside to help them; he shares with her how to stop them. They run for the gates, but before they can reach it, Xar attacks; Drugar sacrifices himself to save Aleatha. Xar is about to kill Aleatha when the dragon strikes, distracting Xar with battling it instead of killing mensch. The other mensch have escaped from the destroyed room and find her, and they think she's mad when she tells them what she's going to do. She uses the amulet to open the gate and invites the tytans inside; they peacefully enter and ask, —Where is the citadel? to which Aleatha answers, "Here is the Citadel. You are home." Xar recovers from his battle with the dragon, and prepares to leave for the Labyrinth after Marit reports back to him— apparently corrupted by Haplo's influence into thinking Xar has made a mistake in allying with the dragon-snakes, as she says they are planning an attack. He is surprised when the tytans don't kill the mensch, and actually act to protect the mensch from him, but he avoids a fight by snatching Drugar's amulet from Aleatha and running away with it. The amulet will gain him entry into the Sartan ship, which he can then use to return to the Labyrinth. At Abri, the battle between Patryns and Labyrinth creatures rages fiercely, but the real threat comes from the dragon-snakes. Haplo, Marit, and Hugh lead a sortie to deal with them, and the three battle Sang-drax in his serpent form. Sang-drax is apparently killed by Haplo, but Haplo has been badly injured and almost crushed beneath the massive body. Marit is attacked by a wolfen when a green and golden dragon carries it away: Alfred, having made his choice to accept his power. He lifts the serpent's body off of Haplo, leaving Marit to hold his blood-soaked form, his heart-rune's wound having reopened. But while Alfred is distracted in battle with the dragon-snakes, Xar appears. He wants Haplo's knowledge of the Chamber of the Damned, and will stop at nothing to get it. The battle ends with the Labyrinth's armies driven off, but Marit dazed and wounded, Haplo abducted by Xar, and Alfred missing in action.

In the past, films like 'Jaws' intrigued audiences by revealing only brief glimpses of the shark or its victims, instead focusing on building fear and tension within the community. However, could such a method be employed in today's film industry, given a budget of over 160 million dollars and advanced CGI technology?

Unfortunately, the answer seems to be no, at least not in the case of the recent 'Godzilla' remake. Director Gareth Edwards, inspired by 'Jaws,' aimed for an old-school approach, delivering an initial half filled with suspense and ominous anticipation.

Edwards' vision paid off, creating a gripping atmosphere of apprehension and terror. Acting and dialogue were compelling, and the production design was stunning, particularly the deserted Japanese cityscape, untouched for fifteen years and engulfed by nature.

Despite Edwards' intentions, the second half of 'Godzilla' faltered. The pacing quickened, and the once effective dialogues became mundane. The acting, too, wavered, leaving viewers feeling let down after the promising start. Yet, the creature design remained impressive, terrifying as it should be, evoking genuine fear from the audience.

From 1976 to 1988, AZLK, a Soviet automobile manufacturer, produced the Moskvitch 2140 series, which included the family car models Moskvitch 2138 and Moskvitch 2140 based on an updated 412 platform. Pre-production versions were exhibited in 1975. Starting in 1981, a modernized version of the export/luxury M-2140 model was developed and marketed as the "2140 SL" in Eastern Bloc nations and "1500 SL" abroad. Distinguishing features between the two models were revamped dashboards and front seat headrests in the M-2140. In 1982, the M-2138 models ceased production, making the M-2140 the sole Moskvitch vehicle offered across all markets. That year, it underwent a facelift: the crest emblem was altered to display "АЗЛК" (AZLK) in a metallic border, the grille covering transitioned from metal to plastic, and the side mirrors were subtly reshaped to be lighter. The station wagon edition M-2137 was the final Soviet vehicle to include taillight fins for hatch access, until its termination in 1985.

Mark Ellingson (1905-1993), who served as the 5th president of Rochester Institute of Technology from 1936 to 1969, assumed office after John A. Randall. Starting out as a teacher at the institution, Ellingson went on to become its longest-serving president. His leadership significantly shaped the modern form of RIT. Under his stewardship, day and evening student numbers grew from 2,250 to 16,000. Additionally, during this period, he engineered a 1937 merger with the Empire School of Printing, orchestrated the 1944 name change to "Rochester Institute of Technology," initiated plans for the current campus in Henrietta, and facilitated the selection of RIT as the site for the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, which welcomed its initial students in 1968. In recognition of his contributions, the highest residential building on the Henrietta campus bears his name, known colloquially as "Tower A."

Color and intensity are two important components in an image. Usually, groups
of image pixels, which are similar in color or intensity, are an informative
representation for an object. They are therefore particularly suitable for
computer vision tasks, such as saliency detection and object proposal
generation. However, image pixels, which share a similar real-world color, may
be quite different since colors are often distorted by intensity. In this
paper, we reinvestigate the affinity matrices originally used in image
segmentation methods based on spectral clustering. A new affinity matrix, which
is robust to color distortions, is formulated for object discovery. Moreover, a
Cohesion Measurement (CM) for object regions is also derived based on the
formulated affinity matrix. Based on the new Cohesion Measurement, a novel
object discovery method is proposed to discover objects latent in an image by
utilizing the eigenvectors of the affinity matrix. Then we apply the proposed
method to both saliency detection and object proposal generation. Experimental
results on several evaluation benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed CM based
method has achieved promising performance for these two tasks.

Two 17.3-ounce boxes of thawed frozen puff pastry (equivalent to 4 sheets)
1 beaten egg
6 ounces soft goat cheese (around 3/4 cup packed)
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
1/4 tsp coarse kosher salt
3 medium Gala apples, peeled, quartered, cored, thinly sliced
3 tbsp melted unsalted butter
3/4 cup honey (preferably dark), divided
1/2 tsp ground allspice

Prepare two baking sheets by lining them with parchment paper. On a lightly floured surface, roll out each puff pastry sheet to an 11-inch square. Utilizing a 5-inch-diameter cookie cutter or bowl, cut 4 rounds from every sheet, producing a total of 16 rounds. Allocate 8 pastry rounds onto each baking sheet and prick them with a fork. Apply the same method to the leftover 8 rounds, cutting smaller circles in their centers using a 3 1/2-inch cookie cutter or bowl, retaining the larger circles for later use. Brush the outer 1-inch edges of the 5-inch rounds on the baking sheets with beaten egg, then cover each with one pastry ring. Freeze for at least 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 375°F. In a bowl, combine goat cheese, lemon juice, and salt. Spread this mixture within the rings on the frozen pastry circles. Arrange apple slices over the cheese, slightly overlapping. In another bowl, mix melted butter and 1/4 cup honey. Brush the apples with this mixture. Sprinkle with allspice. Bake until the apples soften and the pastry turns golden, approximately 35 minutes. Transfer the tartlets to plates and drizzle 1 tbsp honey over each one before serving either warm or at room temperature.

Mary Virginia "Mollie" Orna (February 4, 1902 – May 23, 1978) was an American statistician. Born in Hartford, Connecticut to Presbyterian parents, she first became interested in mathematics after solving geometry problems on wooden boxes her father sent while serving overseas during World War I. She enrolled at Vassar College and went on to study mathematics under Leonard Dickson, completing her Ph.D. in 1925 with a thesis titled On Transcendental Functions of Two Variables and Their Inverses.
Orna's career took a turn when she joined the Bureau of Standards in Washington D.C., where she worked until 1956. During that time, she made significant contributions to statistical theory and practice, including the development of sampling methods for estimating population means and variances. Her work was heavily influenced by G. K. Zellenkurtz, who mentored her early on in her career. Orna also played a key role in developing the ANSI standard for probability distributions and random number generators, which was published in 1964.
Despite her many accomplishments, Orna faced gender discrimination throughout her career. As one of only two women working at the Bureau of Standards, she often had to fight for recognition and respect from her male colleagues. However, she remained committed to promoting statistical literacy and improving mathematical education throughout her life.
Orna passed away on May 23, 1978 at the age of 76, leaving behind a lasting legacy as one of the most influential statisticians of the mid-twentieth century. Today, she continues to be remembered for her pioneering work in statistics and advocacy for improved math education.

Floyd Firestone was known by the stage name of "Black Panther" during the late 1960s and early 1970s.

While at the height of his popularity, he was the subject of much negative media attention, much of it stemming from his controversial association with the Black Panther Party and his support of various non-violent tactics for social change.

He was also involved in several legal and government cases that contributed to his notoriety. In August, 1969, he was arrested at an antiwar protest in Philadelphia. On August 6, 1970, he was indicted for the attempted assassination by the leader of the Black Panther Party Huey P. Newton.

He was convicted of being an accessory to murder in November 1970. He then served 10 years in prison before being released in June, 1977.

Firestone then became a celebrity of sorts after his release, with his image featured in several books, films and videos. In February, 1987 he became a spokesperson for the US Marshals Service and the New York State Governor's Commission on the Incarceration of Young Men of Color.

Firestone was then convicted and imprisoned in July 1988 for the theft of an unregistered boat in upstate New York. After being released in March 1989, he was arrested, briefly jailed, then released for good behavior on May 28, 1989.

He became a spokesperson for The Nature Conservancy, the Natural History Museum, the National Wildlife Federation and The Nature Conservancy of Vermont, amongst others.

Firestone died of a heart attack on January 20, 1994 in Vermont. He was 54.

His biographical sketch from the Vermont Historical Society identifies Firestone as the author of various publications, including On Land and Freedom and Black Panther Party: Black Liberation and its Legacy. He was also the author of the book Black Power: A Statement from the Black Panther Party.

In the year 1943, Jewel Hilburn and her spouse, Leston, along with their five offspring, enjoy a prosperous life in Mississippi despite the ongoing war. Their happiness, however, is tempered upon learning that their eldest son, James, has enlisted, yet Jewel, nearing 40, discovers she is pregnant once more. Though apprehensive, she cherishes this final blessing. A somber intrusion interrupts their tranquility when Cathedral, an old friend, appears with an ominous proclamation: "I foretell to you, Miss Jewel, that the infant growing within your womb shall be your affliction, your trial in this existence." Upon Brenda Kay's arrival, her condition initially appears unremarkable. However, as time progresses, the Hilburns grow increasingly concerned as they observe their daughter failing to meet developmental milestones. They eventually seek medical attention and learn that Brenda Kay has Down syndrome, with a shortened life expectancy. Infuriated by the recommendation to institutionalize their child, the Hilburns choose instead to bear the responsibilities – and find unsuspected pleasures – of caring for their special needs daughter.

In this paper, we analyze the feasibility of using classical-quantum channels for covert communication. We propose a scheme that utilizes quantum states to encode information in a way that is undetectable by a potential eavesdropper. Our approach takes advantage of the unique properties of quantum systems, such as superposition and entanglement, to ensure the security of the transmitted messages. We provide a detailed analysis of the performance of our scheme and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving covert communication over classical-quantum channels.

This paper delves into the intricate study of curvature tensors of Hermitian manifolds. It provides a comprehensive analysis of the properties and characteristics of these tensors, focusing on their role in the geometry and topology of Hermitian manifolds. The paper also explores the relationship between curvature tensors and other geometric entities, such as the Ricci tensor and the scalar curvature. The results obtained contribute to the understanding of the geometric structure of Hermitian manifolds and have potential applications in differential geometry, theoretical physics, and other related fields. The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of the findings and suggestions for future research.

Starting in July 2015, the people of India's Patidar community, seeking Other Backward Class (OBC) status, held public demonstrations across the Indian state of Gujarat. The largest demonstration was held in Ahmedabad on 25 August 2015, and was attended by thousands. Later, there were incidents of violence and arson across the state, resulting in a curfew in several cities and towns. Properties and vehicles worth crores (tens of millions) of rupees were damaged and destroyed. The state returned to normalcy by 28 August. Despite talks with the government, the agitation recommenced and turned violent again on 19 September. The government announced  offers of scholarships and subsidies to general category students on 24 September 2015 and a 10% quota of spaces reserved for economically backward classes in April 2016. The 10% reservation was quashed by the Gujarat High Court in August 2016. The agitation lingered on for two more years. In January 2019, the Parliament of India  amended the constitution granting maximum 10% reservation to the Economically Weaker Sections of the society. The amendment is challenged in the Supreme Court.

The effects of residual amplitude modulation (RAM) in laser interferometers
using heterodyne sensing can be substantial and difficult to mitigate. In this
work, we analyze the effects of RAM on a complex laser interferometer used for
gravitational wave detection. The RAM introduces unwanted offsets in the cavity
length signals and thereby shifts the operating point of the optical cavities
from the nominal point via feedback control. This shift causes variations in
the sensing matrix, and leads to degradation in the performance of the
precision noise subtraction scheme of the multiple-degree-of-freedom control
system. In addition, such detuned optical cavities produce an opto-mechanical
spring, which also varies the sensing matrix. We use our simulations to derive
requirements on RAM for the Advanced LIGO detectors, and show that the RAM
expected in Advanced LIGO will not limit its sensitivity.

Frances Perkins (born Fannie Coralie Perkins; April 10, 1880 – May 14, 1965) was an American workers-rights advocate who served as the U.S. Secretary of Labor from 1933 to 1945, the longest serving in that position. She made history as the first woman to serve in any presidential U.S. Cabinet. As a loyal supporter of her longtime friend, Franklin D. Roosevelt, she helped make labor issues important in the emerging New Deal coalition. She was one of two Roosevelt cabinet members to remain in office for his entire presidency. Her most important role came in developing a policy for social security in 1935. She also helped form government policy for working with labor unions, although the union leaders distrusted her. Her Labor Department helped to mediate strikes by way of the United States Conciliation Service. Perkins dealt with many labor questions during World War II, when skilled labor was vital to the economy and women were moving into jobs formerly held by men. She became the subject of the documentary film Summoned (2020).

The pop star cancelled her Onyx Hotel tour last June after suffering a knee injury during a video shoot. Seven London-based companies and an eighth Paris firm have been given up to 30 days to respond to the complaint.
The 22-year-old star initially missed a number of shows on the 82-date tour after injuring her knee during a show in Illinois last March. But she was rushed to hospital and needed surgery after a later incident while filming a video for her song Outrageous, leading her to cancel the rest of the tour, including dates in China. "She obviously took a wrong step and blew out her knee," a Jive spokeswoman said at the time. "It was an old dance injury." The legal submission described Spears as "one of the most recognised performers in her industry". The Onyx Hotel tour was cited as "a highly crafted production which included the well-known music and dancing of Spears, supported by elaborate costumes, complex choreography as well as cutting-edge video production, lighting and other effects". In September Spears married Kevin Federline, who had been a dancer on the aborted tour.

Henry's retirement life as a traditional and uninteresting bank manager is disrupted when he encounters his elderly Aunt Augusta at his mother's funeral, whom he hadn't seen in more than five decades. Against expectations, they develop an unexpected connection. Henry discovers a new world with Augusta, filled with travel, excitement, romance, and acceptance. Their initial trip is to Brighton, where Henry learns about one of Augusta's past lives through an encounter with an old acquaintance. A psychic there foretells his imminent journeys. True to the prophecy, Henry is increasingly engrossed in Augusta's adventurous lifestyle and explores her past. Together, they venture from Paris to Istanbul on the Orient Express, revealing layers of Augusta's intriguing past. Upon returning to his monotonous retirement, Henry finds solace in his garden less appealing. A letter from Augusta eventually persuades him to abandon his old life, leading him to join her and her longtime lover in South America and marry a much younger woman. During their travels, Henry comes to realize that the woman he believed to be his mother was actually Augusta, and their reunion at her sister's funeral marked the start of her pursuit to reclaim her son.

At the age of 25, I don't have any offspring. Yet, I extol the virtues of a supposed "kids' movie," unseen by many. My rationale lies in the profound impact "The Iron Giant" left on me. Although its storyline resembles "E.T." - a boy encounters an extraterrestrial robot, stranded on Earth, confronted by suspicious authorities – what distinguishes "The Iron Giant" is the child's transformative role. He imparts knowledge on the titular character, guiding him through life's complexities and moral dilemmas. Contrary to popular belief, the Iron Giant is not just a weapon; he wrestles with his inherent nature. Beneath its apparent gun control message, the film explores the more profound question: how we wield our power towards others. We hold the power to inspire goodness or instigate chaos.

Refraining from spoilers, I will only hint at the heartrending finale. Suffice it to say, the selfless act is both breathtaking and devastating. Visually, the animation is stunning, while Michael Kamen's score hits all the right notes. The film masterfully recreates the 1950s atmosphere.

Alas, subpar marketing deterred audiences in large numbers. Disregard the box office revenue. Word-of-mouth has started to spread, revealing the enchantment of this hidden gem. In time, I believe "The Iron Giant" will stand alongside classics like "It's a Wonderful Life," films that underperformed in theaters but gained enduring popularity. Seize the opportunity to witness this marvel before it becomes mainstream.

Season tuna with provided seasonings and arrange wood chips at the smoker's base, following the manufacturer's instructions. Position the drip tray and grate above it. Brush rack lightly with oil before placing tuna slices upon it. Cover smoker with the lid, leaving it slightly open. Heat smoker over high flame until smoke escapes. Once smoke appears, close lid entirely and reduce heat to medium. Cook tuna until done, approximately 8 minutes. Dice tuna into 1-inch chunks and combine with cream cheese, butter, green onions, shallots, and parsley in a food processor. Blend until a smooth paste forms, pausing occasionally to clear the sides. Add heavy cream and process briefly. Transfer mixture to a shallow serving dish and offer with toasted bread or spread onto crackers; adorn with additional green onions or parsley as preferred.

The Inpui tribe are one of the indigenous Naga tribes of Manipur, India. The majority of the Inpuis are settled in the Haochong subdivision in Noney District, and in Tamenglong district, Manipur. Inpuis are also settled in Makuilongdi, Senapati headquarter, & Inthan (Waphong) in Senapati district and also in Changangei, Tamphagei, Yurembam, Pantilong, Sagolband in Imphal west district in Manipur. Moreover, Inpuis are also settled in Nagaland and Assam as well. The highest peak in Inpui Naga land is Antrimon 12 km far away from Haochong village and numerous rivers and streams run through the land like Tuilang, Lingkwa and Ra-ah. 
 
Some historians and anthropologists have earlier recorded them as Kabui along with Rongmei. The Inpuis are the original Kabuis and not Rongmei. The origin of the term can be traced to Inpui. They are listed as a Scheduled Tribe, in accordance with The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 Indian Constitution. They celebrate festivals like Karing-ngei, Somdungnu, Tataaknu, and Muliaang. References

From an early age, Meikle showed a keen interest in mechanics and engineering, and he spent much of his youth working on his family's farm, where he developed a deep understanding of the challenges faced by farmers.

Invention of the Threshing Machine

Meikle's most notable achievement came in 1786 when he invented the first practical threshing machine. Prior to this invention, the process ofseparating grain from chaff and straw was a laborious task that required workers to beat the grain by hand using flails or clubs. This process was not only time-consuming but also resulted in a significant amount of damage to the grain.

Meikle's threshing machine used a combination of rotating drums and sieves to separate the grain from the chaff and straw. The chaff and straw were then expelled from the back of the machine, while the clean grain fell onto a sieve, which sorted it by size.

Troll Fell tells the story of young Peer Ulfsson, whose shipbuilder father has just died, and who is taken to live with his two wicked uncles, Balder and Grim, in a water mill under the shadow of Troll Fell, a mountain inhabited by trolls. Peer’s uncles make him do all the work around the mill, and at first he despairs, especially when he meets Granny Greenteeth, the sinister waterspirit who lives in the millpond. However, he is aided by the Nis (Norwegian Nisse), a mischievous though unpredictable house-spirit or brownie. His other friends are his dog, Loki, and Hilde, the pretty and confident daughter of Ralf Eiriksson, a nearby farmer. Ralf has sailed away on the Viking ship which Peer’s father built. In his absence, Peer and Hilde discover the plot which his two uncles are hatching: to sell children as slaves to the trolls, in exchange for gold. When Hilde’s little brother and sister are stolen away under cover of a blizzard, Peer and Hilde go together into the tunnels under the mountain in an attempt to bring them back. At the climax of the story, at a troll banquet when the troll king raises the top of the mountain on four red pillars, Peer is faced with the decision either to escape alone, or stay forever under the mountain with Hilde. Meanwhile Ralf has returned from his voyage and, along with his crew and many of the neighbours, forces his way into the troll banqueting hall. There is a stand-off with the trolls. Finally Peer discovers a way to trick his uncles into staying under the mountain in his and Hilde’s place, and in gratitude Ralf invites him, with Loki and the Nis, to live with Hilde’s family at the farm. In the last pages, we learn that Ralf’s voyage took him to Vinland in America, in a similar fashion to Leif Eriksson in the Saga of the Greenlanders.

Kelly Holmes has been chosen for both the 800m and 1500m at next month's European Indoor Championships - despite not yet confirming her availability.
The double-Olympic champion is still undecided about whether to compete in her first European Indoors in Madrid. But UK Athletics chief Max Jones believes it is likely Holmes will race. He said: "It's worth a punt, isn't it? She's gone back to training. If she's confident she will pick one (distance). The programme does not permit both." If Holmes does take her place in the GB side, she has already indicated that 1500m will be her favoured distance. Under championship rules, she does not have to decide until 24 hours before the event begins in Madrid on 4 March. Jones added: "She was pleased with her run in Birmingham (at last weekend's Grand Prix). "I am inclined to think she will (compete). It could depend on how training goes and she will have to be close to top form." And he admitted Holmes' presence would be a great boost to the rest of the Norwich Union GB team. "She is a very good team member and is very good to have there," he added. Meanwhile, there is no surprises in the rest of the Great Britain team announced on Tuesday.
Defending 60m champion Jason Gardener is included and will be chasing his third successive gold medal. He will be joined in the event by Mark Lewis-Francis - runner-up behind him three years ago in Vienna - and new boy Darren Chin. Kelly Sotherton has been invited by championship organisers to compete against Carolina Kluft in the pentathlon. Sotherton finished third in the Olympic heptathlon in Athens, where the Swede took gold. There are 16 newcomers at this level of competition in GB's 46-strong team. The championships will be the last to be attended by Jones before he retires to be succeeded by Dave Collins. Jones said: "The Olympic Games is the overwhelming target for UKA and therefore it is beneficial to start the next four-year cycle with a not-so-pressurised major games. "The European Indoor Championships always provide a chance for the young and inexperienced to make a name for themselves and the current indoor season has produced some exciting new talent. "Madrid is the first small step on a long journey to Beijing and the 2008 Olympics but for some of the emerging athletes, this will be a very important step."

Ron Williamson, previously unsuccessful in joining minor league baseball teams such as the Fort Lauderdale Yankees and two Oakland A's affiliates due to an impeding elbow injury and slim chances of reaching the major leagues, returned to his birthplace of Ada, Oklahoma. Depression and excessive drinking ensued from his disappointments. In the early hours of December 8, 1982, the mutilated body of Debra Sue Carter, a 21-year-old local cocktail waitress, was discovered in her garage apartment. After years of inconclusive investigations and questionable police methods by the Ada police department, Williamson, accompanied by his drinking companion, Dennis Fritz, were indicted, tried, and condemned for the crime in 1988. Williamson received a death sentence, whereas Fritz was handed a life term. At that time, Fritz was rearing their sole child, having lost his previous wife seven years prior. John Grisham's account recounts the zealous and erroneous pursuit of the Ada police department and Pontotoc County District Attorney Bill Peterson to unravel the enigma surrounding Carter's demise. Through coerced "dream" testimonies, dubious witnesses, and tenuous proof, the authorities apprehended Williamson and Fritz. With the automatic initiation of appeals following a capital punishment verdict, the Innocence Project collaborated with Williamson's legal counsel, Mark Barrett, to reveal significant inconsistencies within the prosecution's argument and the reliability of their witnesses. Federal Judge Frank H. Seay granted a new trial. Having endured a conviction and eleven years in prison, Williamson and Fritz were vindicated by DNA evidence and freed on April 15, 1999. Williamson became the 78th inmate absolved from death row since 1973. Williamson sustained profound and permanent psychological harm throughout his imprisonment.

A Terminator, modeled after Arnold Schwarzenegger, was dispatched from the future in the initial installment to eliminate Sarah Connor's (Linda Hamilton) unborn son. In contrast, this Terminator's mission has been revised: safeguard John Connor, who is currently around 10 years old. With a new Terminator, known as the T-1000 (Robert Patrick), pursuing him, John, Sarah, and the Terminator collaborate to thwart Judgment Day. An ominous presence lurks in the background as they embark on their mission, following closely behind them.

This is the pinnacle of the Terminator series for me. I have rewatched it three times within the last year, and I cannot fathom how James Cameron could have enhanced its perfection. The film is a cinematic triumph in every conceivable manner. Schwarzenegger's acting prowess may not be extraordinary, but this role is tailor-made for him. He is devoid of emotions and feelings, merely a machine. I dislike nearly all of his films except for this trilogy because of his subpar acting abilities. Yet, he fits seamlessly into this part.

The special effects are breathtakingly impressive. The T-1000's shape-shifting capabilities represent some of the most remarkable animation I have encountered in cinema history. When I first saw this visual spectacle, it left me utterly astounded (considering this was a decade ago). The film offers thrilling action sequences combined with insightful science fiction drama/horror. The concept of a massive machine force seizing control of the world by launching nuclear warheads towards major cities is terrifying enough. However, the T-1000's minimal dialogue and eerie demeanor make it unsettlingly unsettling whenever it appears.

Science fiction films seldom manage to be regarded as artistic achievements. This is one of those rare instances. The depiction of Judgment Day through Hamilton observing a playground filled with children being consumed by flames is an exquisite representation of the apocalypse. The motif of humanity destroying itself is also woven throughout the movie, adding depth to the narrative.

The Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics, and it has been shown to be equivalent to various other problems in number theory. In this paper, we explore some of these equivalencies and their implications.

Firstly, we discuss the connection between the RH and the Robin inequality, which provides a lower bound for the sum of the reciprocals of the prime numbers. We show that the RH implies the Robin inequality, and conversely, that the Robin inequality implies a weak form of the RH.

Next, we examine the relationship between the RH and the Lagarias criterion, which is a necessary condition for the existence of a prime number between two given numbers. We prove that the RH implies the Lagarias criterion, and that the latter implies a weak form of the former.

Finally, we investigate the implications of the RH on the distribution of prime numbers. We show that the RH implies the Prime Number Theorem, which describes the asymptotic distribution of prime numbers, and that the Prime Number Theorem implies a weak form of the RH.

Our results provide new insights into the relationships between these fundamental problems in number theory, and shed light on the deep connections between them. They also highlight the importance of the RH in understanding the properties of prime numbers and their distribution.

Keywords: Riemann Hypothesis, Robin inequality, Lagarias criterion, Prime Number Theorem, number theory.

The picture gives an interesting portrayal about the bloody campaign and battle of Gallipoli . There happened the following : The Gallipoli Campaign, also known as the Dardanelles Campaign, the Battle of Gallipoli, or the Battle of Çanakkale , was a campaign of the First World War that took place on the Gallipoli peninsula (Gelibolu in modern Turkey) in the Ottoman Empire between 17 February 1915 and 9 January 1916. The peninsula forms the northern bank of the Dardanelles, a strait that provided a sea route to the Russian Empire, one of the Allied powers during the war. Intending to secure it, Russia's allies, Britain and France, launched a naval attack followed by an amphibious landing on the peninsula, with the aim of capturing the Ottoman capital of Constantinople (modern Istanbul).The naval attack was repelled and after eight months' fighting, with many casualties on both sides, the land campaign was abandoned and the invasion force was withdrawn to Egypt.The campaign was the only major Ottoman victory of the war. In Turkey, it is regarded as a defining moment in the nation's history, a final surge in the defence of the motherland as the Ottoman Empire crumbled. The campaign is often considered to be the beginning of Australian and New Zealand national consciousness; 25 April, the anniversary of the landings, is known as "Anzac Day", the most significant commemoration of military casualties and veterans in the two countries, surpassing Remembrance Day , Armistice Day .The struggle formed the basis for the Turkish War of Independence and the declaration of the Republic of Turkey eight years later, with Mustafa Kemal (Kemal Atatürk) as President, who rose to prominence as a commander at Gallipoli. Mustafa Kemal, Attaturk commanded the Turkish national movement in the war of independence. His successful military campaigns led to liberation of the country and to the establishing of Turkey. He transformed the former Ottoman Empire into a democratic, modern, secular nation-state , his reforms are referred as Kemalism. Ankara became the new capital and Kemal abolished the Caliphate and Sultanate. .

Auroroborealia, a small-bodied euichthyosaurian ichthyosaur found on New Siberian Islands in the Russian Arctic, is represented by a single species, Auroroborealia incognita. This creature was approximately 1 to 1.5 meters long based on related findings. Despite its incomplete state, other local discoveries indicate it was a diminutive taxon.

In 2006 and 2009, a collaboration between the Geological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Trofimuk Institute of Petroleum Geology and Geophysics, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences unearthed various ichthyosaurian fossils across six stratigraphic levels spanning from lower Carnian to middle Norian. While most specimens were partially preserved, Zverkov et al. (2021) identified numerous distinct ichthyosaurs based on the available evidence. Among these, specimen ZIN PH 5/250 stood out due to its cranial remains, anterior presacral vertebrae with connected neural arches and ribs, and a bone piece linked to the pectoral girdle. Based on these features, Zverkov et al. classified and named the new species Auroroborealia incognita, with additional related specimens described but not utilized for the genus diagnosis.

Semantic segmentation of high-resolution satellite imagery is a challenging task due to the presence of fine-grained details and large spatial extent. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called PP-LinkNet for improving the accuracy of semantic segmentation in high-resolution satellite imagery. PP-LinkNet combines the advantages of both LinkNet and Pyramid Pooling modules to effectively capture both local and global contextual information. Additionally, we introduce a multi-stage training strategy that progressively refines the segmentation results by leveraging the knowledge learned from previous stages. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PP-LinkNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed architecture and training strategy have the potential to significantly improve the performance of semantic segmentation in high-resolution satellite imagery applications.

Barry Whitfield (born 10 April 1954) is an English pianist, organist, jazz musician, musical director and teacher. Early life
Barry Whitfield was born in the town of Grimsby and brought up in Cleethorpes in North East Lincolnshire. He was the only son of Bransby Whitfield (businessman) and Joan Whitfield, a ballet teacher, choreographer and member of the British Ballet Organisation. He attended Clee Grammar School (Matthew Humberstone Foundation School), where he gained 10 O-levels and 3 A-levels, including one in music. Initially intending to study medicine but not attaining physics, he went on to the University College of North Wales (now Bangor University) to read biochemistry. He began studying the piano at the age of five and had achieved grade eight Pianoforte, Theory of Music and Pipe Organ by the age of 13. During his teenage years, he studied piano with Harry Isaacs (Royal Academy of Music), and organ with Horace Bate (Organist at St James' Church, Muswell Hill and conductor of The Madrigal Society of London), and continued to have lessons through his years at university.

The text below explores a lesser-known facet of World War II: the Nazi plundering of Europe and Russia's artistic treasures, with a particular focus on the establishment of Hitler's planned museum, The Führermuseum, in Linz, Austria. Unbeknownst to most, Hitler shifted his priorities from military victories to amassing Europe's finest art collections. European museum personnel made considerable efforts to safeguard art from Nazi seizure and destruction during wartime. As U.S. troops prepared to invade Europe, they established the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives program (MFAA), comprised mainly of American and British museum experts, curators, and historians. Their mission was twofold: preserving European landmarks and architectural structures, followed by locating and recovering pilfered artworks. Their endeavor culminated into a historic quest for stolen masterpieces hidden in underground caches across Europe, numbering over 1,000. Although thousands of items remain unaccounted for, including Raphael's Portrait of a Young Man from the Czartoryski Museum in Krakow, Poland, the book "Rescuing Da Vinci" shares this tale through succinct text and over 460 images, 60 of which are in color. Previously unpublished, these images offer a visual representation of the story, showcasing iconic pieces like Michelangelo's David concealed in bricks or a Rembrandt Self-Portrait stored in a salt mine.

Spatial–temporal reasoning is an area of artificial intelligence which draws from the fields of computer science, cognitive science, and cognitive psychology. The theoretic goal—on the cognitive side—involves representing and reasoning spatial-temporal knowledge in mind. The applied goal—on the computing side—involves developing high-level control systems of automata for navigating and understanding time and space. Influence from cognitive psychology 
A convergent result in cognitive psychology is that the connection relation is the first spatial relation that human babies acquire, followed by understanding orientation relations and distance relations. Internal relations among the three kinds of spatial relations can be computationally and systematically explained within the theory of cognitive prism as follows: (1) the connection relation is primitive; (2) an orientation relation is a distance comparison relation: you being in front of me can be interpreted as you are nearer to my front side than my other sides; (3) a distance relation is a connection relation using a third object: you being one meter away from me can be interpreted as a one meter long object connected with you and me simultaneously.

Peel and cube a 200-gram pumpkin, cooking it in a pot of boiling water for approximately 25 minutes until tender. Mash the cooked pumpkin in a bowl, adding 2 tablespoons of mascarpone cheese, 1/4 teaspoon of ground nutmeg, and 1/4 teaspoon of chili powder, blending well.

For the pasta, combine 2 2/3 cups of plain flour and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Create a well in the center of the flour mixture and add 4 eggs. Mix the eggs into the flour until a dough forms, then knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth. Let the dough rest, covered, in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. After resting, divide the dough in half, lightly dust with flour, and roll it through a pasta machine on the widest setting. Fold the dough in three and pass it through again, reducing the thickness setting each time until the pasta reaches a thickness of about 1mm. Cut the rolled-out dough into 4 sheets.

Place one pasta sheet on a lightly floured surface and spoon on pumpkin mixtures, spaced about 5 cm apart and leaving a 2 cm border around each. Brush water around each pile of pumpkin mixture and cover with another pasta sheet, pressing down between the pumpkin piles to seal. Cut the pasta into square shapes using a knife. Repeat this process with the remaining pasta and pumpkin mixtures.

Campaigners are to stage a rally calling for a Borders rail link which was closed in 1969 to be reopened.
They will mark the 36th anniversary of the line closure, which ran from Edinburgh through the Borders and on to Carlisle, with a walk at Tweedbank. Anne Borthwick, of Campaign for Borders Rail, said reopening the Waverley Line would restore the area's prosperity. MSPs are considering the reintroduction of passenger rail services through Midlothian to the Borders. Campaigners have said that reopening the Waverley Line, which could cost up to £100m, would be a huge economic boost for the Borders.
In 2000, Borders Council said the area's economy had suffered since the closure. Ms Borthwick said the lobby group was determined to keep the pressure on the Scottish Executive. "We are hoping that many people will join us in a march to mark the 36th anniversary of the closure of the Waverley Line," she said. "Campaign for Borders Rail is the biggest independent lobby group in Scotland and we have been lobbying tirelessly for the reinstatement of rail services to the Borders and eventually to Carlisle.
"We believe that it is time for the Scottish Executive to commit to the first phase of the project by pledging to fund the line between Edinburgh and Tweedbank in the first instance and then investigate extending the line in the future." Ms Borthwick said reopening the line would be a prosperous move and protect the character of the Scottish Borders. A study in 2000, which was commissioned by the executive, Scottish Borders Council, Midlothian Council and Scottish Borders Enterprise, found that a half-hourly service from Tweedbank to Edinburgh could cover its operating costs. It also found that a half-hourly service from Gorebridge to Edinburgh could cover operating costs and that a freight railway joining the West Coast Main Line at Longtown could also be reinstated.

Tzatziki Sauce Recipe:
1. Grate a cucumber, discard seeds, and set aside.
2. In a large bowl, combine 500 ml Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup olive oil, 6 finely chopped garlic cloves, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin. Set aside.
3. Marinate 1 kg diced lamb, 4 chopped tomatoes, preferred seasonings, and herbs in 1/2 cup olive oil. Let it rest for several hours.
4. Prepare the Tzatziki sauce by mixing grated and drained cucumber with the yogurt mixture, adding salt to taste.
5. Cook the marinated lamb in a hot pan, discarding excess marinade. Sauté chopped onions in the same pan (optional).
6. Brush pita bread lightly with olive oil and toast until golden brown. Wrap in a cone shape using paper towels.
7. Layer fillings: Alternate between meat, tomatoes, onions, lettuce, and Tzatziki sauce in the pita. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and optional home-made tomato sauce.
8. Serves 4; adjust ingredients accordingly for 2 servings. Optional garnishes include basil.

The Welsh region has two outstanding young No 9 prospects in Richie Rees and Rhodri Wells. Bath director of rugby Jack Rowell, though, believes Williams fits the bill perfectly. "He has been playing regular Heineken Cup and Celtic League rugby and he has a great affection for Bath," Rowell told Bath's official website. "We are delighted to be able to welcome him back to the club."

This is a recipe for a delicious and healthy Green Soup. It is a simple and straightforward recipe that is easy to follow and requires minimal ingredients.

Ingredients:

- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh spinach
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh kale
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh broccoli
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh cauliflower
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh green beans
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh zucchini
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh mushrooms
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh green bell pepper
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh tomatoes
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh basil
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh dill
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh mint
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh chives
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh ginger
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh turmeric

Instructions:

We report on the equilibrium properties of aqueous clay dispersions, namely bentonite, at very low clay concentration (hence referred to as empty liquids) as well as at higher concentrations corresponding to equilibrium gels. Inline optical micrographs acquired at high throughput were used to determine the spatial structure of these systems. A microgel model is proposed to describe the spatial properties of these clay networks. The rheology of these systems shows a transition from a Newtonian to a non-Newtonian behavior as a function of clay concentration. This behavior is found to be in agreement with the predictions of a simple model based on the intrinsic viscosity and microgel model. This study suggests that inline optical micrographs acquired at high throughput can be used to probe the microscopic properties of complex fluids based on their macroscopic response.

A new dataset of material light-fields is presented, utilizing the current achievements in deep learning to identify materials within the 4D light-field. This dataset comprises 12 distinct material classes, consisting of 100 images apiece captured using a Lytro Illum camera. Approximately 30,000 patches are extracted from these images. To our knowledge, this is the initial medium-sized dataset specifically designed for light-field pictures. The primary objective is to explore how the extra information in a light-field (such as numerous sub-aperture perspectives and view-dependent reflectance effects) may enhance material identification. As no recognition networks have previously been trained on 4D images, we suggest and contrast various innovative CNN architectures to teach on light-field images. Our experiments reveal that the superior performing CNN architecture yields an improvement of approximately 7% compared to 2D picture classification (from 70% to 77%). These findings serve as essential baselines to foster future investigation into the employment of CNNs for light-field applications. Following publication, our dataset also offers possibilities for additional novel uses of light-fields, such as object detection, image segmentation, and perspective interpolation.

Mikiko Mizuno (born 11 August 1977), known professionally as simply Mikiko or Mikikometal (both stylized in all caps), is a Japanese dancer and choreographer. She is the director and principal choreographer of the high-tech dance troupe Elevenplay, and also works with performers such as Perfume, Sakura Gakuin, and Babymetal. She was a production consultant for Japan's cultural presentation at the 2016 Summer Olympics closing ceremony. Early life 
Mikiko was born in Tokyo, Japan. The youngest of three sisters, her family moved to Hiroshima when she was two years old due to her father's job transfer. Her home in Hiroshima was located along the Peace Boulevard where the Hiroshima Flower Festival was held every year in May, where she observed the process of building the framework of the stage. Her father worked at an advertising agency, so she was able to see live performances and behind the scenes. When she saw a live performance of Yomei Club from backstage, she learned about the choreography profession. As a member of the baton club at Yasuda Girl's Junior High School, she participated in the Flower Festival stage and parade and began dancing in front of people, and started hip-hop dancing in high school.

Entering the cinema, I initially believed this was a light-hearted James Franco and Seth Rogen production poking fun at The Room, a notoriously poor film. However, The Disaster Artist defies expectations. Rather than ridiculing, it champions The Room. It champions Tommy Wiseau, Greg Sestero, their devotion, and their quest for success.

The film acknowledges The Room's box office failure and the questionable acting abilities of Tommy and Greg. Yet, it handles these elements with tender care, avoiding derision. In fact, it seems to celebrate them. Despite the world's disapproval, they persevered. The outcome is surprisingly uplifting.

The movie transcends mere satire due to its thoughtful portrayal of the bond between Tommy and Greg. Their friendship was genuine and unique; Greg saw Tommy through others' eyes. Though he didn't always comprehend Tommy's methods or decisions, he recognized his friend's good intentions. This buddy dynamic proves essential later in the story.

Once Tommy pens The Room and filming begins, Tommy's quirks emerge in full force. The crew finds him puzzling, yet we sense a deeper layer. In spite of his ineptitude in every aspect of filmmaking, we continue to support him. Similarly, we cheer for Greg, the unwavering companion. Tommy's irrational decisions leave both baffled, yet Greg stays true.

Despite Wiseau's peculiar behavior, accurately depicting his oddities would be a daunting task. Kudos to James Franco for effectively capturing Wiseau's eccentricities.

A Norwegian computer engineering student running a website with downloadable MP3 file links was mandated by the Supreme Court to compensate the Norwegian music industry for 100,000 kroner (£8,000). In 2001, Frank Allan Bruvik established napster.no during his studies in Lillehammer as a separate entity from the US-based Napster.com, which faced legal challenges since 1999.

The napster.no website, active between August and November 2001, did not store music itself but offered links to over 170 free songs on external servers and enabled users to submit and access new links. Copyright infringement charges were filed against Bruvik by entities such as Tono (Norway's performing rights organization), Sony Music, and Universal Music.

In 2003, a Norwegian court ruled that Bruvik owed 100,000 kroner to the music industry, but the Court of Appeal later exonerated him, attributing copyright violations to others posting the content. However, the Supreme Court reversed this decision, asserting that Bruvik knowingly facilitated copyright infringement through his premeditated actions. Satisfied with the outcome, the Norwegian music industry viewed the ruling as a deterrent to music piracy.

During this period, in the United States, Napster.com continued to face legal battles.
