On a sunny brae, alone I lay
One summer afternoon;
It was the marriage-time of May
With her young lover, June.
From her mother's heart, seemed loath to part
That queen of bridal charms,
But her father smiled on the fairest child
He ever held in his arms.
The trees did wave their plumy crests,
The glad birds caroled clear;
And I, of all the wedding guests,
Was only sullen there!
There was not one, but wished to shun
My aspect void of cheer;
The very grey rocks, looking on,
Asked, "What do you here?"
And I could utter no reply;
In sooth, I did not know
Why I had brought a clouded eye
To greet the general glow.
So, resting on a heathy bank,
I took my heart to me;
And we together sadly sank
Into a reverie.
We thought, "When winter comes again,
Where will these bright things be?
All vanished, like a vision vain,
An unreal mockery!
The birds that now so blithely sing,
Through deserts, frozen dry,
Poor spectres of the perished spring,
In famished troops, will fly.
And why should we be glad at all?
The leaf is hardly green,
Before a token of its fall
Is on the surface seen!"
Now, whether it were really so,
I never could be sure;
But as in fit of peevish woe,
I stretched me on the moor.
A thousand thousand gleaming fires
Seemed kindling in the air;
A thousand thousand silvery lyres
Resounded far and near:
Methought, the very breath I breathed
Was full of sparks divine,
And all my heather-couch was wreathed
By that celestial shine!
And, while the wide earth echoing rung
To their strange minstrelsy,
The little glittering spirits sung,
Or seemed to sing, to me.
"O mortal! mortal! let them die;
Let time and tears destroy,
That we may overflow the sky
With universal joy!
Let grief distract the sufferer's breast,
And night obscure his way;
They hasten him to endless rest,
And everlasting day.
To thee the world is like a tomb,
A desert's naked shore;
To us, in unimagined bloom,
It brightens more and more!
And could we lift the veil, and give
One brief glimpse to thine eye,
Thou wouldst rejoice for those that live,
Because they live to die."
The music ceased; the noonday dream,
Like dream of night, withdrew;
But Fancy, still, will sometimes deem
Her fond creation true.

Supervised semantic segmentation normally assumes the test data being in a
similar data domain as the training data. However, in practice, the domain
mismatch between the training and unseen data could lead to a significant
performance drop. Obtaining accurate pixel-wise label for images in different
domains is tedious and labor intensive, especially for histopathology images.
In this paper, we propose a dual adaptive pyramid network (DAPNet) for
histopathological gland segmentation adapting from one stain domain to another.
We tackle the domain adaptation problem on two levels: 1) the image-level
considers the differences of image color and style; 2) the feature-level
addresses the spatial inconsistency between two domains. The two components are
implemented as domain classifiers with adversarial training. We evaluate our
new approach using two gland segmentation datasets with H&E and DAB-H stains
respectively. The extensive experiments and ablation study demonstrate the
effectiveness of our approach on the domain adaptive segmentation task. We show
that the proposed approach performs favorably against other state-of-the-art
methods.

Deep learning's triumph in image segmentation is largely dependent on an abundance of meticulously labeled training data. Obtaining such data, however, proves challenging due to the considerable time and expertise investment, especially when it comes to labeling 3D medical images. While self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution, most SSL methods concentrate solely on image-wide global harmony, disregarding the importance of local harmony essential for capturing intricate structural details in dense prediction tasks like segmentation. In this study, we introduce the PriorGuided Local (PGL) SSL model, designed to learn regional consistency in the latent feature domain via spatial transformations. By employing these transformations to generate distinct perspectives of the same image, we utilize the resulting location relationships between views to synchronize feature maps from corresponding local regions across multiple views. Subsequently, we establish a local consistency loss to minimize voxel disparities between aligned feature maps, enabling PGL to generate distinctive local region representations and preserve structural detail. Our experimental results, obtained from evaluating the model on four publicly accessible computerized tomography (CT) datasets encompassing 11 significant human organs and two tumors, demonstrate significant enhancement in downstream segmentation performance when employing a pre-trained PGL model as a network initializer, surpassing both random and initialization with global consistency-based models. Code and pre-trained weights can be accessed at: https://git.io/PGL.

A castle named Schloss Heiligenberg stands to the east of Jugenheim, which is part of Seeheim-Jugenheim, approximately 12 kilometers south of Darmstadt, Germany. Situated atop the Heiligenberg, it offers breathtaking vistas of the Rhineland extending to the Palatinate. Currently, it serves as the administrative hub for the Amt Für Lehrerbildung.

The castle's construction began at the turn of the 19th century. Grand Duchess Wilhelmine of Hesse-Darmstadt and her son, Prince Alexander of Hesse-Darmstadt, expanded the castle between 1862 and 1867, under the architectural guidance of Georg Moller. From 1852, Alexander, third son of Grand Duke Louis II of Hesse-Darmstadt, primarily resided in Darmstadt or Schloss Heiligenberg, except during military campaigns. On October 28, 1851, Alexander wed countess Julia Hauke, a lady-in-waiting to his sister, Tsarina Maria Alexandrovna of Russia. The Battenberg/Mountbatten line was established by this union. Throughout the late 19th century, the Schloss played host to the Russian Tsar and his family, along with various monarchs, princes, and diplomats, due to the family's extensive royal connections.

The novel is prefaced by a section entitled "Questions", which consists of four passages numbered in Roman numerals. I Chandra Chagoo is threatened by Abdul Khan, who believes Chagoo has been asking questions in order to gather evidence for the police. II Dr Gauri Subbiah contemplates confronting Chagoo and demanding exactly what he knows about her past. She fears he knows everything. III Dr Ram Mahipal lectures a class of medical students about the importance of asking questions. Privately he contemplates imminent professional ruin for asking the wrong question. IV Professor Phaterpaker also contemplates professional ruin as a result of Ram Mahipal's question, the answer to which Chagoo already knows. The preface ends. The main body of the novel begins with the heading: Answer The Commissioner tells Ghote that a criminal named Abdul Khan has supplied Bombay film stars with drugs from the Mira Behn Institute. Ghote is ordered to find who stole drugs from the institute and arrest them under a false charge to prevent a scandal. Ghote tells the Commissioner that he recently caught an airline stewardess, Nicky D'Costa, smuggling drugs for Abdul Khan. The Commissioner says he will assign another officer to manage Nicky D'Costa as an informant and that it will take a better officer than Ghote to bring Abdul Khan to justice. Ghote questions Asha Rani, a movie star. Her "friend" Mr Ganguly took a sample of a medicine called A.C.E. and nearly died. Khan, who also supplied Mr Ganguly with cocaine, supplied the A.C.E. At the institute, Ghote interviews Professor Phaterpaker. The Professor says he will go to any lengths to protect the institute. The institution's work is largely concerned with making new medicines from the venom of poisonous snakes. Dr Subbiah immediately suspects Chandra Chagoo of having stolen the A.C.E. and leads Ghote to the reptile room. When the door is unlocked they find Chagoo dead with a Russell's viper loose in the room. The next day the Commissioner assigns Ghote to investigate Chagoo's death to prevent the scandal being exposed by another officer. Ghote realises that Chagoo did not have a key to lock the reptile room door and must have been murdered. Ghote interviews Dr Ram Mahipal, who left a reptile-room key in his old office at the institute when he suddenly quit his job. Ghote learns from the building manager that Mahipal returned in order to access his computer files on the night Chagoo died. Dr Subbiah, Professor Phaterpaker, Dr Mahipal and the building manager were all in the building at the time. Ghote suspects that the murder may be an employee at the nearby hospital. He enlists the inspector originally assigned to Chagoo's death to test this theory. On their next meeting Mahipal says he returned to teaching in hopes of instilling integrity in young medical students. Mahipal left the institute because he believed that Phaterpaker faked results, possibly on a regular basis. Phaterpaker takes the news that Chagoo was murdered calmly, remarking that Mahipal was slipshod and implying that he was dismissed for this. Ghote tries to determine exactly why Mahipal left, but Phaterpaker is vague. When Phaterpaker realises he himself is a suspect, he is affronted but admits "cutting corners" and acts like a man with something to hide. Ghote concludes that Phaterpaker is trying to use Mahipal as a scapegoat to protect the institute. Dr Subbiah reacts badly when asked about her relations with Chagoo, however Ghote concludes she is not the killer. Ghote discovers that Dr Mahipal's father works as a cook at the medical school and is a Brahmin, whereas Mahipal claims to be a member of the Dalit caste. Ghote deduces that Mahipal misrepresented himself in order to get a university scholarship reserved for the lower classes. Mahipal confesses this is so. Ghote suggests Chagoo came to learn Mahipal's secret and was murdered because of this. Mahipal denies this and reveals that he left the institute because Phaterpaker was removing lab animals that gave undesirable results. At the police station, Ghote is dismayed when the inspector he is working with points out one of the three scientists must surely hang for the crime and expresses a preference that it be Dr Subbiah. At the institute Ghote accuses Phaterpaker of falsifying test results. Phaterpaker confesses his results are fake. He became aware that Chagoo was stealing drugs from the institute but was forced to agree to a truce because Chagoo knew Phaterpaker was removing lab animals. Ghote considers the reptile room and realises wooden stool must have been used to break the glass, so he decides to have it dusted for fingerprints. At the police station Ghote learns that Nicky D'Costa has murdered, her throat slit after asking too many questions of Abdul Khan. Ghote is angry enough to confront the commissioner, but learns Khan had arranged to be in hospital during the murder. The forensic tests do not find a match between any fingerprints on the stool and Ghote's three suspects. Nor can they prove it was used to break the glass of the viper's cage. Ghote goes home and argues with his wife, then inspiration strikes and he returns to the institute. There he searches the grounds for evidence someone could gain access by night. The security guard catches Ghote and he must call his fellow inspector to rescue him. Afterwards Ghote chances upon Dr Subbiah. Ghote deduces that Phaterpaker persuaded her to "anticipate" the results of her experiments, as Phaterpaker himself was once persuaded. The conversation between Ghote and Subbiah is interrupted when, by chance, they pass the funeral of Nicky D'Costa. Ghote tells Subbiah how Nicky D'Costa was murdered and proceeds to question her about her test results. Subbiah remarks that Abdul Khan was a patient at the teaching hospital recently. Ghote asks whether she anticipated her results before completing the actual experiment. She admits faking her results. Ghote now believes that Subbiah is the murderer. He accuses her and she reacts in amazement, saying that Chagoo was clearly strangled. Ghote realises that he only saw the body laying face down, and the inspector originally assigned to the case never forwarded the medical examiner's report. Ghote realises that Chagoo could not have been strangled by Subbiah or Phaterpaker because neither of them have the necessary strength. Dr Mahipal has a withered arm, eliminating him as a suspect. Returning to the police station, Ghote talks to the forensic expert who examined the stool from the institute reptile room. The expert admits he only compared the fingerprints on the stool to the three suspects Ghote named; Subbiah, Phaterpaker and Mahipal. Without Khan's file in front of him, he could not identify the fingerprints. Khan's file is retrieved and his fingerprints are a perfect match. Ghote realises he can arrest and charge Khan with murder and recalls, with satisfaction, the words used by Commissioner's at the start of the case: "Frankly, Inspector, it will take a better man than you to put paid to Abdul Khan".

Fiat may restructure its automobile business by separating Ferrari and bringing Maserati and Alfa Romeo closer together, according to the Financial Times. This move comes after Fiat reached a $2bn settlement with GM regarding Fiat's ownership. To fund this overhaul, Ferrari, which Fiat owns a 56% stake in, could be listed on the stock market. Previously, in 2002, Fiat sold a minority stake in Ferrari to Italian bank Mediobanca for €775m, valuing the company at €2.3bn. If Maserati were moved within Alfa Romeo, the two brands could share marketing, distribution, and research & development costs, resulting in commercial synergies. Both Ferrari and Maserati sold approximately 10,000 cars combined and both companies achieved profitability in 2003. Fiat, Italy's largest private sector employer, declined to comment on these potential changes. Following the recent termination of its alliance with GM, which involved a $2bn payment from GM, analysts believe this reorganization demonstrates Fiat's newfound ability to grow its business.

Former UK Foreign Secretary, William Hague, has reportedly earned a six-figure sum from his various roles outside of politics, according to recently released financial documents. 

The documents reveal that Mr Hague has been earning substantial amounts from his work as a speaker, author, and consultant. His earnings from these roles are in addition to his parliamentary pension, which he receives following his service as an MP and cabinet minister.

Mr Hague, who served as the leader of the Conservative Party from 1997 to 2001 and as Foreign Secretary from 2010 to 2014, has been a prominent figure in British politics for several decades. Since stepping down from his role as Foreign Secretary, he has taken on a number of lucrative roles in the private sector.

The financial documents show that Mr Hague has earned over £800,000 from his work as a speaker alone. He is represented by the Washington Speakers Bureau, which also represents other high-profile figures such as former US Secretary of State, Condoleezza Rice, and former Prime Minister, Tony Blair.

In addition to his speaking engagements, Mr Hague has also earned significant sums from his work as an author. His books, which include histories of William Pitt the Younger and William Wilberforce, have been well received and have added to his earnings.

Furthermore, Mr Hague has also worked as a consultant for several major companies. His consultancy work has reportedly earned him a further six-figure sum.

The release of these financial documents has led to some criticism of Mr Hague. Critics argue that it is inappropriate for former politicians to earn such large sums from private sector work, particularly when they continue to receive a parliamentary pension. However, supporters of Mr Hague argue that he is entitled to pursue a career outside of politics and that his earnings reflect his skills and experience.

Mr Hague has not commented on the release of the financial documents.

myself and if I go--
I have watched
the city from a distance at night
and wondered why I wrote no poem.
Come! yes,
the city is ablaze for you
and you stand and look at it.
And they are right. There is
no good in the world except out of
a woman and certain women alone
for certain. But what if
I arrive like a turtle,
with my house on my back or
a fish ogling from under water?
It will not do. I must be
steaming with love, colored
like a flamingo. For what?
To have legs and a silly head
and to smell, pah! like a flamingo
that soils its own feathers behind.
Must I go home filled
with a bad poem?
And they say:
Who can answer these things
till he has tried? Your eyes
are half closed, you are a child,
oh, a sweet one, ready to play
but I will make a man of you and
with love on his shoulder--!
And in the marshes
the crickets run
on the sunny dike's top and
make burrows there, the water
reflects the reeds and the reeds
move on their stalks and rattle drily.

olive oil

Take about 1 cup of the cauliflower florets, toss them with some olive oil, salt, and pepper, spread them on a baking sheet and roast them at 425F until brown and crispy on the outside, about 3o minutes. Set aside. In a large soup pot, fry the lardons until almost crispy, then remove them from the pot, leaving the fat. Add the onion, celery, and garlic to the fat in the pot, stir and cook for about 2 minutes until the onion begins to soften. Then stir in the bay leaf, the potato pieces and the remaining cauliflower and cook, stirring occasionally for about 5-7 minutes. Add 4 cups of the chicken stock, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook, covered, for about 20 minutes, until the cauliflower and potatoes are soft. Remove the bay leaf and stir in the cream. Puree the soup using a handheld blender, or in batches in a blender, until it is creamy and smooth. Return to the heat for another 5 or so minutes until heated through. At this point you can also add some more broth (or cream!) if you'd like to thin the soup a bit. Add salt and pepper to taste. Just before serving, stir in the creme fraiche. Divide the soup into serving bowls, top each bowl with pieces of roasted cauliflower and crispy lardons.

Medical imaging can greatly benefit from few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS). The majority of current FSS approaches rely on ample labeled semantic categories for instruction. However, these methods might not be suitable for medical images because of insufficient annotations. To tackle this predicament, we present the following innovations: (1) A new self-supervised FSS system tailored for medical images, eliminating the need for annotations during the learning process. Moreover, superpixels produce pseudo-labels to offer guidance; (2) An adjustable local prototype gathering component integrated within prototypical networks, designed to resolve the persistent issue of unequal representation between the foreground and background in medical image segmentation; (3) We validate the versatility of our suggested strategy for medical images through experiments on three distinct tasks: abdominal organ separation for CT and MRI, along with cardiac segmentation for MRI. Our findings indicate that, compared to traditional FSS techniques reliant on manual annotations, the presented method excels in medical image segmentation.

In this study, we examine the finite element approximation of Biot's consolidation model in poroelasticity utilizing MINI and stabilized P1-P1 elements. Our investigation focuses on the convergence of the completely discretized model via spatial discretization with these finite element types and the implicit Euler scheme in time. Furthermore, we tackle the problem of non-physical oscillations that emerge in the pressure estimation for minimal permeabilities and/or minute time intervals. We demonstrate that a Stokes-stable finite element combination is insufficient for generating a monotonic pressure discretization within these conditions. Subsequently, we propose a stabilization term to eliminate the oscillations and report numerical findings corroborating the monotonicity of the stabilized methods.

Shanda expressed intentions to expand its holding in Sina, possibly acquiring it entirely. The resulting entity would offer a comprehensive suite of services, including online role-playing games, news, entertainment, and wireless messaging.

Sina announced that this investment would not affect their business operations. In a statement, their board of directors pledged to uphold the interests of all stakeholders, including shareholders, employees, and customers. Both entities are publicly traded on the NYSE's Nasdaq index. Between January 12 and February 10, Sina disclosed in an SEC filing that approximately $230m was spent on purchasing its shares. There was a significant increase of over 10% in Sina's stock price on Friday due to takeover rumors. After hours trading saw an additional 6.4%, raising the closing price to $27.24. Analysts predict further gains upon resumption of trading in New York on Tuesday, following the public holiday. Accurately distinguishing pixel classes in quantitative image analysis frequently relies on the segmentation process. Nevertheless, imaging artifacts like the partial volume effect and sensor noise can complicate this task. These factors enhance the pixel intensity disparity within each class, resulting in overlapping intensities among them. This heightened discrepancy renders threshold-based segmentation techniques inadequate due to indistinct overlap zones in the histograms of pixel intensities. Class uncertainty escalates further when dealing with multicomponent systems, such as unsaturated moist granular media. In this study, we suggest an image processing methodology enhancing segmentation precision for multiphase systems. Initially, dubious boundary areas between classes are detected and discarded, enabling thresholding for individual-class regions. Subsequently, these boundaries are categorized via a distance function, and eventually, the segmentations are merged into a solitary labeled image. Ingredients
• 8 each bone-in chicken thighs (about 3 ½ pounds)
• Kosher salt and black pepper
• 2 cups chicken broth
• 2 cups water
• ½ cup white vinegar
• 2 tablespoons olive oil
• 4 medium garlic cloves, peeled and smashed
• 1 large shallot, finely chopped (about ¼ cup)
• Leaves from 3 sprigs fresh thyme, plus 1 sprig
• 1 pound mustard greens, washed, dried, and torn into bite-size pieces
• ¼ cup heavy cream

Instructions
1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. In a large bowl, combine the broth, water, vinegar, olive oil, garlic, chopped shallot, and thyme leaves; set aside.
2. In a large Dutch oven or heavy pot, layer the chicken thighs, greens, and thyme sprig, alternating and starting and ending with the greens. Pour the broth mixture over the top and press gently on the greens to submerge them.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for about 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the greens are wilted.
4. Transfer the chicken and greens to a platter using a slotted spoon. Cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
5. Increase the heat to medium and bring the liquid to a boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by about half. Stir in the heavy cream and return to a boil. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes, or until thickened. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
6. Pour the sauce over the chicken and greens. Serve.

Ingredients:

- 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup apple cider vinegar
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1 bunch of kale, stems removed and leaves torn into bite-size pieces
- 1 bunch of collard greens, stems removed and leaves torn into bite-size pieces
- 2 tablespoons unsalted butter

Instructions:

1. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper on both sides.

2. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. 

3. Add the chicken, skin-side down, and cook until the skin is golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip the chicken and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.

4. In the same pot, add the sliced onion and cook until it's soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until it's fragrant.

5. Pour in the apple cider vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring the vinegar to a simmer and let it cook until it's reduced by half, about 5 minutes.

6. Return the chicken to the pot and add the chicken broth. Bring the liquid to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it cook for 20 minutes.

7. After 20 minutes, add the kale and collard greens to the pot, pushing them down into the liquid. Cover the pot again and continue to cook for another 10 minutes, or until the greens are wilted and the chicken is cooked through.

8. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the butter until it's melted and the sauce is creamy. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt and pepper if needed.

9. Serve the chicken with the greens and sauce spooned over the top. Enjoy your Vinegar-Braised Chicken With Greens!

Quantum manipulation via light-matter interactions necessitates the importance of coherence. In this study, we present the discovery of remarkably stable valley polarization and valley coherence in bilayer WS2. The photoluminescence emission from bilayer WS2 adopts the polarization of its excitation beam, whether it's circularly or linearly polarized, and remains consistent at room temperature. The nearly perfect circular polarization of the luminescence signifies the interplay of spin, layer, and valley freedom within the bilayer system. Conversely, the linearly polarized photoluminescence illustrates the quantum coherence existing between the two disparate band extremes in the momentum domain - commonly referred to as valley quantum coherence - within atomically thin bilayer WS2. This finding expands possibilities for quantum control in atomic-scale semiconductors.

In this paper, we propose a new challenge and benchmark dataset called VisDA (Visual Domain Adaptation) to evaluate the performance of domain adaptation methods in computer vision tasks. Existing domain adaptation benchmarks focus mainly on text classification and neglect the unique challenges posed by visual data. VisDA addresses this gap by providing a diverse set of image datasets from various domains, including object recognition, scene understanding, and medical imaging.

The VisDA challenge consists of multiple task-specific sub-challenges, each with its own evaluation metric. These sub-challenges are designed to test different aspects of domain adaptation, such as adaptability to new classes, styles, and domains. We also provide a set of baseline models that utilize popular domain adaptation techniques, allowing participants to compare their approaches against established methods.

To further facilitate research in this area, we will host an annual competition where participants can submit their adapted models and compete against others. The winner will be selected based on their performance on a held-out test set.

We believe that VisDA will serve as a valuable resource for researchers working on domain adaptation in computer vision, encouraging them to develop more effective and robust methods that can handle diverse real-world scenarios.

Specifically, our method consists of two main components: a DNN model trained by AL and a saliency map generator. Firstly, we train a DNN model using only a small number of manually labeled samples via AL. Then, we use the trained DNN model as a teacher network to generate pseudo labels for unlabeled data. Finally, we combine these pseudo labels with the original ones to retrain the DNN model. This process can be iterated until convergence. Time-series remote sensing data provide an abundant trove of data useful for various applications, including tracking land cover alterations, crop observation, coastal transformations, flood hazard estimation, and urban growth analysis. In this study, we tackle the issue of forecasting urban expansion using time-series satellite imagery. Leveraging prior research, we present a two-step methodology grounded in semantic image segmentation for urban expansion prediction. The initial stage focuses on extracting data about urban areas across diverse time scales and readying it for subsequent training. The second phase integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) techniques to recognize temporal characteristics and anticipate urban expansion. This paper reports on experiments employing multiple multi-date satellite images depicting the three biggest cities in Saudi Arabia: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. Our findings suggest that the proposed technique outperforms existing approaches, as evidenced by enhancements in Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification precision.

The Chancellor has announced a £1.8bn package to help households with the cost of living, in his spring statement.

Rishi Sunak said the measures would help people "get through the next few months" of higher prices.

It includes a cut in the energy price cap, and £500m for households in council tax bands A to D.

The BBC's Laura Kuenssberg said the chancellor was "stepping up to help millions of households".

But shadow chancellor Rachel Reeves said help "should have been sooner" and accused Mr Sunak of "playing catch up".

Here are the key points from the statement:

What's happening to the energy price cap?
The energy price cap, which limits the amount suppliers can charge customers, will be cut in April by £200 per year.

It means around 28 million households will pay less for their gas and electricity.

Earlier this month, supporting measures were announced, including a £150 council tax rebate for most homes in England and a £200 discount on energy bills owed by households who get financial help with their council tax.

Why are people getting money off their council tax?
Mr Sunak said £500m would be available to help those in council tax bands A to D.

He said around 80% of households would receive a £150 council tax rebate. But those in bands A to D - typically the least valuable properties - would receive a minimum £350 payment.

The rebate will be paid directly into bank accounts from April, the chancellor said.

How much is the help worth in total?
The chancellor said the support package would be worth £1.8bn.

On top of the help with council tax, Mr Sunak said the Energy Price Guarantee would be extended, so that all households would pay no more than £2,500 a year for their energy bills.

Without the help, forecasts showed average household energy bills could have been as much as £3,500 from October.

Why did the chancellor make the announcement?
Mr Sunak said the announcement was designed to help people "get through the next few months".

He said: "We have a responsibility to help those who are paying the highest price for global inflation."

What else did he say?
The chancellor said the government would also make a one-off payment of £1bn to help people with business rates and council tax.

> Adversarial patches are small patches that can be attached to physical objects to fool image classifiers. In this paper, we propose a new type of adversarial patch, called an IPatch, that can be used to fool image classifiers remotely. An IPatch is a small patch that can be attached to a physical object to fool image classifiers when the object is viewed from a distance. We show that IPatches can be used to fool image classifiers in a variety of settings, including when the object is viewed from a distance, when the object is viewed through a camera, and when the object is viewed through a camera with a zoom lens. We also show that IPatches can be used to fool image classifiers in a variety of domains, including face recognition, object recognition, and scene recognition.

We introduce a method that allows to automatically segment images into
semantically meaningful regions without human supervision. Derived regions are
consistent across different images and coincide with human-defined semantic
classes on some datasets. In cases where semantic regions might be hard for
human to define and consistently label, our method is still able to find
meaningful and consistent semantic classes. In our work, we use pretrained
StyleGAN2~\cite{karras2020analyzing} generative model: clustering in the
feature space of the generative model allows to discover semantic classes. Once
classes are discovered, a synthetic dataset with generated images and
corresponding segmentation masks can be created. After that a segmentation
model is trained on the synthetic dataset and is able to generalize to real
images. Additionally, by using CLIP~\cite{radford2021learning} we are able to
use prompts defined in a natural language to discover some desired semantic
classes. We test our method on publicly available datasets and show
state-of-the-art results.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs), commonly employed in medical image segmentation and 3D navigation for robotic Minimally Invasive Surgeries (MISs), typically utilize down sampling layers to expand their receptive fields and extract abstract semantic information. However, these down sampling layers reduce the spatial dimensions of feature maps, potentially harming image segmentation accuracy. In contrast, atrous convolution serves as an alternative to down sampling layers, expanding the receptive field without diminishing the spatial dimensions of feature maps. This paper introduces an approach for optimally setting atrous rates to secure the maximum and complete receptive field using the least possible atrous convolutional layers. Additionally, we present a novel DCNN design, termed Atrous Convolutional Neural Network (ACNN), which combines cascaded atrous II-blocks, residual learning, and Instance Normalization (IN). Performance evaluation of the suggested ACNN on Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) image segmentation reveals that it surpasses U-Net and Deeplabv3+'s segmentation Intersection over Unions (IoUs), but boasts fewer trainable parameters.

US Open champion Svetlana Kuznetsova has tested positive for a banned drug, according to Belgian authorities.
Belgian sports minister Claude Eerdekens said that the Russian world number five tested positive for the stimulant ephedrine on 19 December. Kuznetsova was playing in an exhibition event in Charleroi at the time. Eerdekens said: "There is a problem. Ephedrine was discovered. She remains innocent until proved guilty. She can ask for it to be tested again." The situation remains unclear as the tournament was not commissioned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the International Tennis Federation (ITF) or the Women's Tennis Accosiation (WTA). The test was carried out by regional Belgian authorities and Kuznetsova has not yet been able to have a B sample tested.
Speaking at the Australian Open on Monday, before Eerdekens identified her, Kuznetsova said: "I'm not worried. I'm not using anything to push myself. "I have not been notified of any positive test, and I think it is unfair that it's come out the way it did." Eerdekens said that confirmation of the findings was sent last Friday to the player's address in Spain, as well as to the Belgian prosecutors' office and the Belgian and Russian tennis federations. He conceded Kuznetsova might have taken a medicine which contained the banned substance. "We have simply stated a fact," he said. "It is for the federation concerned to impose the disciplinary measures after a procedure that respects the defence.
"Either the ephedrine was taken to improve her performance or it is because she took some medicine legitimately to cure an infection." However, Kuznetsova's naming was condemned by Russian tennis chief Shamil Tarpishchev. "First of all, this Belgian sports minister has broken every ethical rule in the book by naming a player without any proof of wrongdoing, without any basic evidence," Tarpishchev said. "We all know the basic principle in doping cases. If there is a positive sample, then they should notify the International Tennis Federation (ITF) as well as the national federation within three days," he said. "This is not the case here. As of today we have not received any statement from the doping officials, nor did the ITF. "Today I called the ITF headquarters and they told me they know nothing about it. "If WADA (the World Anti-Doping Agency) was behind the testing, then we would also have known something by now. "Otherwise, all these looks to me as pure fiction and fabrication of the facts."

Ingredients:
- 8 ounces of pasta (fettuccine, penne, or your choice)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 pound Italian sausage, casings removed
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 ounces mushrooms, sliced
- 1/2 cup black olives, pitted and halved
- 1/2 cup white wine (optional)
- 1 cup tomato sauce
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Cook the pasta according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
2. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the Italian sausage and cook until browned, breaking it up into smaller pieces with a wooden spoon.
3. Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until translucent. Then, add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, until fragrant.
4. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they are soft and release their moisture, about 5-7 minutes.
5. If using white wine, pour it into the skillet and let it simmer until it has reduced by half.
6. Stir in the tomato sauce and black olives, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Let the sauce simmer for about 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream. Let the sauce heat through, but be careful not to let it boil.
8. Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss it with the sauce until it is well coated.
9. Divide the pasta amongst serving plates and garnish with fresh parsley.
10. Serve hot and enjoy your delicious Pasta Alla Boscaiola!

Heat oven to 425°F. Thoroughly rinse chicken, discarding its giblet package or saving it for later use. If required, trim any excess fat from chicken cavity. The year 2004 saw an alarming surge in cybercrime, with reports of malicious hacking incidents and online fraud schemes skyrocketing across the globe.

According to experts, the growth in high-speed internet access and the increasing dependence on digital technologies have created an environment in which cybercriminals can thrive.

"We've seen a significant increase in the number of cyber attacks over the past year," said Dr. Mark Loman, a leading expert in cybersecurity. "Everything from email scams to sophisticated network breaches is becoming more common."

One of the most disturbing trends in cybercrime is the rise of phishing scams. These are emails or text messages that appear to be from legitimate sources but actually aim to trick users into divulging sensitive information such as passwords or credit card numbers.

Let me start off by saying that I was introduced to the films of Terrence Malick in 1998 when I watched and was blown away by 'The Thin Red Line.' It is one of the best war movies ever made and while I can rant about it at length, that review belongs on a different page. It was with great anticipation that I waited for 'The New World.' I was lucky enough to get tickets to an advance screening and the theatre was full of people like me. Their take on the film was almost as interesting as the film was.

'The New World' is a film that will draw out one of two very powerful emotions: Love or Hate. I really don't believe there is a middle ground in this case. I think it is quite possibly the most beautifully photographed film I have ever seen. It is astonishing. The score from James Horner is, in my opinion, his greatest work. He's a wonderful composer but he has exceeded himself on every level. This is a movie that can be watched like art (because it is) and listened to as a symphony (it might as well be one). Very few movies leave me stunned and 'The New World' is so luscious that I think it is worth the journey, even if it is only to look at how beautiful it is and listen to how glorious it is. Is that a superficial way of looking at things? Perhaps, but they are the film's two most brilliant qualities.

'The New World' does have problems and I think it falls very much into a 'buyer beware' category. Malick's movie is long -- very long -- and feels every moment of it. I don't mind these things because I found it enchanting; many in the audience with me did not. These are not people who are 'dumb,' or who 'don't get it.' They are people who are used to 99% of the films that you will see. 'The New World' is very self-indulgent at times. No one can reasonably defend the pace of the film. I want to and I can't. This is a movie so full of substance that it is detrimental. It is so rich and textured that it would be hard to say where things could have been improved, but aside from the first forty minutes which deal largely with the question of whether or not the Europeans can survive the first winter or not, the dramatic 'action,' that is, the engine of a script that pushes one scene into the next, is idling at best. 'The New World' has a plodding pace and it took me on a nice quiet stroll that I enjoyed immensely. I can not, in good conscience though recommend to the man on the street that he go to see it. If less than a third of the theatre I was in walked out, I'd be stunned. I lost count because so many people left. Mostly the middle hour and a half of the film is to blame. Scenes drift from one to the next -- they're stunning and textured and personally I enjoyed them -- but they involved a lot of hanging out. Two people hanging out in the woods. I understand that the film has deep meditative and philosophical meanderings about man's relationship with nature and how one impacts the other. I get it. But a lot of the love story is about two people hanging out in the woods. All the time. If one of them had said 'Let us go watch the grass grow for the afternoon,' it would have been the most honest line in the entire film. It is the only thing I will fault Malick for here because it really does kill the film for a lot of people. His intelligence should not be questioned. I wish only he'd tried to focus the script a bit more and been specific rather than general. Can two people from different cultures be together? We get it already. We got it an hour ago. Oh, more grass growing ... must watch ... ha! Forgive my little joke.

The argument to be made though is that this film has not been made for everyone (the studio is no doubt surprised to learn this and will be scrambling to recover their money -- they did a good thing in making it but they're going to lose their shirts). It was made by Terrence Malick for Terrence Malick. I'm glad to have seen it but I spoke with twenty people who were not. There will be constant arguments on the user boards here at the IMDb. The film is going to have rabidly fanatical supporters who think everyone else is just too stupid to get it. And it is going to be criticized by many, many others who died a thousand deaths just trying to sift through the movie.

Two final thoughts: the first is that I hate myself for having to say anything negative about Malick or his film. He's a special film-maker and his films make it worth going to the theatre. 'The New World' is great but flawed and it is dishonest for anyone to pretend otherwise -- such behaviour is deceitful and pretentious.Thought number two is that although the film is equal parts challenging and rewarding (as great movies should be) it is especially important in the case of 'The New World' to see it in the theatre. It is so majestic in scope that I don't believe the greatest home theatre can do it justice. It is truly epic in its cinematography and score. If it doesn't win Oscars for both we will have witnessed a massive artistic injustice. NOTHING this year, NOTHING has come close to being a threat to 'The New World' for either of those two categories. Appreciate them as they were intended to be seen.

Spaghetti with Pan Fried Chicken and Cherry Tomato Puree
 
Serve up a quick and easy pasta dish that's perfect for kids and adults alike with this pan-fried chicken and cherry tomato puree recipe. Both the chicken and the tomato puree can be prepared well in advance, making this a great choice for busy families.

Ingredients 
300g cherry tomatoes, halved
1 garlic clove, chopped
1 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp red wine vinegar
6oz spaghetti
1 small chicken breast, cut into strips
1 tbsp plain flour
1 egg, beaten
30g breadcrumbs
30g grated parmesan
1 tbsp olive oil
freshly ground black pepper

Method
1. To make the tomato puree, place the tomatoes in a small pan with the garlic, olive oil and red wine vinegar. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft.
2. Season with pepper, then blend until smooth. Pour into a bowl and wipe the pan clean.
3. Bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the spaghetti according to the packet instructions.
4. Meanwhile, prepare the chicken. Place the flour, egg and breadcrumbs in three separate bowls. Dip the chicken strips first in the flour, then the egg (allowing any excess to drip off) and then the breadcrumbs.
5. Heat the oil in the wiped-out pan and fry the chicken strips for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden-brown and completely cooked through.
6. Drain the spaghetti and either stir into the tomato puree or serve with the tomato puree poured over. Serve with the chicken strips and a grating of parmesan.

The Polyglot Petition for Home Protection was the first world-wide proclamation against the manufacturing and international trade in liquor and drugs as well as the prohibition of legalised vice. It served as a first major campaign to raise public awareness of the need for international agreements on controls for opium and its derivatives. Description of the petition
Addressed to all rulers and nations of the world, this petition to adopt prohibition was written by the American Woman's Christian Temperance Union (WCTU) president Frances Willard in 1884. It was carried across the world by at least four World WCTU missionaries who gathered signatures of nearly eight million people in more than fifty countries. The signatures can be categorized in three basic sections: signatures of individual women, written endorsements of men, and attestations of leaders of groups that had endorsed the petition. The signed petitions from the U.S. (over 750,000) were sent to Mrs. Rebecca C. Shuman in Evanston, Illinois who trimmed and mounted them on white muslin, one-half yard in width and bound with red ribbon on one side and blue ribbon on the other. Signed petitions from Great Britain (350,000 signatories) came in already mounted on cloth in time for presentation to the U.S. president in February 1885. The Polyglot Petition is archived in the Woman's Christian Temperance Union Administration Building in Evanston, Illinois, United States of America.

Three viewings of this film have left me in awe, yet it isn't everyone's cup of tea. Marty Scorsese himself faced a 25-year battle to secure funding for its production.

Despite my appreciation, I comprehend why some consider the film dull and excessive in length. Contrarily, I find it perfectly paced.

Most likely, the film's theme is the cause of disconnection for many viewers. In today's era of rampant secularism and materialism, a film like this can only seem antiquated.

At its core, this is a movie chronicling the spiritual journey from egoistic self-absorption to radiant, selfless love. Thus, it represents the true essence of Christianity.

What sets this film apart for me is its compelling portrayal of this self-transcendence process, coupled with its connection to the collective missionary phase of historical Christianity. Although the Japanese exhibit remarkable refinement in their cruelty, they embody a deeper personal and cultural understanding than the unenlightened Portuguese missionaries, oblivious to their cultural arrogance.

The intricacies of this narrative required nearly three hours of skillful cinematic artistry to unfold and culminate spiritually and historically.

In summary, for those familiar with the Christian path of self-transcendence into humbled love, this film is a triumph. For others, it may appear tedious.

For those intrigued by this exploration of self-transcendence, I recommend "The Assassin" by Hsiao-hsien Hou – a film showcasing the Taoist interpretation of this inner journey.

Remove the insides of 50g Kabocha squash and set aside. In a pot, cook the squash with 50g squash and 150ml water until softened. Blend the cooked squash, 150g squash insides, 150ml water, 50ml milk, and 2 tbsp sugar together until smooth. Heat the mixture in the pot and add 1 tbsp white miso, blending well. Taste and add sugar if needed. If too thick, add more milk. Soften the reserved squash by heating it in plastic wrap in the microwave, then mash. Combine mashed squash and 150g Shiratamako in a bowl, adding water gradually to knead into a dough consistency. Form into 2cm balls, making an indentation in each with a finger. We present approaches for the study of fluid-structure interactions subject
to thermal fluctuations. A mixed mechanical description is utilized combining
Eulerian and Lagrangian reference frames. We establish general conditions for
operators coupling these descriptions. Stochastic driving fields for the
formalism are derived using principles from statistical mechanics. The
stochastic differential equations of the formalism are found to exhibit
significant stiffness in some physical regimes. To cope with this issue, we
derive reduced stochastic differential equations for several physical regimes.
We also present stochastic numerical methods for each regime to approximate the
fluid-structure dynamics and to generate efficiently the required stochastic
driving fields. To validate the methodology in each regime, we perform analysis
of the invariant probability distribution of the stochastic dynamics of the
fluid-structure formalism. We compare this analysis with results from
statistical mechanics. To further demonstrate the applicability of the
methodology, we perform computational studies for spherical particles having
translational and rotational degrees of freedom. We compare these studies with
results from fluid mechanics. The presented approach provides for
fluid-structure systems a set of rather general computational methods for
treating consistently structure mechanics, hydrodynamic coupling, and thermal
fluctuations.

Dean Cornwell (March 5, 1892 – December 4, 1960) was an American illustrator and muralist. His oil paintings were frequently featured in popular magazines and books as literary illustrations, advertisements, and posters promoting the war effort. Throughout the first half of the 20th century he was a dominant presence in American illustration. At the peak of his popularity he was nicknamed the "Dean of Illustrators". Background
Cornwell was born in Louisville, Kentucky. His father, Charles L. Cornwell, was a civil engineer whose drawings of industrial subjects fascinated Cornwell as a child. He began his professional career as a cartoonist for the Louisville Herald. Soon thereafter he moved to Chicago, where he studied at the Art Institute and worked for the Chicago Tribune. In 1915 he moved to New Rochelle, New York, a well known artist colony, and studied in New York City under Harvey Dunn at the Art Students League of New York. Eventually he traveled to London to study mural painting as an apprentice to Frank Brangwyn.

FOR THE CRUST:
1 cup Graham cracker crumbs
3 tbsp Sugar
1/4 cup Butter, melted

FOR THE FILLING:
8 oz Cream cheese
9 oz Sugar
1.5 oz Cornstarch
12 oz Goat cheese
5 oz Sour cream
3/4 tsp Cinnamon
3/4 tsp Ginger
1/4 tsp Nutmeg
1/4 tsp Cloves
8 oz Pumpkin puree
4 Eggs
1 Egg yolk

Preheat oven to 350°F (176°C). In a medium bowl, combine graham cracker crumbs and sugar. Drizzle melted butter over top and mix well. Coat a springform pan with baking spray. Press graham crumb mixture onto the bottom of the pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 250°F (121°C) and place a cake pan filled with water halfway up in the oven to steam. In a large bowl fitted with a paddle attachment, beat cream cheese and sugar together on low speed. Add cornstarch, scrape sides, and continue beating for 2 minutes. Add goat cheese and sour cream, scrape sides, and beat for another 2 minutes. Incorporate spices, followed by pumpkin puree, scraping sides as necessary. Finally, add eggs and egg yolk, one at a time, until fully combined. Transfer batter to springform pan and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes without fan. Cheesecake is cooked when it no longer jiggles in the center. Allow to cool completely for 5 hours or overnight before slicing with a warm knife.

Steady states of the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system are obtained and classified based on the central redshift. As the central redshift approaches zero, these states can be approximated by a steady state of the Vlasov-Poisson system. For his discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1969, along with Richard P. Feynman and Jack Steinberger.

In addition to his work on weak force interaction, Beam made important contributions to the development of the quark model of matter, which is a fundamental theory of physics explaining the nature of matter.

Beam passed away on July 1, 2021, at the age of 86. He was widely regarded as a pioneer in the field of particle physics and his work continues to inspire students and researchers today.

Procedures: Select twelve unblemished organically grown small lemons, preferrably Meyer (a small type). Wash and dry the lemons. If using store-bought lemons, scrub them carefully to remove any pesticides. Cut a thin slice from the top and the bottom of each lemon. Set one lemon on end and make a vertical cut 3 quarters of the way through the fruit, so that the 2 halves still remain attached at the base; do not cut it in half. Turn the lemon upside down and rotate it so that you can make a second vertical cut down the center, crosswise to the first, leaving the bottom Fill each cut with as much salt as it will hold. Carefully place the lemon at the bottom of a hot, sterilized, wide-mouthed quart glass jar. Proceed in this manner with the remaining lemons, compressing them in the jar until no space is left and the lemon juice has risen to the top. Seal and set aside at room temperature. More lemons may be added in the following days as the lemon rinds begin to soften. Make sure the lemons are covered with juice at all times, adding freshly squeezed lemon juice if necessary. The lemons are ready to use when the rinds are tender, in 5 to 6 weeks. Rinse them lightly before using. Once opened, refrigerate preserved lemons for up to 6 months.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20cm springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper. Wrap the exterior twice with aluminum foil. Blend cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until silky. With the processor running, incorporate cornstarch, followed by eggs, one at a time, pausing occasionally to scrape sides. Incorporate vanilla, zest, juice, creams, and 1/4 tsp salt. Process only until combined. Add chocolate and pulse until smooth. Transfer mixture into the pan and place it in a larger baking pan. Fill the larger pan with water up to the midpoint of the cheesecake pan's sides. Cook for 45 minutes, then remove from oven, but keep the cheesecake inside for an additional hour. Release pan from the water bath, discard foil, and let the cake cool completely in the pan on a wire rack. Cover and refrigerate overnight. To release, set pan on a hot, damp towel to help loosen the base. Use a palette knife to gently separate the edge of the cheesecake from the pan, then transfer it onto a serving platter. Adorn with fruit by artfully arranging it atop the cheesecake and drizzling passionfruit puree on top. Slice with a clean, heated, dry knife.

the Kullback-Leibler, Bhattacharryya, R\'enyi and Cauchy-Schwartz divergences.

reviewed. A class of divergences is extended to multiway divergences for

People's assertion that he lacked a detailed plan for the Star Wars saga doesn't resonate with me. Although he didn't have an exhaustive roadmap with each step charted out, he did have a general blueprint. The primary arguments put forth are Leia, Anakin, and the Emperor. These points actually bolster the argument that he did possess a "plan." Initially, Leia was merely the princess of Alderaan and the leader of the rebellion, whereas Luke's sister was intended to be a distinct character. Now, they are merged into a single character. Similarly, Anakin Skywalker, who was once a Jedi fighting alongside Kenobi, met his demise at the hands of Vader, Kenobi's padawan who succumbed to the dark side and betrayed the Jedi Order - both characters combined. The Emperor, a shady politician controlled by the enigmatic Darth Sidious, the Dark Lord of the Sith - another instance of merging characters. George Lucas aimed to create a twelve-part epic, but in the 70's/80's, he couldn't produce that many films. To streamline his narrative and conserve resources, he consolidated characters into a more compact storyline. I use the term "plan" loosely since it is challenging to pinpoint another person's intentions; it could be as elementary as jotted ideas on index cards.

A close associate of former Yukos boss Mikhail Khodorkovsky has told a court that fraud charges levelled against him are "false".
Platon Lebedev has been on trial alongside Mr Khodorkovsky since June in a case centring around the privatisation of a fertiliser firm. The pair claim they are being punished by the authorities for the political ambitions of Mr Khodorkovsky. Mr Lebedev said there were "absurd contradictions" in the case. Opening his defence, he said he could not see the legal basis of the charges he faced, which also include allegations of tax evasion. "To my embarrassment, I could not understand the file of complaints against me," he told a Moscow court. Mr Lebedev headed the Menatep group, the parent company of Yukos.
Mr Lebedev and Mr Khodorkovsky, who each face a possible 10 year jail sentence if convicted, will be questioned by a judge over the next few days. Mr Khodorkovsky began his testimony last week, telling the court that he objected to the way that the "running of a normal business has been presented as a work of criminal fiction". The charges are seen by supporters as politically motivated and part of a drive by Russian President Vladimir Putin to rein in the country's super-rich business leaders, the so-called oligarchs. Yukos has been presented with a $27.5bn (£13bn) tax demand by the Russian authorities and its key Yugansk division was auctioned off to part settle the bill. The company's effort to gain bankruptcy protection in the US - in a bid to win damages for the sale - were dismissed by a court in Texas.

Rang De Basanti is a thought-provoking film by the director, focusing on modern-day individuals and their connections to the past. The younger generation, familiar with Mac-D but fond of traditional Indian meals, holds onto national values primarily through food. This movie transcends typical Bollywood tropes, featuring minimal music, few exotic locations, and intense emotional depth.

Rang De Basanti invites self-reflection, prompting viewers to consider authentic ways of honoring freedom. One poignant quote resonated deeply: "I believed there were two kinds of people – those who die weeping, and those who disappear in silence. But today, I discovered a third category: those who laugh."

Director Rakesh Omprakash Mehra showcases bravery and innovation in this project. The casting choices were brilliant, especially veterans Om Puri and Anupam Kher, although underutilized. Each character develops throughout the film, allowing ample room for the actors to shine. Mehra's unique vision has made him a trailblazer in contemporary Indian cinema, having previously impressed with films like Aks (starring Amitabh Bachchan and Manoj Bajpai) in 2001.

The exceptional use of cinematography sets Rang De Basanti apart. Through skillful juxtaposition, the director seamlessly blends the present with the past, leaving audiences captivated by the behind-the-scenes efforts and the dedication of the actors.

From its uplifting opening to the gripping finale, Rang De Basanti inspires and challenges viewers.

Adapromine is a Russian-marketed antiviral medication belonging to the adamantane class, chemically linked to amantadine (1-aminoadamantane), rimantadine (1-(1-aminoethyl)adamantane), and memantine (1-amino-3,5-dimethyladamantane). Its antiviral properties resemble those of rimantadine yet it exhibits a more extensive range of action, combating influenza strains of types A and B. In the 1980s, adapromine-resistant influenza A virus strains emerged in Mongolia and the Soviet Union alongside resistant rimantadine and deitiforine strains. Animal EEG investigations indicate that adapromine, along with adamantanes such as amantadine, bromantane (1-amino-2-bromophenyladamantane), and memantine, present stimulating psychoactive effects akin to those of psychostimulants and potentially antidepressant effects. The nature of these psychostimulant effects diverges from those of typical psychostimulants like amphetamine; instead, adamantane derivatives are often referred to as "adaptogens" and "actoprotectors."

Ngangom Bala Devi (born 2 February 1990) is an Indian professional footballer who currently plays as a forward for Rangers Women in the Scottish Women's Premier League and the Indian national team. She is also the first Asian to play and score in a professional league in Scotland and also the first South Asian to sign a professional contract.

Early Life and Career

Devi was born in Manipur, India. Her interest in football was sparked by her father, who played the game at a local level. She began her professional career as a footballer in 2005 with Manipur Police Sports Club in the Indian Women's League (IWL). After five years in this team, she moved to New Radiant SC of Maldives, where she spent just one season before returning to her former club.

Bala Devi has also represented India at the international level, playing in the SAFF Women's Championship and the Women's Asian Cup qualifiers. Over the years, she has been an integral part of the Indian national team and has scored several crucial goals.

Move to Rangers F.C. 

Bala Devi signed an 18-month contract with Scottish club Rangers F.C in January 2020, making her the first Indian woman to be signed by a professional club in the United Kingdom. This move was facilitated through a partnership between Rangers and Bengaluru FC. Devi made her debut against Hearts, scoring in the final two minutes of the match. Her consistent performances have received widespread recognition and commendation.

Style of Play and Legacy

Devi is known for her strength, agility, and precision in front of the goal. She is capable of playing as both a forward and attacking midfielder and has earned comparisons to her male counterparts in Indian Football.

Devi's move to Rangers was a landmark moment in Indian football history, particularly for women in the sport. Her career demonstrates the possibility of Indian talent finding opportunities in prestigious international leagues; a fact that has been acclaimed as instrumental in fostering ambition and aspiration among young Indian women interested in football.

Honours and Awards

Among her many accolades, Bala Devi was crowned AIFF Women's Player of the Year twice, in 2014 and 2015. She was also the top scorer in the Indian Women's League in three consecutive seasons, from 2016 to 2019. Achievements at international level include being part of the SAFF Women's Championship-winning squads of 2010 and 2016.

Sure, here's a recipe for bow ties with sausage and leek sauce:

Ingredients:

* 1 pound bow tie pasta
* 1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
* 2 medium leeks, chopped (about 2 cups)
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1/4 cup white wine (optional)
* 1/4 cup chicken broth
* 1/4 cup heavy cream
* 1 tablespoon tomato paste
* 1 teaspoon dried thyme
* Salt and pepper to taste
* Grated Parmesan cheese for serving (optional)

Instructions:

1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the bow tie pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water and then drain the pasta.
2. In a large skillet, cook the Italian sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the sausage from the skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, add the chopped leeks and minced garlic. Cook until the leeks are softened and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
4. If using white wine, add it to the skillet and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
5. Add the chicken broth, heavy cream, tomato paste, and thyme to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring the mixture to a simmer.
6. Add the cooked sausage back into the skillet and stir to combine.
7. Add the cooked bow tie pasta to the skillet and toss to combine, adding some reserved pasta cooking water if the sauce is too thick.
8. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Serve the bow ties with sausage and leek sauce hot

Crude oil prices surged back above the $47 a barrel mark on Thursday after an energy market watchdog raised its forecasts for global demand.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned demand for Opec's crude in the first quarter would outstrip supply. The IEA raised its estimate of 2005 oil demand growth by 80,000 barrels a day to 84 million barrels a day. US light crude rose $1.64 to $47.10, while Brent crude in London gained $1.32 to $44.45.
The Paris-based IEA watchdog, which advises industrialized nations on energy policy, said the upward revision was due to stronger demand from China and other Asian countries. The fresh rally in crude prices followed gains on Wednesday which were triggered by large falls in US crude supplies following a cold spell in North America in January. The US Department of Energy reported that crude stockpiles had fallen 1m barrels to 294.3m. On top of that, ongoing problems for beleaguered Russian oil giant Yukos have also prompted the IEA to revise its output estimates from Russia - a major non-Opec supplier. "I think that prices are now beginning to set a new range and it looks like the $40 to $50 level," said energy analyst Orin Middleton of Barclays Capital.

Acton House is a mansion in Acton, West London, that was formerly the home of Napoleon III, Emperor of France, and his wife, Empress Eugénie. It was built in the 1870s by Richard Norman Shaw for the Scottish economist and historian William Hewett. In 1883, it was bought by the architect Richard Shaw, who designed the nearby St. Barnabas Church.

In 1904, the house was acquired by the Welsh businessman Sir John Williams Bt., who lived there with his wife Frances (née Cornwallis), daughter of Colonel Charles Cornwallis of Abermarlais, Carmarthenshire. The couple's eldest daughter, Ursula, married Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg, the son of the Austrian ambassador, in 1919.

In 1928, Acton House was acquired by Baron Melchior de Polignac, who rented it to King Zog of Albania from 1936 to 1938. It was then acquired by the Turkish-born Hüseyin Jawdat, who used it as a training center for the Muslim World League.

Since 1958, it has been the home of the International Youth Hostel. In 1985, it was Grade II* listed by English Heritage.

To create Vanilla Bean Rooibos Ice Cream:
1. Heat 1 cup whole milk, 2 cups heavy cream, a split Madagascar Vanilla Bean with seeds scraped, and 3 tbsp honey in a saucepan till it barely simmers. Remove from heat.
2. Steep 2 tbsp organic Rooibos tea leaves within this mixture for an hour.
3. Warm 1 cup heavy cream in a separate bowl over low heat. Strain the milk-rooibos tea mixture into this bowl, discarding the leaves but retaining the vanilla bean.
4. Whisk 6 large egg yolks in a bowl. Progressively add the warmed milk-tea mixture to the eggs. Return this combined mixture to the saucepan and cook gently, stirring often, till it thickens lightly and coats the spoon's back. Strain the mixture into the held-back heavy cream.
5. Infuse the strained vanilla bean into the cold mixture for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for 4-8 hours or until the temperature drops to 40°F or lower.
6. Remove the vanilla bean. Combine the chilled cream mixture with 1 tsp amaretto liquor and process in an ice cream maker as directed.
7. For Dulce de Leche, bring 1 quart whole milk, 1 cup sugar, 1 vanilla bean (split and seeded), and 3 tbsp honey to a gentle simmer in a saucepan. Cook for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, till it thickens significantly. Cool completely before using.
8. Mix chopped raw almonds (3/4 cup) with the prepared ice cream right before freezing. Swirl in the cooled Dulce de Leche prior to serving.

In a large mixing bowl, combine 1/2 cup Sour Bread Starter with 2 cups warm water. Gradually mix in 1 cup rye flour and blend. Let sit in a warm spot (around 85°F) for 20 to 40 hours, adjusting sourness. Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water; add to mixture. Combine salt and gradually incorporate the remaining 1.5 cups rye flour. Introduce white flour, bit by bit, and continue to mix. Once a stiff dough forms, rest for 10-15 minutes before turning onto a floured surface for kneading. Transfer dough to a greased bowl, cover, and let it double in size in a warm location (approximately 1 to 1.5 hours). Divide dough into 2 portions, setting aside about 1/2 cup for later. Yet, it was on December 3rd, 1991 that British telecommunications company Vodafone sent the world's first SMS text message - marking the beginning of a revolution in communication and ushering in the age of mobile phone usage.

Since then, mobiles have become ingrained in our daily lives, transforming how we communicate with one another both domestically and internationally. On-chip gadgets and diagnostic chips at the point of care consist of numerous elements including nanosensors, which necessitate interaction with other device components. Inter-component communication within these devices calls for efficient solutions like molecular communication. Among various methods, kinesin-driven MT motility emerges as an effective approach for transporting informational units between parts. Determining the ideal configuration for these conduits, however, remains difficult. This study introduces a mathematical optimization model for determining the optimal channel shape and dimensions for any transmission duration. Three distinct models are derived for rectangular, regular polygonal, and regular polygonal ring channels. The results indicate that the most effective channel designs are square-shaped for rectangular channels and circular-shaped for other classes. Furthermore, among all two-dimensional structures, the design with the highest information transmission rate is the circular-shaped channel.

Despite deep convolutional neural networks achieved impressive progress in
medical image computing and analysis, its paradigm of supervised learning
demands a large number of annotations for training to avoid overfitting and
achieving promising results. In clinical practices, massive semantic
annotations are difficult to acquire in some conditions where specialized
biomedical expert knowledge is required, and it is also a common condition
where only few annotated classes are available. In this work, we proposed a
novel method for few-shot medical image segmentation, which enables a
segmentation model to fast generalize to an unseen class with few training
images. We construct our few-shot image segmentor using a deep convolutional
network trained episodically. Motivated by the spatial consistency and
regularity in medical images, we developed an efficient global correlation
module to capture the correlation between a support and query image and
incorporate it into the deep network called global correlation network.
Moreover, we enhance discriminability of deep embedding to encourage clustering
of the feature domains of the same class while keep the feature domains of
different organs far apart. Ablation Study proved the effectiveness of the
proposed global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Extensive
experiments on anatomical abdomen images on both CT and MRI modalities are
performed to demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our proposed
model.

Most current semantic segmentation techniques utilize a U-Net structure with an encoder-decoder configuration. However, it remains difficult for a basic U-Net with simple skip connections to capture the global multi-scale context effectively: 1) Not every skip connection setup is beneficial due to the compatibility problem between encoder and decoder stages, and certain skip connections may even deteriorate segmentation performance; 2) The standard U-Net performs inferior to its skip connection-free counterpart on certain datasets. In light of these discoveries, we put forward a novel segmentation framework called UCTransNet, which incorporates a suggested CTrans module within the U-Net design, from a channel standpoint with attention mechanism.

More specifically, the CTrans module represents an alternative to U-Net's skip connections, comprising two sub-modules: a CCT (Channel Cross Fusion with Transformer) sub-module and a CCA (Channel-wise Cross-Attention) sub-module. The CCT sub-module performs multiscale channel fusion using Transformers, while the CCA sub-module channels the fused multiscale channel-wise information towards decoder features to eliminate ambiguity. Consequently, the proposed connection consisting of CCT and CCA can substitute the original skip connection to address semantic discrepancies for precise medical image segmentation. The experimental findings indicate that our UCTransNet generates more accurate segmentation outcomes and delivers consistent enhancements compared to the state-of-the-art for semantic segmentation across various datasets and conventional architectures featuring transformers or U-shaped structures. Repository: <https://github.com/McGregorWwww/UCTransNet>.

Serves 4 as leftovers

Ingredients (for 2 servings):

1 tbsp butter, softened

1 medium butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and diced

1 onion, diced

3 garlic cloves, finely diced

1 (14.25-ounce) can chopped tomatoes

½ cup water

½ cup milk

1 cup butternut squash puree (about 1/2 pound)

salt

1 teaspoon ground black pepper

1 cup dry white wine

2 cups chicken stock, or water

1 cup fresh baby arugula, washed and chopped, and torn leaves for garnish

½ cup chopped fresh dill

4 cups fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves, plus more for garnish

Directions:

1. Heat a 15-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add butter and sauté until it reaches a depth of 10 inches (about 3 minutes). Remove from the heat and set aside.

2. When the butter is gone, add the butternut squash and onion. Cook for 5 more minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes, then the water, milk, and stir vigorously until the sauce thickens, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper, to taste. Transfer the mixture to a food processor and pulse until it separates and starts to form a smooth puree. Transfer the puree to a large saucepan.

3. Bring to a boil. Add 2 cups of the stock (or water) and reduce heat for 2 minutes. Stir in the baby arug. Reduce the heat for 10 seconds, then add the wine and remaining stock. Lower heat to a simmer and cook until the wine has reduced by almost half and the soup is thick, about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.

4. Stir in the parsley, drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve. Garnish with fresh dill and parsley leaves.

Image segmentation, a significant area of investigation in computer vision, continually attracts the attention of researchers due to its crucial role in image processing. Despite the widespread use of clustering methods in this domain, there is a persistent demand for more effective approaches. This paper introduces a new clustering-based image segmentation technique. Our focus lies in the utilization of color spaces, specifically the lab color model. We employ the well-known hard clustering method K-means, but since its efficiency hinges on selecting an appropriate distance metric, we opt for the cosine distance measure. Following the clustering process, we apply a Sobel filter to the segmented image for smoothing. Subsequently, we analyze the filtered image using the marker watershed algorithm to derive the ultimate segmented version of our initial image. To assess the effectiveness of our method, we evaluate the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR).

4 large eggs
4 large egg whites
1 cup nonfat milk
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, minced
1/4 teaspoon fresh ground pepper
5 cups chopped spinach, wilted (see Tip)
4 cups whole grain bread (cut into 1-inch cubes, crusts removed if desired)
1 cup ham steak, diced
1/2 cup jarred roasted red pepper, chopped
3/4 cup shredded gruyere cheese or 3/4 cup swiss cheese
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a 7-by-11-inch glass baking dish or a 2-quart casserole with cooking spray. Whisk eggs, egg whites and milk in a medium bowl. Add mustard, rosemary and pepper; whisk to combine. Toss spinach, bread, ham and roasted red peppers in a large bowl. Add the egg mixture and toss well to coat. Transfer to the prepared baking dish and push down to compact. Cover with foil. Bake until the custard has set, 40 to 45 minutes. Uncover, sprinkle with cheese and continue baking until the pudding is puffed and golden on top, 15 to 20 minutes more. Transfer to a wire rack and cool for 15 to 20 minutes before serving. TIPS. Tip: To wilt spinach, rinse thoroughly with cool water. Transfer to a large microwave-safe bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and punch several holes in it. Microwave on High until wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Squeeze out excess moisture before adding the spinach to the recipe. MAKE AHEAD TIP: Prepare casserole through Step 2; refrigerate overnight. Let stand at room temperature while the oven preheats. Bake as directed in Step 3.

Jamil El-Banna, 45, from west London, was seized in Afghanistan where he had gone to help with relief efforts.

Born on May 16, 1959, in New York City, Andrew Litton is an accomplished American orchestral conductor.
